candidates.title: Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure
candidates.snippet:
Broadcom has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42 billion in financing to support the AI company's massive infrastructure expansion, according to Anthropic's IPO filing reviewed by Reuters. The financing could cover roughly one-third of Anthropic's $125.2 billion commitment to lease tensor processing unit (TPU) computing capacity over five years.
The post Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure
Broadcom has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42 billion in financing to support the AI company’s massive infrastructure expansion, according to Anthropic’s IPO filing reviewed by Reuters . The financing could cover roughly one-third of Anthropic’s $125.2 billion commitment to lease tensor processing unit (TPU) computing capacity over five years.
The arrangement highlights the increasingly close relationship between Anthropic and Broadcom, which spans chip supply, equipment leasing and financing. Broadcom is expected to become Anthropic’s largest compute supplier in 2027 as the AI company expands the infrastructure required to train and operate its Claude models.
Under the financing agreement, Broadcom can designate a financing partner, and Anthropic could convert debt instruments into equity. Anthropic said in its filing that it does not expect to sell any of the notes before completing its planned initial public offering.
The financing comes as Anthropic prepares for an IPO that could potentially value the company at about $2 trillion, according to Reuters. The company’s extensive spending commitments show the enormous capital requirements of developing frontier AI models and building the infrastructure needed to run them at scale.
Anthropic’s $125.2 billion TPU commitment covers a five-year lease of computing capacity. Google and Broadcom have collaborated on multiple generations of Google’s TPUs, specialized processors designed for artificial intelligence workloads.
Anthropic announced an expanded partnership with Broadcom and Google in April 2026 that is expected to give the company access to multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU computing capacity beginning in 2027.
The relationship could also create a significant new revenue stream for Broadcom. Anthropic is expected to become Broadcom’s largest compute customer in 2027, while Broadcom projects approximately $115 billion of AI semiconductor revenue in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028.
The financing strategy resembles moves by Nvidia, which has increasingly used its balance sheet and investments to help customers finance AI infrastructure containing its chips. Broadcom’s arrangement with Anthropic similarly connects financing with future demand for its semiconductor technology.
Anthropic also identified risks associated with the relationship. In its IPO prospectus, the company said Broadcom’s roles as both a hardware supplier and financing partner could create “potential conflicts of interest” affecting Anthropic’s access to computing infrastructure.
Broadcom’s decisions involving hardware availability and pricing could potentially influence Anthropic’s ability to secure enough computing capacity to support its operations.
Anthropic disclosed that it deposited cash into a restricted account for Broadcom’s benefit in April 2026 under the convertible debt arrangement. Under certain circumstances, the company could be required to contribute additional amounts to that account.
The filing also warned that certain payment or performance defaults could make a substantial portion of Anthropic’s lease obligations immediately payable, while potentially limiting the company’s ability to use the $42 billion Broadcom financing facility to satisfy those obligations.
The relationship illustrates the increasingly interconnected economics of the AI infrastructure market, with chip suppliers, cloud providers and AI developers entering large financing and procurement agreements as they race to build computing capacity.

candidates.title: Etched fields funding offers at $40B+ valuation, sources say
candidates.snippet: Etched fields funding offers at $40B+ valuation, sources say TechCrunch
candidates.text:
Although it’s only been a couple of months since Etched raised $700 million at a $21 billion valuation , the AI chip startup is already being plied with investment offers at double or more its value, according to people familiar with the company.
Etched is reviewing incoming bids that range from $40 billion from top-tier investors to $50 billion from lesser-known backers, one person said. These fundraising talks are early, so terms of any deal, should one happen, may change. Etched declined to comment.
While this may seem like a fast timetable to raise another mega round, Etched is pursuing a particularly expensive segment of the AI industry: building full AI hardware systems powered by its own proprietary chips. The person familiar with these offers said that if it raises as much as its last round, this could give Etched a cushion of as much as 3.5 years of runway.
There are reasons why VCs are hot to own a piece of Etched. The four-year-old startup shows promise of challenging Nvidia. Not only did quant trading firm Jane Street lead the last $700 million round, it is also a customer that took delivery of an early system. Etched said in July that it had already secured $1 billion in customer orders, including the one from Jane Street, after manufacturing its test chip at a TSMC factory this summer.
Co-founder and COO Robert Wachen previously told TechCrunch that investors are so enthusiastic because Etched has designed two new components from scratch to speed up inference — the computing process that happens after a user submits a prompt.
The company claims its chips can process more tokens faster and at a lower cost than Nvidia’s. That’s the reason its processors have been so attractive to Jane Street, for whom a microscopic advantage in speed can yield massive profits.
The startup has also impressed investors with its ability to attract engineers from Nvidia, with roughly 15% of Etched’s 400-person workforce having previously worked at the chip giant, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Etched also operates a new 10-megawatt data center in Silicon Valley and established a facility in Taiwan to coordinate production near TSMC.
Co-founders Gavin Uberti and Chris Zhu famously met in an advanced math course at Harvard, while Wachen was Uberti’s roommate and they dropped out to pursue the company.
In terms of fast rounds at big leaps in valuations, Etched already has a history of them. The startup announced a $300 million round at a $10.3 billion valuation led by Sequoia in July. It announced the $700 million round at a $21 billion valuation in September. Back-to-back funding rounds, which essentially act as a single financing split into two tranches with separate valuations, are increasingly common among the buzziest startups.

candidates.title: SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips
candidates.snippet:
SpaceX is seeking approximately $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia artificial intelligence chips, with the Elon Musk-led company discussing the potential financing with banks and asset managers, according to a Reuters report. The proposed financing would consist of approximately $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion of investment-grade debt.
The post SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips
SpaceX is seeking approximately $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia artificial intelligence chips, with the Elon Musk-led company discussing the potential financing with banks and asset managers, according to a Reuters report . The proposed financing would consist of approximately $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion of investment-grade debt.
Asset manager PIMCO is among the parties SpaceX has been discussing financing with, while Apollo is expected to lead the transaction and help distribute the debt to a broad group of investors.
The financing would support SpaceX’s purchase of Nvidia hardware as Musk expands the computing infrastructure supporting his companies’ artificial intelligence ambitions.
Musk recently said xAI’s Colossus 2 data center could more than double the number of Nvidia chips it uses by December. He also said the company plans to rely exclusively on Nvidia hardware when building its data centers.
The potential $40 billion financing illustrates the rapidly increasing capital requirements associated with building large-scale AI infrastructure as technology companies compete for advanced GPUs, power, data center capacity and networking equipment.
Morgan Stanley estimates the broader AI infrastructure market will require approximately $1.5 trillion of external financing by 2028, even as banks and other investors become more selective about underwriting large AI-related projects.
Nvidia has also been working with major financial institutions to expand the pool of capital available for AI infrastructure.
In August, Nvidia partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR on financing platforms intended to mobilize more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure projects.
The financing effort also highlights the increasingly close relationship between AI computing demand and credit markets.
Advanced Nvidia GPUs represent one of the largest capital expenses for companies building frontier AI systems, while the scale of new clusters increasingly requires financing structures more commonly associated with major infrastructure projects.

candidates.title: Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin
candidates.snippet:
Intesa Sanpaolo's improved €35 billion ($39 billion) takeover bid for Monte dei Paschi di Siena has secured the support of MPS’s largest shareholder, Delfin, according to Reuters.
The post Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin
Intesa Sanpaolo’s improved €35 billion ($39 billion) takeover bid for Monte dei Paschi di Siena has secured the support of MPS’s largest shareholder, Delfin, according to Reuters .
Delfin, which owns a 17.6% stake in MPS, has committed to tendering its shares into Intesa’s cash-and-stock offer and voting against a defensive strategy proposed by MPS Chief Executive Luigi Lovaglio.
The support represents an important development for Intesa because Delfin had previously been viewed as a key ally of Lovaglio.
MPS shareholders are scheduled to vote on October 29 on the bank’s defense strategy. Lovaglio needs support from two-thirds of shareholders for the plan to proceed.
Intesa recently increased the cash portion of its offer by another €800 million, raising the cash component by 25%. The enhancement increases the overall value of the bid by approximately 2.3% based on MPS’s October 2 closing price.
Under the revised terms, Intesa is offering €1.25 in cash plus 1.6 newly issued Intesa shares for each MPS share tendered.
Intesa has warned that it intends to withdraw its offer if MPS shareholders approve the defense strategy.
MPS has also been pursuing a plan to take Mediobanca private and merge the business into MPS. That proposal is also expected to go before shareholders on October 29.
Intesa has said it would retain approximately half of MPS’s branch network to address competition concerns while keeping MPS’s holdings in Mediobanca and Generali.
The proposed takeover comes amid a broader period of consolidation across Italy’s banking sector, with Intesa entering the contest for MPS after the lender had itself acquired control of Mediobanca and become a major shareholder in insurer Generali.

candidates.title: Fintech Startups: $28.6B H1 Funding and 7 Recent Rounds
candidates.snippet: Fintech Startups: $28.6B H1 Funding and 7 Recent Rounds AI Funding Tracker
candidates.text:
This list covers fintech startups that closed a disclosed round between June and October 2026, at Series C or earlier, and published at least one traction figure. Seven companies qualified, from an AI accounting platform valued at $1 billion to a Riyadh-based SME lender.
The capital behind them is concentrated. Fintech startups raised $28.6 billion worldwide in the first half of 2026, up 22.7% year over year, while deal count fell 25.7% to 1,605 rounds, according to Crunchbase.
$28.6B Global fintech venture funding, H1 2026
1,605 Fintech deals in H1 2026, down 25.7%
$27.5B Q3 2026 fintech investment, FinTech Global
$404.5M Raised in the six USD rounds on this list
Fintech startups funding in 2026: totals and deal counts
Crunchbase counted $28.6 billion in fintech venture funding in H1 2026. That was 17.3% below the $34.6 billion raised in H2 2025, the sector’s strongest half-year since late 2022.
Fewer, larger rounds drove the annual gain. Spread across 1,605 deals, the H1 2026 total works out to about $17.8 million per round. The same data implies about $23.3 billion across 2,161 deals in H1 2025, or about $10.8 million per round. Average check size rose 65%.
US companies took $15 billion, more than 52% of the global total. The UK followed with $2.7 billion.
The US raised 5.6 times as much as the UK, which took 9.4% of H1 funding. That left about $10.9 billion, or 38.1%, for every other country combined.
FinTech Global publishes quarterly totals that run higher than Crunchbase’s, because its tracker counts a wider set of deals that includes insurtech and cybersecurity companies. Its figures below should not be compared with the Crunchbase totals above. Average deal size is calculated from its totals.
Quarter Fintech funding Deals Average deal size

Q3 2025 $20.3B 959 $21.2M

Q3 2026 funding fell 11% from the Q2 peak but rose 35% from Q3 2025, while deal volume dropped 6% year over year. The average Q3 deal grew from $21.2 million to $30.7 million, a 45% increase.
The first three quarters of 2026 add up to $78.2 billion across 2,665 deals. For the AI side of the same peak quarter, see our ranking of the biggest AI funding rounds of Q2 2026 .
Selection rules and round sizes
Each company needed a round announced in the past 18 months and confirmed by a company statement or trade publication. Rounds are capped at Series C, so Series D raises such as Valon’s $150 million fall outside the list. Each company also had to publish a traction figure: customers, clients or assets.
The list is grouped by what each startup sells. One group builds software for corporate finance teams. A second sells software to banks and lenders. The third runs credit or cash products on its own books.
The six USD rounds total $404.5 million, with a median of $71.25 million. Taktile, Rillet and Spiko account for $300 million, or 74.2% of that sum. Cleavr’s €8 million seed is left off the chart because it was announced in euros.

candidates.title: RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors
candidates.snippet:
Raytheon, an RTX business, has secured a multi-year contract valued at up to $24.4 billion for Standard Missile-6 interceptors, significantly expanding long-term production of the missile system for the U.S. Navy.
The post RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors
Raytheon, an RTX business, has secured a multi-year contract valued at up to $24.4 billion for Standard Missile-6 interceptors, significantly expanding long-term production of the missile system for the U.S. Navy.
The agreement covers five years and includes two additional option years, giving Raytheon a potential seven-year production framework for SM-6 interceptors.
The contract is designed to provide the U.S. Navy with a more consistent and reliable supply of SM-6 missiles as demand increases for weapons capable of supporting both offensive and defensive missions.
The new order builds on previous long-term production agreements between Raytheon and the Department of War and represents a major effort to increase the availability of one of the Navy’s key missile systems.
SM-6 is designed to perform several missions from a common missile platform, including anti-air warfare, anti-surface warfare and ballistic missile defense.
Raytheon describes SM-6 as the only combat-proven weapon capable of performing all three missions.
The missile has been successfully fired from multiple U.S. Navy ship-based platforms as well as land-based launchers, giving military operators flexibility in how the system is deployed against different types of threats.
The size and duration of the contract also provide Raytheon and its suppliers with greater visibility into future demand, supporting investments intended to increase manufacturing capacity.
Raytheon has been expanding its skilled workforce, strengthening relationships with suppliers throughout the defense industrial base and introducing additional automation into its manufacturing operations.
Those investments are intended to remove production constraints and support substantially higher SM-6 output for both near-term and longer-term requirements.
The SM-6 agreement follows other major multi-year missile production awards for Raytheon as the company and the U.S. government work to expand munitions production capacity.
Raytheon’s missile portfolio spans integrated air and missile defense, precision weapons, interceptors, hypersonic technologies and other systems used across land, air, sea and space.
RTX employs more than 180,000 people globally and generated more than $88 billion in sales in 2025.
KEY QUOTE:
“SM-6’s multi-mission capability is vital to our customer, and Raytheon is intensely focused on meeting the demand. By continuously investing in our operations and facilities, we are removing constraints and boosting capacity to ensure we deliver this critical capability our sailors depend on.”
Phil Jasper, President of Raytheon

candidates.text:
GlobalFoundries To Operate Two New York Semiconductor Fabs Under Up To $21 Billion U.S.-Japan Initiative
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
GlobalFoundries To Operate Two New York Semiconductor Fabs Under Up To $21 Billion U.S.-Japan Initiative
GlobalFoundries has been selected as the technology provider and operator for two new semiconductor manufacturing facilities at its Malta, New York, campus under a U.S.-Japan initiative providing up to $21 billion in funding. Pasted markdown
The initiative stems from a U.S.-Japan trade and investment agreement and is designed to expand semiconductor manufacturing capacity in the United States while strengthening supply chains serving automotive, industrial, connected infrastructure, and other markets.
Japan will provide the investment, while GlobalFoundries will contribute its semiconductor technologies, manufacturing expertise, and operational capabilities.
An initial investment of approximately $10 billion is expected to accelerate construction of a new 300mm semiconductor fab scheduled to come online in 2029.
An additional investment of approximately $10 billion would fund construction of a second fab at the Malta site.
The first facility is expected to add approximately 900,000 300mm wafers of annual U.S. manufacturing capacity when fully operational. A second fab would add approximately the same amount.
GlobalFoundries expects the broader project to create approximately 27,000 construction and semiconductor ecosystem jobs along with more than 1,000 high-skilled manufacturing jobs in New York’s Capital Region.
The company plans to break ground on the first fab later in 2026. GlobalFoundries said the Malta site is already permitted and shovel-ready, allowing the project to use existing infrastructure to accelerate construction.
Separately, GlobalFoundries agreed with the U.S. Department of Commerce to amend its existing CHIPS and Science Act award and reallocate $955 million to accelerate investments in silicon photonics, silicon-germanium technology, and advanced packaging.
The company will make those investments at its facilities in Malta and Burlington, Vermont, to increase U.S. manufacturing capacity for technologies used in communications infrastructure and data centers.
Under a separate agreement, the U.S. Department of Commerce will receive an equity interest of approximately 4% in GlobalFoundries.
The expansion also builds on GlobalFoundries’ relationships with customers and semiconductor industry partners in the United States and Japan.
Renesas said it is planning around the new New York capacity as an extension of its own production footprint, while Tokyo Electron expects to support the expanded semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.
Apple also highlighted its existing relationship with GlobalFoundries to manufacture chips for Apple products in the United States, while Cirrus Logic said the new facilities will provide access to additional domestic capacity for next-generation mixed-signal products.
General Motors said the additional domestic manufacturing capacity could support a stronger semiconductor supply chain as vehicles require greater processing power for technologies including centralized computing, artificial intelligence, autonomy, and software-defined vehicle systems.
KEY QUOTES:
“This is a bold new initiative for semiconductor manufacturing, bringing together the United States and Japan with GF’s differentiated technology and decades of manufacturing expertise to accelerate trusted capacity in New York. GF was selected because fabs of this scale require more than capital. They require differentiated technology, operational excellence and a proven ability to execute. That combination is what positions GF to make this first-of-its-kind initiative a success.”
Tim Breen, Chief Executive Officer of GlobalFoundries
“President Trump’s historic U.S.-Japan Trade Deal is delivering another massive manufacturing investment into America. With Japan’s investment funding and GlobalFoundries’ partnership, two large semiconductor chip manufacturing facilities will be built in the U.S., creating thousands of high-paying jobs for American workers. This is how the President’s trade agreements result in transformational American industrial assets that strengthen our national and economic security.”
Howard Lutnick, U.S. Secretary of Commerce
“GlobalFoundries’ expansion in Malta is a tremendous vote of confidence in New York’s world-class workforce, innovation ecosystem and the Capital Region’s growing role as a global hub for semiconductor manufacturing and innovation. We also look forward to working with the Government of Japan and partnering with their world-leading semiconductor supply chain ecosystem in the years to come. This investment will create thousands of construction jobs, support more than 1,000 highly skilled manufacturing jobs and reinforce New York’s position as a global hub for the semiconductor industry.”
Kathy Hochul, Governor of New York
“Since 2009, the people of this site have built one of the nation’s most advanced semiconductor manufacturing operations. These two great countries entrusting GF to operate two new fabs is a powerful vote of confidence in our workforce, our technology and New York’s Capital Region. With the potential to create thousands of new jobs, we are working with education and workforce partners to build the next generation of semiconductor talent. This is a milestone for our employees, our region and the future of advanced manufacturing in New York.”
Grant McEwan, General Manager of Fab 8 at GlobalFoundries
“We’ve partnered with GlobalFoundries to produce essential chips for Apple products right here in the United States, as part of our $600 billion commitment to American investment. As an inaugural member of Apple’s American Manufacturing Program, GlobalFoundries shares our belief in the power of American innovation and ingenuity. candidates.snippet:
IBM reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $17.1 billion, an increase of 5% year over year and 6% at constant currency, supported by growth in its Software and Infrastructure businesses. The technology company also reported net income from continuing operations of $2.2 billion, up 26% from the prior year, as demand for enterprise software, artificial intelligence capabilities, and infrastructure solutions supported its financial performance.
The post IBM Reports Q3 2026 Revenue Of $17.1 Billion, Net Income Of $2.2 Billion, And Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
IBM Reports Q3 2026 Revenue Of $17.1 Billion, Net Income Of $2.2 Billion, And Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
IBM Reports Q3 2026 Revenue Of $17.1 Billion, Net Income Of $2.2 Billion, And Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook
IBM reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $17.1 billion, an increase of 5% year over year and 6% at constant currency, supported by growth in its Software and Infrastructure businesses. The technology company also reported net income from continuing operations of $2.2 billion, up 26% from the prior year, as demand for enterprise software, artificial intelligence capabilities, and infrastructure solutions supported its financial performance.
IBM reported diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $2.31, up 26% from $1.84 in the third quarter of 2025. On an operating non-GAAP basis, diluted earnings per share increased 11% to $2.95, compared with $2.65 a year earlier.
Gross profit increased to $9.7 billion, although the GAAP gross profit margin declined 50 basis points to 56.8%. Operating gross margin was 58.5%, compared with 58.7% in the prior-year quarter.
IBM’s GAAP pretax income reached approximately $2.5 billion, representing a pretax margin of 14.6%. Operating non-GAAP pretax income rose 9% to $3.3 billion, and the operating pretax margin improved 70 basis points to 19.3%.
The company’s Software division generated $7.8 billion in quarterly revenue, an increase of 8% as reported and 9% at constant currency. Software remained IBM’s largest operating segment, benefiting from continued demand for hybrid cloud, data management, and enterprise transaction processing solutions.
Within Software, Red Hat revenue increased 11%, while Data revenue grew 19%, or 20% at constant currency. Transaction Processing revenue rose 9%, reflecting demand for enterprise systems that support mission-critical business operations.
Automation revenue declined 3%, partially offsetting growth elsewhere in the division.
Software segment profit reached approximately $2.7 billion, compared with $2.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025. The segment’s profit margin improved to 35% from 32.9%, reflecting stronger operating performance.
IBM Consulting generated $5.3 billion in quarterly revenue, remaining broadly flat year over year on a reported basis and increasing 2% at constant currency.
Within Consulting, Strategy and Technology revenue rose 2% (4% at constant currency), while Intelligent Operations revenue fell 2%.
The Consulting segment reported profit of $653 million, compared with $686 million a year earlier, with its profit margin declining to 12.2% from 12.9%.
IBM Infrastructure reported revenue of $3.7 billion, up 4% and 5% at constant currency.
Hybrid Infrastructure revenue increased 8%, supported by particularly strong performance in Distributed Infrastructure, where revenue rose 31%, or 32% at constant currency.
IBM Z revenue declined 20%, while Infrastructure Support revenue decreased 3%. Despite those declines, the Infrastructure segment increased profit to $715 million from $644 million, with its profit margin improving to 19.3%.
The Financing segment generated $192 million in revenue, down 4% year over year.
Cash generation was another significant component of IBM’s quarterly performance. The company reported $4 billion in net cash provided by operating activities, an increase of approximately $900 million from the prior-year quarter.
Free cash flow rose to about $3 billion, up from $2.4 billion a year earlier. IBM also returned $1.6 billion to shareholders through dividend payments during the quarter.
For the first nine months of 2026, IBM generated $11.8 billion in operating cash flow, an increase of $2.6 billion year over year. Free cash flow reached $7.8 billion, up from $7.2 billion in the same period in 2025.
IBM reported nine-month revenue of $50.2 billion, compared with $47.8 billion a year earlier. Net income reached approximately $5.6 billion, up from $5 billion.
The company ended September 2026 with $11.1 billion in cash, restricted cash, and marketable securities, compared with approximately $14.5 billion at the end of 2025.
IBM invested approximately $11.4 billion in acquisitions during the first nine months of 2026. Total debt, including $12.7 billion associated with IBM Financing, reached $63.8 billion, an increase of $2.6 billion since year-end 2025.
After its third-quarter results, IBM reaffirmed its full-year revenue growth outlook and raised its free cash flow expectations.
The company continues to anticipate constant-currency revenue growth of 4% to 5% for 2026. At current foreign exchange rates, currency movements are expected to have a neutral effect on annual revenue growth.
IBM now expects full-year free cash flow to increase by more than $1 billion compared with 2025, reflecting stronger cash generation and operational execution.
The board also approved a regular quarterly cash dividend of $1.69 per share, payable December 10, 2026, to shareholders of record as of November 10.
With that payment, IBM will have maintained consecutive quarterly dividend payments every year since 1916.
IBM’s results reflect its continued focus on enterprise software, hybrid cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence, and productivity improvements as the company works to translate technology investments into stronger growth and cash generation.

IBM’s technology and expertise are helping organizations drive growth and serve customers with greater speed, precision and efficiency than ever before. candidates.title: DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US restrictions
candidates.snippet: DeepSeek has reportedly raised $15 billion in one of China's largest funding rounds, just days after the U.S. ordered federal agencies to remove its technology over national security concerns.
candidates.text:
In Brief
Posted:
6:11 AM PDT · October 22, 2026
Image Credits: GREG BAKER/AFP / Getty Images
Kate Park
DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US restrictions
Just two days after the U.S. ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek’s AI technology from their systems over security concerns, the Chinese AI lab has raised about $15 billion, about 100 billion yuan, one of the biggest funding rounds in the country, Bloomberg reported.
Potential investors include Chinese battery maker CATL and Tencent, the company behind WeChat, among others, according to the report.
The reported funding follows DeepSeek’s investment round in June, when it raised more than $7 billion at a valuation of $50 billion. The company was also reportedly seeking an additional $1.5 billion at a valuation of around $71 billion in July , with plans for a potential IPO in China as early as next year.
The Hangzhou-based AI startup is ramping up spending on AI infrastructure and open models for domestic and international markets, even as it faces restrictions in the U.S., the report said. Its expansion could further intensify competition among domestic rivals.
The massive funding round is the latest sign of investors pouring billions into AI companies around the world, including those in China, to compete in the global AI race. Chinese company Kimi developer Moonshot AI secured $2 billion at a $20 billion valuation in May. Manus AI raised more than $500 million earlier this month. Meanwhile, Chinese companies Zhipu AI (Z.ai) and MiniMax, which both went public in Hong Kong in January, have market capitalizations of roughly $29 billion and $7.2 billion , respectively, as of today.
DeepSeek was founded in 2023 by Liang Wenfeng , who previously co-founded Chinese quantitative hedge fund High-Flyer, which helped finance DeepSeek’s early development. The AI startup gained global attention in early 2025 with its free-to-use, open-weight RI reasoning model, challenging the dominance of U.S. AI companies. Liang retains an estimated 81.6% stake in its Chinese operating entity following its earlier funding round, according to corporate ownership data analyzed by WireScreen.
DeepSeek did not immediately respond to a TechCrunch request for comment.

candidates.text:
Jabil Reports Q4 Revenue Of $10.6 Billion And FY2026 Revenue Of $36 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Jabil Reports Q4 Revenue Of $10.6 Billion And FY2026 Revenue Of $36 Billion
Jabil reported preliminary fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 net revenue of $10.6 billion as the manufacturing services company closed a year marked by strong growth in AI infrastructure and other end markets.
For the quarter ended August 31, 2026, Jabil generated U.S. GAAP operating income of $602 million and GAAP diluted earnings per share of $3.76. Core operating income was $675 million, while core diluted earnings per share reached $4.40.
For the full fiscal year, net revenue reached $36.0 billion, representing 21% growth. GAAP operating income totaled $1.7 billion and GAAP diluted EPS was $9.75. Core operating income reached $2.1 billion, with core diluted EPS of $13.09.
Jabil also generated more than $1.5 billion of adjusted free cash flow during fiscal 2026 while expanding its core operating margin by 40 basis points.
The company said growth was supported by increasing demand for AI infrastructure along with strength across automotive, healthcare, energy infrastructure, defense and aerospace, and warehouse and retail automation.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Jabil expects net revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion. GAAP operating income is projected between $481 million and $541 million, with GAAP diluted EPS ranging from $2.78 to $3.18.
Core first-quarter operating income is expected between $592 million and $652 million, with core diluted EPS between $3.80 and $4.20.
For the full 2027 fiscal year, Jabil expects revenue of $44.5 billion, which would represent approximately 24% growth. The company forecasts a core operating margin of 6.1%, up approximately 30 basis points, and core diluted EPS of $17.55, representing projected growth of 34%.
Adjusted free cash flow for fiscal 2027 is expected to be approximately $1.6 billion.
Jabil said the outlook reflects expanding customer relationships and committed business supporting newly added capacity. The company continues to take on more engineering, supply chain and manufacturing responsibilities for customers while maintaining what it describes as an asset-light operating model.
Jabil operates more than 100 sites globally and provides engineering, supply chain and manufacturing services across a broad range of industries.
KEY QUOTES:
“We delivered a fourth quarter that exceeded our expectations, closing an exceptional fiscal 2026 in which we grew revenue 21%, expanded core operating margin 40 basis points and generated more than $1.5 billion in adjusted free cash flow. Our teams supported significant growth in AI infrastructure, delivered strong performance across several other end markets and brought critical new capacity online. These results reflect the progress we’ve made in moving up the value chain, taking on more of our customers’ engineering and manufacturing complexity while maintaining an asset-light model. I’m proud of our teams and the stronger business we’re building together.
“Our fiscal 2027 outlook reflects the strength of Jabil’s diversified portfolio, with accelerating AI demand complemented by solid growth in automotive, healthcare, energy infrastructure, defense and aerospace, and warehouse and retail automation. This breadth of growth, together with expanding customer relationships and committed business supporting our new capacity, gives us confidence in the year ahead. We expect revenue of $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin expansion of 30 basis points to 6.1%, core diluted earnings per share growth of 34% to $17.55, and adjusted free cash flow of approximately $1.6 billion. As customers turn to Jabil for more of their engineering, supply chain and manufacturing needs, we see significant opportunities to sustain profitable growth, invest in our capabilities and return substantial capital to shareholders.”
Mike Dastoor, CEO of Jabil

Posts News
AI giant Legora hits $8.8 billion valuation after fresh funding round
By Legal Cheek on Oct 22 2026 10:47am
Battle to become legal AI’s number one platform attracts eye-watering investment
Legora chief exec and co-founder Max Junestrand
Legal AI platform Legora has secured another bumper funding round, pushing its valuation to a whopping $8.8 billion (£6.6 billion).
The Swedish-founded company has raised a further $550 million (£410 million) in a Series E round, just seven months after securing the same amount at a $5.6 billion (£4.2 billion) valuation. That represents a jump of more than 50% in less than a year.
The latest round was led by Atreides Management, with new investors including Baron Capital, Fidelity and JPMorgan. Existing backers including Accel, Benchmark and General Catalyst also participated, taking Legora’s total funding to more than $1.4 billion (£1 billion) since it was founded in 2023.
The fresh cash comes amid a period of rapid growth for the legal tech company, which says its annual recurring revenue has now surpassed $200 million (£150 million). It took less than 18 months to climb from $1 million (£750,000) to $100 million (£75 million), with the next $100 million (£75 million) arriving in under six months.
Max Junestrand, Legora’s CEO and co-founder, said:
“The opportunity in legal is enormous and we are still early. AI is changing the role of the lawyer, with more time for judgement and advice, and it is reshaping how law firms and in-house legal teams are organised and how their work gets done.”
The funding comes as competition heats up between Legora and rival legal AI platform Harvey, which secured its own $550 million (£410 million) funding round in September, taking its valuation to $15.5 billion (£11.6 billion).
The rivalry recently produced a rather awkward coincidence when the two companies unveiled new products bearing exactly the same name just hours apart. Both offerings, called ‘Intake’, are designed to help in-house legal teams manage requests from across their businesses, with AI handling routine tasks and freeing up lawyers for more complex work.

candidates.title: Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap
candidates.snippet:
Blackstone announced the final close of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners V at $8.7 billion, with the energy-focused private equity fund reaching its hard cap after attracting demand that significantly exceeded its fundraising target.
The post Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap
Blackstone announced the final close of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners V at $8.7 billion, with the energy-focused private equity fund reaching its hard cap after attracting demand that significantly exceeded its fundraising target.
BETP V is more than 50% larger than its predecessor vehicle and extends Blackstone Energy Transition Partners’ strategy of making control-oriented equity investments in energy-related businesses. The strategy focuses on building companies that can support growing global electricity demand while improving energy reliability, affordability, and efficiency.
Blackstone said the Energy Transition Partners strategy has generated a 34% net internal rate of return since 1997 as of June 30. The firm has committed more than $34 billion of equity globally through the strategy across a range of energy sectors.
BETP V began its investment period in June and has already funded three platform companies: Kindle, Fisterra, and Viridon. These platforms are backing management teams focused on developing and operating new power generation assets and electric transmission infrastructure.
The fund has also completed three acquisitions centered on energy efficiency, infrastructure resiliency, and technology. These include Flow Control Holdings, a provider of engineered flow-control components used in data center liquid cooling systems; Dresser Utility Solutions, which supplies meters, regulators, pressure-relief valves, and infrastructure repair products for gas and water utilities; and DarkVision, a provider of technology-enabled inspection services for critical energy infrastructure.
Blackstone said that since January 2025, BETP has committed more than $11 billion to new equity investments across the energy transition ecosystem. The activity has included investments in critical energy equipment manufacturers such as MacLean Power Systems, Delta Star, Power Grid Components, Arlington Industries, and Advanced Cooling Technologies.
The strategy has also invested in essential services businesses including Alliance Technical Group and Shermco, energy data analytics provider Enverus, and natural gas-fired power infrastructure including Hill Top Energy Center, Wolf Summit Energy, and Potomac Energy Center.
At the same time, Blackstone has been monetizing several mature investments held by predecessor funds. Recent transactions include an agreement to sell Aypa Power, which operates a 6 GW North American battery storage portfolio, and the sale of a majority interest in Sabre Industries, a manufacturer of infrastructure products serving power utilities, telecommunications companies, and data centers.
Blackstone also completed the initial public offering of Legence, a provider of specialty mechanical contracting and engineering services serving data centers, healthcare facilities, and other high-specification commercial and industrial markets.
BETP generally excludes investments involving the ownership and extraction of hydrocarbon reserves. Blackstone said its approach centers on providing flexible capital to management teams that can expand energy infrastructure, manufacturing capabilities, and related services.
The final close comes as Blackstone continues expanding its broader energy transition investment portfolio alongside its global alternative asset management businesses. Blackstone manages more than $1.3 trillion in assets across strategies including real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries, and hedge funds.
KEY QUOTES:
“We believe there is a generational opportunity for experienced investors in the energy transition to provide solutions to the challenges posed by growing demand for electricity. By backing exceptional management teams with flexible, patient equity capital to increase manufacturing capacity, recruit and train skilled labor and construct new critical energy infrastructure assets, BETP is delivering those solutions and in the process building these companies to scale, creating jobs and generating lasting value for our investors. We are deeply grateful for the trust of our investors and look forward to deploying BETP V in investments that advance the transition to a more affordable, reliable and cleaner energy future.”
David Foley, Global Head Of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners

candidates.title: USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers
candidates.snippet:
The Trump administration has announced an $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief program that will provide one-time payments to U.S. farmers during the 2026 harvest season as producers contend with higher input costs and temporary market disruptions.
The post USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers
The Trump administration has announced an $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief program that will provide one-time payments to U.S. farmers during the 2026 harvest season as producers contend with higher input costs and temporary market disruptions.
According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture announcement, the Farm Service Agency will administer the program, funded under the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act. Payments are intended to provide proportional support to producers using a uniform formula tied to modeproducers with proportional supporthe calculation will incorporate Farm Service Agency-reported planted acres, Economic Research Service cost-of-production estimates, and World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates for yields and prices.
Commodity-specific payment rates for Title I commodities are expected to be released in November. USDA said it will announce the payment methodology for other eligible commodities separately.
Participation in the Harvest Fuel Relief program will not require producers to be linked to crop insurance. USDA is nevertheless encouraging farmers to use enhanced risk-management tools available through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act to manage future price volatility and other agricultural risks.
The department is also seeking information from producers of non-Title I commodities. Specialty crop growers and fishermen are encouraged to submit data on higher fuel costs so USDA can consider those expenses when setting payment rates.
Farmers interested in participating are being encouraged to establish a Login.gov account before the application period opens. USDA plans to make pre-filled applications available online for producers whose Login.gov accounts are connected to USDA systems.
The newly announced program follows several other agricultural support initiatives cited by USDA. The department said the Farmer Bridge Assistance program delivered $12 billion in one-time payments to more than 560,000 farmers earlier in 2026. USDA also said nearly $14 billion in gross payments were recently provided through Agriculture Risk Coverage and Price Loss Coverage programs.
The Harvest Fuel Relief program adds another targeted assistance mechanism as USDA seeks to offset a portion of operating and market pressures affecting agricultural producers during the 2026 crop year.
KEY QUOTE:
“President Trump is the most pro-farmer president of my lifetime and he is continuing to put Farmers First every day. Today, I am proud to announce alongside President Trump more targeted relief is coming to our farmers through the Harvest Fuel Relief program. This $8 billion dollar investment will help bring certainty to our farmers during this harvest so they can continue to feed our nation.”
Brooke L. Rollins, U.S. Secretary Of Agriculture

candidates.snippet:
Carlyle has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire an approximately $7.7 billion portfolio of unsecured personal loans from Truist, expanding the investment firm’s asset-backed finance activity and its role as a capital partner to banks managing their balance sheets.
The post Carlyle To Acquire $7.7 Billion Personal Loan Portfolio From Truist appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Carlyle To Acquire $7.7 Billion Personal Loan Portfolio From Truist
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Carlyle To Acquire $7.7 Billion Personal Loan Portfolio From Truist
Carlyle has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire an approximately $7.7 billion portfolio of unsecured personal loans from Truist, expanding the investment firm’s asset-backed finance activity and its role as a capital partner to banks managing their balance sheets.
The portfolio consists primarily of fixed-rate, fully amortizing personal loans made to super-prime and prime borrowers. Carlyle described the assets as a seasoned pool of consumer loans and said the transaction reflects growing demand from banks for private capital solutions that can help optimize balance sheets and manage portfolios more efficiently.
The acquisition is being led by Carlyle’s Asset-Backed Finance team within its Global Credit platform. The team invests across private fixed income and asset-backed assets, providing financing and acquiring portfolios from banks, specialty finance companies, asset owners, and other businesses.
Carlyle said the transaction demonstrates its ability to deploy capital at scale while underwriting large pools of consumer credit. The firm also views high-quality consumer lending as an important component of the broader asset-backed finance opportunity.
The deal builds on Carlyle’s experience working with banks on large and complex portfolio transactions and further expands its existing relationship with Truist.
Carlyle’s Global Credit platform managed approximately $211 billion in assets as of June 30, 2026. Across the broader firm, Carlyle had approximately $485 billion in assets under management at the same date, spanning Global Private Equity, Global Credit, and Carlyle AlpInvest.
The transaction also highlights the continued growth of private credit and asset-backed finance as banks look for alternative sources of capital and more flexible ways to manage loan portfolios. By acquiring seasoned assets directly from financial institutions, private investment firms can provide liquidity while gaining exposure to established pools of consumer credit.
Sidley Austin served as legal advisor to Carlyle in connection with the transaction.
The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
KEY QUOTES:
“Banks are increasingly turning to private capital to help manage their balance sheets, and this transaction reflects the scale and specialized underwriting capabilities that Carlyle’s asset-backed finance platform brings to those relationships. It underscores our ability to commit capital and execute at scale, and our conviction in high-quality consumer credit as a core part of the asset-backed finance opportunity.”
Akhil Bansal, Partner And Head Of Asset-Backed Finance At Carlyle

candidates.text:
UnitedHealth Group Raises 2026 Outlook As Q3 Operating Earnings Rise To $6.6 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
UnitedHealth Group Raises 2026 Outlook As Q3 Operating Earnings Rise To $6.6 Billion
UnitedHealth Group reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $112.7 billion and earnings from operations of $6.6 billion, while raising its full-year earnings outlook as profitability improved across UnitedHealthcare and Optum.
The company reported diluted earnings of $4.56 per share and adjusted earnings of $4.69 per share.
UnitedHealth Group now expects full-year 2026 earnings of at least $19.50 per share and adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share.
Third-quarter earnings from operations increased from $4.3 billion in the prior-year period, driven by what the company described as disciplined execution across UnitedHealthcare and Optum.
Net earnings attributable to UnitedHealth Group shareholders reached $4.11 billion, compared with $2.35 billion a year earlier.
The company generated $5.1 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, equivalent to 1.2 times net income.
UnitedHealth Group’s medical care ratio improved to 88.4% from 89.9% in the third quarter of 2025.
The improvement reflected medical cost management initiatives, pricing discipline, benefit design changes, and enhancements to care delivery focused on affordability and integrated value-based care.
The quarter included $610 million of favorable prior-period medical reserve development related to 2026 dates of service.
UnitedHealth Group’s operating cost ratio also improved to 12.8% from 13.5% a year earlier, reflecting operating efficiencies while the company continued investing in technology, processes, employees, and consumer and clinician experiences.
The company has repurchased $5 billion of common stock and paid $6.2 billion in dividends through the first nine months of 2026.
UnitedHealthcare served 48.3 million people and generated third-quarter revenue of $86.3 billion.
UnitedHealthcare operating earnings increased to $2.83 billion from $1.81 billion a year earlier, while its operating margin improved to 3.3% from 2.1%.
The company attributed the improvement to benefit changes, pricing discipline, and stronger medical and operating cost management.
UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual generated $20.2 billion in revenue, compared with $19.9 billion in the prior-year quarter.
Medicare & Retirement generated $42.4 billion in revenue, while Community & State revenue totaled $23.7 billion.
UnitedHealth Group said at least 69% of members were enrolled in four-star or higher Medicare Advantage plans under the 2027 Stars results, in line with expectations.
Optum generated $66.9 billion in third-quarter revenue and $3.73 billion in earnings from operations.
Optum Health posted a significant improvement in profitability, with operating earnings increasing to $735 million from $41 million in the prior-year period.
Its operating margin increased to 3.2% from 0.2%, reflecting stronger operating discipline and medical cost management across its value-based care markets.
Optum Insight revenue increased 3% to $5.5 billion, while operating earnings rose to $1.28 billion from $920 million.
The business continues developing AI-enabled healthcare solutions designed to streamline clinical documentation, improve payment accuracy and speed, and reduce administrative work for clinicians.
Optum Rx generated $39.9 billion in revenue and $1.72 billion in operating earnings, up from $1.55 billion a year earlier.
UnitedHealth Group also outlined several initiatives focused on healthcare affordability and access.
The company has committed $1 billion to the United Health Foundation for initiatives including rural healthcare, maternal and children’s health, and behavioral health.
UnitedHealthcare is also working to eliminate 30% of its current prior approval volume by the end of 2026 and nearly two-thirds of prior approval requirements for pediatric care.
The company is supporting approximately 1,500 rural hospitals and associated clinicians by accelerating payments, shortening reimbursement timelines, and exempting those clinicians from most prior approval requirements.
UnitedHealth Group also plans to expand doula coverage nationally through employer-sponsored plans, with more than 7 million members expected to be eligible by January 2027.
The company has also committed to passing through 100% of manufacturer drug rebate discounts to clients by January 1, 2028 as part of efforts to improve pharmacy benefit transparency and affordability.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our third quarter results reflect the discipline and execution our teams are bringing to every part of our business, as we continue evolving UnitedHealth Group to deliver a simpler, more supportive experience for patients and the clinicians who care for them.”
Stephen Hemsley, Chief Executive Officer of UnitedHealth Group

candidates.snippet:
RTX’s Raytheon business secured a five-year contract, with two additional option years, valued at up to $6.3 billion for production and sustainment of Standard Missile-3 Block IB interceptors.
The post RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $6.3 Billion Contract For SM-3 Block IB Interceptors appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $6.3 Billion Contract For SM-3 Block IB Interceptors
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $6.3 Billion Contract For SM-3 Block IB Interceptors
RTX’s Raytheon business secured a five-year contract, with two additional option years, worth up to $6.3 billion, to produce and sustain Standard Missile-3 Block IB interceptors.
The agreement is part of a broader set of contracts between Raytheon and the Department of War and is intended to support replenishment of missile defense inventories.
Raytheon said the SM-3 Block IB has been used successfully in combat and remains an important component of U.S. and allied missile defense capabilities.
The company has been investing in production capacity and manufacturing improvements to increase output of critical munitions, including the broader Standard Missile family.
Raytheon will produce under the new contract primarily at its facilities in Tucson, Arizona, and Huntsville, Alabama.
The SM-3 Block IB is a ship- and land-based interceptor designed to defeat short- to intermediate-range ballistic missiles during the midcourse phase of flight.
The system was first used in combat in 2024.
It is part of the U.S. Navy’s extended-range integrated air and missile defense architecture alongside the SM-3 Block IIA and other members of the Standard Missile family.
The multi-year structure is designed to provide greater production stability as Raytheon works to replenish inventories and respond to evolving missile threats.
Raytheon is one of RTX’s three major businesses and provides integrated air and missile defense systems, missiles, sensors, radars, interceptors, space systems, hypersonic technologies, and other defense capabilities.
RTX employs more than 180,000 people globally and reported more than $88 billion in sales in 2025.
KEY QUOTES:
“This award underscores Raytheon’s commitment to increasing production of critical munitions, ensuring our customers have the defensive capabilities they need, when they need them. SM-3 Block IB has proven its relevance in combat and this contract helps ensure we can replenish inventories and keep pace with the evolving threats the U.S. Navy, MDA and their partners face around the world.”
Phil Jasper, President of Raytheon

candidates.text:
BakerAvenue Wealth Management Receives Strategic Investment From Constellation Wealth Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
BakerAvenue Wealth Management Receives Strategic Investment From Constellation Wealth Capital
BakerAvenue Wealth Management received a strategic minority investment from Constellation Wealth Capital to support the firm’s next phase of growth. BakerAvenue manages $6.3 billion in assets and provides integrated wealth management, concentrated stock management, tax preparation, estate planning, and corporate trustee services.
The firm will remain majority-owned and controlled by its existing leadership team following the transaction.
The investment provides BakerAvenue with additional long-term capital to expand its service offering and operating infrastructure.
The firm plans to grow its integrated tax preparation and estate planning capabilities as well as its corporate trustee services.
BakerAvenue also intends to pursue opportunities in new markets, advisor recruitment, and additional organic growth channels.
The company was founded in 2004 and has built its strategy around coordinating investment management with tax and estate planning.
BakerAvenue said its integrated model is designed to provide clients with more coordinated and tax-aware financial guidance across their broader financial picture.
The firm reported a 23% compound annual growth rate in organic AUM from 2021 through 2025.
BakerAvenue serves high-net-worth individuals, families, trusts, foundations, and endowments.
The company also provides specialized concentrated stock management and corporate trustee services through BakerAvenue Trust Company.
Constellation Wealth Capital focuses on providing long-term capital and strategic support to scaled independent registered investment advisers.
Colchester Partners served as financial advisor to BakerAvenue.
Alston & Bird served as legal counsel to BakerAvenue, while Gibson Dunn served as legal counsel to Constellation Wealth Capital.
KEY QUOTES:
“We founded BakerAvenue 22 years ago with a firm belief that people, community, and culture should be at the heart of everything we do. With CWC, we found a partner who shares those values and our vision for the future. We’re excited about what we can accomplish together as we look to broaden and deepen the impact we make for the families and clients we serve.”
Simon Baker, Founder and Executive Chairman of BakerAvenue
“This marks an exciting new chapter for BakerAvenue. We were intentional in finding a partner aligned with our long-term vision. We believe CWC’s deep understanding of the wealth management industry, collaborative approach, and experience supporting the growth of independent wealth management firms will help us deepen what we do best and expand the infrastructure behind our operating model. Clients will continue working with the same team and philosophy, now supported by additional resources.”
Tom Ngo, CEO and Partner of BakerAvenue
“BakerAvenue has built a distinctive business, combining an integrated approach to wealth management with a strong culture and a deep commitment to its clients. Our partnership reflects a shared vision for the future and a commitment to long-term growth. We look forward to working alongside Simon, Tom and the entire BakerAvenue team as they continue to build on their success and pursue the next chapter for the firm.”
Karl Heckenberg, President and Managing Partner of Constellation Wealth Capital
“BakerAvenue’s strong organic growth, integrated wealth management model, and compelling investment program provide a solid foundation for its next phase. We see significant opportunities to build on that foundation. Our focus is on providing the long-term capital and strategic resources to help the team continue to execute on their strategic priorities. We’re excited about what we can accomplish together while supporting the independence and entrepreneurial approach that have contributed to BakerAvenue’s success.”
Pat McHugh, Partner and Head of Investments at Constellation Wealth Capital

candidates.title: AI chip startup Tenstorrent more than doubles its valuation to $6.2 billion in funding round
candidates.snippet: AI chip startup Tenstorrent more than doubles its valuation to $6.2 billion in funding round The Economic Times
candidates.text:
Synopsis
Based in Santa Clara, Tenstorrent has just secured an impressive $1.5 billion in its latest funding round, propelling the AI chip startup's valuation to $6.2 billion, a leap since late 2024. This investment will significantly bolster the production of their Galaxy servers, which are crucial across various applications. Among the diverse investors backing this initiative are renowned firms like ARK Invest and T.
Listen to this article in summarized format Listen
Reuters
Tenstorrent said on Monday it raised $1.5 billion in a late-stage funding round that valued the AI chip startup at $6.2 billion post-money, more than doubling its valuation from December 2024.
Here are some more details:
The Santa Clara, California-based company said it would use the funding to scale production of its Galaxy servers, which combine dozens of its AI chips to power applications including chatbots, coding assistants and video generators.
Tenstorrent develops AI chips and software using RISC-V, an open-source chip architecture that enables companies to design processors without license fees and reduce dependence on proprietary chip ecosystems such as Arm's
The Series E round was led by Trace Capital and Innovation X. Other backers included Cathie Wood's ARK Invest, Sandisk , Morgan Stanley, T. Rowe Price and Tether Investments.
Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller, a prominent chip architect, previously led Tesla's efforts to develop a self-driving chip for electric vehicles and held key design roles at Apple and AMD among others.
The startup's last funding round raised more than $693 million in December 2024 at a $2 billion pre-money valuation, with Samsung Securities and AFW Partners leading the financing.

candidates.title: Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target
candidates.snippet:
Pantheon has closed its latest global private equity secondaries program with $6 billion in commitments, significantly exceeding the strategy's original $3.5 billion target.
The post Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target
Pantheon has closed its latest global private equity secondaries program with $6 billion in commitments, significantly exceeding the strategy’s original $3.5 billion target.
Pantheon Global Secondaries Fund VIII and related vehicles finished fundraising approximately 71% above target, marking the firm’s largest private equity secondaries capital raise to date.
The program attracted continued support from existing investors while also bringing in new limited partners, including significant commitments from investors across Asia and the Middle East.
Pantheon said the fundraising reflects continued institutional demand for private equity secondaries as investors look for diversified exposure, portfolio liquidity, and access to established private equity assets.
The fund will invest across both LP-led and GP-led secondary transactions, with an emphasis on the global mid-market. Pantheon plans to use its existing relationships with private equity managers to target funds and companies it believes can be acquired at attractive valuations.
The strategy is designed to build a diversified portfolio across investment vintages, managers, and geographies, with a particular focus on buyout strategies.
Pantheon said it deployed approximately $3.35 billion across 17 private equity secondary transactions in 2025, highlighting the scale of deal flow available to the strategy.
The firm has been investing in private equity secondaries since 1988, making the strategy a longstanding component of its broader private equity platform. Pantheon’s private equity business represents approximately $41 billion of assets within a broader private markets platform managing roughly $84 billion.
The firm also invests across primary fund commitments and co-investments, in addition to secondaries. Pantheon believes this broader exposure gives it additional data, relationships, and sourcing capabilities when evaluating secondary transactions.
Its global private markets platform spans private equity, infrastructure, and private credit, allowing the firm to evaluate opportunities across multiple asset classes and transaction types.
Pantheon said the latest fundraising underscores investor appetite for experienced secondaries managers capable of sourcing proprietary transactions and selectively accessing hard-to-reach private equity managers.
KEY QUOTES:
“Pantheon is recognized for its early leadership in secondaries, and our private equity secondaries strategy continues to be a compelling way for our investors to access high-quality private equity exposure with the diversification benefits the asset class provides. The depth of our GP relationships and access to extensive data across private equity funds and companies amassed over decades enables us to have conviction and be disciplined about the assets we buy and the partners we back, particularly in the mid-market where access and selection matters most. We enter this next phase with strong conviction in our ability to keep identifying compelling opportunities for our investors.”
Amyn Hassanally, Partner And Global Head Of Private Equity Secondaries At Pantheon
“We are pleased to complete our largest private equity secondaries fundraise to date at $6bn, building on nearly four decades of experience in this market. Our clients value our ongoing focus on the mid-market and our differentiated, longstanding relationships with hard-to-access, top-performing GPs. We are grateful for the continued support of our long-term investors in our private equity secondaries strategy, and are pleased to welcome a strong cohort of new investors this cycle, including significant commitments from Asia and the Middle East.”
Florence Dard, Chief Client Officer At Pantheon

candidates.title: Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders
candidates.snippet:
Waymo closed a $5 billion term loan, marking the autonomous driving company’s first debt financing as it continues expanding its commercial operations in the United States and internationally. PIMCO, Blackstone, and Sixth Street participated as lead syndicated lenders in the financing. Capital Group, Loomis Sayles, and T. Rowe Price also participated as significant lenders.
The post Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders
Waymo closed a $5 billion term loan, marking the autonomous driving company’s first debt financing as it continues expanding its commercial operations in the United States and internationally. PIMCO, Blackstone, and Sixth Street participated as lead syndicated lenders in the financing. Capital Group, Loomis Sayles, and T. Rowe Price also participated as significant lenders.
Additional lenders included Apollo, Blue Owl, Diameter Capital Partners, Franklin Templeton, Fidelity Management & Research Company, HPS Investment Partners, and Oaktree.
Goldman Sachs served as the sole lead bookrunner for the transaction.
The debt financing follows a $16 billion equity investment Waymo closed earlier in 2026 to accelerate the expansion of the Waymo Driver and the company’s autonomous ride-hailing business.
Waymo said the addition of debt capital gives it greater financial flexibility while strengthening its balance sheet as it scales its operations.
The company has been expanding its commercial footprint rapidly and recently launched service in its 15th U.S. city.
Waymo has also announced plans to enter additional international markets as it looks to extend its autonomous driving technology beyond the United States.
The company said proceeds from the term loan will support the continued expansion of its fully autonomous ride-hailing service across domestic and international markets.
Waymo’s ability to raise debt represents another step in its transition from a technology development operation into a larger commercial transportation business.
The company has historically relied heavily on equity capital to finance development of its autonomous driving technology, fleet operations, mapping infrastructure, vehicle integration, and geographic expansion.
Adding a large term loan provides Waymo with another source of capital as it increases fleet deployments and enters additional cities.
Waymo said its growing commercial momentum allowed it to complement its equity financing with debt while preserving flexibility for future growth opportunities.
The financing also brings a broad group of major institutional credit investors onto Waymo’s capital structure, including alternative asset managers, traditional investment managers, and private credit firms.
Waymo said it intends to continue scaling its autonomous ride-hailing network while maintaining its focus on road safety and transportation accessibility.
The company’s Waymo Driver technology operates vehicles without a human driver and is designed to support fully autonomous passenger transportation.
As the company expands, capital requirements could include additional vehicles, fleet facilities, charging and maintenance infrastructure, technology development, and the operational resources required to support new markets.
Waymo described the financing as an important milestone in its development as a scaling commercial enterprise and said the additional capital will help it move faster while expanding thoughtfully.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our strong momentum has enabled us to complement our equity financing with debt, providing additional financial flexibility to strengthen our balance sheet and position us to capitalize on the significant opportunities ahead.”
“This financing supports our long-term flexibility to execute with speed, scale thoughtfully, and continue leading the autonomous vehicle industry responsibly. As Waymo grows, we remain fiercely focused on improving road safety and making transportation more accessible.”
Steve Fieler, CFO of Waymo

candidates.title: U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio
candidates.snippet:
The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Energy Dominance Financing has announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization projects across Vistra's nuclear fleet in Pennsylvania and Ohio.
The post U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio
The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing has announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization projects across Vistra’s nuclear fleet in Pennsylvania and Ohio.
The financing is intended to increase electricity production from existing nuclear facilities, support continued plant operation, and address growing electricity demand across the 13-state PJM Interconnection region.
Vistra’s planned investments encompass the Beaver Valley nuclear facility in Pennsylvania and the Davis-Besse and Perry plants in Ohio.
Together, the projects are expected to preserve nearly 4 GW of existing baseload nuclear generation, which the Energy Department said is enough to power more than 3 million homes.
The projects are also expected to add 433 MW of new nuclear generating capacity through improvements to existing facilities.
Rather than requiring entirely new generating stations or comparable new transmission corridors, the projects are designed to extract additional output from plants that are already operating.
The investments are expected to support approximately 3,000 project-related jobs spanning engineering, construction and planned outage work while helping preserve thousands of permanent jobs associated with the nuclear facilities.
The planned investments are also expected to support operation of the plants for an additional 20 years beyond their existing licenses.
The conditional commitment includes an option for the Energy Department to finance potential future nuclear uprates at Vistra’s Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant in Texas.
The financing advances the federal government’s broader strategy of extending existing nuclear generation and increasing electricity production from the U.S. nuclear fleet.
However, the $4.2 billion commitment remains conditional.
Vistra must satisfy technical, legal, environmental and financial requirements before the Energy Department enters into definitive financing agreements and begins funding the loan.
KEY QUOTES:
“President Trump promised to unleash an American nuclear renaissance, and the Energy Department is delivering. By getting more power out of the nuclear plants we already have, we can deliver more affordable, reliable, around-the-clock energy for American families and businesses.”
Chris Wright, U.S. Secretary of Energy
“President Trump and Secretary Wright have set a clear direction for America’s nuclear future, and EDF is financing the projects that advance that mission. These investments will extend the life of existing reactors, increase nuclear generation, and deliver abundant, around-the-clock power to lower costs and power American prosperity for decades to come.”
Gregory A. Beard, Director of the Office of Energy Dominance Financing
