candidates.title: Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy
candidates.snippet:
Ares Management has raised approximately $4.2 billion for its inaugural Ares Global Structured Solutions Fund and affiliated vehicles, significantly exceeding the strategy's original $1 billion fundraising target.
The post Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy
Ares Management has raised approximately $4.2 billion for its inaugural Ares Global Structured Solutions Fund and affiliated vehicles, significantly exceeding the strategy’s original $1 billion fundraising target.
The fund, known as AGSS, is managed by the Ares Private Equity Secondaries team and is designed to provide flexible capital solutions to private equity managers pursuing a range of strategic objectives.
Ares plans to use the strategy to partner with managers seeking capital to increase their general partner commitments to funds, seed new strategies through structured limited partner commitments and facilitate succession planning.
The strategy gives Ares a dedicated pool of capital for structured GP solutions as private equity firms seek alternatives to traditional fundraising and financing structures.
Ares said its funds have deployed nearly $9 billion across structured solutions transactions since 2013, giving the firm more than a decade of experience in this part of the secondaries market.
The new fund is intended to increase the scale at which Ares can work with private equity managers while expanding the types of financing and liquidity solutions available through its Secondaries platform.
In addition to structured solutions, Ares’ GP-focused offerings include continuation vehicles and GP stakes, giving the firm multiple ways to provide capital to asset managers and their underlying portfolios.
The fundraising also broadens Ares’ Private Equity Secondaries strategy at a time when private markets managers are increasingly seeking capital for fund commitments, new product launches, ownership transitions and other strategic initiatives.
Ares Private Equity Secondaries is part of the broader Ares Secondaries Group, which has more than 30 years of experience providing liquidity solutions to limited partners and general partners across private equity, real estate, infrastructure and credit.
The Ares Secondaries Group managed approximately $44 billion of assets as of June 30, 2026.
Across its broader platform, Ares Management had more than $671 billion in assets under management as of June 30. The company operates across North America, South America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East and invests across credit, real estate, private equity and infrastructure.
KEY QUOTES:
“The successful close of AGSS highlights the increasing demand for tailored GP solutions in today’s market environment and the innovative leadership of the Ares Secondaries platform. Throughout the firm’s history, Ares has been a close partner to leading managers, and AGSS expands upon our existing GP capabilities, providing creative solutions for their growth initiatives. AGSS reflects the breadth and scale of our platform as well as the confidence of our LPs in this significant market opportunity.”
Blair Jacobson, Co-President of Ares
“For more than a decade, Ares Private Equity Secondaries has been an established provider of structured solutions that support leading GPs in their strategic initiatives, and this dedicated pool of capital further strengthens our ability to act as a scaled partner to a broader set of managers. With over 30 years of secondaries market experience, we believe our team brings the skills, deep relationships and data-driven insights to deliver differentiated capital solutions and a collaborative approach across Ares Secondaries’ comprehensive suite of GP offerings, including structured solutions, continuation vehicles and GP stakes. We are grateful for the support of our investors and look forward to our continued work with GPs as they advance their goals for long-term value creation.”
Nate Walton, Head of Private Equity Secondaries at Ares

candidates.snippet:
MidOcean Energy has concluded its 2026 equity capital raise with more than $4 billion of closed and pending equity commitments secured over the past 12 months, giving the liquefied natural gas company additional capital to expand its global LNG portfolio.
The post MidOcean Energy Secures More Than $4 Billion In Equity Commitments To Accelerate Global LNG Growth appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
MidOcean Energy Secures More Than $4 Billion In Equity Commitments To Accelerate Global LNG Growth
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
MidOcean Energy Secures More Than $4 Billion In Equity Commitments To Accelerate Global LNG Growth
MidOcean Energy has concluded its 2026 equity capital raise with more than $4 billion of closed and pending equity commitments secured over the past 12 months, giving the liquefied natural gas company additional capital to expand its global LNG portfolio.
The total significantly exceeded MidOcean’s original $2 billion target and includes commitments from new strategic and institutional investors along with significant additional commitments from existing shareholders.
MidOcean Energy was formed and is managed by EIG and is building a diversified global portfolio of LNG assets.
New investors participating in the capital raise include the Private Department of Sheikh Mohammed bin Khalid Al Nahyan, Idemitsu Kosan, NYK Line through Diamond Gas MidOcean, The Arab Energy Fund, Shizuoka Gas and certain Korean institutional investors.
The investor group includes strategic companies, sovereign-linked institutions and financial investors, giving MidOcean a broader capital base as it evaluates additional LNG investments.
MidOcean plans to use the capital to increase balance-sheet flexibility and pursue a pipeline of growth opportunities spanning both operating, cash-generating LNG assets and development-stage projects.
The company has already assembled an LNG portfolio with interests across Canada, Australia, the United States and Latin America. It also has an LNG shipping and marketing presence in Singapore and corporate headquarters in London.
MidOcean said it will continue evaluating additional opportunities consistent with its investment strategy, with an emphasis on building a diversified portfolio that can generate cash flow while providing long-term growth optionality.
The fundraising comes as MidOcean continues to position LNG as a major component of energy security and global economic growth. The company believes geographic diversification can become particularly important during periods of market disruption because a global portfolio provides multiple potential supply and delivery points.
The additional capital gives MidOcean greater capacity to pursue transactions as LNG projects require substantial funding and long development timelines.
MidOcean is backed by EIG, which specializes in energy and energy-related infrastructure investments. EIG had approximately $27.1 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2026.
During its 44-year history, EIG has committed more than $55 billion to 429 projects or companies across 44 countries and six continents.
KEY QUOTES:
“The progress achieved in this capital raise represents a major milestone for MidOcean and supports our strategy of building a scaled, diversified and resilient global LNG platform. We are pleased to welcome a distinguished group of new investors and thank our existing shareholders for their continued support and confidence.”
“We believe LNG will continue to play an essential role in supporting energy security and global economic growth, and that MidOcean is well positioned to benefit from these long-term market fundamentals. Current events also highlight the importance of geographic diversification with the ability to reliably serve clients from multiple delivery points.”
R. Blair Thomas, Chairman of MidOcean Energy and Chief Executive Officer of EIG
“In just a few years, MidOcean has grown from concept to a fully integrated global LNG platform, and this capital raise further strengthens our financial flexibility and positions us to continue advancing our robust growth strategy. We have built a high-quality LNG portfolio with strong cash flow characteristics and meaningful growth optionality, and we are well positioned to move decisively on the pipeline of opportunities we have identified. We look forward to building on this momentum and creating value for our investors.”
De la Rey Venter, Chief Executive Officer of MidOcean Energy

candidates.snippet:
Nebius Group has secured a $3.5 billion senior secured financing facility from Citi to support the continued expansion of its global AI infrastructure footprint. The 364-day facility will provide additional capital for data center development, GPU procurement, and general corporate purposes as Nebius continues building out capacity for its AI cloud platform.
The post Nebius Secures $3.5 Billion Citi Facility To Fund AI Data Center And GPU Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Nebius Secures $3.5 Billion Citi Facility To Fund AI Data Center And GPU Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Nebius Secures $3.5 Billion Citi Facility To Fund AI Data Center And GPU Expansion
Nebius Group has secured a $3.5 billion senior secured financing facility from Citi to support the continued expansion of its global AI infrastructure footprint. The 364-day facility will provide additional capital for data center development, GPU procurement, and general corporate purposes as Nebius continues building out capacity for its AI cloud platform.
The financing initially bears interest at Term SOFR plus 2.75% per year, with the spread increasing up to a maximum of 3.50% per year, subject to additional adjustments.
Nebius said the facility is part of a broader strategy to diversify and sequence its sources of capital while maintaining flexibility over when and how it raises longer-term financing.
The company’s funding base also includes customer prepayments, operating cash flows, and other financing mechanisms. By adding the Citi facility, Nebius said it can support near-term expansion while preserving the ability to access other forms of capital for growth in 2027 and beyond.
Nebius is also evaluating asset-backed financing supported by long-term customer commitments. The company said it currently has more than $40 billion of investment-grade customer commitments under long-term contracts, providing another potential source of financing as its infrastructure requirements grow.
Citi served as mandated lead arranger, agent, and security agent for the transaction.
Nebius is building a full-stack AI cloud platform designed for developers and enterprises working across model training, data infrastructure, production deployment, AI agents, and other AI services.
The Amsterdam-based company has been expanding its global data center and compute capacity to meet rising demand for GPU infrastructure. The new facility gives Nebius more financial flexibility as it continues to invest in hardware, capacity, and supporting infrastructure.
Nebius said the financing reflects its approach of maintaining a disciplined balance sheet while matching different funding sources to specific stages of its growth plans.
KEY QUOTES:
“We continue to execute our funding strategy as planned, and are pleased to have secured this financing from a leading global financial institution. This is a result of our disciplined approach to managing our balance sheet to fund our portfolio of projects, and once again demonstrates our ability to choose when and how we raise capital to support our growth.
“Sequencing our financing is how we optimize our long-term cost of capital. This facility provides additional financing to support our near-term capacity build-out. We still have a range of capital sources available to us to finance the next phase of growth, including asset-backed financing based on investment-grade customer commitments of more than $40 billion of long-term contracts.”
Ophir Nave, Chief Operating Officer Of Nebius

candidates.snippet:
EnCap Investments has closed a continuation vehicle with approximately $3.5 billion in capital commitments for EnCap Minerals and Rock River Minerals, giving the firm and its partners additional time to retain exposure to a large portfolio of Permian Basin mineral and royalty interests.
The post EnCap Investments Closes $3.5 Billion Minerals Continuation Vehicle For Permian Basin Assets appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
EnCap Investments Closes $3.5 Billion Minerals Continuation Vehicle For Permian Basin Assets
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
EnCap Investments Closes $3.5 Billion Minerals Continuation Vehicle For Permian Basin Assets
EnCap Investments has closed a continuation vehicle with approximately $3.5 billion in capital commitments for EnCap Minerals and Rock River Minerals, giving the firm and its partners additional time to retain exposure to a large portfolio of Permian Basin mineral and royalty interests.
The vehicle is managed by EnCap and anchored by funds affiliated with Melange Capital Partners. EnCap said investor demand exceeded the amount required for the transaction, with participation from both existing investors and new institutional investors.
According to EnCap, the transaction represents the largest capital raise to date for a continuation vehicle focused on the upstream energy sector. It also provides existing investors with a liquidity option while allowing EnCap and participating investors to continue owning the assets and receiving exposure to their long-term cash flows.
The underlying portfolio was assembled through partnerships with Fortis Minerals, OGX Resources, Piedra Energy III, and Pegasus Resources. Pegasus continues to manage the assets.
The portfolio consists of approximately 134,000 net royalty acres of mineral and royalty interests in the core of the Permian Basin and currently generates net production of approximately 37,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
Activity across the acreage is supported by several major Permian operators. ExxonMobil, Diamondback Energy, Occidental, and ConocoPhillips collectively account for approximately 48% of activity across the portfolio, according to EnCap.
Unlike many operating energy assets, mineral and royalty interests generally do not require the mineral owner to fund drilling and development capital expenditures. EnCap highlighted that characteristic as part of the portfolio’s long-duration cash-flow profile and said the assets provide exposure to high-quality development inventory and operator economics in the Lower 48.
The continuation vehicle expands EnCap’s ability to hold the mineral portfolio beyond the typical life of the funds that initially acquired and developed the assets. The structure also creates a mechanism for investors seeking liquidity to exit while other investors maintain or establish exposure to the assets.
EnCap has been investing in the U.S. energy industry since 1988. The firm has raised 25 institutional investment funds totaling more than $47 billion and currently manages capital for more than 350 U.S. and international investors.
Evercore served as exclusive financial advisor to EnCap on the continuation vehicle, while Kirkland & Ellis served as EnCap’s legal counsel. Latham & Watkins advised Melange on the transaction.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are grateful to our limited partners for their continued support and for the opportunity to keep owning this exceptional asset well into the future. We have long held strong conviction in the Permian Basin, and we believe it will remain a critical economic engine for many years to come, particularly as industry innovation continues.”
“We also want to thank the Pegasus team and the other management teams who built this portfolio alongside EnCap and created tremendous value along the way. EnCap was an early mover in acquiring upstream minerals at scale, and we continue to execute that strategy today through our flagship institutional funds. We look forward to making this Continuation Vehicle a success for all investors.”
Doug Swanson, Managing Partner Of EnCap Investments

Bengaluru-based AI startup Sarvam AI is in early discussions to raise $250 million to $300 million at a valuation of $3 billion, potentially doubling its valuation in four months, according to an ET report.

The company is expanding its efforts across AI models, computing infrastructure and enterprise deployments. It plans to build a trillion-parameter AI model and establish an office in San Francisco to recruit researchers. Sarvam has also hired Sashikumar Sreedharan, the former head of Google Cloud India.

candidates.text:
SBG Funding Surpasses $3 Billion In Small-Business Financing As 2026 Originations Reach $867 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 15, 2026
SBG Funding Surpasses $3 Billion In Small-Business Financing As 2026 Originations Reach $867 Million
SBG Funding has surpassed $3 billion in financing delivered to more than 28,000 U.S. small businesses since its founding in 2017, as the company continues to report rapid growth in annual originations.
The New York City-based financing company originated $867 million during the first nine months of 2026, already exceeding the $794 million originated during all of 2025. SBG Funding said it is on pace to originate approximately $1.15 billion for the full year.
The company’s growth has accelerated significantly in recent years. Annual originations increased from $189 million in 2022 to $422 million in 2024 and $794 million in 2025. SBG Funding originated $7.9 million during its first months of operation in 2017.
Alongside the financing milestone, SBG Funding introduced a new brand identity centered on the tagline “Capital That Keeps Up” and launched a redesigned website. The positioning emphasizes fast, flexible, and responsible financing for established small businesses with steady revenue.
SBG Funding provides capital for purposes including payroll, equipment purchases, working capital, and other operational needs. Through a single application, business owners can be matched with revenue-based financing, term loans, lines of credit, equipment financing, invoice financing, or SBA financing of up to $10 million.
The company said financing decisions typically arrive within 24 hours and applying does not affect an owner’s credit score. Each applicant works with a dedicated adviser who manages the process from application through funding.
SBG Funding operates as both a direct provider of revenue-based financing and a marketplace connecting businesses with financing products through a broader lender network. The company serves businesses across all 50 states, with significant activity in construction, manufacturing, healthcare, retail, food and beverage, and trucking and transportation.
Customers have completed more than 64,000 financing transactions with SBG Funding, including repeat transactions from businesses returning for additional capital. The company said its adviser model allows returning clients to work with people who are already familiar with their businesses and cash flow patterns.
SBG Funding was also named to the Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies for the fifth consecutive year in 2026, ranking No. 778.
KEY QUOTES:
“Small businesses don’t schedule their opportunities. A contractor wins a bid on Monday and needs equipment by Friday, or a restaurant’s walk-in cooler fails in the middle of July. Capital That Keeps Up is our promise that the money moves as fast as those owners do, and after more than 64,000 transactions, we know what that takes.”
Jeffrey Sachs, Founder And CEO Of SBG Funding
“When a customer comes back for more capital, their adviser already knows the business. That’s a big reason the second decision is often faster than the first.”
Adam Block, Vice President Of Sales And Operations At SBG Funding

candidates.text:
Israel Startup Funding Hits $2.77 Billion, Five Firms Raise $1.9 Billion
Epil Bodra
| October 1 | Funding Feed , Industry & Events
Share
Israel Startup Funding : Israeli startups closed 28 funding rounds during September 2026, with investors concentrating heavily on cybersecurity, enterprise AI and technologies designed to support autonomous AI agents. Wonderful, Cyera, Island, Upwind and Covenant accounted for nearly 70% of the month’s total investment.
The Israeli tech scene witnessed an inflow of around $2.77 billion into startups in September 2026; however, the breakdown of investments reveals more details about the situation.
Out of 28 rounds of financing, five firms received $1.9 billion together, accounting for almost 69% of the investments made in September. In the rest 23 rounds, an amount of around $870 million was raised by other startups.
Cybersecurity and artificial intelligence featured prominently throughout the month, particularly among businesses developing technologies to help enterprises adopt, operate and secure autonomous AI agents.
Five Mega-Rounds Drive September’s Funding Activity
Enterprise AI startup Wonderful recorded September’s largest transaction, raising $550 million on September 2 at a valuation of $5 billion. The investment came just six months after the company secured $150 million at a $2 billion valuation.
Founded in early 2025, Wonderful has raised more than $800 million to date, expanded into over 35 markets and grown its workforce to approximately 650 employees.
Cybersecurity company Cyera followed with a $400 million investment from Goldman Sachs on September 22. The transaction extended its Series G round, bringing its total funding raised in 2026 to $1.4 billion and pushing its valuation beyond $12 billion.
Island secured another $400 million on September 24, reaching a valuation of $6.4 billion as it expands its enterprise browser technology into a broader control platform for employees and AI agents.
Cloud security company Upwind added $300 million, taking its valuation to $3.8 billion. The figure represents a substantial increase from the $1.5 billion valuation recorded during its $250 million funding round in January.
Completing the five largest transactions was defense technology startup Covenant, which emerged from stealth with $250 million at a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
Together, these investments established the financial weight of September’s largest deals, while funding activity continued across several other technology segments.
Cybersecurity Investors Look Beyond Traditional Protection Tools
One of September’s recurring investment themes was the growing need to secure enterprise environments where AI agents operate alongside human employees.
Several startups attracted funding for technologies addressing this changing security landscape.
Reco raised $55 million with backing from AT&T to expand its security platform as businesses introduce more AI agents into their operations. AIR Security secured $50 million to develop what it describes as a firewall for AI agents.
Cymphony received $25 million in Series A funding for a platform focused on mapping identities, permissions, information and behaviour across people and AI systems.
Meanwhile, Blackstone led a $27 million investment in Huskeys, which is developing an agentic AI layer for web application firewalls.
Consumer cybersecurity also attracted investor attention. Guardio secured $40 million at a valuation of $1.1 billion. The company reported surpassing one million paying customers and reaching $150 million in annual recurring revenue.
The range of transactions illustrates how cybersecurity investment is extending beyond conventional protection tools into technologies designed around the operational demands of AI adoption.
AI Agents Emerge as a Common Thread Across Industries
The emphasis on autonomous AI systems was not restricted to cybersecurity.
Euno raised $23 million to develop technology that allows AI agents to access and use organisational knowledge inside large enterprises. Keewano secured $12 million in seed funding to build a database designed for AI agents working with complex information.
Legal technology startup Chamelio also raised $26 million in Series A funding to develop AI agents capable of handling routine legal workflows while directing matters requiring human judgement for further review.
Elsewhere, DataAgent emerged from stealth with a $10 million pre-seed round to develop self-healing infrastructure powered by autonomous agents.
The activity highlights an emerging focus within September’s funding announcements: investment is flowing not only towards businesses offering AI-powered applications, but also towards the infrastructure required to make autonomous systems practical in enterprise settings.
HiBob and Buildots Secure Major Investments Outside the Five Largest Deals
September’s fundraising activity extended into human resources technology, construction software and data security.
Salesforce led a $166 million investment in HR technology company HiBob, valuing the business at $3.5 billion. Its workforce management platform provides organisational data and permissions that can support the deployment of AI tools within companies.
The Israeli construction technology firm, Buildots, managed to raise $130 million at an estimated value near $1 billion. The company’s artificial intelligence platform has become more common in large data center constructions since there are serious consequences associated with delay.
Data security company MIND raised $72 million in Series B funding, tripling its valuation to $300 million. The company has raised $112 million to date and reached a $10 million annual revenue run rate within 18 months of beginning commercial sales.
These investments added substantial capital to September’s overall total beyond the five largest transactions.

Forbion Raises €2.3 Billion Across Two New Life Sciences Funds
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Forbion Raises €2.3 Billion Across Two New Life Sciences Funds
Forbion raised €2.3 billion ($2.6 billion) across two new investment funds, marking the largest fundraising in the life sciences venture capital firm’s history.
The fundraising exceeded its original target and brings Forbion’s total assets under management to approximately €7.5 billion.
The capital was raised for Forbion Growth Opportunities Fund IV and Forbion Ventures Fund VIII.
Together, the funds are expected to finance approximately 30 biotechnology companies.
Initial investments have already been completed.
Investors include MN, PGGM, KfW Capital, Kauffman Foundation, Eli Lilly and Company, and other existing and new institutional investors.
Growth Opportunities Fund IV will primarily target later-stage biopharmaceutical companies in Europe and North America developing therapies for areas of significant unmet medical need.
Ventures Fund VIII will invest in therapeutics-focused biotechnology companies, including established businesses and newly created ventures built around promising assets and experienced teams.
Over its 20-year history, Forbion has financed 142 companies, including 37 businesses created by the firm.
Portfolio companies have produced 21 approved medical products that have reached more than 1.6 million patients globally.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our successful fundraising gives us significant dry powder in a market characterized by a general shortage of capital. This allows us to select the most exciting biotech companies for investment.”
Sander Slootweg, Managing Partner and Co-Founder of Forbion

New American Funding Adds Mullinix Mortgage Group With $2 Billion Career Volume
New American Funding has added the Mullinix Mortgage Group, expanding the independent mortgage lender’s presence across North Carolina and South Carolina while bringing one of the region’s highest-producing mortgage professionals and his team onto its platform.
The Mullinix Mortgage Group was founded by Will Mullinix, who has more than 20 years of mortgage industry experience and has originated more than $2 billion in mortgages during his career. The group focuses on residential purchase and refinance lending and is licensed across North Carolina, South Carolina, Maryland, Virginia, Tennessee, Georgia, and Florida.
Mullinix was ranked the No. 1 mortgage originator in North Carolina by loan volume by Scotsman Guide in both 2025 and 2026. He was also most recently ranked No. 33 nationwide.
The group serves homebuyers through offices in Charlotte and Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina. Its lending capabilities include conventional, jumbo, physician, first-time homebuyer, bridge loan assistance, FHA, and VA programs. Mullinix Mortgage Group also provides construction and home equity planning for primary residences, second homes, and investment properties.
The full Mullinix Mortgage Group support team and loan officers are joining New American Funding as part of the move. Team members include Taylor Linde, Morgan Wise, Lenzi Moore, Don Walker, and Marty Pizzo.
New American Funding said the addition will provide Mullinix and his team with a broader product platform, technology infrastructure, and operational support as they continue expanding in the Carolinas and other markets. Mullinix, who was born and raised in Wilmington, North Carolina, later moved to Charlotte and has developed a significant presence across the region. candidates.text:
Axiom Secures $2 Billion Convertible Preferred Investment At $37.5 Billion Enterprise Value
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Axiom Secures $2 Billion Convertible Preferred Investment At $37.5 Billion Enterprise Value
Axiom Solutions International has secured a $2 billion convertible preferred equity investment led by General Catalyst and Koch Equity Development, along with co-investors, at an initial enterprise value of $37.5 billion.
Axiom is currently Flex’s Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment and is expected to be separated into an independent publicly traded company during the first quarter of 2027.
Funds affiliated with General Catalyst, Koch Equity Development and participating co-investors agreed to purchase $2 billion of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock in Axiom.
On a pro forma basis following the separation, the investment will be entirely in Axiom.
The proceeds are expected to help finance Axiom’s previously announced acquisition of EPC Power and provide the company with additional balance-sheet capacity as it prepares to become independent.
Net proceeds can be used to fund part of the EPC Power purchase price, repay equity bridge or other intermediate financing related to that acquisition, pay dividends on the preferred stock or support general corporate purposes.
Flex separately secured committed term-loan financing for the remaining portion of the EPC Power transaction.
The preferred stock will initially pay a 10% annual cash dividend before the separation.
Following the separation, the dividend will step down to 6% annually if paid in cash or 7% if paid in kind, subject to potential increases after the fifth anniversary of the separation and other adjustments.
General Catalyst will also receive the right to nominate one director to Axiom’s board after the separation is completed.
The investment remains subject to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions.
Flex expects Axiom to focus on power, thermal and compute infrastructure supporting growing artificial intelligence infrastructure demand.
PJT Partners is serving as financial adviser and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom is providing legal counsel to Flex.
Davis Polk & Wardwell is serving as legal counsel to General Catalyst.
KEY QUOTES:
“This investment provides equity funding for our recently announced acquisition of EPC Power and will allow Axiom to have a strong balance sheet as we prepare to stand up as an independent, publicly traded company squarely focused on the power, thermal, and compute infrastructure the AI era demands. General Catalyst brings deep conviction in applied AI and a long track record partnering with companies building category-defining leaders, and we’re glad to have them partner with us as Axiom enters its next chapter. This transaction reflects the value we see in Axiom’s business today and will translate into lasting value for Flex shareholders as the separation comes together.”
Revathi Advaithi, Chief Executive Officer of Flex and Expected Chief Executive Officer of Axiom
“Axiom sits at the center of the power and infrastructure buildout that AI demands, and we’ve been impressed by the team’s execution and the scale of the opportunity ahead. We look forward to partnering with Axiom for the long term as it becomes an independent company and continues to invest in the technology and capacity this next phase of growth requires.”
Hemant Taneja, Chief Executive Officer of General Catalyst
“AI diffusion requires modern power solutions at scale. Under Revathi’s leadership, we believe Axiom will become the defining power company of the AI era.”
Madhu Namburi, Managing Director at General Catalyst

Oaktree Asset-Backed Finance Fund Closes At $2 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry

Oaktree Asset-Backed Finance Fund Closes At $2 Billion
Oaktree has closed its Asset-Backed Finance Fund (ABF I) with $2 billion in commitments across the fund and related investment vehicles. The final close reached the fund’s fundraising target and attracted a globally diversified group of institutional investors.
Investors included U.S. public pension plans and sovereign wealth funds, reflecting growing institutional interest in private asset-backed finance strategies.
The close is in addition to Oaktree’s separate asset-backed vehicle focused on private wealth investors.
Oaktree’s strategy provides flexible capital to originators across areas including equipment leasing, transportation, consumer finance, real estate and infrastructure.
The firm has been investing in asset-backed finance for more than two decades.
Across its broader asset-backed finance platform, Oaktree has invested more than $19 billion and developed relationships with hundreds of third-party originators.
ABF I also builds on Brookfield’s partnership with Oaktree, which dates to 2019.
The strategy now uses Brookfield’s global operating platform to support sourcing, underwriting and investment analysis across the asset-backed finance market.
Brookfield’s broader asset-based finance platform totals more than $60 billion.
Its investment areas include specialty finance, residential non-qualified mortgages, aviation lending, music royalties, fund finance and digital infrastructure leases.
Oaktree operates as part of Brookfield’s $416 billion credit platform.
KEY QUOTE:
“As the private asset-backed market grows, its sheer variety across sectors, structures and risk/return makes the market difficult to navigate. We see that as opportunity, giving us real freedom to pursue the best relative value. Our approach is simple: survey a very broad market for less-crowded lending opportunities, and subject them to Oaktree’s critical eye. candidates.title: Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data
candidates.snippet:
Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health and private-sector partners have announced a coordinated $1.8 billion commitment of funding, data, computing resources and measurement technology to create foundational biological data for predictive AI models.
The post Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data
Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health and private-sector partners have announced a coordinated $1.8 billion commitment of funding, data, computing resources and measurement technology to create foundational biological data for predictive AI models.
The initiative is intended to build an open resource that researchers can use to develop AI systems capable of predicting how biological systems and human cells respond to interventions.
The Department of Energy plans to invest more than $500 million over five years in laboratory measurement, modeling and computation.
NIH will coordinate datasets, repositories and knowledge bases generated through more than $500 million of previous federal investment, with Biohub working to standardize that information for AI model training.
Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta are collectively investing another $300 million in the Virtual Biology Initiative.
Biohub previously committed $500 million to the initiative, including $400 million for technologies such as cryo-electron tomography, advanced microscopy and biological engineering tools, plus $100 million for external research.
The broader effort aims to provide the data required to develop virtual biological models that could allow researchers to conduct portions of experiments digitally before moving into physical laboratories.
DOE will contribute through its Genesis Mission, drawing on resources including exascale supercomputers, X-ray and neutron scattering, cryo-electron microscopy and autonomous laboratories across the National Laboratory system.
NIH will contribute through its Bio Genesis Mission and existing biomedical repositories and research programs.
Other participating scientific organizations include the Allen Institute, Broad Institute, Gladstone Institutes, Human Cell Atlas, Human Protein Atlas and Wellcome Sanger Institute.
NVIDIA will contribute accelerated computing infrastructure, software and technical expertise, while Renaissance Philanthropy is helping expand funding for data generation.
KEY QUOTES:
“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally. The insights that come from this could unlock a far greater understanding of disease and open up completely new paths for cures. Because of this potential, the creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together. We invite the worldwide scientific community to join us in this project.”
Alex Rives, Head of Science at Biohub
“Generating the data to solve predictive systems biology requires scaling past the limits of what any single organization can produce today. By joining the Virtual Biology Initiative as a founding member, Isomorphic Labs is helping build a massive, multimodal data foundation. This initiative will generate the data needed to push the industry closer to the next significant breakthrough for biology.”
Max Jaderberg, President of Isomorphic Labs
“This partnership represents a critical step forward in leveraging artificial intelligence for public benefit. By combining DOE’s exascale computing, experimental measurement, and modeling assets, including premier user facilities at the Joint Genome Institute, the Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, and advanced structural beamlines with the unique AI models, tool development, and biological data capabilities of Biohub, we are setting a new standard for open science that will accelerate discoveries in both medicine and biotechnology.”
Dario Gil, DOE Under Secretary for Science
“By combining resources and expertise, we can accelerate the development of universal cell models with sufficient biological complexity to predict how any cell responds to an intervention. The return from these models could be broad and profound, resulting in substantially faster timelines for medical breakthroughs as compared with attempting to attain the same results through laboratory experiments alone.”
Nicole Kleinstreuer, Ph.D., NIH Deputy Director for Program Coordination, Planning, and Strategic Initiatives
“The quest to build a virtual cell is one of the great collective scientific challenges and key to understanding the mechanisms of life. We will not solve this challenge without open, experimental biological data at an unprecedented scale, showing how living cells behave and respond to changes. This investment in biological data generation will help create an open, standardized data commons, which will lay the foundations researchers around the world need to better model biology.”
Pushmeet Kohli, VP of AI for Science at Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Google Cloud

candidates.text:
Lamb Weston: Q1 Revenue Rises To $1.67 Billion As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Lamb Weston: Q1 Revenue Rises To $1.67 Billion As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
Lamb Weston reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter net sales of $1.67 billion, up 1% from $1.66 billion in the prior-year period and above the company’s expectations.
Sales volume increased 2%, while price and mix declined 2%.
Net income totaled $29 million compared with $64 million a year earlier.
Adjusted net income was $103 million, unchanged from the prior-year period.
Diluted earnings per share declined to $0.21 from $0.46, while adjusted diluted EPS increased to $0.75 from $0.74.
Adjusted EBITDA totaled $286 million compared with $302 million a year earlier.
North America remained the company’s strongest-performing segment.
North America net sales increased 5% to $1.14 billion as sales volume grew 7%, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of volume growth.
North America adjusted EBITDA increased 11% to $287 million.
The gains reflected higher volumes, cost-saving initiatives, tariff refunds, and increased equity-method investment earnings.
International revenue declined 8% to $529 million.
International adjusted EBITDA declined 54% to $27 million as lower European sales volumes, higher manufacturing costs, factory underutilization, inflation, and prior-year potato crop costs pressured results.
Lamb Weston said capacity optimization efforts in North America have increased utilization by approximately 10 percentage points.
The company also ended production at its Broekhuizenvorst facility and transitioned customer fulfillment elsewhere in its network to improve international utilization and costs.
Operating cash flow totaled $235 million during the quarter.
Capital expenditures were $91 million.
Lamb Weston ended the quarter with $166 million in cash and cash equivalents and another $1.24 billion of available liquidity under its revolving credit facility.
The company returned $52 million to shareholders through dividends during the quarter.
Its board subsequently declared another quarterly dividend of $0.38 per share.
Following the better-than-expected first quarter, Lamb Weston increased several fiscal 2027 targets.
The company now expects net sales to increase at a low-single-digit rate compared with its previous forecast of flat to 1% growth.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to between $1.125 billion and $1.215 billion from $1.10 billion to $1.20 billion.
Adjusted diluted EPS guidance increased to $3.05 to $3.35 from $2.95 to $3.25.
Lamb Weston continues to expect between $750 million and $800 million of operating cash flow during fiscal 2027.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are off to a solid start to the year, delivering first quarter net sales and profit above our expectations.”
“Our first quarter results were driven by continued momentum in North America where our strong customer relationships fueled sales volume growth and we continued to drive cost savings.”
“We continue to experience unexpected inflationary pressure across key input costs and freight expense. Our teams are addressing cost inflation by working with suppliers and hedging where possible.”
“At the same time, we continue to make meaningful progress advancing our Focus to Win strategy, including cross-functional efforts to sharpen our prioritization of markets and channels.”
Mike Smith, President and CEO of Lamb Weston

candidates.snippet:
Wolfspeed received a conditional commitment from the U.S. Department of War for up to $1.5 billion in long-term financing to support domestic production of silicon carbide materials and wide bandgap power devices, with an additional focus on U.S. national security applications.
The post Wolfspeed Secures Conditional $1.5 Billion U.S. Department Of War Loan Commitment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Wolfspeed Secures Conditional $1.5 Billion U.S. Department Of War Loan Commitment
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
Wolfspeed Secures Conditional $1.5 Billion U.S. Department Of War Loan Commitment
Wolfspeed received a conditional commitment from the U.S. Department of War for up to $1.5 billion in long-term financing to support domestic production of silicon carbide materials and wide bandgap power devices, with an additional focus on U.S. national security applications.
The financing would be provided through the Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital and is structured as a senior secured delayed-draw term loan facility with a 30-year tenor.
Wolfspeed plans to use the potential financing to strengthen its U.S. semiconductor manufacturing capabilities across silicon carbide and gallium nitride technologies.
The company said the financing could support upgrades to its gallium nitride epitaxy capabilities for next-generation communications infrastructure and electronic warfare systems.
It also plans to develop radiation-hardening capabilities for existing silicon carbide products and future gallium nitride products.
Wolfspeed said silicon carbide and related semiconductor technologies are increasingly important across defense, aerospace, artificial intelligence, critical infrastructure, and other strategic commercial markets.
The company’s domestic manufacturing footprint includes operations in North Carolina, New York, and Arkansas.
The financing is expected to support a multi-year program to strengthen Wolfspeed’s leadership in U.S. silicon carbide materials and power devices.
Wolfspeed also plans to establish, expand, or onshore domestic low-voltage and high-voltage gallium nitride power-device production capabilities.
Additional priorities include advancing GaN-on-SiC radio-frequency epitaxial wafer technology and developing domestic radiation-hardening capabilities.
The company said the financing would also strengthen its capital structure and provide additional long-duration funding for strategic investments.
Under the contemplated structure, Wolfspeed would be required to issue warrants to the Department of War representing up to 7.5% of the company’s fully diluted equity.
Those warrants would be issued on a pro rata basis as financing tranches are funded.
The transaction remains subject to substantial due diligence, negotiation and execution of definitive agreements, governmental approvals, appropriations, third-party consents, and other closing conditions.
Wolfspeed said there is no assurance that definitive agreements will be completed or that the financing will ultimately be funded.
The conditional commitment represents another step in Wolfspeed’s broader effort to strengthen its financial foundation while expanding its role in the domestic wide bandgap semiconductor supply chain.
KEY QUOTES:
“SiC and GaN have critical national security applications. With this financing, the company would be well positioned to not only continue to serve the DoW but also expand its capabilities for the benefit of U.S. national security as a whole.”
Robert Feurle, Chief Executive Officer of Wolfspeed
“We believe the scale and 30-year tenor of this conditional commitment reflects the long-term importance of the technology and manufacturing capabilities Wolfspeed has built in the United States. This financing would strengthen our continued advancement of silicon carbide materials and wide bandgap power devices, reinforcing our efforts to build a more resilient U.S. semiconductor and defense industrial base.”
Robert Feurle, Chief Executive Officer of Wolfspeed
“This conditional 30-year commitment represents another significant milestone in our ongoing efforts to optimize Wolfspeed’s capital structure and improve our financial foundation. Subject to the satisfaction of diligence, negotiation of definitive agreements, and other financial, legal, and investment conditions, the broader commitment is expected to provide additional long-dated capital to support our strategic priorities, improve financial flexibility, and further position Wolfspeed for long-term value creation.”
Gregor van Issum, Chief Financial Officer of Wolfspeed

Eka Robotics Hits $1.45 Billion Valuation After $150 Million Funding Round for Physical AI
Eka Robotics raises $150 million at a $1.45 billion valuation to advance physical AI, touch-sensitive robotic grippers and industrial automation.
By
Samarjit Kaur
on
October 21, 2026
Share
Eka Robotics is developing physical AI technology that combines force-sensitive robotic grippers with machine learning to improve object handling.
Eka Robotics, a startup developing artificial intelligence (AI) systems for robots, has secured a $1.45 billion post-money valuation after raising $150 million in Series A funding. Founded by Massachusetts Institute of Technology professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, the company is developing technology that lets robots pick up and handle objects faster and more precisely.
The funding round was led by venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) & F-Prime.
The startup’s approach combines a force-sensitive robotic gripper with a deep-learning model trained to respond to physical contact, addressing a longstanding challenge in robotics.
Also Read: Indian Startup Unveils Vision Nano 250g UAV for Special Forces, Claims 25-Minute Flight Time
How Eka Robotics is Changing Robotic Manipulation
Eka Robotics says its system can pick up about 1,500 objects weighing up to 1 kg per hour, compared with about 600 for a human. The company also reports a success rate of more than 95% when picking up objects.
Unlike conventional approaches that rely heavily on visual information, Eka uses what it calls a vision-force-action model. The system combines visual & language inputs with physical-force information, helping the robot adjust its grip when handling delicate objects.
Its robotic hand includes additional force sensors and a more flexible design than traditional grippers. This allows it to respond to contact rather than relying on sight alone.
The founders use physics simulations and reinforcement learning to train the system. This approach can generate thousands of hours of robotic experience in minutes, reducing reliance on lengthy recordings of humans demonstrating tasks.
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign professor Kris Hauser told TechCrunch that the robot could adapt to numerous objects without retraining. However, the technology’s performance in industrial settings remains to be established.
Also Read: AI Startup Demoverse Raises $600K to Let Consumers Co-Create Products With Brands
Industrial Deployment Remains the Next Test
Eka Robotics is running confidential pilot projects with industrial customers that involve pick-and-place operations and wire manipulation. These tasks involve moving objects into position and handling wires during assembly.
The company faces the actionable challenge of proving that its systems can operate reliably on production lines for extended periods. Hauser also questioned how readily the approach could be adapted to industrial tasks beyond basic object handling.
Agrawal said the company’s gripper hardware costs less than $1,000 and is currently rated for five million duty cycles. The longer-term target is 20 million cycles, matching the benchmark cited for standard industrial robotic arms.
Eka Robotics bets that combining physical feedback with AI training can bridge the gap between robots that perform well in demonstrations and machines that work reliably in factories.

candidates.snippet:

candidates.text:
Clean Power Alliance Secures $1.4 Billion Prepay Bond To Generate $91.1 Million In Renewable Energy Savings
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Clean Power Alliance Secures $1.4 Billion Prepay Bond To Generate $91.1 Million In Renewable Energy Savings
Clean Power Alliance has closed its seventh energy prepayment bond transaction, a $1.4 billion financing expected to generate approximately $91.1 million in renewable energy cost savings during the bond’s initial seven-year period.
The transaction is projected to deliver average savings of approximately $12.7 million annually. With the latest issuance, Clean Power Alliance has now completed $8.3 billion in prepay bond transactions and locked in $519.1 million in total savings across the initial periods of the seven transactions.
Across the entire program, CPA said its average annual savings total approximately $65 million.
The organization uses its prepay bond program to lower the cost of renewable power purchases. As a not-for-profit government agency, CPA can issue tax-exempt bonds and use the proceeds to prepay for electricity generated from renewable resources such as solar, wind, geothermal, and hydropower. In exchange for the upfront payments, energy suppliers provide discounts that CPA said have historically ranged from 8% to 12%.
CPA uses those savings to support lower and more stable electricity rates as well as customer programs, workforce development, skills training, and community energy infrastructure projects.
The latest transaction is CPA’s first prepay bond with J.P. Morgan serving as underwriter and J.P. Morgan Ventures Energy Corporation acting as the prepaid energy supplier. CPA said it also represents the first electric prepay transaction in the United States completed with J.P. Morgan.
Moody’s assigned the bonds an investment-grade Aa3 rating, while Kestrel designated them as Green Bonds.
During the initial seven-year period, CPA expects to receive approximately 1.14 million megawatt-hours of PCC1-eligible energy annually. PCC1 represents California’s highest-tier category of renewable energy.
The electricity covered by the transaction will come from existing long-term power purchase agreements representing a combined 440.8 megawatts of wind resources. CPA said the structure will help diversify its renewable energy portfolio while reducing exposure to energy market volatility.
The transaction was completed under a November 2025 authorization from CPA’s board of directors allowing the organization to execute up to $4.5 billion of new prepay transactions through June 30, 2027.
Clean Power Alliance serves 38 communities across Los Angeles and Ventura counties and provides electricity to approximately three million residents and businesses.
KEY QUOTES:
“CPA’s prepay strategy is an important tool for delivering on our commitment to provide clean, reliable and affordable energy. By building on the success of previous transactions, we’re able to secure substantial savings that reduce costs while advancing our mission to serve our communities with clean power options at competitive rates.”
Ted Bardacke, Chief Executive Officer Of Clean Power Alliance
“Reaching 8.3 billion in prepay transactions reflects the strength and scalability of this financing strategy. This latest transaction achieves long-term energy cost savings through strategic financial partnerships, helping us maintain competitive rates while supporting a diverse portfolio of renewable energy resources.”
David McNeil, Chief Financial Officer Of Clean Power Alliance

candidates.snippet:
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles has completed its Anniversary Campaign after raising a record $1.35 billion to support pediatric care, research, and education. The milestone represents the largest fundraising effort in the hospital’s 125-year history.
The post Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Marks $1.35 Billion Anniversary Campaign Milestone appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Marks $1.35 Billion Anniversary Campaign Milestone
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Marks $1.35 Billion Anniversary Campaign Milestone
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles has completed its Anniversary Campaign after raising a record $1.35 billion to support pediatric care, research, and education. The milestone represents the largest fundraising effort in the hospital’s 125-year history.
CHLA announced the campaign’s completion during its 2026 gala at The Event Deck at L.A. LIVE. The event brought together philanthropists, community leaders, patients, celebrities, and other supporters while recognizing Ellen K and Kourtney and Justin Turner with the hospital’s Courage to Care Award.
The Anniversary Campaign was supported by thousands of donors, corporate partners, foundations, families, and CHLA employees. Campaign co-chairs Nikki DeLoach and Jeffrey Worthe led the effort, while Jimmy Kimmel, Sugar Ray Leonard, Chuck Lorre, and Jamie Lee Curtis served as honorary campaign chairs.
CHLA said the $1.35 billion raised will help advance pediatric medicine, accelerate scientific research, expand education initiatives, and support access to specialized care for children. The hospital is the largest provider of hospital care for children in California and operates research and education programs alongside its clinical services.
The gala also recognized Ellen K for her longstanding support of CHLA. Her involvement began after her son received emergency care at the hospital. She has since helped raise more than $4 million through KOST 103.5’s annual Giving Tuesday broadcast and has served as a longtime co-host of CHLA’s Walk & Play L.A.
Kourtney and Justin Turner were honored for more than a decade of volunteerism, fundraising, advocacy, and philanthropic support. Their work through the Justin Turner Foundation has included programs supporting children with serious illnesses and their families.
The evening also highlighted the Jackie and Gene Autry Orthopedic Center, which provides pediatric orthopedic care and includes programs focused on spine and neuromuscular disorders, hip preservation, sports medicine, and hand and upper-extremity care. The celebration concluded with a performance by Michael Bublé.
KEY QUOTES:
“As we celebrate Children’s Hospital Los Angeles’ 125th anniversary, this gala marks a defining moment in our history and an opportunity to recognize the extraordinary generosity that made the Anniversary Campaign’s success possible. Thanks to the remarkable generosity of our supporters, CHLA will continue to be at the forefront of pediatric medicine, accelerate scientific discoveries, and ensure children have access to world-class care for generations to come.”
Paul S. Viviano, President And Chief Executive Officer Of Children’s Hospital Los Angeles
“On behalf of everyone at CHLA, it is my pleasure to thank Nikki DeLoach and Jeff Worthe for so beautifully leading the Campaign. I would also like to recognize Jimmy Kimmel, Sugar Ray Leonard, Chuck Lorre, and Jamie Lee Curtis for serving as Honorary Campaign Chairs. Most importantly, it is generous individuals like all of you, who ensure CHLA will have a brilliant future for the next 125 years.”

candidates.text:
1Komma5Grad Secures $1.35 Billion Valuation And Plans Over $112 Million Investment In Energy AI
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
1Komma5Grad Secures $1.35 Billion Valuation And Plans Over $112 Million Investment In Energy AI
German home electrification startup 1Komma5Grad secured a valuation of $1.35 billion in its latest financing round as the company increases investment in its energy artificial intelligence business, according to Reuters .
The company plans to invest more than €100 million, or approximately $112 million, in its Heartbeat energy AI platform during 2027.
1Komma5Grad describes itself as a home electrification company and is developing Heartbeat to automate a range of energy-related processes.
The platform targets functions including energy trading, billing, and metering, creating an AI-based layer to manage residential energy systems and related services.
The increased investment reflects the company’s strategy to expand beyond installing home energy systems and build software capabilities around how those assets are managed.
1Komma5Grad is also considering a significant geographic expansion.
CEO Philipp Schroeder said the company plans to expand into the United States beginning next year, citing strong investor interest as one factor behind the potential move.
The U.S. market could become an important part of the company’s next phase as it scales Heartbeat and its broader home electrification platform.
The company had previously considered a U.S. initial public offering but shelved those plans in 2025 amid uncertainty surrounding renewable energy and trade policy.
Schroeder said the company’s 2027 performance will play an important role in determining whether and when 1Komma5Grad ultimately moves ahead with a U.S. IPO.
The company has also confirmed a target of approximately $750 million in revenue for its 2026 financial year.
Hitting that target, alongside continued expansion of Heartbeat and a potential U.S. market entry, would add milestones as management evaluates the company’s longer-term capital markets strategy.
The latest financing gives 1Komma5Grad a $1.35 billion valuation while providing further support for its push to use AI to automate energy management and related processes across its platform.

candidates.text:
Michigan Students Receive 25,252 College Admission Offers And $1.274 Billion In Scholarship Opportunities Through MI College Match
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Michigan Students Receive 25,252 College Admission Offers And $1.274 Billion In Scholarship Opportunities Through MI College Match
Michigan students participating in MI College Match have received 25,252 college admission offers and more than $1.274 billion in scholarship opportunities through the statewide direct-admission initiative, allowing thousands of students to explore college options without completing a traditional college application.
MI College Match connects Michigan high school students with participating colleges and universities based on academic achievements, interests, preferences and other information submitted through the platform. The program opened to students on August 26, with students who completed profiles by September 21 becoming eligible for the initial round of admission offers released October 5.
Participating students have received an average of 14 college offers, while every student participating in the initial release received at least one admission offer. A total of 26 Michigan colleges and universities are participating, and the initiative is connected with more than 350 high schools through College Bound Michigan.
Each admission offer included information about either the Michigan Achievement Scholarship or the Community College Guarantee, helping students and families understand financial assistance that could make postsecondary education more affordable.
MI College Match is a partnership between Michigan College Access Network, EAB and participating Michigan higher education institutions. The initiative uses EAB’s Match technology to enable colleges to proactively identify students who may be a good fit and extend admission and scholarship opportunities directly to them.
Instead of requiring students to identify colleges, complete individual applications and then wait for admission decisions, MI College Match reverses parts of the traditional process by allowing participating institutions to approach eligible students directly.
Students create profiles containing information about their academic performance, interests, college preferences and other attributes. Participating colleges then review those profiles to determine whether to extend admission and scholarship opportunities.
The program is particularly focused on expanding college opportunities for students who may be less likely to pursue higher education, including students from low-income families, first-generation college students and students of color.
Participating institutions include Albion College, Alma College, Aquinas College, Baker College, Bay College, Calvin University, Cleary University, Davenport University, Grand Rapids Community College, Grand Valley State University, Great Lakes Christian College, Kalamazoo College, Lake Michigan College, Lawrence Technological University, Monroe County Community College, Montcalm Community College, Mott Community College, North Central Michigan College, Oakland University, Saginaw Chippewa Tribal College, Schoolcraft College, Spring Arbor University, University of Detroit Mercy, University of Michigan-Dearborn, University of Michigan-Flint and The University of Olivet.
The initiative also supports Michigan’s Sixty by 30 attainment goal, which seeks to have 60% of working-age adults earn a postsecondary credential or degree by 2030. MI College Match is intended to contribute to that objective by providing admission opportunities earlier and reducing barriers associated with the conventional college application process.
Students can continue creating MI College Match profiles through June 1, 2027, and participating institutions are expected to issue additional offers on a monthly basis. More institutions were also still preparing offers at the time of the announcement, meaning the number of admission and scholarship opportunities is expected to continue increasing.
KEY QUOTES:
“An admission offer is an invitation to see yourself in college, and affordability is essential to turning that invitation into an opportunity. By including information about the Michigan Achievement Scholarship and Community College Guarantee with every MI College Match offer, we are making sure students and families know that financial support is available. This is about connecting Michigan students with both the opportunity to attend college and the resources that can help make that postsecondary education affordable.”
Dr. Beverly Walker-Griffe, Executive Director of the Michigan Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential
“These numbers demonstrate what is possible when we rethink the way students experience the college-going process. Rather than asking students to discover colleges on their own, complete an application and wait to find out if they are wanted, MI College Match flips the process. It puts colleges directly in front of students with a clear message: ‘We see your potential, we want you here, and we’re inviting you to take a closer look.’”
Ryan Fewins-Bliss, Executive Director of the Michigan College Access Network
“An admission offer can change the conversation for a student and a family. When students learn that a college is interested in them before they’ve gone through a lengthy application process, they can begin thinking about college in a fundamentally different way.”
Hope Krutz, President of EAB’s Enroll360 Division

candidates.title: Exclusive: Daytona, a startup building the ‘agentic cloud,’ valued at $1 billion in latest funding round
candidates.snippet: Exclusive: Daytona, a startup building the ‘agentic cloud,’ valued at $1 billion in latest funding round Fortune
candidates.text:
AI agents need somewhere to work—and Ivan Burazin thinks the existing cloud providers aren’t the right answer. Now Burazin, the cofounder and CEO of Daytona, a San Francisco-based startup, has turned the idea of a new kind of cloud just for AI agents into a unicorn business.
Recommended Video
Daytona said Tuesday it has raised a $60 million Series B venture capital round at a $1 billion valuation. FirstMark led the round. It was joined by an A-list roster of Silicon Valley founders, including Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo and Zoom’s Eric Yuan, plus strategic investors Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next and Okta Ventures.
Burazin told Fortune that about $50 million of the round came from existing investors. The new funding brings the amount Daytona has raised to date to about $91 million.
Why agents need their own computers
An AI agent that writes and runs code, browses the web or operates business software needs to use a computer—either an actual machine, or a virtual one, running in the cloud. For many use cases, having a virtual machine is preferable—it allows the AI agent to operate even if the person running the agent shuts down their laptop, and because virtual machines can be configured with only the software and network access the agent needs to do a particular task and nothing more, it is generally a safer way to run AI agents. A virtual machine, or “sandbox” as they are sometimes called, minimizes the chance that the agent will run amok and take damaging unauthorized actions, or that an outside party could hijack the agent and get it to divulge sensitive data.
Daytona was founded in 2023 by Burazin, Goran Draganić and Vedran Jukić to automate software development environments for large enterprises. When the founders saw that agents would need computers too, Burazin said, they “basically gave our competitors all our customers, rebuilt everything, had like three months left of revenue in the bank, and then relaunched this thing.”
Daytona currently provides these sandboxes to many of the leading AI companies, which use the virtual machines to allow their models to practice tasks over and over inside sandboxes during training and testing. Daytona says AI data company Snorkel, which also helps customers test and benchmark AI models, has provisioned more than one million sandboxes on its platform. It also counts Anthropic, OpenAI, Nvidia , Cursor, Cognition, Meta and Cohere among its customers.
Burazin said that Daytona’s revenue run rate grew 25-fold between January and September. “We’ve been growing on average every single month 50.9%,” Burazin said.
Existing cloud providers, such as Amazon’s AWS, Microsoft’s Azure, or Google’s Google Cloud Platform, allow customers to spin up virtual machines. But doing so takes between 30 seconds and many minutes, depending on the complexity of the configuration. This, Burazin said, is far too long for the future of agentic work, when companies may be deploying thousands or even tens of thousands of AI agents, each of which may need access to different software tools depending on the task they are being asked to complete.
Daytona can configure a new sandbox for an AI agent in 60 milliseconds, according to Burazin. That is roughly half the time it takes to blink. The trick, he said, is to pre-distribute snapshots of configured machines onto the physical drives of servers. When an agent needs a machine, Daytona attaches processing power and memory and resumes the snapshot. Agents can also clone a running computer to try different approaches in parallel. “You can literally replicate the computer into two and try both outcomes, and then replicate again and again and again until it gets the desired outcome,” Burazin said.
When he pitched investors, Burazin said, many asked “why the hell do we need this? You know, AWS can do this thing.” His answer is that hyperscalers built nearly everything on a few core services optimized for maximum utilization. To match Daytona’s performance, he argued, they would need to create a whole new company inside their existing cloud services. He conceded the hyperscalers could do this, but said it would not be easy for them to rebuild their infrastructure to serve AI agents instead of human users.
The scale involved is easy to underestimate. Burazin pointed to Muse, the personal agent Meta launched in September. He said it has “a computer underneath for every single chat.” By his back-of-the-envelope math, Muse would need $2.8 billion worth of sandboxes to serve 100 million users.
“We believe the next infrastructure shift is from human-centric cloud primitives to agent-native ones,” Matt Turck, a partner at FirstMark, said in a statement.
AI models run on GPUs. But to do work, they need CPUs.
Burazin also distinguishes what Daytona is building from the “neocloud” providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius. Those neoclouds are designed to train and run AI models. The data centers they are standing up are stuff full of graphics processing units, or GPUs, the computer chips optimized to run AI models. But to run virtual machines, a data center needs lots of traditional central processing units, or CPUs, that can run all kinds of different software. “The inference clouds is where the agent thinks, and our cloud is where the agent works,” Burazin said.
“We internally sort of believe that the number of dollars spent on CPUs will probably be higher than the dollars spent on GPUs in the foreseeable future,” he said, “which seems sort of counterintuitive today.”
The demand is so great that he forecasts a coming CPU shortage. “I strongly believe that there will be a CPU crunch,” he said. “The amount of CPU machines that we will need if we want to keep growing at this trajectory actually doesn’t exist right now.”

Blackstone Credit & Insurance served as lead lender and joint lead arranger on the financing.
HPS, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo also served as joint lead arrangers.
The combined company brings together broader security detection capabilities, expanded customer relationships, and greater operating scale.
Analogic is headquartered in Salem, New Hampshire, and provides advanced imaging, detection, automation, and power technology solutions.
Its portfolio serves aviation security, ports and borders, critical infrastructure, healthcare, and industrial markets.
Analogic combines imaging technologies, artificial intelligence, precision power, automation, and lifecycle support capabilities.
Blackstone Credit & Insurance said the financing demonstrates its ability to provide large-scale and flexible capital to established platforms.
BXCI invests across private investment grade, asset-based lending, public investment grade and high yield, infrastructure debt, direct lending, collateralized loan obligations, sustainable resources, and opportunistic credit.
Altaris, which focuses exclusively on healthcare investments, manages $10 billion of equity capital and has invested in more than 50 companies since its founding in 2003.
Leidos has approximately 50,000 employees globally and reported annual revenue of approximately $17.2 billion for the fiscal year ended January 2, 2026.

Brad Colman, Global Head of Healthcare Investing and Sponsor Coverage for Private Credit Strategies at Blackstone Credit & Insurance
