candidates.snippet:
Volato Group, which is in the process of rebranding as SOAR AI, entered into a common stock purchase agreement with an institutional investor for an equity facility of up to $1 billion.
The post SOAR AI Secures Up To $1 Billion Equity Facility To Support AI Infrastructure Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
SOAR AI Secures Up To $1 Billion Equity Facility To Support AI Infrastructure Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
SOAR AI Secures Up To $1 Billion Equity Facility To Support AI Infrastructure Expansion
Volato Group, which is in the process of rebranding as SOAR AI, entered into a common stock purchase agreement with an institutional investor for an equity facility of up to $1 billion.
The company said the facility is designed to support the development of its Ohio AI infrastructure campus and additional powered industrial sites it is exploring in the U.S. and internationally.
SOAR AI retains control over whether, when, and how much capital it draws from the facility and has no obligation to sell any shares.
The company’s Ohio campus currently has 154 MW of power available, with a roadmap to increase capacity to 480 MW.
Proceeds from any future draws are expected to support power, cooling, data center infrastructure, GPU compute deployments, and the development of additional AI infrastructure locations.
SOAR AI said its development strategy focuses on reusing existing industrial sites and electrical infrastructure where practical rather than building entirely new facilities.
The Ohio campus is the first location to use this approach, and the company is also evaluating additional brownfield and similar industrial sites domestically and internationally.
The financing follows commercial agreements announced in September 2026.
SOAR AI entered into a master services agreement and two four-year, take-or-pay orders with a large AI customer representing $1.17 billion in aggregate contract value.
Those orders include approximately $133 million in contractual customer prepayments and call for dedicated, single-tenant AMD GPU clusters.
The contractual start dates are December 31, 2026, and June 30, 2027.
The company said it is also in active discussions with additional prospective customers for available and planned AI infrastructure capacity.
SOAR AI expects the equity facility to complement customer prepayments, project-level financing, and other sources of capital as it expands.
Under the agreement, each sale is limited to 10% of average daily trading volume, with combined daily sales capped at $6 million.
Subsequent sales must be spaced at least two trading days apart and cannot occur when the prior day’s volume-weighted average price was the lowest of the preceding 10 trading days.
The investor also agreed not to sell short or hedge SOAR AI’s common stock during the term of the agreement.
The investor may not own more than 4.99% of the company’s outstanding common stock at any time.
Without stockholder approval, total issuances under the facility are capped at 19.99% of the shares outstanding on the signing date under NYSE American requirements.
No sales can begin until a resale registration statement covering the shares is filed with and declared effective by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
SOAR AI said the company can terminate the agreement without penalty on one trading day’s notice, provided no put notice is pending.
Volato Group expects its corporate name change to SOAR AI, Inc. to become effective on October 19, 2026, subject to applicable regulatory and stock exchange requirements.
The company is building an AI infrastructure platform combining data center infrastructure, high-density GPU compute, high-performance networking, and related technologies for AI, machine learning, and high-performance computing workloads.
KEY QUOTES:
“We have approximately $1.2 billion of contracted customer orders, an Ohio campus with 154 MW of power available today and a roadmap to 480 MW, and additional sites under active exploration. The opportunity in front of us is measured in hundreds of megawatts across multiple sites. This facility is sized to support that opportunity, and it gives us the flexibility to fund growth on our timeline as we bring contracted capacity online.”
Chris Ensey, Chief Executive Officer of SOAR AI
“The terms were structured to minimize market impact in the event we draw on the facility. We control the timing and size of every draw, sales are capped by trading volume, and the investor cannot short our stock. We intend to use the facility as our growth requires, alongside customer prepayments, project-level financing and other sources of capital.”
Mark Heinen, Chief Financial Officer of SOAR AI

Omni Bridgeway Closes $1 Billion Legal Finance Fundraise
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Omni Bridgeway Closes $1 Billion Legal Finance Fundraise
Omni Bridgeway closed its Funds 4 and 5 Series 2 capital raise at the full targeted size of $1 billion. The final close expands the legal finance firm’s institutional investor base while maintaining a high level of participation from existing investors.
Investors representing 99% of Series 1 commitments reinvested in Series 2.
More than 50% of Series 2 capital was committed by repeat Series 1 investors.
The fundraising increases Omni Bridgeway’s assets under management to approximately A$5.9 billion, or $4.2 billion.
The close comes as Omni Bridgeway marks its 40th year operating as a specialist investor in legal assets and its 25th year listed on the Australian Securities Exchange.
Funds 4 and 5 Series 2 will invest across legal assets diversified by jurisdiction, area of law, and investment strategy.
Omni Bridgeway is contributing approximately 20% of the capital in Series 2 through general partner co-investment.
As of June 30, 2026, the firm had completed 822 investments across its platform.
Omni Bridgeway reported a portfolio-wide multiple of invested capital of 2.4x across multiple decades and economic cycles.
The company said its capital model is designed to provide funded parties with dedicated capital committed to individual matters.
Omni Bridgeway also emphasized that it remains the sole decision-maker on its capital commitments and that funding availability is not dependent on other portfolio outcomes, third-party underwriting, syndication, or broader capital market conditions.
The $1 billion fundraising forms part of a broader capital strategy that also includes sidecar capital and structured finance solutions.
Omni Bridgeway plans to continue scaling and diversifying its legal finance platform across jurisdictions and areas of law.
The company operates with approximately 160 professionals across more than 20 locations and 15 countries.
KEY QUOTES:
“In legal finance, institutional capital is consolidating around mature, scaled managers with proprietary origination and work-out capability, and a track record of disciplined underwriting that has performed through multiple economic cycles.”
“Our successful close, the 99% reinvestment rate, and the sophisticated institutional quality of our investment base reflect our leading position within legal finance.”
“Funded parties increasingly and rightly focus on capital availability, long-term stability and commitment authority. Every dollar we commit is matched by dedicated fund capital earmarked to that matter. Omni Bridgeway is the sole decision-maker, and the availability of our capital commitment is not exposed to the outcome of other portfolio investments, capital market conditions, third-party underwriting or syndication. Counterparties increasingly recognize and value these differentiators – and accordingly assign a premium to our capital.”
“The US$1 billion raised in connection with Funds 4 and 5 Series 2 sits alongside a broader capital strategy, with sidecar capital and structured finance solutions continuing to expand alongside our core funds, supporting Omni Bridgeway’s aim of further scaling and diversifying its platform.”
Raymond van Hulst, Managing Director and CEO of Omni Bridgeway

Hightower Signature Wealth Brings In $1 Billion Team Synergy Capital Solutions
Hightower Advisors announced that Synergy Capital Solutions has joined Hightower Signature Wealth, adding approximately $1 billion in assets under management to the platform.

Synergy takes a collaborative approach to financial planning and portfolio management, working with clients to align investment and wealth management strategies with their goals, priorities, and values.

Hightower Signature Wealth’s model combines personalized financial advice with centralized infrastructure, allowing advisors to spend more time working directly with clients while benefiting from the resources and scale of a larger wealth management organization.
Synergy was founded more than four decades ago and has developed a broad range of wealth management solutions intended to support clients through different stages of their financial lives.
The firm’s leadership includes Mark Burns, CEO, Chief Investment Officer and Co-Founder; Jordann M. Andrusiak, CFP, Advisor and Chief Operating Officer; and Eric M. Nahat, CEPA, Advisor and Co-Chief Investment Officer.
Following the Synergy transaction, Hightower Signature Wealth has approximately $40 billion in assets under management, more than 160 advisors, and over 35 locations nationwide.
Hightower said it expects to announce additional Hightower Signature Wealth acquisitions through the end of 2026.
Hightower Advisors oversees more than $350 billion in assets and provides investment management, financial planning, retirement planning, 401(k) consulting, and cash management services through its network of advisor businesses.
The broader Hightower platform is designed to serve as a growth partner for independent wealth management firms seeking additional technology, investment capabilities, operational infrastructure, and strategic resources while maintaining their client-focused advisory models.

“Synergy has built its practice around the idea that wealth should enable clients to live with greater purpose and confidence. This philosophy is one we share, and we are thrilled to build on our longstanding relationship as we formally welcome the Synergy team to HTSW.”
Jennifer Frazier, President of Hightower Signature Wealth

Mark Burns, CEO, Chief Investment Officer and Co-Founder of Synergy Capital Solutions
“Our advisory relationships have always started with collaboration and a clear view of each client’s goals, priorities and values. As part of HTSW, we can preserve our personalized approach while drawing on broader capabilities to meet clients’ needs as their financial circumstances evolve.”
Jordann M. Andrusiak, CFP, Advisor and Chief Operating Officer at Synergy Capital Solutions
“We have built a broad spectrum of wealth solutions designed to help clients navigate each stage of their financial lives. HTSW gives us greater flexibility to deliver the valued strategies and advice that support clients’ long-term goals.”
Eric M. Nahat, CEPA, Advisor and Co-Chief Investment Officer at Synergy Capital Solutions

candidates.title: OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility
candidates.snippet:
OpenText completed a $1 billion senior secured notes offering and amended its revolving credit facility as the enterprise software company refinances upcoming debt maturities and extends portions of its capital structure.
The post OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility
OpenText completed a $1 billion senior secured notes offering and amended its revolving credit facility as the enterprise software company refinances upcoming debt maturities and extends portions of its capital structure.
The offering consists of $500 million aggregate principal amount of 6.700% senior secured notes due in 2031 and $500 million of 7.150% senior secured notes due in 2033.
By issuing debt with maturities extending into the next decade, OpenText is addressing nearer-term obligations while giving itself more time before a significant portion of the newly issued principal comes due.
The company also amended its revolving credit facility, primarily extending its maturity from December 19, 2028, to October 1, 2031, subject to the terms and conditions of the facility.
Together, the notes offering and revolving-credit amendment represent a significant refinancing initiative designed to reduce OpenText’s exposure to upcoming maturities in 2027 and 2028.
OpenText plans to use the net proceeds from the offering, together with cash on hand, primarily to redeem its entire $1 billion principal amount of 6.900% senior secured notes due in 2027.
The planned redemption includes the applicable premium, accrued and unpaid interest and other costs and expenses associated with retiring the securities.
Replacing the 2027 notes with debt maturing in 2031 and 2033 substantially extends the company’s repayment timetable.
The new notes carry coupons of 6.700% and 7.150%, compared with 6.900% on the securities being redeemed.
Because the new financing is divided evenly between the two tranches, OpenText has created a more staggered maturity structure rather than replacing the entire $1 billion obligation with another single maturity.
That can help reduce refinancing concentration by spreading future principal requirements across separate years.
OpenText also intends to use available proceeds to purchase up to $300 million in principal amount of its outstanding 3.875% senior notes due in 2028 through an existing tender offer.
The company expected to redeem the 2027 notes and settle the tender offer on October 2, 2026.
If the company purchases the full $300 million targeted under the tender offer, the transaction would further reduce the amount of debt approaching maturity over the next two years.
The refinancing therefore addresses both OpenText’s 2027 secured notes and a portion of its 2028 senior notes.
The strategy gives the company greater visibility into its debt obligations while shifting more of its capital structure toward maturities beginning in 2031.
OpenText’s amended revolving credit facility similarly pushes an important source of liquidity further out.
A revolving credit facility provides companies with flexible access to capital that can be borrowed, repaid and drawn again subject to the facility’s terms.
Extending its maturity through October 2031 reduces the risk that OpenText would need to renegotiate or replace the facility during the same period in which other debt obligations were approaching maturity.
The amendment can therefore provide additional financial flexibility alongside the new notes.
The newly issued securities are senior secured obligations.
They are guaranteed on a senior secured basis by OpenText subsidiaries that also guarantee or act as co-obligors under the company’s revolving credit facility, first-lien term loan facility and existing 2027 notes.
That structure gives holders of the new notes security interests consistent with other senior secured creditors covered by the company’s financing arrangements.
Senior secured debt generally ranks ahead of unsecured obligations on specified collateral, which can provide lenders with additional protection if a borrower faces financial difficulties.
For OpenText, secured financing can provide access to substantial long-term capital, but it also requires collateral to support the obligations.
Refinancing is particularly important because managing maturity schedules can help companies avoid large amounts of debt coming due in a concentrated period.
Rather than waiting until the 2027 notes approach maturity, OpenText is addressing the obligation ahead of time and replacing it with longer-dated capital.
This can reduce near-term refinancing risk and give management more flexibility in cash flow and capital allocation.
The tradeoff is that the company will continue carrying significant interest expense over an extended period.
While the 6.700% tranche carries a slightly lower coupon than the 6.900% notes being redeemed, the 7.150% tranche carries a higher rate.
The overall economics will also reflect the redemption premium, tender consideration and other transaction expenses.
Still, the primary objective appears to be extending maturities and improving the timing of OpenText’s debt obligations rather than simply reducing borrowing costs.
The refinancing comes as OpenText continues managing a capital structure associated with its position as a large enterprise software provider.
Software companies with recurring revenue models can often support meaningful debt balances because subscription and maintenance revenue may provide relatively predictable cash flows.
However, large debt obligations still require active management, particularly as maturities approach and interest-rate conditions change.
The current transaction allows OpenText to address those obligations proactively.
It also gives the company additional time to generate cash flow that can potentially be used for debt reduction, investment in its business or other corporate priorities before the new 2031 and 2033 maturities arrive.

candidates.title: Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years
candidates.snippet:
Amazon has announced a new community investment program that will add more than $1 billion in funding over the next five years to communities where the company operates data centers in the U.S.
The post Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years
Amazon has announced a new community investment program that will add more than $1 billion in funding over the next five years to communities where the company operates data centers in the U.S.
The initiative, called Built Together, is part of a broader set of commitments Amazon is making as investment in AI and cloud computing drives rapid construction of data center infrastructure across the country.
Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman said the company intends to direct the additional funding toward education, workforce development, energy affordability, water and energy conservation, and locally selected community priorities.
Under the education component, Amazon plans to support free community college and workforce training for residents living near its data center operations.
The company estimates that more than 300,000 students could gain access to certificate or associate degree programs over the next five years, with Amazon covering remaining out-of-pocket costs after financial aid.
Eligible areas of study are expected to include electrical work, HVAC, fiber optics, IT, healthcare, education, public safety, and advanced manufacturing.
Amazon is also expanding its Modular Training Center network. The company currently operates three centers, has six more under development, and plans to build 16 more.
Each center is designed to train approximately 2,000 to 4,000 people annually through certification programs lasting four to 16 weeks.
Amazon said that by the end of 2028, the expanded network could prepare as many as 100,000 workers annually for skilled jobs.
Built Together will also fund energy-efficiency improvements for schools, public buildings and homes in counties hosting Amazon data centers.
Amazon plans to support improvements at more than 300 schools and community buildings and more than 30,000 homes during the next five years.
Potential upgrades include HVAC systems, heat pumps, insulation, water heaters, batteries, and solar installations. Amazon estimates participating households could save approximately $700 annually on energy costs.
Amazon also said it has contracted for more than 65 water projects near its operations globally, expected to return more than 8 billion gallons of water annually to local communities.
The new investment framework will give local nonprofits, community foundations, and residents input on how Amazon deploys additional funding for priorities including roads, parks, affordable housing, fire department equipment, food security, and school improvements.
Alongside Built Together, Amazon introduced an Amazon Data Center Commitment outlining how it plans to develop and operate facilities.
The commitments include working with utilities to ensure data center electricity rates cover required energy and infrastructure improvements, eliminating nondisclosure agreements with government agencies involved in projects and holding community open houses.
Amazon also plans to publicly report data center energy use, energy efficiency, water use, water efficiency, and the percentage of power coming from carbon-free resources annually.
The company said new sites will use backup generators meeting the EPA’s Tier 4 emissions standard or equivalent standards outside the U.S.
Amazon reported a 2025 global Power Usage Effectiveness ratio of 1.14 for its data centers and said it was 75% of the way toward its goal of becoming water positive across its data center operations by 2030.
Amazon also said its average data center consumes less than 13,000 gallons of water per day, compared with approximately 170,000 gallons for what it described as a typical data center.
Over the past three years, Amazon said it has separately contributed more than $1 billion to U.S. communities where it maintains a meaningful data center presence.

Kahua Secures Bain Capital Growth Investment At Valuation Above $1 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Sep 30, 2026
Kahua Secures Bain Capital Growth Investment At Valuation Above $1 Billion
Kahua has secured a minority growth investment from Bain Capital’s Tech Opportunities business at a valuation above $1 billion, giving the construction technology company additional capital to accelerate its next stage of expansion.
The investment follows Kahua reaching $100 million in annualized revenue, a major milestone for the company’s AI-powered enterprise construction platform. Kahua plans to use the new capital to continue investing in artificial intelligence and product innovation, while expanding its go-to-market organization, customer success operations, and talent development initiatives.
Kahua is designed for organizations managing large and complex capital programs, particularly projects in which numerous stakeholders, workflows, and data sources must remain connected over multiple years. Its platform brings people, processes, and project data into a single, configurable, and governed environment, providing owners and delivery teams with a system of record spanning the asset lifecycle.
The company serves more than 2,500 customers across a range of industries and currently supports more than $400 billion in capital programs through its platform. Kahua said the governed data and operational context within the platform also provides a foundation for deploying AI directly within the workflows customers use to plan, manage, and make decisions about major assets and construction programs.
Kahua has focused heavily on highly regulated and mission-critical markets, including the federal government, defense, transportation, healthcare, and education sectors. The company also sees opportunities as capital spending increases across energy, digital infrastructure, data centers, and other large asset categories.
Many organizations overseeing these programs continue to operate through fragmented software systems and disconnected processes. Kahua’s strategy is to consolidate those workflows and associated information into a governed platform that can provide portfolio-level visibility and collaboration from initial funding and planning through construction and long-term operation.
The Bain Capital investment is expected to help Kahua further develop AI capabilities that can operate using the project data, permissions, and context already contained within its platform. The companies also plan to invest in broader product development and commercial expansion as Kahua grows across industries and markets.
Bain Capital Tech Opportunities invests in growing technology companies and will bring experience scaling enterprise software businesses to the partnership. Parent firm Bain Capital, founded in 1984, operates across private equity, growth and venture investing, capital solutions, credit and real assets. Bain Capital has approximately $225 billion in assets under management, more than 2,000 employees, and 24 offices across four continents.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’ve spent years building Kahua into the system organizations rely on to run their most complex programs, and this investment validates that work.”
Scott Unger, CEO and Co-Founder of Kahua

Philip Meicler, Partner at Bain Capital Tech Opportunities

candidates.text:
Vintage Investment Partners Raises $920 Million, Increasing AUM To More Than $4.8 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Vintage Investment Partners Raises $920 Million, Increasing AUM To More Than $4.8 Billion
Vintage Investment Partners has raised $920 million in new capital, increasing the global venture investment platform’s assets under management to more than $4.8 billion.
The capital will expand Vintage’s ability to invest in venture funds and venture-backed companies through primary, secondary, and co-investment strategies. The firm is focused exclusively on venture capital and invests through relationships with venture managers across the U.S., Europe, and Israel.
Vintage said the new capital comes as technology companies are remaining private for longer periods, resulting in a greater share of their value being created before an eventual public listing or exit. The firm also sees artificial intelligence contributing to the formation and growth of a new generation of technology companies that are reaching significant scale while remaining privately held.
The fundraising also comes as venture capital becomes increasingly concentrated among a relatively small number of investment firms. Citing the Q2 2026 PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, Vintage noted that three firms accounted for nearly half of all venture capital raised during the first half of 2026.
Vintage has raised more than $1.1 billion over the past three years across its primary, secondary, and co-investment strategies. The firm said the expanded capital base will allow it to support venture managers, portfolio companies, and investors while addressing increasing demand for liquidity across private markets.
Founded in 2003, Vintage maintains offices in Tel Aviv, London, and New York. Its investment platform combines relationships with venture managers and companies with proprietary data covering thousands of venture funds and businesses.
The firm operates Fund of Funds, Secondaries, and Growth investment strategies, providing institutional investors with multiple ways to gain exposure to venture capital markets. Vintage also operates Value+, a value creation platform connecting companies in its ecosystem with a network of more than 650 global enterprises. According to Vintage, those connections have generated hundreds of millions of dollars in commercial opportunities.
Alongside the fundraising, Vintage announced several leadership changes. Tzlil Kovetz has been promoted to Partner after more than five years with the firm, progressing from Associate through the organization.
Chief Value Officer Ilan Leiferman has also been promoted to Partner. Leiferman leads the firm’s Value+ platform. Vintage additionally appointed Brachie Sprung as Chief Investor Relations Officer, bringing approximately two decades of experience spanning venture capital, fundraising, investor relations, and strategic communications.
Vintage’s existing partner group includes Co-Managing Partners Asaf Horesh and Abe Finkelstein, along with Amit Frenkel, Iren Reznikov, and Leyla Holterud.
KEY QUOTES:
“More value is being created in private markets, over shorter timelines, than at any point in the history of venture. In a moment like this, one thing hasn’t changed, it’s only become more decisive: many of the most successful founders continue to partner with a relatively small group of highly sought-after venture managers. That is exactly where we invest, and earning a seat with them is the hardest, most important work we do. With more than $1.1 billion raised over the past three years across primary, secondary and co-investment strategies, we can support fund managers, companies and investors in more ways, while helping address the growing demand for liquidity across the venture ecosystem.”
Asaf Horesh, Co-Managing Partner At Vintage Investment Partners
“We are deeply grateful to our LPs for the trust they continue to place in Vintage. By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
Ernst & Young Wins Two Defense Audit Contracts Worth Up To $869.4 Million
Ernst & Young LLP was awarded two contracts by the Defense Finance and Accounting Service with a combined maximum potential value of approximately $869.4 million for financial statement audit services covering major U.S. military funds.
The larger award is a labor-hour contract with a maximum value of $455.43 million for financial statement audit services supporting the Department of War Office of Inspector General.
Under that contract, Ernst & Young will perform audits of the Navy General Fund, Marine Corps General Fund, and Department of Navy Working Capital Fund for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
The work will be performed primarily in Tysons, Virginia, along with additional locations inside and outside the continental United States.
The contract includes a one-year base period and four individual one-year option periods, with an expected completion date of December 31, 2031.
Subject to the availability of funding, approximately $96.53 million in fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance funds is expected to be obligated before performance begins.
The award resulted from a competitive acquisition in which the government received one quote.
The Defense Finance and Accounting Service Contract Services Directorate in Columbus, Ohio, is the contracting activity.
Separately, Ernst & Young was awarded a second labor-hour contract with a maximum value of $413.95 million for audit services covering the Department of the Air Force General Fund and Working Capital Fund financial statements.
Work under the Air Force contract will be performed in McLean, Virginia.
The contract has a 12-month base period plus four individual one-year option periods.
The government listed an expected completion date of December 31, 2027 for the award.
Subject to funding availability, approximately $58.78 million in fiscal 2027 Air Force operations and maintenance funding will be obligated.
That contract also resulted from a competitive acquisition in which one quote was received.
Combined, the two awards provide Ernst & Young with potential contract value of approximately $869.38 million.
The engagements cover financial statement auditing across the Navy, Marine Corps, Department of Navy Working Capital Fund, and Air Force, expanding Ernst & Young’s role in supporting financial oversight across major U.S. defense organizations.

candidates.text:
ENERGYRE CLOSES $815 MILLION FINANCING PACKAGE -ONE OF THE LARGEST SOLAR-ONLY FINANCING DEALS IN SOUTH CAROLINA HISTORY
News provided by
energyRe
Oct 12, 2026, 10:52 ET
Share this article
Share this article
energyRe Logo
Transaction Advances energyRe's 1.8+ Gigawatt Solar Portfolio; Brings Total Funds Raised to more than $1.9 Billion
HOUSTON , Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- energyRe today announced the successful closing of an $815 million financing package for five projects based in South Carolina – a collection of utility-scale solar projects totaling approximately 360 megawatts (MW) of new generating capacity across the Palmetto State. The financing is a giant step toward the company's goal of investing $2 billion in South Carolina by 2030. The $815 million transaction represents one of the largest solar-only project financing deals in South Carolina's history, underscoring the state's emergence as a hub for large-scale energy development.
"This portfolio financing is our largest to date, and it reflects the confidence our lenders have in both the quality of our assets and our team's ability to deliver," said Pedro Pereira, Chief Financial Officer of energyRe . "South Carolina is at the center of our growth strategy, and this closing moves us meaningfully closer to our goal of investing $2 billion in the state by 2030. These projects will create jobs during construction and operations and deliver affordable, reliable power to South Carolina homes and businesses for decades to come."
The financing was supported by Bank of America, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Santander, with Bank of America serving as documentation agent and Santander serving as financial advisor to energyRe. The deal marks a significant milestone in energyRe's commitment to delivering reliable and affordable energy to the communities it serves.
The transaction covers five solar projects across South Carolina that are contracted under 25-year power purchase agreements and will provide tens of millions in revenue for local governments.
The financing was structured and executed by energyRe's M&A and Capital Markets team, led by Surya Mohan, working alongside Santander and the company's lending and tax equity partners.
"This financing secures the capital to advance these projects and demonstrates energyRe's ability to finance its development portfolio at scale," said Surya Mohan, Senior Vice President, M&A and Capital Markets at energyRe. "I'm proud of our M&A and Capital Markets team for leading this transaction, and grateful to our lenders, tax equity partner, advisors and colleagues across energyRe for the work that brought it together."
energyRe has broken ground on approximately 450 MW in the last year and has nearly 700 MW in operation or late-stage development. The company's 1.8+ GW portfolio spans 20 projects in South Carolina, North Carolina, Nebraska and Oklahoma. Combined with previous financing packages, energyRe has raised more than $1.9 billion in support of its solar project portfolio to date.
"Santander is pleased to have advised on and financed a landmark transaction that will serve as a cornerstone for energyRe's and South Carolina's clean energy portfolio," said Nuno Andrade, Head of North America Structured Finance and Global Head of Digital Structured Finance for Santander's Corporate & Investment Bank . "Santander's leading position in renewable energy financing supported energyRe's ability to execute this transaction."
"CIBC is proud to have supported energyRe as it advances its utility-scale solar portfolio in South Carolina, expanding critical energy infrastructure and helping drive the transition to a more reliable and sustainable power system," said Ines Serrao, Managing Director and Head of U.S. Project Finance & Infrastructure, CIBC .
"We are proud to support energyRe's portfolio of solar projects across South Carolina, which demonstrates how public and private capital can work together to expand energy resources. This transaction reflects the type of investment our $250 billion Critical Infrastructure Finance Initiative was created to advance," said Omer Farooq, Head of Asset Finance within the Global Sustainable & Infrastructure Finance Group at Bank of America .
About energyRe
energyRe is an American-led energy company created to develop innovative infrastructure projects that meet rising electricity demand with affordable and reliable energy. Our company portfolio combines generation, transmission and storage with a "community first" approach to project development, bringing together industry-leading expertise and local know-how. Learn more at www.energyre.com .

SINGAPORE and AMSTERDAM , Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Euronext Amsterdam-listed SWI Group ("SWI"; SWICH) today announces an €800 million capital increase with institutional investors.
The capital increase is realized through the issuance of new ordinary shares by SWICH in several series, increasing the total share capital to 558,399,385 ordinary shares. This increases the total equity raised since March 2026 to over €1 billion.
The transaction marks a major milestone in SWI Group's transformation, providing substantial additional equity capital to accelerate the consolidation and expansion of its transatlantic digital infrastructure and AI compute platform across Europe and the United States.
As part of the transformation announced by the Group, the proceeds will support the development and scaling of the Group's data center and AI compute capacity, including power infrastructure, compute deployments and the execution of its development pipeline on both sides of the Atlantic.
The capital increase materially strengthens SWI Group's balance sheet and provides the Group with additional financial capacity to execute its growth strategy at scale, including further investment into AI and increasing its stake in existing investments. It also broadens its institutional shareholder base while enhancing market liquidity and increasing the Company's free float to approximately 20% of the share capital.
"This transaction is about keeping up to speed with the compute and data center markets. We have a clear strategy, a substantial pipeline and a strong position across Europe and the United States. We are very pleased to welcome new investors who share our long-term ambition for the Group," said Max-Hervé George, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of SWI Group .
As part of the transaction, certain investors are granted options in relation to their shares conditional on ECM milestones.

SWI Capital Holding Ltd. ( www.swi.com ), listed on Euronext Amsterdam under the ticker SWICH (ISIN: SGXPZ11CH7U7), is the holding company of the SWI Group. candidates.title: US Startup Funding Cools, but Modal Labs’ $750 Million Round Shows AI Still Commands Big Money

US Startup Funding Cools, but Modal Labs’ $750 Million Round Shows AI Still Commands Big Money
Epil Bodra
| October 17 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Only two US startups raised $200 million or more during October 10-16, even as major investments in AI infrastructure, construction technology and biotechnology kept venture capital activity moving.
The biggest venture capital deals in the United States became less frequent during the week of October 10-16, but investors were still willing to commit substantial sums to companies operating in high-demand technology sectors.
New York-based AI infrastructure company Modal Labs dominated the week’s funding activity, raising $750 million in a Series D round that valued the business at $15.75 billion. The investment was comfortably ahead of other announced transactions, with construction technology company Icon taking second place after securing $200 million.
The gap between the two deals was striking. Only two funding rounds reached the $200 million mark during the period, according to Crunchbase’s ranking of announced investments in US-based startups.
Modal Labs Leads Weekly US Startup Funding With $750 Million Series D
Modal Labs emerged as the clear leader in the latest US startup funding rankings after completing a $750 million Series D round led by Accel.
The financing placed the company’s valuation at $15.75 billion, making it the largest announced US startup investment tracked by Crunchbase for the week.
The funding comes alongside a significant revenue milestone. Modal Labs said its annual revenue run rate had recently surpassed $1 billion, an indication of the scale at which its AI infrastructure business is operating.
That figure is a measure of revenue at an annualised pace rather than confirmed revenue collected over a completed financial year.
Nevertheless, it provides important context for a financing round of this size.
Modal Labs’ position at the top of the weekly rankings also reflects the considerable sums investors are prepared to commit to businesses supporting AI infrastructure, even during a quieter period for exceptionally large venture deals.
Icon Secures $200 Million as Construction Automation Attracts Investors
While artificial intelligence produced the largest deal, construction technology accounted for the second-biggest investment.
Austin-based Icon, known for its work in 3D-printed homes, raised $200 million in a Series D financing round led by Baillie Gifford and BlackRock.
The company said it was on track to achieve fourfold revenue growth in 2026, providing a business backdrop to the new investment.
Icon’s funding demonstrates that substantial venture capital commitments are extending beyond conventional software and AI businesses. Its work in automated construction places it in a different segment of the technology market, where physical infrastructure and industrial processes are central to the business.
Biotechnology Startups Secure More Than $200 Million Across Two Deals
Biotechnology also featured among the week’s largest fundraising announcements, with Soufflé Therapeutics and Estuary Biotherapeutics attracting significant capital.
Soufflé Therapeutics secured $135 million through a Series B round led by Juvia Group.
Estuary Biotherapeutics, meanwhile, launched with $103 million in financing. That amount included a $93 million Series A led by RA Capital Management and $10 million in previously undisclosed seed funding.
The distinction matters because Estuary’s announced financing was not entirely new Series A capital. The $103 million figure includes both its latest investment round and earlier seed backing.
Together, the two biotechnology companies accounted for $238 million in disclosed financing, keeping the sector among the prominent recipients of venture funding during the period.
AI Software Investment Continues Beyond Modal Labs
The week’s activity in artificial intelligence was not limited to infrastructure.
Labelbox secured $100 million in Series E funding led by Infinitum Partners, while Suki announced a $90 million Series E involving investors including Healthier Capital and Crosslink Capital.
North.cloud also joined the funding rankings with a $60 million Series B led by PeakSpan Capital.
These investments point to continued venture capital interest across different parts of the AI-related business landscape. Modal Labs accounted for the largest individual transaction, but other software-focused companies were also able to attract sizable financing rounds.
Healthcare, Insurance and Semiconductor Firms Join Funding Rankings
Several businesses outside the week’s largest AI and biotechnology deals also secured substantial backing.
Abby Care raised $82 million in a Series C round led by Transformation Capital, reflecting investor interest in home care services.
Insurance startup Stand completed a $70 million Series C led by Saga Ventures, with the financing valuing the company at $1 billion.
In semiconductor infrastructure, Mueon raised $65 million through a Series A led by Maverick Silicon. The company is developing a modular platform aimed at AI and hyperscale computing.
The inclusion of these businesses adds breadth to the week’s funding picture. Capital reached companies involved in healthcare delivery, insurance and computing infrastructure, alongside the better-funded AI and biotechnology sectors.
What the Latest US Startup Funding Numbers Reveal
The October 10-16 funding rankings illustrate a market in which exceptionally large deals were limited, rather than one in which major investment activity had disappeared.
Modal Labs alone raised more than three times the amount secured by Icon, the second-largest recipient. That concentration is particularly notable because the week’s remaining announced deals were all below $200 million.
At the same time, the distribution of investments across multiple industries suggests that venture capital activity was not confined to a single technology

The Islamic Development Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development have signed a new Cooperation and Co-financing Agreement aimed at mobilizing up to $750 million for sustainable agricultural development, food systems, and rural transformation.

candidates.text:
IsDB And IFAD Aim To Mobilize $750 Million For Food Systems And Rural Transformation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
IsDB And IFAD Aim To Mobilize $750 Million For Food Systems And Rural Transformation
The Islamic Development Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development have signed a new Cooperation and Co-financing Agreement aimed at mobilizing up to $750 million for sustainable agricultural development, food systems, and rural transformation.
The expanded partnership will combine the institutions’ financing capabilities, development expertise, and international reach to support investments designed to strengthen food security, reduce poverty, and create economic opportunities in rural communities across their common member countries.
IsDB and IFAD are developing a joint action plan that will translate the agreement into individual investments. Priority areas include agribusiness value chains, market access, rural finance and financial inclusion, climate adaptation, sustainable natural resource management, and water access.
The agreement is also expected to expand opportunities for private-sector investment supporting agribusinesses and rural small and medium-sized enterprises. The organizations plan to combine different forms of development and commercial financing to support projects across the food and agricultural economy.
The wider IsDB Group will participate through affiliates including the Islamic Corporation for the Development of the Private Sector, the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation, and the Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit. The approach is intended to combine development finance, trade finance, investment, and risk mitigation capabilities.
The new agreement expands a relationship between IsDB and IFAD that dates back to 1980. Since then, the organizations have jointly financed 29 projects with a combined value of approximately $1.45 billion.
The additional $750 million mobilization target represents a significant expansion of that collaboration and is intended to increase the scale of investments addressing agricultural productivity, rural livelihoods, market connectivity, and resilience.
KEY QUOTES:
“This renewed partnership between IsDB and IFAD builds on nearly five decades of successful cooperation. Together, we will leverage our collective expertise and resources to strengthen resilience, expand opportunities, and improve the lives of rural communities across our member countries.”
Dr. Muhammad Al Jasser, Chairman Of The IsDB Group
“Through this agreement, we are scaling up investment in the first mile of food systems to create jobs, increase incomes and build more prosperous and resilient rural economies. When rural people have the opportunity to build businesses, connect to markets, and earn a decent living, the benefits extend far beyond rural areas.”
Alvaro Lario, President Of IFAD

DCC Energy Sells Nexora To One Equity Partners For $725 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
DCC Energy Sells Nexora To One Equity Partners For $725 Million
DCC Energy agreed to sell its technology division, Nexora, to investment subsidiaries of funds managed or advised by One Equity Partners for an enterprise value of $725 million, cash-free and debt-free. The transaction is subject to customary regulatory approvals and is expected to close on or after March 1, 2027.
Nexora operates a group of specialist technology businesses connecting technology brands with customers across workplaces, classrooms, live entertainment, digital infrastructure, and the home.
The company said One Equity Partners will become its new owner and investment partner, providing a platform to accelerate growth and invest further in its people and capabilities.
Nexora also expects the partnership to create additional opportunities for its customers, vendor partners, and employees.
The divestiture comes as DCC Energy moves toward its previously announced acquisition by Dragon Bidco, a company indirectly owned by funds and investment vehicles advised by Energy Capital Partners and KKR.
DCC Energy and Dragon Bidco announced that acquisition on July 27, 2026, and DCC Energy shareholders approved the transaction scheme on September 18.
Under the acquisition terms, DCC Energy shareholders are entitled to receive 6,525 pence in cash per share plus potential additional consideration of as much as 125 pence per share if specified conditions related to the Nexora disposal are satisfied or waived before July 31, 2027.
Based on an assumed March 1, 2027 completion date and no specified leakage before closing, DCC Energy currently expects the Nexora transaction to generate approximately $701 million in net proceeds.
That would result in estimated additional consideration of 42 pence per DCC Energy share. The final amount will be determined after the Nexora sale closes.
If the applicable disposal conditions are not satisfied or waived by July 31, 2027, no additional consideration related to the Nexora sale would be payable to DCC Energy shareholders.
DCC Energy said Nexora has developed a strong market position during its time within the group and credited the company’s employees with contributing to its growth.
Nexora CEO Clive Fitzharris is leading the business into its next phase under One Equity Partners.
One Equity Partners is a middle-market private equity firm focused on the industrial, healthcare, and technology sectors across North America and Europe.
The firm was founded in 2001, spun out of J.P. Morgan in 2015, and has completed more than 500 transactions worldwide. It operates offices in New York, Chicago, Frankfurt, and Amsterdam. Cons…
Jefferies International is serving as sole financial advisor to DCC Energy on the Nexora divestiture, while Hogan Lovells is acting as English legal advisor.

“Nexora has been an important part of the DCC Group for many years and has built a strong market position through the expertise and commitment of its people. As it begins this next chapter, we would like to thank our colleagues across Nexora for their contribution to DCC Energy and wish them every success for the future.
This transaction recognizes the quality of the business that the Nexora team has built and, subject to completion, will deliver additional value for DCC Energy shareholders. We believe One Equity Partners is well placed to support Nexora’s continued growth, investment and long-term development, benefiting employees and customers alike.”
Donal Murphy, Chief Executive of DCC Energy

candidates.text:
Leslie’s Files Chapter 11 To Cut Debt By About $685 Million And Secure $150 Million In New Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
Leslie’s Files Chapter 11 To Cut Debt By About $685 Million And Secure $150 Million In New Capital
Leslie’s has entered into a restructuring support agreement with a group representing more than 80% of its existing lenders and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as the pool and spa retailer seeks to substantially reduce its debt and strengthen its financial position.
The restructuring is expected to eliminate approximately $685 million, or 90%, of Leslie’s outstanding funded debt.
The agreement also includes commitments for $150 million of new capital, consisting of $90 million of new-money debtor-in-possession financing and $60 million of equity financing. Certain parties to the restructuring agreement fully backstop the equity investment.
Leslie’s has filed voluntary petitions for prearranged Chapter 11 proceedings in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas.
The company expects to emerge from Chapter 11 in early 2027 and anticipates that a group of its existing lenders will hold majority ownership following the restructuring.
Leslie’s said the transaction is intended to provide a deleveraged balance sheet, additional liquidity and greater financial flexibility to reinvest in its operations and customer experience.
The company is also reducing its physical retail footprint. Leslie’s announced the closure of 76 stores and said all remaining locations outside of stores that were recently closed will remain open and operational.
The retailer plans to continue evaluating its real estate portfolio during the Chapter 11 process to better align its store network with customer demand and its long-term business strategy.
Leslie’s said stores and digital operations will continue serving customers throughout the restructuring. The company is seeking court authorization to continue paying employee wages and benefits, maintain customer programs and honor vendor obligations.
Gift cards and loyalty program benefits will continue to be honored.
In addition to the $90 million new-money DIP facility, Leslie’s is seeking approval for a fully committed $225 million DIP asset-based financing facility from its existing ABL lenders.
The company said the financing arrangements are expected to provide sufficient liquidity to operate through the Chapter 11 process.
Support: Simpson Thacher & Bartlett and Haynes and Boone are serving as legal advisers. BRG is serving as financial and restructuring adviser, Centerview Partners is serving as investment banker and C Street Advisory Group is serving as strategic communications adviser. Hilco Global has been retained to assist Leslie’s with its real estate portfolio.
KEY QUOTES:
“Today’s announcement marks an important milestone in our commitment to our customers and our business. With a stronger balance sheet and greater financial flexibility, Leslie’s can reinvest across the business to strengthen operating execution and deliver an even better experience for our customers, both in-store and online. Leslie’s is here to stay, and I am deeply grateful to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support as we work to position Leslie’s for a strong future.”
Jason McDonell, Chief Executive Officer of Leslie’s

Oct 14, 2026
Accelevation Secures $650 Million Credit Agreement Led By Bank Of America, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, KeyBank And PNC
Accelevation Holdings entered into a new $650 million senior secured credit agreement that replaces credit facilities established before the company’s initial public offering and provides additional financial flexibility to support its long-term growth strategy.
The financing consists of a $400 million revolving credit facility and a $250 million Term Loan A, both of which mature in 2031. The facilities are currently priced at Term SOFR plus 1.50% to 2.50%, representing a substantial reduction from the company’s previous borrowing rate of SOFR plus 4.50% to 5.25%.
Accelevation said the new financing strengthens its balance sheet, extends its maturity profile, lowers borrowing costs, and gives the company additional flexibility to invest in its operations and pursue strategic priorities. The refinancing follows Accelevation’s transition to the public equity markets and comes as the company operates with a lower level of debt.
Bank of America served as administrative agent and collateral agent. BofA Securities, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, KeyBank National Association, and PNC Capital Markets served as joint lead arrangers. BofA Securities and JPMorgan Chase Bank also served as joint bookrunners.
Accelevation designs, manufactures, and installs customized structural, electrical, and mechanical systems for mission-critical infrastructure, combining U.S.-based manufacturing with nationwide field service capabilities.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased to announce the closing of these new facilities, which strengthen our balance sheet and enhance our financial flexibility as we continue to execute our growth strategy. As we transition to the public equity market with a lower level of debt, it was important to access more cost-efficient capital. The new facilities extend our maturity profile, reduce our borrowing costs, and provide flexibility to continue investing in our business. We believe this capital structure positions us well to support our customers and execute our long-term strategic priorities.”
Ken Krause, Chief Financial Officer of Accelevation

By Amit Chowdhry

Pagaya Closes $650 Million Auto ABS Deal, Marking 100th Securitization
Pagaya Technologies closed RPM 2026-5, a $650 million asset-backed securitization backed by auto loans, marking the company’s 100th ABS transaction since completing its first securitization in 2018.
The milestone brings Pagaya’s lifetime ABS issuance to more than $44 billion across multiple consumer asset classes.

Pagaya has built its securitization program around a broader capital markets platform that combines long-term committed capital with diversified funding sources.

Pagaya uses machine learning, a large data network, and AI-driven underwriting technologies to support consumer credit products for financial institutions, their customers, and investors.
Its proprietary API and capital solutions are integrated into partner platforms to support loan decisioning and access to financial products.
The company’s 100th securitization represents another milestone in the expansion of its capital markets business since launching its ABS program eight years ago.

candidates.text:
Dwight Capital And Dwight Investment Management Close $607 Million In Seniors Housing Financings During Q3 2026
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Dwight Capital And Dwight Investment Management Close $607 Million In Seniors Housing Financings During Q3 2026
Dwight Capital and its affiliate, Dwight Investment Management, completed $607 million in seniors housing financings during the third quarter of 2026, supporting skilled nursing facilities, assisted living communities, and other healthcare real estate assets across 17 states. The transactions included HUD-insured loans, bridge financings, and revolving lines of credit (RLOCs), reflecting the firms’ continued activity in the seniors housing and healthcare financing markets.
Among the largest transactions was a $71.25 million bridge loan supporting a four-property, 646-bed skilled nursing portfolio spanning Montana and Colorado. The financing was used to acquire two facilities in the Denver metropolitan area and complete cash-out refinancings of two existing properties in Montana.
The loan features a 30-month term, a six-month extension option, and provisions for future funding. The borrower intends to increase occupancy and implement operational improvements at the newly acquired Colorado facilities before pursuing permanent financing for the portfolio. Josh Levin originated the transaction.
Another major financing involved $52 million in HUD Section 232/223(f) loans for a five-property, 577-bed skilled nursing portfolio in Arkansas. The loans will refinance existing debt, including acquisition financing associated with the sponsor’s December 2025 purchase of the facilities.
The Arkansas financing features a 35-year, fully amortizing structure, providing the borrower with long-term financing for the portfolio. Adam Offman and Yossi Benish originated the loans.
Dwight also completed several significant bridge financing transactions involving skilled nursing properties in Ohio. These included a $54.5 million bridge refinancing for a 583-bed skilled nursing portfolio, accompanied by a $9 million revolving line of credit.
Another Ohio transaction involved a $46.5 million bridge acquisition loan for a 290-bed skilled nursing facility, together with an $8.5 million revolving line of credit.
Additional transactions included a $25 million bridge refinancing for a 234-bed skilled nursing facility in Bedford, Ohio, and a $17 million bridge refinancing for a 130-bed facility in Cleveland, accompanied by a $2.5 million revolving line of credit.
Beyond skilled nursing facilities, Dwight provided an $11.4 million bridge acquisition loan for a 351-bed assisted living portfolio located in Ohio and Minnesota.
The firms also maintained substantial activity in the HUD-insured lending market during the quarter. Notable transactions included $47.2 million across four HUD Section 232/223(f) loans for a four-property, 379-bed skilled nursing portfolio in Illinois.
Additional HUD-insured financings included a $26.9 million loan for a 170-bed skilled nursing facility in New Jersey, a $26.3 million loan for a 156-bed facility in New Hampshire, and a $23.3 million loan for a 280-bed skilled nursing facility in New York.
Dwight also completed an $18.4 million HUD Section 232/223(f) loan for a 151-bed skilled nursing facility in the southeastern United States.
The range of transactions demonstrates the firms’ ability to provide financing solutions for different stages of healthcare real estate ownership, including acquisitions, refinancing, operating improvements, and transitions from short-term debt to permanent financing.
Bridge loans can provide borrowers with financing flexibility while they execute operational improvements or prepare properties for longer-term financing. HUD-insured loans, meanwhile, can offer extended repayment periods and fully amortizing structures that support long-term property ownership.
Dwight Capital provides commercial real estate financing through balance-sheet bridge loans, new construction loans, FHA/HUD-insured loans, C-PACE financing, mezzanine debt, and preferred equity. The company services a loan portfolio exceeding $17 billion across its affiliates.
Dwight Investment Management, formerly known as Dwight Securities Management, is an SEC-registered investment adviser specializing in commercial real estate credit. The firm manages funds and accounts focused on private credit strategies, using proprietary deal sourcing, institutional underwriting, and active asset management.
Working alongside Dwight Capital’s HUD lending and servicing platform, Dwight Investment Management sources, underwrites, and closes commercial real estate loans nationwide.
The $607 million in third-quarter financings highlights the firms’ continued involvement in providing capital to seniors housing operators and investors, supporting acquisitions, debt restructuring, and long-term financing needs across the healthcare real estate sector.

Angle Health Raises $600 Million at a $2.7 Billion Valuation to Continue Expanding Affordable Healthcare Access for Small Businesses
October 1, 2026
Healthcare IT News
6 Min Read
Healthcare IT News
Share This!
Facebook X Pinterest LinkedIn
Since Launching in 2021, Angle Health has Emerged as the Leading Alternative to Traditional Health Insurance Plans for Small Businesses Nationwide, Now Serving More than 5,000 Employers, Offering Customized Health Plans in 47 States, and Delivering Four Consecutive Quarters of Profitability
Angle Health , the first AI-native healthcare benefits platform, today announced a $600 million equity financing at a $2.7 billion valuation, consisting of a $200 million Series C financing and a $400 million tender offer. The round, led by Vitruvian Partners with participation from new investor Town Hall Ventures and existing investors Blumberg Capital, Portage Ventures, PruVen Capital, and Y Combinator, is expected to close later this month.
The announcement comes at a time when employers are facing the largest increase in health insurance costs in two decades . Small and midsize businesses are hit especially hard, with limited options that are costly, confusing, and difficult for employees to navigate, or simply unaffordable. This dynamic impacts a growing number of Americans as the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics has consistently reported small business employment growth outpacing that of larger businesses, a trend that is poised to accelerate as AI breaks down barriers to entrepreneurship.
“Access to great healthcare shouldn’t depend on the size of the company you work for,” said Ty Wang, Co-Founder and CEO at Angle Health. “Small businesses employ tens of millions of Americans, yet they have historically had the least options available to them for healthcare coverage and almost no control over its costs. We built Angle Health to fix that. This financing enables us to reach more of the local businesses that power our country and continue to deliver a personalized, higher-quality, more affordable healthcare experience to everyday Americans. We are particularly excited to partner with Vitruvian, as we specifically sought out a group with deep expertise at the intersection of healthcare, technology, and financial services and a proven track record of successfully scaling companies through growth-oriented partnerships.”
By combining a modern, AI-driven technology platform with an integrated approach to local, personalized healthcare access, Angle Health enables employers with as few as two employees to offer their employees sophisticated, customized benefits and personalized healthcare journeys, improving experiences and outcomes across the ecosystem. Employers choosing Angle Health benefit from increased choice, transparency, and stability. Their employees have access to an expanding suite of AI-powered navigation and targeted clinical capabilities, facilitating healthier, lower-cost, and more satisfied plan members, while concurrently removing administrative friction for the clinicians serving those members. The company’s Benefit Builder platform brings unprecedented transparency to group underwriting, allowing brokers to generate firm, underwritten quotes in minutes, customize plans in real time, and access the industry’s first-of-its-kind Health Scorecard. Today, the company serves over 5,000 employers with customizable plans available in 47 states.
“Angle Health has replaced the archaic systems and manual workflows of a century-old industry with a healthcare platform built for the AI-era,” said Jeremy Gelber, Partner at Vitruvian. “Its combination of technology, industry-leading growth and retention, and financial stability in an increasingly volatile market is proof that the team at Angle Health has built something truly needed. At Vitruvian, we focus on aligning capital with change, so we are thrilled for the opportunity to help Angle Health scale its impact and expand access to high-quality healthcare for working Americans.”
Building From a Position of Strength
Angle Health enters its next phase from a position of financial strength, with 120% year-over-year growth and four consecutive quarters of EBITDA and GAAP net income profitability. Angle Health now serves over 5,000 employers with nearly $1 billion in annualized premium-equivalents. Angle Health’s renewal pricing is consistently below market benchmarks, helping drive strong customer retention. This financing comes less than 10 months after announcing its Series B financing.
The capital will support Angle Health’s long-term strategy and mission to reimagine healthcare access in America by challenging the traditionally opaque, expensive, and disjointed experience offered by legacy insurers. Angle is investing in rebuilding the underlying infrastructure and pathways to care, making it easier for Americans to access high-quality treatment while helping businesses better manage healthcare costs. This includes continued investment in its AI-native technology platform and seamless navigation across hyper-local, condition-specific care options, creating greater transparency and a better experience for brokers, employers, employees, and the clinicians who serve them.
Continued Momentum
Beyond its financial and business performance, Angle Health continues to expand its ability to deliver more affordable, high-quality healthcare while helping employers manage rising costs. The company has launched care delivery programs with best-in-class partners to provide lower-cost, high-quality access to services including high-cost medications, infusions, outpatient surgery, and radiology. Angle Health has also delivered some of the most stable health plan renewal rates in the market, with median year-over-year rate increases of just 5-7%, compared with a median increase of 18% for SMBs .
These milestones reinforce Angle Health’s progress toward building a more efficient, affordable, and accessible healthcare experience f

Gray Media Closes $600 Million Term Loan And Extends $680 Million Revolver
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Gray Media Closes $600 Million Term Loan And Extends $680 Million Revolver
Gray Media closed a new $600 million Term Loan G and extended the maturity of its revolving credit facility as part of a broader refinancing program affecting more than $1.25 billion of debt. The new term loan matures July 15, 2030.
It was priced at 350 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate and issued at a 0.5% original issue discount.
Gray also reduced its existing $750 million revolving credit facility to $680 million.
The revolver’s maturity was extended from December 1, 2028 to July 15, 2030.
Proceeds from Term Loan G were used to repay part of Gray’s Term Loan D due December 1, 2028.
Following the repayment, approximately $150 million of Term Loan D remains outstanding.
The refinancing follows Gray’s August 2026 issuance of $750 million of 7.5% senior secured first-lien notes due 2034.
Proceeds from that issuance were used in part to repay $675 million of 10.5% first-lien notes due 2029.
Gray said the transactions collectively extended maturities on more than $1.25 billion of debt and lowered overall borrowing costs.
The company now has no material debt maturities until after both the 2026 and 2028 political election cycles.
Its nearest maturities are the remaining $150 million of Term Loan D due in December 2028 and $350 million of notes due in July 2029.

candidates.snippet:

The post Blue Bird Secures $600 Million Credit Facility Led By BMO And Bank Of America appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Blue Bird Secures $600 Million Credit Facility Led By BMO And Bank Of America
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Blue Bird Secures $600 Million Credit Facility Led By BMO And Bank Of America
Blue Bird has completed a $600 million senior secured credit facility refinancing that more than doubles its committed borrowing capacity and extends its debt maturity to September 2031.
The new financing replaces Blue Bird’s previous $250 million credit facilities, which were scheduled to mature in November 2028.
The refinancing consists of a $300 million revolving credit facility and a $300 million delayed draw term loan.
Borrowings under the delayed draw term loan are available for up to 24 months after closing or until the entire $300 million has been drawn.
Blue Bird can use the term loan to refinance existing debt and primarily fund capital projects, research and development and working capital.
At closing, the school bus manufacturer had approximately $86 million of carry-over debt drawn under the new facilities and more than $670 million of available liquidity.
The refinancing also reduces Blue Bird’s borrowing costs.
The interest-rate margin is now SOFR plus 1.25% to 2.25%, depending on leverage, compared with SOFR plus 1.75% to 3.25% under the previous facilities.
The agreement also eliminates the prior 0.10% credit spread adjustment.
Blue Bird’s maximum total net leverage ratio increases to 3.25 times, with a temporary 0.50-times step-up for four quarters after a qualifying acquisition of at least $75 million.
The accordion feature has also been expanded to the greater of $250 million or one times trailing 12-month EBITDA, with additional capacity available subject to a leverage test.
BMO served as administrative agent, joint lead arranger and joint bookrunner.
Bank of America served as syndication agent, joint lead arranger and joint bookrunner.
CIBC Bank USA, Fifth Third Bank, Regions Bank and TD Bank also served as joint lead arrangers and joint bookrunners.
KEY QUOTES:
“While Blue Bird already has a very strong balance sheet, this refinancing more than doubles our available borrowing capacity, lowers our cost of debt and extends maturity out to 2031. It gives us the flexibility to continue to invest in our operations and product development, while maintaining a conservative balance sheet. We appreciate the strong support from our bank group, led by BMO.”
Razvan Radulescu, Chief Financial Officer of Blue Bird

Penguin Solutions: Q4 Revenue Jumps 68% To Record $567 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Penguin Solutions: Q4 Revenue Jumps 68% To Record $567 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
Penguin Solutions reported record fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net sales of $566.7 million, up 68% from $337.9 million in the prior-year period.
Operating income increased 458% to $69.5 million.
Non-GAAP operating income rose 129% to $89.8 million.
Net income increased to $93.2 million from $9.4 million a year earlier, representing growth of 888%.
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $93 million from the prior-year period.
Diluted earnings per share increased to $1.29 from $0.11, while non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to $1 from $0.43.
Penguin said performance accelerated during the second half of fiscal 2026 following the launch of its AI Factory Platform and a greater focus on AI-driven data center demand.
Revenue growth accelerated from relatively flat levels during the first half to 48% in the third quarter and 68% in the fourth quarter.
For full-year fiscal 2026, Penguin generated $1.73 billion in net sales, up 26%.
Annual operating income increased 185% to approximately $166 million.
Net income reached $181 million, up 611%, while adjusted EBITDA increased 37% to a record $256 million.
Full-year diluted EPS was $2.60 compared with $0.28 in the prior year, while non-GAAP diluted EPS increased 51% to $2.87.
Penguin added six AI Infrastructure data center customers during the fourth quarter, including four neocloud providers.
Across fiscal 2026, the company added 17 new AI Infrastructure customers, while 12 existing customers expanded their business with Penguin.
One new customer selected Penguin to deploy and operate a 36,000-GPU AI factory in Norway and has $10 billion in contracted compute from a major AI lab.
Another publicly traded neocloud customer with more than $3 billion in signed multi-year contracts selected Penguin for AI infrastructure deployment and 24/7 operations services.
Penguin also advanced its ClusterWareAI platform with self-managing agentic AI capabilities that can automatically detect and remediate GPU performance issues.
The company closed an oversubscribed $750 million convertible senior notes offering due 2031 carrying a 0% coupon.
Based on accelerating AI Infrastructure demand, Penguin raised its fiscal 2027 outlook.
The company now expects approximately $2.43 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue at the midpoint, representing roughly 40% growth, plus or minus 10 percentage points.
Penguin also expects GAAP diluted EPS of approximately $3.50 and non-GAAP diluted EPS of approximately $4.45, representing year-over-year growth of roughly 35% and 55%, respectively.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our company performance accelerated significantly in the second half of fiscal 2026 following the launch of our AI Factory Platform and increased focus on the data center market.”
Kash Shaikh, President and CEO of Penguin Solutions
“The proof is in the results. After relatively flat year-over-year net sales in the first half, growth accelerated to 48% in Q3 and 68% in Q4, driving second-half growth of 58%.”
Kash Shaikh, President and CEO of Penguin Solutions
“As we enter fiscal 2027, our memory business remains strong, and our AI Infrastructure business is accelerating further.”
Kash Shaikh, President and CEO of Penguin Solutions

The latest investment follows the introduction of Harvey’s first post-trained open-weight AI model and the launch of Harvey LAB, the company’s Legal Agent Benchmark, as it expands its technology and capabilities for legal professionals.
The funding round brought together existing investors, including Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Coatue, Conviction, Elad Gil, Evantic, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Verified Capital and WNDR. New investors participating in the round include Diffusion, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sapphire Ventures and Whale Rock.
Harvey’s co-founders, Winston Weinberg and Gabe Pereyra, said the opportunity for businesses to strengthen their competitive advantage through AI has reached an important stage, adding that the company aims to become a global partner for legal teams seeking to advance their AI capabilities.
The co-founders also said Harvey plans to recruit and develop a leading team in the sector to support clients through the next phase of AI-driven transformation.
Harvey has established a presence among major law firms, with 80% of firms in the Am Law 100 using its platform. Its customer base also includes leading in-house legal teams at some of the world’s largest companies, including five of the Fortune 10.
The new funding strengthens Harvey’s position in the legal AI market as it continues developing tools designed to help legal professionals use AI across their operations while building and retaining control over their institutional knowledge and intelligence.
