candidates.title: Legal AI Legora Raises $550M Series E at $8.8B Valuation
candidates.snippet: Legal AI Legora Raises $550M Series E at $8.8B Valuation Wowtale
candidates.text:
Legal teams aren’t treating AI as a mere assistant anymore. Instead of help on individual tasks like contract review or case research, they’re handing entire multi-step workflows to agents. Legora has pushed that shift harder than most legal AI companies. In-house legal teams made up only a small slice of its customer base a year ago; in the third quarter of this year, they accounted for more than 40% of new customers. In the US, now Legora’s largest market by revenue, more than half of the AmLaw 50 are customers — a striking footprint given the company only opened its first US office in spring 2025.
Legora calls itself the agentic operating system for legal professionals. The pitch is to embed AI across the three high-stakes, time-consuming tasks that fill a lawyer’s day: sifting through mountains of documents for what matters, researching case law and statutes, and drafting contracts and opinions. Founded in Stockholm in 2023, Legora launched its platform in October 2024 and now has more than 1,000 employees across 18 offices, serving more than 140,000 legal professionals at over 2,400 law firms and in-house legal teams in more than 80 markets. The new funding will support expansion across North America — where Legora has offices in New York, Denver, Chicago, Houston, San Francisco, Toronto, and Mexico City — along with Europe and Asia-Pacific, and will deepen investment in the Legora aOS, including new agentic intake, horizon-scanning, and legal-research products.
Founder and CEO Max Junestrand had no legal background when he started the company. The idea came from watching a friend who’d just joined a law firm spend an entire summer summarizing court rulings — prompting the question of why people were doing by hand what software could already handle. Junestrand holds a master’s in computer science with a focus on machine learning from Sweden’s KTH Royal Institute of Technology, a business degree from the Stockholm School of Economics, and a master’s in engineering from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and passed through McKinsey and venture capital along the way — giving up a promising esports career to found the company instead.
Without any legal-industry connections, he embedded himself for months inside Mannheimer Swartling, the largest law firm in the Nordics, observing lawyers’ actual workflows and iterating on the product on the spot. Co-founders Sigge Labor and August Erséus joined him. “The opportunity in legal is enormous and we are still early,” Junestrand said. “AI is changing the role of the lawyer… and it is reshaping how law firms and in-house legal teams are organized and how their work gets done. We chose investors who share our long-term view and know what it takes to build a lasting company.”
CFO David Eckstein added: “Growth only counts if the business underneath it holds up. We have passed $200 million in ARR, and we want every dollar of it to be a durable one.”
Legora said it raised a $550 million Series E at an $8.8 billion post-money valuation . Atreides Management led the round, with new investors Baron Capital, Capital Group, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Glade Brook Capital Partners, and J.P. Morgan. Every major existing investor also returned, including Accel, Benchmark, Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst, ICONIQ, Insight Partners, Menlo Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and Sands Capital. The valuation marks roughly a 57% jump from the $5.6 billion mark set just five months earlier, in Legora’s previous Series D.
Atreides Managing Partner and CIO Gavin Baker said “legal is a sophisticated market with demanding buyers, and the bar for software is high. Legora has become the platform that law firms and in-house legal teams adopt and then expand across their organizations, and it has done so while growing at remarkable speed.”
Legora’s fundraising pace has been a story in itself. It started with a $10.5 million Benchmark-led seed in May 2024, followed by a $25 million Series A that July. A $80 million Series B came in May 2025 at a $675 million valuation, led by ICONIQ and General Catalyst, then a $150 million Series C that October at an $1.8 billion valuation, led by Bessemer. This past March, Accel led a $550 million Series D at a $5.6 billion valuation, which NVIDIA’s NVentures extended by $50 million in May — NVIDIA’s first legal-tech investment, per Dealroom data — bringing the round to $600 million total. Around the same time, Legora acquired Qura, a legal research startup whose technology structures case law and statutes across 27 jurisdictions so AI can reason over legal logic rather than just keyword-match it.
Then in April, Legora announced it had crossed $100 million in ARR just 18 months after launch — a pace Bessemer called the fastest enterprise software growth trajectory in history, outpacing OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, and Wiz. The next $100 million, per this week’s announcement, took less than six months; ARR now stands above $200 million.
Legora’s biggest rival in legal AI is Harvey , the San Francisco-based company that raised $550 million at a $15.5 billion valuation this past September — a higher valuation than Legora’s. Contract-management incumbent Clio has made its own AI push, acquiring legal research company vLex for $1 billion. Legora’s own differentiation case rests on building atop foundation models rather than competing with them — it uses Claude as its primary LLM — and designing its product for both human and agent users from day one.

candidates.text:
NETSTREIT Secures $550 Million In New Term Loan Commitments And Amends Facilities
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
NETSTREIT Secures $550 Million In New Term Loan Commitments And Amends Facilities
NETSTREIT has closed $550 million in additional financing commitments and amended existing credit facilities agented by PNC Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist Bank.
The additional financing is being provided through an amendment to NETSTREIT’s term loan agreement agented by PNC Bank.
The commitments include a $100 million increase to the REIT’s existing senior unsecured 5.5-year term loan facility. The full amount was funded at closing.
NETSTREIT also received a $50 million increase to its existing senior unsecured seven-year term loan facility, which was also fully funded at closing.
The largest component is a new $400 million senior unsecured seven-year delayed-draw term loan facility. The facility was undrawn at closing and can be drawn through September 28, 2027.
NETSTREIT used proceeds from the two incremental term loans, together with a remaining $50 million draw under its existing 2032 term loan, to repay its $200 million term loan that had been scheduled to mature in February 2028.
Interest rate swaps previously associated with the repaid term loan remain in place and continue fixing the interest rate on an equivalent amount of borrowings through February 2028.
The company also amended its PNC term loan agreement and credit agreements agented by PNC, Wells Fargo and Truist. Some of the amendments reduce applicable margin spreads.
NETSTREIT said the transactions extend its weighted-average debt maturity profile and leave the company with no material debt maturities until early 2029.
The financing also addresses a significant portion of NETSTREIT’s anticipated debt capital requirements through 2027 and increases available liquidity.
PNC Capital Markets, Huntington National Bank, Truist Securities, Capital One and Regions Capital Markets served as joint lead arrangers for the $100 million incremental term loan.
Those firms were joined by TD Bank and U.S. Bank as joint lead arrangers for the $50 million incremental facility.
The $400 million delayed-draw facility includes PNC Capital Markets, Huntington, Capital One, Regions, TD Bank, Manufacturers and Traders Trust Company, Truist Securities and U.S. Bank as joint lead arrangers.
PNC Capital Markets served as sole bookrunner for the 2031 and 2032 incremental term loans and as one of the joint bookrunners for the 2033 delayed-draw facility.
Morrison & Foerster represented NETSTREIT, while Alston & Bird represented the administrative agents.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased with the closing of our $550.0 million in additional term loan commitments and the full repayment of our 2028 term loan. With these transactions, we have meaningfully extended our weighted average debt maturity profile and have no material debt maturing until early 2029. This additional financing also largely addresses our debt capital needs through 2027 and greatly enhances our liquidity position heading into next year. We sincerely appreciate the continued commitment and support of our trusted banking partners,”
Dan Donlan, Chief Financial Officer of NETSTREIT

candidates.title: ID Finance Secures €545 Million as Plazo Targets €200 Million Credit Portfolio in Spain
candidates.snippet: ID Finance Secures €545 Million as Plazo Targets €200 Million Credit Portfolio in Spain https://ascendants.in/
candidates.text:
ID Finance Secures €545 Million as Plazo Targets €200 Million Credit Portfolio in Spain
Vasundhra Tewari
| October 13 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Barcelona-based fintech ID Finance has secured fresh debt and equity financing to expand its consumer lending operations and accelerate the growth of Plazo , its buy now, pay later platform.
Barcelona-based financial technology company ID Finance has secured €545 million in debt and equity financing, marking a significant step in its plans to expand Plazo, its consumer credit platform in Spain.
The financing involves Spice Expeditions, WashU, Kingsway Capital and i80 Group. While the company has not disclosed how much of the total comes from debt and how much from equity, the funding has two distinct purposes. The equity investment will support Plazo’s expansion, while asset-backed financing from i80 Group will help increase its credit portfolio.
The deal comes as ID Finance looks beyond the short-term lending business on which it built its name. Its next phase centres on Plazo, a platform that combines consumer financial services with flexible payment options.
The company is pursuing that expansion after reporting €243 million in group revenue for 2025. Plazo also reached profitability that year, giving ID Finance a stronger financial foundation as it prepares to scale.
Plazo’s €200 Million Credit Portfolio Ambition
One of the central goals behind the financing is to expand Plazo’s lending capacity.
ID Finance expects Plazo’s credit portfolio to reach approximately €200 million in 2026. The platform currently serves more than 400,000 users and has a reported loan book of €137 million.
Plazo’s recent performance offers some insight into why investors are backing its expansion. According to the company, the platform tripled its credit portfolio in 2025, increased revenue by 300% and became profitable.
From Deutsche Bank Backgrounds to a Growing Spanish Fintech
ID Finance is led by co-founders Boris Batine , its CEO, and Alexander Dunaev, its COO, both of whom previously worked at Deutsche Bank.
Batine’s professional experience also includes Renaissance Capital and the Royal Bank of Scotland, while Dunaev previously headed structured products for Central and Eastern Europe at Deutsche Bank.
The company traces its beginnings to 2012 and has developed a substantial consumer lending operation in Spain.
Its Spanish lending platform has more than 3.7 million registered users. During the first six months of 2026, the business issued over €190 million in loans and generated approximately €100 million in revenue.
Although short-term loans remain an important part of its operations, ID Finance has been broadening its product offering through Plazo, which launched in 2021.
The latest funding illustrates how the business is directing more resources towards a platform that aims to provide everyday financial services alongside consumer credit.
Turrón Brings Interest-Free Instalments to Plazo Users
A key part of Plazo’s expansion is Turrón, a financial product introduced in July 2026.
Turrón combines an electronic money account and debit card with a buy now, pay later facility. Eligible purchases can be divided into interest-free instalments at participating merchants, including online stores and physical retail locations.
According to ID Finance, the product does not charge maintenance fees or subscription costs.
The company is also taking a different approach to acquiring customers. Rather than relying primarily on consumers discovering its service during a merchant’s checkout process, ID Finance intends to introduce Turrón to Plazo’s existing customer base.
That gives it an established audience of more than 400,000 Plazo users to work with as it develops the offering.
The approach also reflects a broader ambition for Plazo. Instead of operating solely as an instalment payment option, it is positioning itself as a consumer finance platform offering multiple services through a single product ecosystem.
i80 Group and Kingsway Capital Deepen Their Involvement
The €545 million financing builds on relationships ID Finance has established with existing financial backers.
Among them is i80 Group, an investment firm founded in 2016 by former Goldman Sachs banker Marc Helwani.
Previously, this company gave ID Finance debt financing worth $150 million in February 2024. The participation of this company in this new deal will also benefit its business operations of providing asset-backed loans.
Kingsway Capital has also maintained a relationship with ID Finance over several years.
In March 2023, Kingsway led a €30 million convertible loan financing arrangement carrying a €235 million valuation cap. That transaction required approval from the Spanish government.
The valuation attached to the latest financing has not been disclosed, making it difficult to determine how the new equity investment values the business.
ID Finance has separately accessed other sources of credit financing. These include a €21 million facility from German asset manager nordIX and an expansion of its eurobond programme in March 2026.
The above transaction raised the existing eurobond balance to €60 million. The bonds earn an annual interest rate of 12%, with maturity in September 2028.
Both of the above transactions emphasize the significance of structured borrowing in funding the company’s loan portfolio.
A €545 Million Deal With an Undisclosed Debt-Equity Split
Although €545 million is a substantial figure, and one important detail remains unanswered: how much represents new equity and how much is repayable financing?
Equity can provide capital for product development, operations and expansion without creating a contractual repayment obligation. Debt financing, meanwhile, allows lenders to increase the amount of credit they extend to customers, but comes with repayment and financing costs.
In ID Finance’s case, the asset-based funding from i80 Group is secured against receivables.

News

/ Sui’s Hashi Bitcoin Finance Network Launches With More Than $500 Million Committed
Sui’s Hashi Bitcoin Finance Network Launches With More Than $500 Million Committed
2 min read
SUIUSD BTCUSD
TL;DR: Hashi, Sui’s native Bitcoin finance infrastructure, will begin a phased mainnet rollout later this month with more than $500 million in committed capital. Anchorage Digital has joined the launch coalition, giving institutional clients routes into Hashi through qualified custody and self-custody infrastructure.
Sui is preparing to bring its Bitcoin finance system to mainnet with something most new DeFi products do not have on day one: half a billion dollars of capital already lined up.
The Sui Foundation said Thursday that Hashi will begin a phased mainnet rollout later this month backed by more than $500 million in capital commitments from its launch coalition.
Anchorage Digital is also joining that coalition as a launch partner.
Hashi is designed to let Bitcoin remain secured on the Bitcoin network while being used as collateral inside financial applications built on Sui.
When BTC enters the system, a corresponding hBTC asset is minted on Sui. That hBTC can then interact with lending markets, vaults and other applications. When the position is unwound, hBTC is burned and the underlying Bitcoin is released.
The distinction between that model and a conventional wrapped Bitcoin token is central to the pitch.
Hashi is attempting to give institutions a way to use BTC as programmable collateral without treating Bitcoin as something that first has to be sold or permanently moved into a separate smart-contract ecosystem.
The $500 million commitment gives those markets a meaningful starting point.
Sui says the initial capital will support lending, borrowing, credit products, vaults, structured products and other Bitcoin-backed applications as individual providers complete their integrations.
The coalition already includes names such as BitGo, Bullish, Cumberland, FalconX and Ledger.
Anchorage adds another important route into the system.
Institutional clients will be able to access Hashi through Anchorage’s Atlas infrastructure for tri-party collateral arrangements while maintaining qualified custody. A second route will use Porto, Anchorage’s institutional self-custody wallet, for firms that want more direct access.
That makes the launch particularly relevant to public companies and funds holding large Bitcoin positions.
Bitcoin treasury companies have accumulated enormous balances, but turning those holdings into working capital usually means selling BTC, borrowing through a centralized lender or entering bespoke financing arrangements.
Hashi is trying to create on-chain alternatives.
The security model will face scrutiny precisely because the amounts involved are potentially large.
Sui says Hashi uses a 2-of-2 multisignature structure involving validators and a guardian layer, with additional controls designed to slow or stop suspicious movements. Its smart contracts have undergone formal verification and the underlying cryptographic protocol has been reviewed.
Those safeguards do not remove risk, but they show the product is being built for a different audience from the early days of experimental Bitcoin DeFi.
More than $500 million has been committed before the phased launch. If a meaningful portion of that capital actually becomes active, Hashi could become one of the larger tests yet of whether institutions want to make long-term Bitcoin holdings productive without giving up exposure to the underlying asset.
Mainnet will show whether the capital waiting at the door actually comes inside.

Sosteneo Raises Over $500 Million for Clean Energy Infrastructure Fund
Kenny Fisher
October 19, 2026
Generali Investments’ clean energy infrastructure investment unit Sosteneo announced that it has secured over €450 million (USD$504 million) in capital commitments for its second flagship fund, including securing over €150 million in new fund commitments and co-investment capital at the fund’s first external close.
Launched in 2025, the fund focuses on construction-ready clean energy infrastructure across European markets, investing where specialist capability across construction, financing and revenue contracting can support asset resilience and long-term value creation. The fund targets investments in physical infrastructure with long-term, stable and visible cash flows across three areas of the energy system, including enabling integration and flexibility, securing clean energy supply, and supporting the decarbonization of industry.
Sosteneo’s predecessor Clean Energy Infrastructure Fund announced its final close last year, raising over €620 million in capital commitments, alongside €80 million in co-investment capital. According to Sosteneo approximately three-quarters of the first fund’s 39 projects are now fully operational. In the second quarter of 2026, Fund I began distributing income generated by its operating assets to investor, and in the third quarter, the fund signed an agreement to sell an interest in an operating asset, marking its first partial realization.
Sosteneo said that the new fund’s first external close includes a new commitment from the largest external institutional investor in its predecessor Fund I, commitments from new institutional investors, and an increased commitment from Generali Insurance Companies, the cornerstone investor in Sosteneo’s flagship funds.
Umberto Tamburrino, Managing Partner and CEO at Sosteneo, said:
“We are pleased with the continued progress of Fund I, with most projects now fully operational after just three years from inception. The commencement of income distributions and the signing of our first partial realisation represent further steps in the maturation of the portfolio. Fund I continues to progress in line with our expectations, providing a strong foundation as we continue to develop the Sosteneo platform and deploy Fund II.”

candidates.text:
Ortet Launches With $500 Million Commitment From Thoreau To Build Patient-Centered Health AI Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Ortet Launches With $500 Million Commitment From Thoreau To Build Patient-Centered Health AI Platform
Ortet launched as a frontier artificial intelligence lab for health with a $500 million commitment from Thoreau. The company is building a full-stack AI platform spanning compute and data infrastructure, frontier research, model development, and deployment.
Ortet’s approach centers on developing a patient-focused foundation model designed to connect the biological, clinical, operational, and financial dimensions of health.
The company said many existing healthcare AI systems are built for narrowly defined tasks and limited datasets, which can limit their ability to learn relationships across a patient’s biology, treatment history, outcomes, and interactions with the broader healthcare system.
Ortet is building a shared intelligence foundation that can improve continuously and adapt across scientific discovery, clinical care, healthcare operations, and financial administration.
The company said knowledge developed in one area could strengthen performance in others through a system designed around the individual patient.
Ortet is led by Co-Founder and CEO Kyunghyun Cho, Ph.D.
Cho co-developed the attention mechanism and Gated Recurrent Unit, technologies that helped establish foundations for modern AI architectures.
He is also the Glen de Vries Professor of Health Statistics at New York University.
Before launching Ortet, Cho spent five years building an AI platform focused on lab-in-the-loop molecular design.
He co-founded Prescient Design and later established Genentech’s frontier research team following Prescient Design’s acquisition.
Ortet’s founding team also includes Co-Founder and Chief AI Officer Keunwoo Choi, Ph.D., who previously developed AI systems at Upstage, Spotify, ByteDance, and Genentech.
Henri Dwyer serves as Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer and previously built and managed Genentech’s largest GPU cluster after engineering roles at Instagram and Lyft.
Jeff Hammerbacher is Co-Founder and Chairman. He is Founder and CEO of Open Athena and previously served as Principal Investigator at Hammer Lab, Founder and Chief Scientist at Cloudera, and Manager of the Data team at Facebook.
Elman Mansimov, Ph.D., serves as Co-Founder and Chief Science Officer and previously worked on neural text-to-image generation as well as post-training and agentic AI platforms at Amazon Web Services.
Claudia Shi, Ph.D., is a Founding Member of Frontier Research and previously worked on AI research and development at Meta Superintelligence Labs.
The $500 million commitment from Thoreau will support development of Ortet’s compute and data infrastructure, health-focused model training and deployment, and continued investment in research and talent.
Ortet has already secured its initial GPU cluster and is building the technical foundation required to move research into production at scale.
The company expects to work with customers across the health ecosystem from launch, using real-world needs to guide development of its models and products.
Goldman Sachs advised on the transaction.
Ortet is a founding Thoreau investment.
Thoreau is building foundational compute, rules, and research infrastructure across healthcare markets including providers, payers, employers, life sciences, and government.
Its initial platform partnerships also include Ensemble, which manages more than $55 billion in net patient revenue, and Penelope Health, a real-time health policy intelligence platform.
KEY QUOTES:
“Patient health should improve with every interaction, but today its data, knowledge, and infrastructure remain too fragmented for that learning to happen at scale. Ortet is building at every layer of the AI stack so that advances in research can translate into systems that understand the complete context of a patient and support better decisions across the continuum of care. Thoreau’s commitment gives us the resources and long-term foundation to pursue that mission with the ambition it requires.”
Kyunghyun Cho, Ph.D., Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Ortet

Sabey Data Center Properties Secures Additional Ares Investment, Bringing Total Commitment Above $500 Million
By Amit Chowdhry

Sabey Data Center Properties Secures Additional Ares Investment, Bringing Total Commitment Above $500 Million
Sabey Corporation and National Real Estate Advisors announced that Ares Secondaries funds have expanded their investment in Sabey Data Center Properties, bringing Ares’ total commitment to the data center platform to more than $500 million.
The additional investment follows Ares’ minority equity investment in Sabey Data Center Properties announced in July 2026.
Sabey Data Center Properties is a fully integrated owner, developer, and operator of hyperscale and enterprise data centers across the United States.
The platform currently operates data center campuses totaling approximately 275 megawatts of capacity in major U.S. markets.
Its development and expansion pipeline is expected to increase the platform to approximately 737 megawatts by 2033.
The additional capital will support Sabey Data Center Properties as it expands infrastructure to meet increasing demand associated with cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and other data-intensive applications.
Sabey Data Center Properties has more than four million square feet of mission-critical space and serves customers across the technology, financial services, healthcare, and other industries.
The company specializes in scalable data center infrastructure designed around operational reliability, efficiency, and lower total cost of ownership.
Sabey Data Center Properties operates as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and National Real Estate Advisors, which manages investments on behalf of institutional clients.
The follow-on Ares investment further aligns the three organizations around the continued expansion of the platform.

candidates.title: Pasadena Quantum Startup Oratomic Raises $475 Million, Reaching $5.4 Billion Valuation
candidates.snippet: Pasadena Quantum Startup Oratomic Raises $475 Million, Reaching $5.4 Billion Valuation Pasadena Now
candidates.text:
Local quantum computing startup Oratomic has raised $475 million in Series B financing, pushing its valuation to $5.4 billion, according to the law firm that represented the company in the transaction.
The financing, announced Oct. 8, brings Oratomic’s total funding to $775 million since its public launch in March. Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati disclosed the amount and valuation, while Oratomic separately announced the cumulative funding figure.
The round was co-led by ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, Index Ventures, General Catalyst and Bezos Expeditions, Wilson Sonsini said. Oratomic previously raised $300 million in a Series A round announced in July.
Oratomic said the new investment will support growth of its scientific and engineering staff, laboratory infrastructure and the systems required to build its quantum computers. Its announcement did not specify how many jobs would be created or how much of the funding would be spent in Pasadena.
The company is developing quantum computers using arrays of neutral atoms, which serve as quantum bits, or qubits. Focused laser beams hold and rearrange the atoms, allowing researchers to explore methods of correcting errors that can interrupt quantum calculations.
The Pasadena company has strong ties to the California Institute of Technology. Chief Executive Dolev Bluvstein was a visiting associate in physics at Caltech as of March, according to the university. Other members of the founding research team include Caltech physics professor Manuel Endres, theoretical physicist John Preskill and Hsin-Yuan (Robert) Huang. Caltech said in March that Huang, an assistant professor of theoretical physics, was on leave while serving as Oratomic’s chief technology officer.
In March, Caltech announced that a team of Caltech and Oratomic researchers had proposed a quantum error-correction method that could reduce the number of qubits needed for a useful machine from millions to as few as 10,000 to 20,000.
That finding is theoretical, not evidence that such a computer has been built. Caltech said the approach still faces substantial engineering challenges, including increasing the size of atomic arrays while keeping error rates low.
In its July funding announcement, Oratomic said it intended to focus on building a fault-tolerant quantum computer rather than developing intermediate commercial products. The October financing gives the company additional resources for that effort. Its October announcement did not establish a timetable for completing a working system, although Oratomic said at its March launch that its mission was to build utility-scale quantum computers by the end of the decade.

candidates.title: Oxide Raises $445M Series D as the Company Proves Vision of Full-Stack Cloud Infrastructure Enterprises Can Own
candidates.snippet: Oxide Raises $445M Series D as the Company Proves Vision of Full-Stack Cloud Infrastructure Enterprises Can Own PR Newswire
candidates.text:
Oxide Raises $445M Series D as the Company Proves Vision of Full-Stack Cloud Infrastructure Enterprises Can Own
News provided by
Oxide
Oct 09, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Eclipse leads financing as Oxide reaches profitability and AMD Ventures invests in its systems-based approach to enterprise computing
EMERYVILLE, Calif. , Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oxide Computer Company , the on-premises cloud computing company, today announced it has raised a $445 million Series D led by Eclipse , with participation from existing investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Riot Ventures, Jane Street, and more. New investors Atreides Management and AMD Ventures also joined the round.
Oxide entered rarefied air earlier this year as it reached profitability, a significant milestone for a rapidly scaling hardware company. With customer demand exceeding current production capacity, the Series D provides additional working capital to secure components, increase manufacturing and serve new and existing customers.
"The accelerating pace of on-prem cloud computing projects has required us to scale manufacturing capacity by 20x over the past 12 months, and yet demand still exceeds supply," said Steve Tuck, co-founder and CEO at Oxide. "We're well-capitalized, and hit an important profitability milestone earlier this year. This funding will allow us to aggressively invest in the materials and manufacturing scale our customers need for years to come."
Oxide's growth comes as the rise of agentic AI intensifies demand for infrastructure that can support a growing mix of compute, memory, networking and data-intensive workloads. The level of complexity required to support these agentic workloads is only achievable or scalable with full-stack systems – something that historically only the world's largest cloud providers could offer and at a price point that is cost-prohibitive for many organizations. With demand for compute, memory and data center capacity outpacing supply, even the hyperscalers are struggling to keep up. These dynamics reinforce that enterprises need the ability to own and control the systems their most critical workloads run on in order to ensure on-demand access to reliable, secure and cost-effective computing.
The Oxide Cloud Computer is a rack-scale integrated system with purpose-built hardware and open-source software that brings the architectural model of the hyperscale cloud to an organization's own data center. By co-designing compute, storage, networking, and software as a single system, Oxide gives enterprises cloud automation and agility with direct ownership over their security, performance, data, and economics.
"The next infrastructure bottleneck is already taking shape. As AI shifts from generating answers to executing work, demand for CPU-based systems is accelerating dramatically," said Seth Winterroth, Eclipse partner. "Oxide was built for this moment. Steve, Bryan, and the team saw years ago that enterprises would need cloud-scale computing they could own and control, and they built the full system to deliver it. Now they're scaling to meet a market that is moving faster than anyone anticipated."
"When we started Oxide in 2019, we knew that there would be increasing demand for owning and operating one's own compute -- and we felt strongly that organizations should be able to control their infrastructure without having to forfeit the modernity of cloud computing," said Bryan Cantrill, CTO and co-founder of Oxide. "The specifics have been surprising -- we certainly did not anticipate the explosion in compute demand from agentic AI -- but today's thirst to control one's own fate is exactly what we sought to slake with Oxide."
Oxide made an early bet that the next era of computing would be built as systems with hardware and software designed together rather than assembled from disparate components. AMD and Oxide have worked closely across the hardware and software stack. As agentic AI creates new demands across compute, memory and networking, AMD Ventures is deepening that relationship through a strategic investment in Oxide.
"Oxide's systems-level approach to enterprise infrastructure is expanding the choices available to customers as their computing needs become more complex," said Sagi Paz, Head of AMD Ventures. "This approach aligns with AMD's commitment to fostering a broad, high-performance computing ecosystem, and we're excited to support the company's next phase of growth."
Oxide customers span organizations with demanding infrastructure requirements across financial services, government, national laboratories, aerospace, and other compute-intensive industries. This infusion of capital further strengthens Oxide's ability to invest for the long term as customers deploy its infrastructure for increasingly critical workloads.
To learn more, visit oxide.computer.
About Oxide
Oxide Computer Company is the creator of the Cloud Computer, a rack-scale system with fully unified hardware and open-source software purpose-built to deliver hyperscale cloud computing to on-premises data centers. Oxide gives developers the elasticity, programmability and unified control of the cloud while enabling enterprises to retain ownership of their infrastructure for greater security, latency, sovereignty and cost predictability. Founded in 2019, Oxide is based in Emeryville, California.

candidates.title: DeepSeek leads $400 million funding round for ex-Tencent scientist's robot AI startup
candidates.snippet: DeepSeek leads $400 million funding round for ex-Tencent scientist's robot AI startup Startup Fortune
candidates.text:
China's low-cost AI lab has mostly built its reputation on open-weight language models. Its investment in Unitree Robotics shows how quickly that strategy is moving toward embodied AI.
DeepSeek's clearest verified robotics move so far is its investment in Unitree Robotics' Shanghai IPO. In August, DeepSeek put 140.8 million yuan into the offering, about $20.8 million. That's according to a stock-exchange filing reported by Reuters. Unitree priced the deal at 150.80 yuan a share and raised about 6.1 billion yuan.
The timing fits a broader capital push. Bloomberg reported on October 6 that DeepSeek was close to securing at least 80 billion yuan, about $12 billion, in a new funding round backed by Tencent and battery giant CATL. That follows DeepSeek closing its first external financing earlier in 2026. The round hadn't been announced as closed, but the fundraising reports show how quickly investor interest has built around a lab that spent its first two years building reputation almost entirely on open-weight language models.
That deal came paired with a procurement pact: Unitree gets priority when buying model-training services and technical solutions from DeepSeek, while DeepSeek gets priority when buying robots or pursuing embodied-AI applications with Unitree. Unitree's 150.80 yuan offering price valued the company near $9 billion, making it the first mainland-listed humanoid robot maker in China.
The problem every humanoid robot company is chasing right now is the same one DeepSeek is approaching through Unitree. It needs a model that can look at an unfamiliar room and reliably turn plain instructions into physical action. Large language models are good at predicting the next word. They are much worse at predicting the next joint angle, and that gap is one of the biggest barriers holding humanoid robots back from general-purpose use.
China is turning humanoid robots into an industrial assembly line and the rest of the world is watching
Chinese humanoid robotics companies are minting unicorns at a pace the rest of the world isn't matching. Robotera raised $200 million in May 2026, Unitree filed a $610 million Shanghai IPO on 335% revenue growth, and China now ships 90% of global humanoid robot units, backed by $20 billion in government subsidies and a manufacturing ecosystem... - humanoid robots in Chinese factories - why China leads humanoid robotics
It also fits a pattern across Hangzhou, the city CNBC has described as China's answer to Silicon Valley for AI and robotics, where DeepSeek, Unitree, and spatial-intelligence company Manycore are part of the same startup cluster. The city's AI cluster has increasingly treated embodied intelligence, not another round of chatbot fine-tuning, as the next real contest.
Frankly, DeepSeek didn't need a robotics bet to stay relevant. Its open-weight models already reshaped how the industry talks about training costs. But as LLM gains become more incremental, physical robots that can actually do useful work offer a new battlefield: one where DeepSeek needs hardware partners such as Unitree.
The US side of the race looks nothing alike
Compare that with how the American humanoid robot field is being financed. Figure AI announced in 2025 that it had exceeded $1 billion in Series C commitments at a $39 billion post-money valuation. That's up from its February 2024 valuation of $2.6 billion, with earlier backers including OpenAI, Nvidia, and Microsoft. Tesla's Optimus has no standalone valuation, but Morgan Stanley has described Tesla as an important enabler in humanoid robotics, while Tesla has said first-generation Optimus production lines are being installed in anticipation of production in 2026. Elon Musk has described $20,000 to $30,000 as a long-term target price, not a confirmed commercial price.
Those are hardware bets backed by Big Tech balance sheets and sovereign-scale venture capital. DeepSeek's Unitree stake is much smaller. But it points the same way: AI model companies want a path from software benchmarks into machines that act in the real world.
Both sides are making the same wager. For the last three years the race that mattered was who builds the best chatbot. Now that's giving way to a race over who builds the best body and brain for a machine that can actually pick things up, walk across a warehouse floor, or fold laundry without supervision. DeepSeek made its name proving a leaner model could compete with OpenAI's. Whether that same discipline translates into motion control and real-world perception is the question its Unitree partnership now has to test.

candidates.title: Chinese Robovan developer Neolix raises nearly $400m Series E
candidates.snippet: Chinese Robovan developer Neolix raises nearly $400m Series E DealStreetAsia
candidates.text:
Neolix Technologies , the Chinese developer of Robovan, has announced it is raising nearly $400 million in a Series E funding round as it seeks to expand overseas and scale commercial operations.
The round, anchored by Boyu Capital , attracted Alibaba’s AEF NextGen Fund, Monolith Management, Granite Asia, Vertex Growth, Meridian Capital, GAC Capital and other investors, the company said on Tuesday.
Existing shareholders, including Trustar Capital, CDH VGC and Yunqi Partners, also participated in the round.
The fundraising comes about a year after it raised $600 million in its Series D financing , the largest private fundraising in China’s autonomous driving sector.
It secured 1 billion yuan ($137.3 million) in an extended Series C round of financing in February 2025.
In 2021, the startup closed a Series B round at “a few hundred million Chinese yuan,” with CICC Capital and SoftBank Ventures Asia jointly leading the deal. It raised nearly 100 million yuan ($13.7 million) in a Series A round in 2019.
Neolix, founded in early 2018, specialises in the development of autonomous logistics vehicles, or the so-called “Robovans” that automate deliveries of goods and cargo in office and industrial parks, university campuses, residences, and central business districts.
Its vehicles and delivery services operate in markets across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Australia, the company said.
Neolix’s cumulative funding has exceeded $1.4 billion, according to the company, which described the latest round as the largest single financing in China’s autonomous driving sector this year.
The company plans to use the proceeds to establish local service hubs in major regional markets and expand its global customer fulfilment network. It will also invest in data training for its artificial intelligence models to improve vehicle safety and performance and reduce operating costs.
“Our goal is to build an efficient, reliable autonomous transport network that becomes part of urban and rural infrastructure and makes affordable logistics accessible to more communities,” said Enyuan Yu, founder and CEO of Neolix.
In June, Neolix received approval from Malaysia’s Ministry of Transport to begin public-road sandbox testing of its Level 4 autonomous delivery vehicles in Cyberjaya, marking its entry into the country’s autonomous mobility programme and advancing its Southeast Asia expansion.
The approval, granted under Malaysia’s National Regulatory Sandbox framework, allows Neolix to begin road trials in Cyberjaya, the country’s smart city hub. The company said the move complements its ongoing expansion efforts in Singapore and the broader Asia-Pacific region.
Neolix will conduct the pilot with Malaysian logistics provider Tiong Nam Logistics, mobility platform Asia Mobiliti, and AI infrastructure company MindHub. The trials will evaluate use cases including parcel delivery, campus logistics and e-commerce fulfilment, with testing expected to run through the second half of the year.
The company said Southeast Asia’s growing e-commerce sector and increasing investment in AI, robotics, and smart mobility make the region a key market for autonomous logistics.

Hercules Capital Closes $400 Million Offering Of 6.7% Notes Due 2029
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
Hercules Capital Closes $400 Million Offering Of 6.7% Notes Due 2029
Hercules Capital has closed an upsized public offering of $400 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.7% unsecured notes due October 2029, providing the venture lender with additional capital for debt repayment, new investments and general corporate purposes.
The notes will mature on October 8, 2029, and carry an annual interest rate of 6.7%, payable semiannually.
Hercules may redeem the notes in whole or in part before maturity at par plus an applicable make-whole premium, giving the company flexibility to refinance or retire the securities early if market conditions or its capital needs change.
The offering received investment-grade ratings from two major agencies. Moody’s Investors Service initially assigned the notes a Baa2 rating, while Fitch Ratings assigned a BBB- rating.
Hercules plans to use the net proceeds to repay outstanding secured or unsecured indebtedness, fund investments consistent with its investment objectives, and support general corporate purposes.
The financing provides additional liquidity for Hercules as it continues deploying capital into high-growth, venture-backed companies.
Hercules primarily provides senior secured venture growth loans, giving technology, life sciences and other innovation-focused companies access to capital that can complement equity financing.
Since its founding in 2003, Hercules has committed more than $28 billion to over 700 companies across its target sectors.
The new notes expand the company’s funding base and provide longer-term capital through 2029 that can be used to support additional lending activity while also managing existing debt obligations.

Delek US Raises $400 Million Through Convertible Senior Notes Offering
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Delek US Raises $400 Million Through Convertible Senior Notes Offering
Delek US Holdings has priced a private offering of $400 million aggregate principal amount of 0% convertible senior notes due 2031.
The company also granted the initial purchasers an option to acquire up to an additional $60 million of notes during a 13-day period beginning when the notes are issued.
The offering was expected to close on September 29, 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Delek plans to use part of the net proceeds to fund capped call transactions designed to reduce potential dilution associated with future conversion of the notes.
The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, including partial repayment of amounts outstanding under Delek’s term loan credit facility together with related accrued interest, fees and expenses.
The notes will not bear regular interest and their principal amount will not accrete.

The initial conversion rate is 11.7219 shares of Delek common stock for each $1,000 principal amount of notes.

Delek may not generally redeem the notes before November 6, 2029, except through a specified cleanup redemption provision.
The capped call transactions have an initial cap price of approximately $117.09 per share, representing a roughly 75% premium to the September 24 closing price.
Delek’s operations include petroleum refining, logistics, pipelines and renewable fuels. Its refining assets have combined nameplate crude throughput capacity of 302,000 barrels per day.

Monroe Capital Prices $398.9 Million Private Credit CLO
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Monroe Capital Prices $398.9 Million Private Credit CLO
Monroe Capital has priced Monroe Capital PC CLO II, a $398.9 million collateralized loan obligation backed primarily by senior secured loans to lower middle-market and traditional middle-market companies. The transaction represents Monroe’s second new-issue CLO completed during 2026 and its fourth CLO transaction over the past 12 months. Deutsche Bank served as lead arranger for the transaction.
The CLO’s capital structure includes investment-grade debt tranches rated from AAA through BBB-. It was also structured to meet applicable risk-retention requirements across the United States, United Kingdom and Europe.
The transaction expands Monroe’s structured products platform, which has issued more than $13 billion since inception.
That platform includes traditional middle-market CLOs, private credit CLOs, broadly syndicated CLOs, asset-backed securitizations, rated feeder vehicles and collateralized fund obligations.
Monroe said the CLO demonstrates its ability to combine directly originated middle-market loans with institutional capital markets financing while maintaining its underwriting and portfolio construction standards.
The firm’s structured products business is led by its senior investment and structured-solutions teams and draws on experience spanning multiple credit cycles.
Monroe has also received industry recognition for its CLO business, including DealCatalyst’s 2026 Boutique Private Credit CLO Manager of the Year award in the under-$5-billion category and its 2026 Innovative Private Credit CLO Manager award.
As of July 1, 2026, Monroe Capital managed $23.8 billion across more than 45 investment vehicles. Its broader platform includes direct lending and alternative credit funds, venture debt, public and private business development companies, separately managed accounts and CLOs.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased with the strong execution of this transaction and the broad support it received from a sophisticated global investor base. This CLO reflects the institutional scale, underwriting discipline, and sourcing advantages we have built across our private credit platform. As borrowers and investors increasingly value certainty, selectivity, and long-term partnership, our focus remains on deploying capital thoughtfully, protecting downside, and generating durable risk-adjusted returns through market cycles.”
Zia Uddin, President of Monroe Capital

We remain focused on scaling the platform responsibly, maintaining disciplined credit standards, and delivering consistent execution for our investors and financing partners.”
Seth Friedman, Managing Director and Head of Structured Solutions at Monroe Capital

candidates.title: Aligned Climate Capital Secures $387 Million Financing Led By Apterra For 126 MW Community Solar Portfolio
candidates.snippet:
Aligned Climate Capital has secured approximately $387 million in construction-to-permanent financing for a 126-megawatt community solar portfolio comprising 20 projects across Illinois and Maryland. Apterra Infrastructure Capital, an affiliate of Apollo, led the financing.
The post Aligned Climate Capital Secures $387 Million Financing Led By Apterra For 126 MW Community Solar Portfolio appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Aligned Climate Capital Secures $387 Million Financing Led By Apterra For 126 MW Community Solar Portfolio
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 15, 2026
Aligned Climate Capital Secures $387 Million Financing Led By Apterra For 126 MW Community Solar Portfolio
Aligned Climate Capital has secured approximately $387 million in construction-to-permanent financing for a 126-megawatt community solar portfolio comprising 20 projects across Illinois and Maryland. Apterra Infrastructure Capital, an affiliate of Apollo, led the financing.
The portfolio includes approximately 115 MWdc across 18 projects in Illinois and 11 MWdc across two projects in Maryland. Once operational, the projects are expected to generate approximately 225 million kilowatt-hours of electricity annually, enough to power roughly 31,500 homes.
The financing is structured to support construction of each project before converting into permanent debt as individual assets begin operations. Aligned said the portfolio approach helps aggregate smaller distributed energy projects into a scale that can attract institutional infrastructure financing.
The Illinois projects are located within Ameren and ComEd utility territories, with a portion participating in the Illinois Shines Adjustable Block Program. The Maryland projects are located in the Delmarva Power and Potomac Edison territories and participate in Maryland’s Community Solar Energy Generating Systems program, which reserves at least 40% of project capacity for low- and moderate-income subscribers.
The lender syndicate includes BankUnited, Stifel, Banco de Crédito e Inversiones, Amalgamated Bank, Siemens, Farmer Mac, and BTG Pactual. BankUnited is serving as depository agent, while BankUnited and Stifel are providing interest rate swaps and Bci is serving as the letter of credit provider.
Aligned has invested in distributed solar through its Aligned Solar Partners strategy since 2018. The strategy acquires distributed solar and energy storage projects from development partners, finances their construction, and manages the assets through operations, focusing on projects that sit between smaller rooftop systems and utility-scale developments.
Aligned Climate Capital manages approximately $2.2 billion in assets and invests exclusively in businesses and projects supporting the clean energy transition. Its two primary strategies are the Aligned Climate Fund, which invests in venture-stage clean energy companies, and Aligned Solar Partners, which owns and operates distributed solar, energy storage, and related projects.
Clifford Chance served as legal counsel to the borrower, while Norton Rose Fulbright represented the lenders.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’re seeing an important shift in distributed energy. Individual projects may be too small for traditional infrastructure investors. But when you bring those projects together into a larger portfolio, you can attract institutional financing that would otherwise be difficult to access. That helps move more projects from development into operation.”
Peter Davidson, CEO Of Aligned Climate Capital
“Community solar is an important and fast-growing part of the distributed generation market, and this portfolio benefits from scale, contracted revenue, and experienced sponsorship. We are pleased to lead this facility for Aligned as it brings these projects online across Illinois and Maryland.”
Ralph Cho, Co-Chief Executive Officer At Apterra

Zelestra has closed $350 million in green financing credit facilities for its 203 MW Reclamation Solar project in Gibson County, Indiana, taking the renewable energy company’s U.S. project financing raised during 2026 to $1.14 billion.

Pilot Fiber Raises Over $330 Million Led By Fengate And Agrees To Acquire Boldyn Networks’ New York And New Jersey Fiber Business
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Pilot Fiber Raises Over $330 Million Led By Fengate And Agrees To Acquire Boldyn Networks’ New York And New Jersey Fiber Business
Pilot Fiber, an enterprise connectivity provider serving the New York metropolitan area, has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire the New York and New Jersey metro fiber business of Boldyn Networks.
To support the acquisition and its continued expansion, Pilot also announced more than $330 million in new financing led by Fengate Asset Management.
The transactions are expected to close during the second quarter of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
The acquisition will significantly expand Pilot’s regional fiber network, extending its owned infrastructure across all five boroughs of New York City and into additional markets throughout New Jersey.
Following completion, Pilot expects its combined owned network to encompass more than 1,600 route miles of fiber, connecting over 1,200 buildings and 50 data centers.
The transaction is Pilot’s second acquisition of 2026, following its purchase of Extenet’s enterprise fiber business in August.
Boldyn’s assets include a New York City fiber network supporting data center connectivity, smart city infrastructure, and enterprise telecommunications services, along with a New Jersey network serving commercial businesses and carriers.
The New Jersey portion of the acquired infrastructure includes more than 860 route miles of fiber, with established connectivity across commercial corridors serving financial services, healthcare, and other industries.
The acquisition will also expand Pilot’s reach into Brooklyn through a dedicated East River crossing and provide additional infrastructure across Queens, the Bronx, Staten Island, and portions of the region extending toward Nassau County.
Other assets include monopole infrastructure supporting low-latency connectivity between major financial exchanges.
The acquired business currently serves approximately 100 enterprise, carrier, and institutional customers.
Pilot plans to integrate these customers into its existing operations and offer its full portfolio of connectivity services across the expanded network.
The company’s services include Dedicated Internet Access, Ethernet Transport, Dark Fiber, Wavelength, and IP Transit, serving organizations requiring high-capacity and reliable network infrastructure.
Pilot emphasizes direct ownership of its fiber network and in-house operations as central components of its service model.
The company reports that its installation process for on-network buildings typically requires five to 15 days, compared with an industry standard of approximately 30 to 90 days.
Fengate Asset Management is providing its equity investment through Fengate Infrastructure Fund V.
Warren Roll, Fengate’s managing director and head of digital infrastructure, is leading the investment and will join Pilot’s board of directors.
Fengate is an alternative investment manager focused on infrastructure, private equity, and real estate, with investments across digital infrastructure, transportation, energy transition, and related sectors.
The new financing will support Pilot’s acquisition strategy as it expands its network ownership and enterprise connectivity capabilities.
Boldyn Networks will also maintain an ongoing commercial relationship with Pilot following the transaction.
Boldyn will continue using the combined fiber infrastructure to support its wireless connectivity operations while concentrating on its broader strategy of deploying wireless networks across transportation systems, government facilities, buildings, major venues, and outdoor locations.
The companies expect their continuing relationship to support connectivity services throughout the region.
The transaction involved several financial and legal advisors.
Guggenheim Securities served as financial advisor to Fengate, while Simpson Thacher & Bartlett provided legal counsel and Leo Berwick advised on tax and financial due diligence.
Goodwin Procter served as legal counsel to Pilot. The Bank Street Group acted as exclusive financial advisor to Boldyn Networks, with Paul Hastings providing legal counsel.
The acquisition and financing mark a significant expansion of Pilot’s metropolitan fiber infrastructure platform, positioning the company to serve a larger customer base across the New York and New Jersey markets.

Boldyn’s network reaches deep into the five boroughs to the border of Nassau County, and throughout northern and central Jersey, with strong carrier and enterprise relationships already in place. Now we get to bring the same customer-first experience that’s defined Pilot from day one to businesses across a much larger part of the region.”
Joe Fasone, CEO Of Pilot Fiber

We are proud to partner with Joe and his team, and Fengate is fully committed to Pilot’s long-term success.”

The financing will support development, construction, acquisition, and operation of Lydian’s portfolio of battery storage and solar projects. Lydian is backed by Excelsior Energy Capital.

The facility is structured to allow Lydian to leverage the value of operating and construction-ready assets while retaining ownership of projects that can generate long-term value.
The financing also provides additional flexibility to advance projects from development through construction as electricity demand and grid modernization accelerate.
Akin Gump served as legal counsel to Lydian.
Eversheds Sutherland represented Infranity.
Infranity manages approximately €15 billion in assets on behalf of institutional investors.
Excelsior Energy Capital closed its second fund at slightly more than $1 billion in 2025 after raising $504 million for its first flagship fund in 2020.

Emre Ersenkal, CEO of Lydian Energy

Sacha Kamp, Global Head of Debt Investment at Infranity
“It gives Lydian efficient, scalable capital to grow its portfolio as demand for reliable, domestically produced power continues to rise.”
Chris Moakley, Managing Partner at Excelsior Energy Capital and Chair of Lydian Energy

candidates.snippet:
Atom Computing was selected by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency to advance to the final stage of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. Stage C of the program carries potential funding of up to $300 million.
The post Atom Computing Advances To Final Stage Of DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Atom Computing Advances To Final Stage Of DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Atom Computing Advances To Final Stage Of DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative
Atom Computing was selected by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency to advance to the final stage of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. Stage C of the program carries potential funding of up to $300 million.
The Quantum Benchmarking Initiative is evaluating whether utility-scale quantum computers can be built on a faster timeline than conventional industry expectations.
Atom Computing was selected for Stage A in early 2025 and advanced to Stage B later that year.
During Stage B, the company developed a detailed plan for building a utility-scale quantum computer, including technology milestones, risk assessments, mitigation strategies, and prototype systems.
During Stage C, an independent government verification and validation team will evaluate whether Atom Computing’s proposed system can be built and operated as designed.
Microsoft has also agreed to provide algorithmic support and error correction codes to Atom Computing as part of the effort.
Atom Computing develops quantum systems based on neutral-atom technology.
The company has demonstrated systems exceeding 1,000 physical qubits and said it has achieved sub-threshold performance with end-to-end quantum error correction across multiple rounds.
In 2025, Atom Computing completed what it described as the industry’s first commercial sale of a logical-qubit quantum computer to QuNorth.
The company also recently signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce involving $100 million.
KEY QUOTES:
“We believe utility-scale quantum computing is closer than many expect, and this milestone reinforces our confidence in the scalability and performance of neutral-atom architectures.”
Dr. Ben Bloom, CEO and Founder of Atom Computing
“Atom Computing’s neutral-atom architecture, combined with its demonstrated progress toward fault-tolerant quantum computing, positions the company at the forefront of delivering practical quantum systems capable of addressing some of the world’s most complex computational challenges.”
Dr. Jonathan King, Chief Scientist and Co-Founder of Atom Computing

Canyon Partners has arranged and anchored NZ$300 million of financing supporting Advent International’s acquisition of NZCR Group, a clinical trials and medical research organization operating across New Zealand and Australia. Canyon served as arranger and anchor lender for the financing.

candidates.text:
Polsky 10: Pyxis secures up to $282.6M | Thrixel launches with new $3M | Inomagen receives $2.9M grant
October 12, 2026
The Polsky 10 is a bi-weekly newsletter featuring 10 things to know from the University of Chicago’s Polsky Center. To get the Polsky 10 sent directly to your inbox every other Friday, sign up here >>
1 // Pyxis Oncology announces up to $282.6M in new funding as it gears up for key clinical milestones.
UChicago Startup Investment Program recipient Pyxis Oncology has raised approximately $110M in a recent public offering to advance its lead cancer therapy, micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO), toward key clinical milestones. The Boston-based biotech, founded on the research from UChicago Professor Thomas Gajewski, AB ’84, PhD ’89, MD ’91, could raise up to another $172.6M based on milestone-linked warrants following the company’s expected release of overall survival data in the first half of 2027. This latest financing gives Pyxis the resources to move MICVO into its next stage of development, including a planned Phase 3 trial in recurrent and metastatic head and neck cancer, as it works to determine whether the antibody-drug conjugate can deliver on promising early clinical results. Read more now .
2 // Thrixel just launched with $3M in funding to take AI to another dimension.
As AI continues to revolutionize the way we produce images, text, graphics, and code, there has been one lasting creativity barrier that AI has struggled to climb… 3D content. The complicated design and building process demands deep technical expertise, beyond the scope of most developers. But now, UChicago computer scientist Rana Hanocka is turning her years of research in AI and computer graphics into a new company to end this roadblock. Thrixel is a 3D creation platform designed to make it easier for AI agents to generate, manipulate, and animate 3D objects. To assist development in the AI pipeline, Thrixel creates structured assets whose individual parts — like a car’s wheels, doors, and chassis — can be identified and manipulated independently, making them easier to use in games, robotics, simulations, and other interactive applications. Alongside news of its launch, Thrixel also announced a raise of $3M in inception funding. Read more now .
3 // This UChicago faculty-founded biotech is getting to the heart of AFib with a new $2.9M grant.
Inomagen Therapeutics , founded by UChicago cardiologist Rishi Arora, is developing a non-viral gene therapy to improve the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). Specifically, Inomagen’s goal is to create a more durable, disease-modifying alternative to current AF treatments that aren’t effective enough for many patients. Most recently, the biotech has been awarded an NIH Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) grant providing up to $2.9M to advance its investigational gene therapy. The two-year award will support preclinical safety and efficacy studies, as well as manufacturing work needed to prepare the therapy for a future Investigational New Drug application with the FDA. Furthermore, this grant builds on $3.67M in previous NIH SBIR funding for Inomagen’s AF program. Read more now .
4 // Great Lakes RENEW Scaling Lab makes a splash.
Chicago is already a natural hub for water technology innovation, with the neighboring Great Lakes responsible for 20% of the world’s surface freshwater — but there has been one major hurdle that the region’s best water entrepreneurs have struggled against. Space. As pointed out in a new Crain’s Chicago Business commentary co-written by Polsky Center Managing Director Samir Mayekar and Current CEO Alaina Harkness, “space represents a serious constraint” for water entrepreneurs with technology that often requires specialized facilities and testing environments to bring to life. Luckily, Mayekar and Harkness propose an exciting new solution can be found in the Great Lakes RENEW Scaling Lab, a new partnership between the Polsky Center and Current that will provide early-stage water technology companies with subsidized lab and office space, necessary equipment, and connections to investors, and industry partners. Read more now .
5 // Where talent and tech collide.
Researchers from four leading Midwestern universities came together at the Fall 2026 Collaboratorium to explore how promising technologies can make the leap from the lab to the market. With its roots at UChicago, the Collaboratorium now also welcomes researchers from Northwestern University, Purdue University, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The late-September event featured 18 teams working across healthcare, energy storage, quantum computing, and more, giving scientists and researchers the chance to pitch their technologies to students and alumni with expertise in customer discovery, market research, commercialization, and entrepreneurship. Read more now on how this hallmark Polsky Center program is creating opportunities to turn scientific ideas into products, companies, and real-world impact.
6 // Meet the new fund working to turn science fiction into science fact.
Cofounded by Chicago Booth Adjunct Associate Professor of Entrepreneurship Jeremie Bacon, SENU Venture Partners is a new Chicago-based venture fund with plans to raise $250M for investment in technologies designed to enhance human capability and longevity. According to its founders, the new fund will invest in companies at the “Day +1” mark — after a technology has proven it works, when the challenge shifts to manufacturing, commercialization, regulation, and the operations of building a scalable business. Specifically, SENU will focus on embodied and physical AI, cybernetics, and acceleration infrastructure, aiming to help deep-tech companies make the leap from scientific possibility to commercial reality. Read more now .

candidates.text:
The RMR Group Secures $272.1 Million Refinancing For Cedars-Sinai Medical Office Portfolio In Los Angeles
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
The RMR Group Secures $272.1 Million Refinancing For Cedars-Sinai Medical Office Portfolio In Los Angeles
The RMR Group announced that it facilitated a $272.1 million interest-only mortgage financing on behalf of a managed joint venture for a medical office portfolio located on the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center campus in Los Angeles.
The financing is secured by 8631 and 8635 West Third Street, two 11-story medical office buildings totaling approximately 330,000 square feet, along with two structured parking garages.
The buildings are connected to Cedars-Sinai Medical Center by skybridge.
Cedars-Sinai and its affiliates serve as the portfolio’s anchor tenants and occupy approximately 60% of the total rentable square footage.
The new loan has an initial two-year term with three one-year extension options.
It carries an interest rate of one-month Term SOFR plus 180 basis points.
Proceeds were used to repay approximately $267 million of existing mortgage debt that was scheduled to mature in February 2027 and to cover closing costs.
The refinancing provides the joint venture with additional term flexibility while maintaining financing for a strategically located healthcare real estate asset.
Morgan Stanley and BNP Paribas provided the financing.
Hogan Lovells Cadwalader US LLP served as counsel to the lenders, while Sullivan & Worcester LLP represented the borrower.
The portfolio is owned by a joint venture for which RMR provides asset and property management services.
The venture is primarily owned by private institutional investors.
Diversified Healthcare Trust, an RMR client, owns a 20% equity interest in the joint venture.
RMR manages more than $37 billion in assets under management through a platform supported by more than 800 real estate professionals across more than 30 offices nationwide.
The firm focuses on commercial real estate, residential real estate, and related businesses.
KEY QUOTES:
“This refinancing reflects the quality of this medical office portfolio, which is located on the campus of one of the nation’s leading healthcare institutions. By refinancing its upcoming maturity with a new loan that provides term extension flexibility, the joint venture is well positioned to continue benefiting from the portfolio’s strong anchor tenancy, strategic location and attractive long-term fundamentals. The successful execution of this transaction underscores the value of RMR’s integrated real estate platform and our ability to deliver capital solutions that support our clients’ investment objectives.”
Adam Portnoy, President and Chief Executive Officer of The RMR Group

Ironbark Financial Group Secures $255.9 Million Investment From Merchant Wealth Partners
Ironbark Financial Group secured a $255.9 million investment from Merchant Wealth Partners to support the next stage of the Australian financial services firm’s growth.

candidates.title: Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award
candidates.snippet:
Three Corners Connector has been selected to proceed to negotiations for potential funding of up to $250 million through the U.S. Department of Energy's Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades, or SPARK, program.
The post Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award
Three Corners Connector has been selected to proceed to negotiations for potential funding of up to $250 million through the U.S. Department of Energy’s Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades, or SPARK, program.
The Oklahoma Office of Management and Enterprise Services applied for the federal funding with Three Corners Connector serving as a subrecipient.
Selection for negotiations does not represent a final award. Funding remains subject to successful negotiations and execution of a formal financial assistance agreement.
Three Corners Connector is a proposed 300-mile high-voltage direct current interregional transmission line connecting the eastern and western electric grids, with endpoints in Oklahoma and Colorado.
The project is designed to more than double the existing 1,320 MW transfer capacity between the two grids.
If finalized, SPARK funding would primarily support engineering and materials associated with the project’s transmission towers.
The project is intended to improve interregional grid connectivity and provide utilities and grid operators with increased ability to move electricity between the Southwest Power Pool and Western Electricity Coordinating Council markets.
Three Corners Connector is progressing through regulatory filings, with final approvals expected in 2026.
Construction is expected to begin after remaining land rights are secured and required regulatory approvals are obtained. The project could become operational as early as 2031.
KEY QUOTES:
“It’s not that we don’t have enough electricity in most areas. Most of the time we lack the transmission capabilities to go from one region where it’s being generated to another region where it’s needed. So the connectors that we’re investing in across the U.S. are ensuring that we have capacity to move the power and energy to where it’s needed.”
Kyle Haustveit, U.S. Department of Energy Under Secretary of Energy
“The Great Plains is a cornerstone of the country’s energy system, and connecting the eastern and western grids here strengthens reliability on both sides. Selection for SPARK funding helps Oklahoma and Three Corners Connector build toward a more resilient energy future, and we look forward to advancing the project alongside the stakeholders who have helped shape its development.”
Bryant Coon, Senior Director of Development for Three Corners Connector

candidates.text:
SWEN Capital Partners Closes €236 Million PE Select Europa 7
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
SWEN Capital Partners Closes €236 Million PE Select Europa 7
SWEN Capital Partners closed SWEN PE Select Europa 7 at €236 million. The fund is the seventh vintage of SWEN’s European multi-strategy private equity program, which has invested directly and indirectly alongside European private equity managers since 2008.
At final close, approximately 80% of the fund had already been committed to underlying investments.
SWEN expects to continue making commitments through the end of 2026 and into the first half of 2027.
Through an overcommitment mechanism, the fund can make commitments equal to as much as 120% of its capital base.
That gives Europa 7 capacity for approximately €283 million of total investment commitments.
The strategy combines primary fund commitments, secondary transactions, and minority direct investments.
Its target allocation is approximately 50% to primary investments, 20% to secondaries, and 30% to minority direct investments.
The structure is designed to provide diversified access to specialist European private equity managers and portfolio companies while allowing SWEN to manage pacing, manager selection, and diversification.
Europa 7 is similar in size to its three immediate predecessors.
Europa 4 raised €261 million, Europa 5 raised €240 million, and Europa 6 raised €255 million.
Europa 7 is also the first fund in the series classified as Article 9 under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation.
SWEN said the vehicle is one of the relatively few European Article 9 private equity fund-of-funds strategies focused on small and mid-sized companies.
