candidates.text:
Arda Emerges From Stealth With $232 Million To Automate Manufacturing Engineering
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Arda Emerges From Stealth With $232 Million To Automate Manufacturing Engineering
Arda Industries has emerged from stealth with $232 million in total funding to develop AI software that helps manufacturers turn new product designs into working assembly lines and update those lines as designs change. The company is targeting a long-term vision of robotic assembly lines that can adapt at software speed.
Arda’s financing includes a $160 million Series A at a $1.5 billion valuation, co-led by Altimeter, Accel, and Khosla Ventures, with participation from XYZ Venture Capital, 8VC, SV Angel, and Felicis. The round follows a $72 million seed led by Accel and Founders Fund, with Khosla Ventures and XYZ Venture Capital also participating.
The company’s AI agent reads CAD files and other design artifacts and generates manufacturing-engineering work that would otherwise require teams to determine assembly order, write work instructions, and lay out production stations. Arda said the software is already deployed at Anduril Industries through its ArsenalOS manufacturing software.
According to Arda, basic work instructions that previously took 10 hours can be produced in about 15 minutes, while more complex engineering workflows that could take up to 30 hours have been reduced to roughly 2.5 hours. The company is initially focused on defense and the data-center supply chain, including manufacturers of transformers and electrical equipment.
Arda is also prototyping AI agents that can program robots to execute its assembly plans. The goal is to reduce the months of custom engineering often required to reprogram automation when products change. Arda will use the funding to expand engineering and research, grow deployments across manufacturing sectors, and develop robotics models for automated assembly.
KEY QUOTES:
“I kept asking: why can we design the next generation of products in America, but not build them here? When a product changes every year, the factory has to be able to change with it. Manufacturing leaders told me their products change constantly, and manufacturing engineering can’t keep pace. Their designs change at software speed, but their factories don’t. So, we built the technology platform that solves this problem. Today, U.S. manufacturers designing innovative consumer hardware products at scale can only make them in Asia. Imagine a fully automated version of Shenzhen in West Texas – that’s what we want to make possible.”
Bob McGrew, Founder And CEO Of Arda
“Our manufacturing engineers are doing two hard things at once. They’re keeping up with design teams that iterate constantly, and they’re scaling production to meet demand. Arda helps them get design changes onto the floor faster and catch potential issues sooner. We would be behind on our production goals without it.”
Matt Grimm, Co-Founder And COO Of Anduril Industries

candidates.snippet:

The post Lockheed Martin Secures More Than $226 Million In Defense Contracts For Apache, Electronic Warfare, And F-35 Programs appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Lockheed Martin Secures More Than $226 Million In Defense Contracts For Apache, Electronic Warfare, And F-35 Programs
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Lockheed Martin Secures More Than $226 Million In Defense Contracts For Apache, Electronic Warfare, And F-35 Programs
Lockheed Martin has received four U.S. Department of Defense contract awards and modifications with a combined value of more than $226 million, supporting Apache attack helicopters, naval electronic warfare systems, and multiple F-35 programs.
The largest award is a $117,118,040 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for Generation II radar frequency interferometer post-production support services for Apache attack helicopters. The contract includes cost-no-fee, cost-plus-fixed-fee, and firm-fixed-price components.
Work locations and funding for the Apache-related contract will be determined as individual orders are issued, with the overall effort expected to continue through October 12, 2031. One bid was solicited and one was received. Army Contracting Command at Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity under contract W58RGZ-27-D-A007.
Lockheed Martin’s Rotary and Mission Systems business also received a $74,294,440 firm-fixed-price modification for production of Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program AN/SLQ-32(V)6 systems. The award includes Foreign Military Sales purchases for Canada, representing 52% of the work, and Japan, representing 47%, along with a 1% purchase for the U.S. Coast Guard.
Approximately $38.4 million in fiscal 2026 Canadian FMS funding, $35.4 million in Japanese FMS funding, and $457,768 in fiscal 2025 Coast Guard procurement funding will be obligated. Work will be performed primarily in Liverpool, New York, and Lansdale, Pennsylvania, through September 2029.
Separately, Lockheed Martin received a $16,111,551 modification supporting avionics test capabilities, cybersecurity modernization, and specialized repair infrastructure for the F-35 Integrated Core Processor. The work also covers engineering, program management, planning, readiness reviews, and introduction-to-service activities intended to support fleet operational readiness.
That F-35 effort will be split evenly between McKinney, Texas, and Palm Bay, Florida, and is expected to be completed in January 2029. Approximately $8.1 million each in fiscal 2026 Air Force and Navy aircraft procurement funding will be obligated.
Lockheed Martin Aeronautics also received an $18,789,801 contract modification for system development, demonstration, and integration supporting an F-35 aircraft variant tailored for an unspecified Foreign Military Sales customer.
Approximately 80% of that work will take place in Fort Worth, Texas, with the remaining 20% at undisclosed locations in the continental U.S. Completion is expected in December 2030, with the full $18.8 million being funded by the FMS customer.
Together, the awards expand Lockheed Martin’s work across rotary-wing survivability and sensing, maritime electronic warfare, F-35 cybersecurity and sustainment infrastructure, and international F-35 development.

candidates.text:
Neogen: Q1 Revenue Rises 6.5% To $222.8 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Guidance
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Neogen: Q1 Revenue Rises 6.5% To $222.8 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Guidance
Neogen reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue of $222.8 million, representing growth of 6.5% and core growth of 8.1%.
Food Safety revenue increased 7.4%, including core growth of 8.1%.
Animal Safety revenue increased 4.2%, with core growth of 8%.
Gross margin increased to 47.4% from 45.4%.
Adjusted gross margin was 49.8% compared with 49.5% a year earlier.
Neogen reported a net loss of $11.9 million, or $0.05 per share.
Adjusted net income increased to $17.5 million, or $0.08 per diluted share, from $9.5 million, or $0.04 per share, a year earlier.
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $41.6 million from $35.5 million.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 18.7% from 17%.
Operating cash flow totaled $12.9 million, and free cash flow reached $4.7 million.
Neogen remains on schedule to begin producing saleable Petrifilm products at its Lansing manufacturing site in November 2026.
The company completed validation of its first Petrifilm SKU in August.
Neogen also announced a collaboration and equity investment in Hinalea Imaging to develop hyperspectral digital imaging solutions for food safety and quality inspection.
The company continues working toward the sale of its global Genomics business to Zoetis, with regulatory reviews expected to conclude by the end of December.
Neogen raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to between $885 million and $890 million from $880 million to $885 million.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to $181 million to $183 million from $180 million to $182 million.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our first-quarter results reflect encouraging progress as the changes underway across the organization continue to take hold.”
“We are strengthening commercial discipline, harmonizing our sales operating model, rebuilding our innovation engine and improving the systems and processes that support inventory optimization and customer service.”
Mike Nassif, President and CEO of Neogen

GTCR Leads $200 Million Second Lien Term Loan For Sophos Refinancing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 17, 2026
GTCR Leads $200 Million Second Lien Term Loan For Sophos Refinancing
GTCR has jointly led a $200 million investment in Sophos through a second-lien term loan raised in connection with the refinancing of the cybersecurity company’s existing $2.45 billion first-lien term loan.
Sophos is a portfolio company of Thoma Bravo and provides cybersecurity software and services to approximately 625,000 customers worldwide, primarily small and medium-sized businesses and mid-market organizations.
The company’s offerings include endpoint and network protection as well as managed detection and response services that combine software with outsourced security expertise to monitor customer technology environments.
Sophos expanded its enterprise cybersecurity business in February 2025 through its acquisition of Secureworks, adding an enterprise-focused managed detection and response operation to its platform.
The financing follows the close of GTCR’s inaugural Capital Solutions Fund, which provides customized minority structured investments to established businesses. Other recent Capital Solutions investments include TELUS Health and Solmetex.
GTCR said its familiarity with the cybersecurity sector and ongoing relationship with Thoma Bravo enabled the firm to move quickly on Sophos’ financing requirements. GTCR manages approximately $45 billion in equity capital and has invested more than $35 billion across over 300 companies since its founding in 1980.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are excited to partner with Thoma Bravo and the Sophos management team. Our ongoing dialogue with Thoma Bravo and familiarity with the sector enabled us to move quickly to address Sophos’ financing needs. This transaction reflects our ability to work alongside existing owners and management to structure bespoke capital solutions.”
Jason Prager, Managing Director At GTCR

candidates.text:
Boston Financial Closes $191 Million Affordable Housing Tax Credit Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Boston Financial Closes $191 Million Affordable Housing Tax Credit Fund
Boston Financial has closed Boston Financial Institutional Tax Credits 63 Limited Partnership, a $191 million multi-investor Low-Income Housing Tax Credit fund that will support the creation or preservation of 1,342 affordable rental homes across 12 states.
The fund, known as ITC 63, secured commitments from seven institutional investors and will deploy capital alongside 14 affordable housing developers across 16 communities. The investments will support both new construction projects and preservation efforts for existing affordable housing.
Boston Financial said several developments in the fund will serve populations including seniors, veterans, people with physical or mental disabilities, and formerly unhoused individuals and families.
One of the developments is Choice Landing in Crestwood, Kentucky, which is being developed by nonprofit organization Pillar. The project is expected to provide 72 affordable homes designed to serve adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
Boston Financial estimates that projects supported by ITC 63 will create 2,210 jobs, generate approximately $249 million in wages and business income, and contribute nearly $90 million in tax revenue to local communities.
The fund also benefits from the support of Boston Financial’s parent company, ORIX USA. Boston Financial said ORIX USA’s balance sheet provides additional flexibility and execution capabilities for its affordable housing platform.
Boston Financial has operated in the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit market since the program’s creation in 1986. The firm said it has worked with more than 200 investors to preserve or build over 420,000 affordable homes.
Boston Financial currently manages more than $16.8 billion in affordable housing equity. The firm was founded in 1969 and was acquired by ORIX Corporation USA in 2016.
ORIX USA is a diversified investment and asset management firm focused on credit, real estate, private equity, and managed solutions for middle-market borrowers and investors. The company and its subsidiaries manage $38.8 billion in assets and commitments as of September 22, 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“ITC 63 reflects the strength of the relationships we have built with both our investor and developer partners over many years. We are deeply grateful for the trust our investors place in us and for the extraordinary work our developer partners do every day to bring affordable housing to communities across the country. Their commitment, creativity, and perseverance are making a meaningful difference in the lives of thousands of families, and we are honored to work alongside them in addressing our nation’s housing challenges.”
Rob Golden, CEO Of Boston Financial
“The affordable housing industry succeeds because of collaboration. Each investment in ITC 63 represents a shared commitment among investors, developers, public agencies, and community members to expand and preserve affordable housing opportunities. We are thankful for the confidence our partners continue to place in Boston Financial and proud to help connect capital with high-quality developments that will create lasting impact in communities for years to come.”
John Schromm, Senior Managing Director And Co-Head Of Investor Capital At Boston Financial
“The support of ORIX USA continues to be a meaningful advantage for our clients and partners. Their commitment to affordable housing and willingness to deploy capital alongside our platform helps us deliver more flexible and creative solutions in an increasingly complex market environment. That support strengthens our ability to serve investors, support developers, and ultimately help finance more affordable housing across the country.”
Mark Tolliver, Senior Managing Director And Co-Head Of Investor Capital At Boston Financial

NorthStar Secures Up To $185 Million Growth Financing From Hercules Capital

NorthStar Secures Up To $185 Million Growth Financing From Hercules Capital
NorthStar Medical Technologies has secured a multi-year growth capital facility of up to $185 million from Hercules Capital to expand production of no-carrier-added Actinium-225 and its radiopharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities. The financing includes $100 million available upfront.
NorthStar plans to use the capital to increase isotope production and expand clinical and commercial drug manufacturing at its vertically integrated radiopharmaceutical campus.

NorthStar is developing production capacity around no-carrier-added Actinium-225, an isotope used in targeted alpha therapies for cancer.
In January 2026, NorthStar became the first company to produce commercial-scale no-carrier-added Ac-225 using electron-accelerator technology.
The company also expanded a partnership with Convergent to support late-stage clinical studies and anticipated commercial demand.
More recently, the FDA accepted NorthStar’s Drug Master File for no-carrier-added Ac-225, providing pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies with a regulatory pathway for incorporating the isotope into clinical and commercial radiopharmaceutical programs.
NorthStar plans to transition to a higher-capacity Ac-225 production line later in 2026.
The company currently has supply and manufacturing agreements with more than 30 pharmaceutical and biotechnology customers, including several large developers of Ac-225-based therapies.

“NorthStar is executing on our vision to become the radiopharmaceutical industry’s most comprehensive strategic supply-chain partner. Terra Secures $183.75 Million Refinancing From Monroe Capital For The Offices At THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands
Terra has secured a $183.75 million loan from Monroe Capital’s Real Estate Platform to refinance The Offices at THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands, the recently completed Class A office component of Terra’s wellness-focused mixed-use development in South Florida.
The refinancing follows completion of the 96,000-square-foot office building during the summer of 2026. Office amenities include rooftop meeting and gathering spaces, community gardens, fitness programming, an elevated outdoor courtyard, health coaching, concierge services, and spa privileges. Monroe Capital’s Real Estate Platform provides structured debt and equity financing across property types and markets. The financing expands Monroe’s middle-market real estate activity while providing Terra with long-term capital following the building’s completion and leasing ramp.

candidates.snippet:

The post USDA Launches $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
USDA Launches $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
USDA Launches $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security
The U.S. Department of Agriculture has announced a $180 million investment to launch its Seed Sovereignty Initiative, a program focused on protecting and better utilizing the plant genetic resources that support American agriculture.
The initiative will direct new funding to the USDA Agricultural Research Service’s National Plant Germplasm System, which maintains more than 600,000 accessions representing over 16,000 species.
USDA plans to use the funding to sequence collections of major crops, identify gaps in the country’s agricultural genetic resources, and make more of the genetic information in the system available for agricultural research and crop development.
The department said the initiative is intended to strengthen U.S. agricultural security, support the development of new crop varieties, and help researchers respond more quickly to pests, diseases, and other challenges affecting agricultural production.
The effort comes as USDA seeks to better understand the genetic resources already held in U.S. collections. The department said many of these collections have not yet been fully sequenced, limiting researchers’ ability to systematically identify potentially valuable traits.
Over the next two years, USDA plans to characterize and sequence numerous collections maintained by the National Plant Germplasm System.
The department will also use advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to analyze the resulting information and identify genetic traits that could potentially benefit American agriculture.
The work could help researchers identify plant characteristics associated with areas such as resistance to emerging pests and diseases and provide additional information for the development of new crop varieties.
USDA described the National Plant Germplasm System as an important repository of agricultural genetic diversity. By combining preservation with large-scale sequencing and analysis, the department aims to make the resource more useful for researchers and agricultural producers.
The Seed Sovereignty Initiative is designed to shift USDA’s approach from primarily preserving agricultural genetic resources toward more actively understanding and strategically using them.
USDA also framed the initiative as an agricultural security measure intended to reduce potential dependence on foreign sources for important plant genetic resources and related information.
The department said foreign competitors have been acquiring and sequencing plant genetic resources from around the world while the United States has yet to fully capitalize on the genetic information within its own collections.
Alongside the $180 million initiative, USDA is expanding an existing Memorandum of Understanding with the U.S. Department of Justice related to competition in agricultural input markets.
Seeds will remain a major focus of the expanded partnership.
USDA said the effort with the Justice Department is intended to promote greater transparency, competition and choice for farmers purchasing seeds and other agricultural inputs.
KEY QUOTES:
“Since President Trump returned to office, he has made it clear that we are putting American farmers first. For too long, the future of our crops and our seeds has not been a priority. That changes today, because we cannot afford to depend on foreign adversaries for next year’s crop. Today’s announcement is another example of this administration focusing on the inputs our agriculture industry depends on and ensuring a future where our farmers are the most productive in the world.”
Brooke L. Rollins, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture
“America’s agricultural resources are a strategic national asset. We need to survey our domestic resources, understand where we are vulnerable, and ensure the United States never has to rely on foreign competitors for critical agricultural resources.”
Stephen Vaden, Deputy Secretary of Agriculture
“The National Plant Germplasm System contains tremendous untapped potential for American agriculture. Modern sequencing will allow us to unlock that potential and put it to work for American farmers, providing them a strong advantage.”
Dr. Scott Hutchins, USDA Under Secretary for Research, Education, and Economics and Chief Scientist

candidates.title: Helion Signs LOI For Up To $175 Million In CHIPS Act Funding, Supporting $225 Million Semiconductor Investment
candidates.snippet:
Helion, an Everett, Washington-based fusion energy company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $175 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. Together with an additional $50 million in private investment, the initiative would support approximately $225 million in research and development focused on advanced semiconductor technologies needed for commercial fusion energy.
The post Helion Signs LOI For Up To $175 Million In CHIPS Act Funding, Supporting $225 Million Semiconductor Investment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Helion Signs LOI For Up To $175 Million In CHIPS Act Funding, Supporting $225 Million Semiconductor Investment
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Helion Signs LOI For Up To $175 Million In CHIPS Act Funding, Supporting $225 Million Semiconductor Investment
Helion, an Everett, Washington-based fusion energy company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $175 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. Together with an additional $50 million in private investment, the initiative would support approximately $225 million in research and development focused on advanced semiconductor technologies needed for commercial fusion energy.
The proposed federal funding would be administered through the Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Research and Development Office and support domestic research, semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, and specialized equipment development.
Helion is developing fusion energy systems that use high-power electrical pulses to generate and recover energy. These systems require specialized power semiconductors capable of rapidly switching substantial amounts of electricity while maintaining efficiency, reliability, and long operating lifetimes.
According to Helion, semiconductor devices meeting its technical requirements are currently available only from overseas manufacturers. Developing domestic production capabilities would help the company reduce supply chain dependencies while supporting the commercialization of its fusion technology.
The proposed funding will support research into next-generation high-voltage semiconductors designed to deliver improved electrical efficiency, longer operating lifetimes, and more effective cooling.
More than $100 million of the investment will support semiconductor and advanced packaging research and development in Everett, Washington.
The work is expected to establish substantial power module manufacturing capabilities in the state and support the creation of more than 100 jobs.
A central component of the project involves developing advanced semiconductor packaging techniques that integrate multiple devices into efficient, scalable power modules.
These modules are expected to support the demanding electrical requirements of Helion’s fusion systems, which must repeatedly manage and recover substantial amounts of energy.
Approximately $80 million will support research into semiconductor tooling, design, and manufacturing processes in collaboration with an industry partner in Burlington, Vermont.
The initiative is intended to expand domestic capabilities for producing specialized semiconductor technologies that are important for commercial fusion power plants.
The remaining project resources will support additional improvements in semiconductor packaging and manufacturing automation.
Beyond fusion energy, the technologies being developed could have applications in electrical grid transmission, defense systems, and other industries requiring efficient management of high-power electrical systems.
The proposed federal award follows several developments in Helion’s fusion energy program during 2026.
The company previously secured $500 million in Series G funding and reported becoming the first private fusion energy company to demonstrate deuterium-tritium fusion while achieving plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius.
Helion is also advancing Orion, its first planned fusion power plant, as it works toward commercial deployment of its energy generation technology.
The company expects domestically manufactured power semiconductors to become an important component of its strategy for scaling fusion power generation.
Under the contemplated award structure, the U.S. Department of Commerce would also receive a $175 million nonvoting interest in Helion, based on the company’s most recent Series G preferred stock valuation, upon execution of a definitive award agreement.
The proposed arrangement remains subject to the completion of a final funding agreement.
Helion’s initiative represents an effort to connect federal semiconductor research investment with the development of emerging energy technologies that require specialized domestic manufacturing capabilities.
KEY QUOTES:
“Building fusion power plants at scale requires us to accelerate the development of technologies like semiconductors that are critical to making fusion possible. This award combined with additional private investment, totaling $225 million, will allow Helion to develop and manufacture advanced semiconductors here in the United States that deliver the efficiency, reliability, and performance our systems require. It’s an important investment in both America’s semiconductor manufacturing base and the future of commercial fusion.”
David Kirtley, CEO Of Helion
“The Trump Administration is accelerating American semiconductor innovation to enhance our domestic energy and power resources. This investment expands domestic research, secures critical supply chains, and creates high-paying American jobs.”
Howard Lutnick, U.S. Secretary Of Commerce
“This CHIPS R&D award will support innovation in next-generation semiconductor power modules and devices critical to advancing fusion energy. Accelerating this R&D domestically will support breakthroughs in America’s ability to convert and deliver power to critical applications in defense, grid transmission, and advanced energy generation.”
Bill Frauenhofer, Executive Director Of Semiconductor Investment And Innovation At The U.S. Department Of Commerce

Generate Capital And KeyState Close $154.5 Million Community Solar Tax Equity Fund

Article
Ledgebrook Inc, a technology-driven excess and surplus lines managing general agency, recently completed the close of a $65 million funding round.
The oversubscribed Series C round was led by existing investor The Stephens Group, LLC . Existing investors Duquesne, Brand Foundry, Floating Point, and American Family Ventures participated in the round, alongside new investors including Hummingbird Nomads.
Gage Caligaris, founder and chief executive officer of the Massachusetts-based Ledgebrook, said the funding will allow the MGA to bring in additional talent to grow and enhance its service to wholesale brokers, offer new insurance products through its platform, and participate further in retaining risk on the insurance it is writing on behalf of its carrier partners.
The firm offers general and professional liability products.
Ledgebrook management and employees will continue to be the largest shareholders in the company. Ryan Morrow, managing director at Stephens Group, will join Ledgebrook’s board of directors.
“The round recognizes the momentum in our business. It positions Ledgebrook to truly establish itself as a premier E&S platform, known for consistent execution on our mission to delight wholesale brokers and for bringing together the best of insurance expertise and technology,” Caligaris said.
Ledgebrook was founded in March 2002, when it raised $4.2 million in seed funding. Since the it has raised another $4.6 million, $24 million and $17 million.
Prior to entering insurance, Ledgebrook founder Caligaris traded commodity derivatives at Barclays. His insurance career started in the actuarial program at Liberty Mutual, where he rose to become senior director of new mobility products.
John Mullen serves as president of E&S for Ledgebrook. Mullen has experience as a retail broker and an E&S underwriter and has worked for multiple regional and global insurance carriers. He joined Ledgebrook from Liberty Mutual.
The Stephens Group is a private investment firm with more than $2 billion of private equity assets under management. Since 2006, Stephens Group has invested in more than 50 companies, targeting industries including industrial products and services, specialty distribution, and vertical software.

VIVA Finance, an Atlanta-based financial technology company specializing in payroll-linked consumer lending, has secured a $150 million credit facility from Viola Credit to expand its lending operations and increase access to affordable personal loans.

candidates.text:
VIVA Finance Secures $150 Million Credit Facility From Viola Credit To Expand Payroll-Linked Consumer Lending
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
VIVA Finance Secures $150 Million Credit Facility From Viola Credit To Expand Payroll-Linked Consumer Lending
VIVA Finance, an Atlanta-based financial technology company specializing in payroll-linked consumer lending, has secured a $150 million credit facility from Viola Credit to expand its lending operations and increase access to affordable personal loans.
The financing will provide VIVA Finance with additional lending capacity as it scales its proprietary payroll-linked credit platform and expands its reach among consumers who have limited access to traditional financial products.
Founded by CEO Jack Markwalter, VIVA Finance focuses on helping working Americans access personal loans through a model that integrates repayments directly with employees’ direct deposits.
Rather than relying exclusively on conventional credit evaluation and repayment mechanisms, the company uses its payroll-linked infrastructure to support responsible underwriting and more predictable loan repayments.
This structure is designed to reduce lending risk and enable VIVA to offer competitive loan terms and lower interest rates than many traditional personal loan alternatives.
The company’s approach targets a segment of the consumer finance market that frequently faces challenges obtaining affordable credit through traditional banks and credit bureaus.
These consumers may encounter limited financing options during unexpected expenses or financial emergencies, potentially pushing them toward higher-cost borrowing alternatives.
VIVA aims to address this gap by offering transparent personal loans with repayment arrangements integrated into existing payroll processes.
The new $150 million facility represents a significant expansion of VIVA’s financing resources and is expected to support growth in loan originations, customer acquisition, and distribution partnerships.
The transaction also builds on the company’s recent efforts to expand its presence across the employee benefits and consumer credit ecosystem.
VIVA has developed strategic distribution relationships intended to make its lending products available through platforms already serving working Americans.
One such relationship is its partnership with BenefitHub, which selected VIVA as a preferred personal loan provider for its Benefits+ voluntary benefits platform. The arrangement integrates VIVA’s lending products into employee benefits offerings, potentially broadening its reach among workers seeking financial wellness solutions.
Viola Credit, the lender supporting the new facility, is a global credit asset manager with approximately $5 billion in assets under management.
The firm specializes in asset-based lending and growth capital for technology-enabled financial services companies, including businesses operating across fintech, property technology, and insurance technology.
Viola Credit has completed more than $3.5 billion in asset-based lending transactions across the United States, United Kingdom, Western Europe, and Australia.
Its investment strategy focuses on providing financing to companies developing technologies and business models that challenge traditional financial markets.
For VIVA Finance, the partnership provides access to institutional credit capital and structured finance expertise as it expands its consumer lending business.
The facility also reflects growing institutional interest in lending models that integrate technology, payroll infrastructure, and alternative underwriting approaches to improve credit accessibility.
As VIVA continues to expand its distribution network, the additional financing is expected to strengthen its ability to serve borrowers who may not qualify for favorable terms through conventional lending channels.
The company plans to use the new credit capacity to support its next phase of growth while maintaining its focus on responsible lending, transparent loan products, and improving financial outcomes for working consumers.
KEY QUOTES:
“This strategic partnership with Viola Credit represents a major milestone for VIVA as we continue to scale our platform and expand our market footprint. Viola Credit’s deep expertise in fintech and structured finance makes them an ideal partner for this next phase of our growth. This debt facility empowers us to bring our responsible credit solutions to even more consumers, helping them achieve financial stability and avoid predatory alternatives.”
Jack Markwalter, CEO And Founder Of VIVA Finance
“VIVA Finance has built an exceptional platform that addresses a critical gap in consumer finance. Their innovative approach to payroll integration and commitment to responsible lending have driven impressive performance. We are thrilled to partner with Jack, Hodges and the entire VIVA team to support their continued expansion and mission.”
Michael Chen, Managing Director And Head Of US Investments At Viola Credit

candidates.snippet:
EZO has reached financial close on a €150 million investment-grade, non-recourse senior debt facility to finance the development of more than 3,000 electric vehicle charge points across the UK and Ireland.
The post EZO Secures €150 Million Senior Debt Facility To Accelerate EV Charging Expansion Across The UK And Ireland appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
EZO Secures €150 Million Senior Debt Facility To Accelerate EV Charging Expansion Across The UK And Ireland
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
EZO Secures €150 Million Senior Debt Facility To Accelerate EV Charging Expansion Across The UK And Ireland
EZO has reached financial close on a €150 million investment-grade, non-recourse senior debt facility to finance the development of more than 3,000 electric vehicle charge points across the UK and Ireland.
The financing will support the design, installation, operation, and maintenance of charging infrastructure representing more than 100,000 kW of capacity. Most of the planned sites will be developed under long-term public-sector concession arrangements with features similar to public-private partnerships.
EZO estimates the charge points could generate well over £1 billion in electricity sales during the next 20 years. A portion of that revenue will be shared with public-sector partners, and the chargers are expected to revert to the public sector when the applicable concessions end.
The debt financing was provided by a consortium of lenders including Aberdeen Investments and Standard Life. EZO said the structure is believed to represent the first investment-grade financing of its type for EV chargers across the UK and Ireland, with revenue generated by the assets ring-fenced to repay the debt over a seven-year period.
Ireland-headquartered EZO has been expanding rapidly into mainland Britain and expects the UK to become its primary EV charging market by 2027. The company has secured local authority-backed public charging contracts in the UK with a combined estimated value exceeding £1 billion.
These agreements include a 20-year concession spanning four counties in Northern Scotland and a 15-year concession across four counties in the English Midlands. EZO said it expects to announce additional significant public-sector contracts in the coming months as it pursues opportunities across Scotland, England, and Wales.
The concessions can include access to desirable charging locations, flexible pricing, regional exclusivity, help with permits and grid connections, and, in some cases, public funding to support deployment. Certain arrangements also include revenue-sharing mechanisms designed to return value to the public sector over time.
EZO is majority owned by Rubicon Capital Management and affiliated entities, including Rubicon Capital Advisors. Rubicon initially acquired a 35% interest in EZO in 2020 and has since increased its ownership to more than 60%, including additional shares acquired alongside the latest financing.
The shareholder group has also added Whitehole, a Spain-based family office with experience in electrification technologies supporting sustainable mobility. Rubicon acted as sole financial advisor to EZO on both the debt and equity capital raises and has been retained to explore additional financing options, including a potential IPO in 2028.
KEY QUOTES:
“EZO’s clear ambition is to make reliable public EV charging more accessible for drivers and communities and we have now demonstrated we can successfully compete for some of the largest and most significant EV infrastructure opportunities in the United Kingdom, while continuing to grow our network and partnerships at home in Ireland. Our focus is on working with strong public and private sector partners to build charging networks at scale across Ireland and the UK. The backing of our investment partners gives us the financial strength to deliver on those commitments, continue investing in our people and technology, and pursue the next generation of opportunities in the EV infrastructure market.”
Ollie Chatten, CEO Of EZO
“This funding represents a significant vote of confidence in EZO, its team and the long-term infrastructure partnerships EZO has secured. We understand this to be the first example of the application of this framework of financing in the EV charging sector and it is expected to become the preferred method of financing this collateral going forward. We are delighted to have executed upon these transactions for the company which build on Rubicon’s long-term support for EZO and its growth in the sustainable transport infrastructure market.”
Conor Kelly, CEO Of Rubicon

Rocket Pharmaceuticals Secures Up To $150 Million Credit Facility From Hercules Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Rocket Pharmaceuticals Secures Up To $150 Million Credit Facility From Hercules Capital
Rocket Pharmaceuticals has secured a credit facility of up to $150 million from Hercules Capital to strengthen its financial position and support the development of its cardiovascular genetic medicine pipeline.
Rocket received $35 million at closing and can draw another $35 million during specified periods at its option, subject to the terms of the agreement.
An additional $30 million could become available following achievement of a specified clinical milestone related to Rocket’s Danon disease program.
A final $50 million tranche is subject to approval by Hercules Capital’s investment committee.

Rocket plans to use the financing to support its pivotal Phase 2 study of RP-A501 for Danon disease and advance its broader cardiovascular pipeline.
As of June 30, 2026, Rocket had $283.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments.
Based on its current operating plan, the company expects those resources plus the initial $35 million borrowing to finance operations into the third quarter of 2028.
If Rocket accesses additional amounts available through the Hercules facility, the company said its cash runway could extend into 2029, depending on borrowing conditions, future draws and operating expenditures.
The financing follows Rocket’s sale of a priority review voucher and is intended to diversify its sources of capital as it advances cardiovascular genetic medicine programs.
LifeSci Capital served as Rocket’s financial advisor on the term loan financing, and PJT served as a capital markets advisor.
KEY QUOTES:
“Building on the sale of our priority review voucher, this financing diversifies our sources of capital and strengthens our ability to execute and deliver on our cardiovascular strategy. The staged structure provides flexibility to align additional funding with progress across our programs. We remain focused on allocating capital thoughtfully, executing the pivotal Danon study and advancing genetic medicines for patients with serious inherited heart diseases.”
Gaurav Shah, M.D., CEO of Rocket Pharmaceuticals
“Rocket is advancing toward important milestones across its cardiovascular pipeline, led by the pivotal Danon program. We are pleased to provide a flexible financing solution that supports the Company’s development priorities. We look forward to working alongside Rocket as it builds on its expertise in cardiovascular genetic medicines.”
R. Bryan Jadot, Senior Managing Director and Group Head of Life Sciences at Hercules Capital

By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
EarnIn Secures Additional $150 Million Debt Facility
EarnIn has secured a new $150 million committed warehouse facility from a major Canadian financial institution, expanding the company’s access to institutional financing as it continues to scale its earnings management and payroll platform.
The new facility represents an additional source of committed debt capital for EarnIn and further diversifies the group of financial institutions supporting the company.
Combined with EarnIn’s existing debt investors, the facility increases the company’s total financing capacity to more than $500 million.
EarnIn plans to use the additional borrowing capacity to support its long-term growth strategy and continued expansion across its product portfolio.
The financing provides the company with additional capital flexibility as it works to broaden the services available to workers and employers through its technology platform.
EarnIn develops earnings management and payroll software intended to give workers greater control over when and how they receive money they have already earned.
Its offerings include products providing on-demand earnings and early access to earnings, allowing eligible workers to access compensation on a schedule that more closely matches their individual financial needs.
The company’s broader portfolio also includes Earn Better by EarnIn and EarnIn Payroll, extending EarnIn’s business beyond its core earnings access capabilities.
As EarnIn’s product suite expands, the company is building a broader platform around the movement and management of employee earnings.
The latest warehouse facility provides additional capacity to support that growth while reducing EarnIn’s reliance on any single source of institutional financing.
Bringing a major Canadian financial institution into EarnIn’s lender group also expands the company’s relationships with international banking partners.
EarnIn believes the more diversified lender base will provide greater flexibility and resiliency as the business grows.
The additional financing capacity is also expected to lower EarnIn’s overall cost of capital, potentially providing the company with more efficient funding as it continues investing in its products and scaling its operations.
With more than $500 million of total financing capacity now available through its debt investors, EarnIn has increased the financial resources available to support continued development of its earnings management and payroll offerings.
The facility represents another step in the company’s strategy to build a diversified institutional capital base that can support longer-term growth.
KEY QUOTE:
“Building a diversified capital base gives us greater flexibility and resiliency as we scale. Adding a major international banking partner strengthens our lender base and lowers our cost of capital, positioning EarnIn for continued growth.”
Jacopo Lenzi, Chief Financial Officer of EarnIn

Everforth ECS Secures $148 Million SUNet Contract Extension

candidates.text:
Barings Provides $138.6 Million Mortgage Financing To Refinance Speedway Commerce Center
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Barings Provides $138.6 Million Mortgage Financing To Refinance Speedway Commerce Center
Barings has provided $138.6 million in first mortgage financing to refinance Speedway Commerce Center, a two-building Class A industrial property in Rancho Cucamonga, California.
The financing was provided to Hillwood, an industrial real estate developer and investor with operations across North America and Europe. Speedway Commerce Center consists of two recently constructed industrial buildings totaling approximately 656,000 square feet.
The property is currently 100% leased and includes modern logistics and distribution features such as high clear heights, extensive loading infrastructure, and significant automobile and trailer parking capacity.
Speedway Commerce Center is located in California’s Inland Empire, one of the country’s largest logistics and distribution markets. The property offers immediate access to Interstate 10 and Interstate 15, providing connections throughout Southern California as well as routes to the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.
The transaction expands the relationship between Barings and Hillwood. The two companies have previously worked together on industrial real estate projects in Europe, while the Speedway Commerce Center financing extends that relationship into Hillwood’s U.S. industrial portfolio.
Hillwood is a Perot Company focused on developing, acquiring, and managing institutional-grade industrial real estate. The company operates across North America and European markets including the United Kingdom, Germany, and Poland.
Barings manages approximately $500 billion in assets globally as of September 30, 2026. The alternative asset manager works with institutional, insurance, and wealth clients across credit, real assets, capital solutions, and emerging markets.
Barings is a subsidiary of MassMutual, with MS&AD holding a minority investment in the firm. The Speedway Commerce Center transaction adds to Barings’ commercial real estate lending activity and provides Hillwood with refinancing for a fully leased logistics asset in a strategically important Southern California distribution corridor.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased to provide this financing to Hillwood, a best-in-class industrial developer with a long track record of delivering high-quality logistics assets in key distribution markets. Speedway Commerce Center is a modern, strategically located industrial asset in one of the country’s most sought-after logistics markets, with excellent transportation connectivity and strong long-term demand drivers.”
Tom Cross, Managing Director At Barings
“Hillwood is pleased to extend its relationship with Barings to our US industrial business, following the firms’ work together in Europe. This financing supports the continued, efficient operation of Speedway Commerce Center and builds on Hillwood’s momentum in the Inland Empire.”
Benton Hyatt, Senior Vice President Of Debt Markets At Hillwood

candidates.title: CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing
candidates.snippet:
CBL Properties completed a $135 million refinancing of the mortgage loan secured by West County Center in St. Louis, addressing the company's final near-term debt maturity.
The post CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing
CBL Properties completed a $135 million refinancing of the mortgage loan secured by West County Center in St. Louis, addressing the company’s final near-term debt maturity.
The new non-recourse loan replaces an existing $136.4 million mortgage that had been scheduled to mature in December 2026.
The refinancing has a five-year term and a fixed interest rate of 7.4%.
Following repayment of the existing mortgage and release of escrow balances, CBL received approximately $2 million of net proceeds.
The transaction also eliminates a cash management sweep associated with the previous loan.
CBL estimates that removing that restriction will unlock more than $7 million of annual free cash flow.
The refinancing brings CBL’s new financing activity during 2026 to nearly $1 billion.
The company said its financings this year have generated approximately $45 million of estimated incremental annual cash flow while addressing all near-term maturities.
Separately, a $22.5 million Community Improvement District bond refinancing tied to West County Center closed in September.
That transaction generated $4.6 million of cash for CBL and another $2.6 million earmarked for property improvements.
Planned projects include upgraded security cameras, escalator replacement, lighting improvements, and parking-area upgrades.
West County Center is a nearly 1.2 million-square-foot regional mall generating annual sales exceeding $900 per square foot.
Its anchors include Macy’s, Dick’s Sporting Goods, and Missouri’s only Nordstrom location.
KEY QUOTES:
“We have completed nearly $1.0 billion in new financing activity in 2026, addressing all of our near-term maturities. These financings have unlocked approximately $45.0 million in estimated incremental annual cash flow and removed maturity risk for the next few years.”
Ben Jaenicke, EVP and CFO of CBL Properties
“The terms we achieved on West County Center reflect the strong leasing and performance of the property in recent years and support the continued financial flexibility of our balance sheet.”
Ben Jaenicke, EVP and CFO of CBL Properties

candidates.snippet:
QumulusAI, an Atlanta-based provider of AI cloud infrastructure, has expanded its equipment lease financing arrangement with Tech Finance Co. (TFC) to approximately $123.6 million, up from the previously announced $26 million in May 2026.
The post QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
QumulusAI, an Atlanta-based provider of AI cloud infrastructure, has expanded its equipment lease financing arrangement with Tech Finance Co. (TFC) to approximately $123.6 million, up from the previously announced $26 million in May 2026.
The expanded financing supports the acquisition and deployment of NVIDIA Blackwell graphics processing units that QumulusAI announced purchasing in May and July 2026.
The financing structure allows the company to expand its computing infrastructure without issuing additional equity, using equipment leases alongside customer deposits to fund hardware purchases.
Under the arrangement, TFC finances approximately 85% to 90% of equipment costs associated with each lease schedule. Customer deposits cover the remaining portion.
The leases have three-year terms, with amortized payment schedules implying an annualized interest rate in the high-single-digit range.
At the end of each lease term, QumulusAI has the option to purchase the underlying equipment or return it without retaining an ongoing equipment obligation.
The structure provides flexibility for managing computing hardware investments in an industry where AI accelerators are expensive and technological capabilities are evolving rapidly.
QumulusAI operates a distributed AI cloud infrastructure platform focused on providing high-performance GPU computing resources for enterprise and AI development workloads.
Its infrastructure strategy emphasizes inference-first deployments, with computing capacity installed in response to customer demand rather than relying exclusively on speculative data center expansion.
The company operates across a network of data center locations, enabling it to bring computing resources closer to customers and provide flexible alternatives to traditional centralized cloud platforms.
NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture is designed to support demanding AI workloads, including large-scale model inference and other accelerated computing applications.
For QumulusAI, the ability to obtain financing for these systems is an important component of its strategy to expand available GPU capacity while managing the substantial capital requirements associated with AI infrastructure.
The company has used a combination of customer deposits, cash generated by existing computing deployments, and financing partnerships to support its growth.
The expanded TFC relationship reinforces that approach by linking infrastructure spending to contracted demand.
Tech Finance Co. has provided equipment financing services since 2004 and began financing AI-related equipment in 2021.
The company specializes in financing structures that help businesses acquire technology infrastructure while reducing upfront capital requirements.
The $123.6 million arrangement gives QumulusAI additional capacity to deploy Blackwell-based computing resources without diluting existing shareholders through new equity issuance.
KEY QUOTES:
“We have funded our GPU deployments the same way since the start. With customer deposits, cash from capacity already in production and financing partners like TFC. Expanding this facility keeps that model in place as we scale, so the hardware is paid for by contracted demand rather than by our shareholders.”
Michael Maniscalco, CEO Of QumulusAI
“In AI infrastructure, getting the hardware is only part of the challenge; the harder part is often having the capital ready to pay for it and put it to work fast. We structured the financing so QumulusAI could turn demand into deployed hardware without waiting on capital, and move as fast as the market is moving.”
Brent Clarbour, Vice President Of Vendor Relationships At Tech Finance Co.

candidates.text:
Unison Energy Secures $120 Million Credit Facility From JPMorgan
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Unison Energy Secures $120 Million Credit Facility From JPMorgan
Unison Energy has closed a five-year, $120 million secured credit facility with JPMorgan Chase Bank to support the continued growth of its distributed energy and on-site power generation portfolio.
The facility also includes an additional $50 million accordion option, subject to credit approval, potentially providing Unison with additional capital as it develops and constructs new distributed energy projects.
Unison plans to use the financing both for its existing portfolio of energy assets and to fund development and construction of new projects.
The Greenwich, Connecticut-based company provides on-site power generation through an Energy-as-a-Service model for critical infrastructure facilities across North America.
Its customers include hospitals, data centers, food and beverage companies, industrial facilities, supply chain and logistics businesses, and hospitality organizations.
Unison designs, builds, owns and operates microgrids at customer locations. Its model is designed to reduce energy costs, improve resiliency during grid outages and lower carbon emissions without requiring customers to make upfront capital investments in the systems.
JPMorgan structured the new financing as a flexible warehouse-style facility.
The structure allows Unison to add and remove qualified projects from the borrowing base, subject to specified credit and operational requirements. That flexibility is intended to give the company a financing platform that can expand alongside its portfolio rather than requiring separate financing arrangements for each new project.
In addition to serving as lender, JPMorgan will act as Unison’s Hedging Provider and Depositary Bank for the transaction.
The financing follows a series of changes at Unison since Tiger Infrastructure Partners acquired the company in 2024.
Mariko Meier was appointed CEO in January 2026, while Al Dahya joined the company as CFO earlier this year.
Tiger Infrastructure has been working to expand Unison’s asset base, management team, and capital resources since making its investment.
The company has added new projects for multiple customers while investing in additional personnel to support its growth.
Unison and its investors see favorable conditions developing for distributed energy infrastructure as electricity demand rises and customers place greater emphasis on power reliability and resilience.
Those trends are particularly important for critical infrastructure and energy-intensive facilities where outages or constrained grid capacity can create significant operational risks.
The JPMorgan facility provides Unison with additional capacity to build new on-site generation projects as it seeks to expand its presence across those markets.
Support: Norton Rose Fulbright advised Unison on the financing. Milbank advised JPMorgan, while Black & Veatch served as Independent Engineer.
KEY QUOTES:
“Closing this financing with JPMorgan is a stepping stone for us, not an end point. Now the real work begins: putting this capital to work growing Unison and building new projects that power some of America’s most important places. We are excited to partner with JPMorgan who can bring the capital we need to support our long-term growth ambitions.”
Al Dahya, CFO of Unison Energy
“JPMorgan’s support of Unison is a clear validation of the Unison strategy and the new leadership at the company. Unison is a growing company with positive macro tailwinds behind its business model, including surging power demand and an increasingly unstable grid. Since Tiger Infrastructure’s initial investment in 2024, we have implemented our value creation playbook focused on assets, people and capital. Unison has increased its asset base with new projects for multiple customers and we have invested heavily in the company’s human capital to help it scale. This credit facility reflects the company’s maturing capital structure and will enhance Unison’s ability to serve its varied customer base.”
Marc Blair, COO and Senior Managing Director of Tiger Infrastructure Partners
“JPMorgan is grateful for the opportunity to work with Unison Energy and Tiger Infrastructure Partners on this important financing. This transaction highlights the strength of our partnership, and we look forward to supporting Unison’s next phase of growth.”
Allyson Goetschius, Executive Director of JPMorgan

candidates.title: Town Raises $108M Series B at a $1B Valuation to Bring AI Assistants to Whole Teams
candidates.snippet: Town Raises $108M Series B at a $1B Valuation to Bring AI Assistants to Whole Teams The Manila Times
candidates.text:
Press
Town Raises $108M at a $1B Valuation to Bring AI Assistants to Whole Teams
Now valued at more than $1B, Town extends its AI work assistant from individuals to whole teams
Tony Vincent
Jean-Denis Greze Published October 19, 2026
4 min
SAN FRANCISCO — October 19, 2026 — Town, the AI assistant built for teamwork, today announced a $108 million Series B. The round was co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures. Existing investors a16z and First Round Capital also participated, along with Better Tomorrow Ventures, Precedent.vc, Scribble Ventures, Serena Ventures, Sparked Ventures, and notable angels, including Brendan Foody, Josh Silverman, Romain Huet, Scott Belsky, Steve Bartel, Taro Fukuyama, and Varun Anand. The round values the company at $1 billion.
Town is Built for Your Most Critical Work
AI personal assistants are beginning to handle the edges of everyday life: dinner reservations, flight changes, subscription cancellations. Those tasks lighten our mental load, but they sit on the margins of the day. Town is built for the center of it. Work fills eight or more hours of most people’s day, and it’s also how people make a living. So when context gets lost or decisions stall, the cost is highest at work.
At work, AI has already made each person far more productive on their own. But most work depends on other people: an updated model from finance, access to an app from an ops lead, input from the field sales team. The faster each person moves, the more they need from their teammates, and work slows to a crawl while they’re waiting for each other.
Today’s AI assistants can’t close that gap. A personal AI assistant knows its user but can’t work directly with the rest of the team. A team bot can see shared channels but can’t see anyone’s inbox or preferences, so it never really knows any one person. Neither can work well with people outside the company.
With Town, each person gets an AI assistant, called a Townie. A Townie connects to its person’s email, docs, calendar, and the core systems they work in. It learns their relationship context, projects, and voice, and takes work off their plate.
How Townies Work Together
Now, for the first time, those assistants can work directly with each other to move projects forward. They ask each other questions, connect the dots, and hand off work. Each Townie still works for its person. A Townie shares only what that person would share, asks permission when needed, and brings them the decisions that need their uniquely human eye. Townies can also work directly with customers, partners, and candidates outside the company over email and text.
Teams can also enable shared workflows. For example, when BizOps adds new fields to the competitor battle cards, it updates the team’s call-prep process once. From then on, every rep’s Townie preps calls with the new competitive analysis built in, updating materials to reflect the improved positioning.
“More people are trusting AI assistants with real tasks, and work is where they need the most help,” said Jean-Denis Greze, co-founder and CEO of Town. “Each Townie learns how its person works so it can take on their core work. Townies can ask each other questions and hand off work, so no one is stuck waiting. AI has made each of us faster on our own. Now, it can make teams faster together.”
Built for Business
Each company owns the context its Townies build. Town takes the scattered knowledge that exists across the business and turns it into a shared, compounding asset that helps your business thrive. Instead of slowing down as you scale, your company grows smarter and faster.
Town leverages models from all the major AI labs, using the best model for each task and keeping customers from getting locked into one lab. By default, nothing a customer connects trains a model. Town is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and has a public data processing agreement (DPA).
“In 2008 Menlo backed Siri to transform the user interface to the Internet. In 2026, the technology has arrived, and the opportunity is bigger than ever,” said Shawn Carolan, Partner at Menlo Ventures. “But focused companies pick their battles, and Town has wisely chosen business over pleasure. A longer way to go, with more demanding requirements, but ultimately the larger. Menlo couldn’t be more excited to support Jean-Denis, Tony and the team on this journey.”
Growth
Town launched publicly in June 2026 with a $55 million Series A and reached 7-digits of ARR in weeks. Since July, paying customers have grown 4x and paying teams are up 9x.
About Town
Town is an AI assistant built for teamwork. Each person gets a Townie that learns their people, projects, and voice, and takes work off their plate. Townies work together across a company and with customers, partners, and candidates. Town is backed by Forerunner Ventures, Menlo Ventures, a16z, and First Round Capital. Learn more at town.com .

candidates.title: Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank
candidates.snippet:
Newegg Commerce has closed a $100 million senior credit facility led and arranged by East West Bank, giving the technology e-commerce company additional financial flexibility as it continues investing in growth initiatives.
The post Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank
Newegg Commerce has closed a $100 million senior credit facility led and arranged by East West Bank, giving the technology e-commerce company additional financial flexibility as it continues investing in growth initiatives.
The facility includes participation from a syndicate of lenders and replaces Newegg’s previous credit arrangements, which matured in August 2026.
Newegg said the expanded financing strengthens its financial position and provides additional flexibility as the company manages ongoing supply dynamics and continues investing across its business.
The transaction also extends the longstanding relationship between Newegg and East West Bank. The lending group cited Newegg’s business model, operating performance, and future growth opportunities as factors supporting the financing.
Newegg plans to continue directing resources toward e-commerce innovation, AI-enabled capabilities, and deeper partnerships with technology brands, suppliers, and customers worldwide.
The company operates an e-commerce platform serving technology enthusiasts, businesses, gamers, PC builders, and IT professionals. Its product portfolio includes PC hardware, consumer electronics, gaming peripherals, servers, workstations, and AI infrastructure.
Newegg also provides services for independent sellers, including marketing, supply chain, and technical solutions intended to help third-party businesses expand through its platform.
The new credit facility gives Newegg additional borrowing capacity as it invests in those areas and navigates changing conditions across the technology supply chain.
Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Diamond Bar, California, Newegg Commerce is publicly traded on Nasdaq under the ticker NEGG. The company has operated for more than two decades and has expanded from its core PC hardware business into a broader technology commerce and services platform.
The $100 million facility expands Newegg’s prior credit arrangements and provides additional capital to support its strategic priorities and ongoing operations.
KEY QUOTES:
“Closing this new facility is an important step for Newegg in further strengthening our financial position and provides us with greater flexibility to navigate ongoing supply dynamics while we continue to invest in growth. We appreciate the commitment and partnership from East West Bank and the rest of our lending group, and the confidence they have shown in Newegg.”
Christina Ching, Chief Financial Officer Of Newegg
“We are pleased to provide this important debt financing to Newegg, a longstanding client in the e-commerce space. This transaction reflects the strength of our relationship, our confidence in their business model, and our commitment to delivering tailored capital solutions to leading growth companies like Newegg. We look forward to supporting their next phase of expansion.”
East West Bank statement

candidates.title: Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation
candidates.snippet:
Meshy surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, up approximately 100-fold from $1 million in less than two years.
The post Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation
Meshy surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, up approximately 100-fold from $1 million in less than two years.
The milestone follows Meshy’s nearly $400 million Series B financing in July 2026 at a $1.5 billion valuation.
Meshy said the financing was the largest funding round to date for an AI 3D company.
The company now serves more than 15 million registered users and over 3,000 companies and educational institutions worldwide.
Users have generated more than 100 million 3D models through the platform.
Meshy said half of the world’s 10 most valuable companies by market capitalization or private valuation are customers.
Approximately 200 Fortune Global 500 companies also use the platform.
Meshy develops multimodal foundation models that generate production-ready 3D assets from text and images.
The company’s technology is used for gaming, film, education, and 3D printing.
Meshy recently released Meshy 7.1, which supports Ultra 4K geometry generation.
The company also open-sourced its alignment benchmark suite for image-to-3D generation.
Alongside the ARR milestone, Meshy launched official iOS and Android applications powered by Meshy 7.
The mobile app enables users to convert photos, sketches, and text into textured 3D models while providing printability checks, AI repair, augmented reality previews, and exports in formats including STL, GLB, FBX, OBJ, USDZ, and 3MF.
Meshy was founded by Ethan Hu, who holds a Ph.D. from MIT.
KEY QUOTES:
“Surpassing $100 million in ARR in under two years reflects the growing demand for AI-powered 3D creation.”
“From game studios and film teams to educators and home 3D printing enthusiasts, our customers are showing just how broadly this technology can be used—and how much opportunity lies ahead.”
Faye Pan, Vice President of Growth at Meshy

candidates.text:
Stable Invests $100 Million To Support Launch Of Alchemist Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
Stable Invests $100 Million To Support Launch Of Alchemist Capital
Stable Asset Management is providing a $100 million seed investment to support the launch and long-term growth of Alchemist Capital, a new biotechnology investment firm founded by Andy Tran.
New York-based Alchemist plans to invest in biotechnology companies across public and private markets.
Its strategy combines fundamental scientific research with a proprietary AI-native research and monitoring engine intended to make biotechnology investing more systematic and scalable.
The firm is targeting companies developing first-in-class or best-in-class medicines and emerging businesses that could become multi-product biotechnology platforms.
Alchemist will focus on differentiated science, potential clinical benefits, and sustainable competitive advantages.
The firm is also targeting companies using AI, computing, and data to transform drug discovery and development, along with supporting life sciences tools and technology platforms.
Tran previously helped build biotechnology investment practices at Andreessen Horowitz and Matrix Capital.
His investment experience includes Tmunity, EQRx, Erasca, Freenome, Genesis Therapeutics, Cartography Biosciences, and Maze Therapeutics.
Tran served on Maze’s board from the company’s early stages through its 2025 IPO.
Before entering investing, he studied bioengineering and computer science at Harvard and conducted CRISPR gene-editing research under Harvard Medical School professor George Church.
Stable manages approximately $5.3 billion and has supported the development of 46 alternative asset managers.
KEY QUOTES:
“Alchemist is exactly the kind of ambitious, differentiated platform Stable was built to support. Andy brings a rare combination of scientific depth, firsthand experience building biotech investment platforms, and conviction in the opportunity ahead.”
Erik Serrano Berntsen, CEO of Stable
“We established Alchemist to combine deep scientific and medical understanding with purpose-built computational infrastructure, giving us a more comprehensive diligence process and a clearer view of how new evidence changes an investment thesis. The engine doesn’t replace the fundamental work. It supercharges it.”
“Stable has helped more founders build institutions than almost anyone in asset management. That’s why we are excited to partner from day one.”
Andy Tran, Founder of Alchemist Capital
