candidates.text:
Spellbook: Interview With Co-Founder And CEO Scott Stevenson About Legal AI, M&A And $100 Million ARR Growth
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Spellbook: Interview With Co-Founder And CEO Scott Stevenson About Legal AI, M&A And $100 Million ARR Growth
Spellbook is the leading AI infrastructure for contract workflows that is deeply integrated into Microsoft Word and Google Docs and supports contract drafting, review, negotiation, and transactional workflows, saving teams upwards of 84% on contract reviews or a full day per week on average. The company launched the first generative AI tool for lawyers in 2022 and now serves more than 5,000 in-house teams and law firms across 80 countries. Pulse 2.0 interviewed Spellbook Co-Founder and CEO Scott Stevenson to learn more about the company’s growth, its $40 million debt financing from RBCx, acquisition strategy, legal AI market consolidation, and plans to reach $100 million in annual recurring revenue.
Scott Stevenson’s Background
Screenshot
When asked about his background, Stevenson shared:
I’m CEO and co-founder of Spellbook. The short version is that at a previous startup, half our angel round went to routine legal paperwork. Most expensive bill we’d ever seen, least value delivered.
And that experience isn’t unusual: 60% of small businesses won’t even call a lawyer because they can’t afford to. That stuck with me.
We started the company in 2018, originally called Rally, and launched the first generative AI tool for lawyers in summer 2022, a few months before ChatGPT came out.
So we’ve been at this longer than most people realize. Now we have more than 5,000 customers in 80 countries, and are beginning to gain industry recognition, including the inaugural Built in Canada Rocketship award for Canada’s fastest-growing company and my inclusion on Financial Post and Caldwell Partners International Inc.’s Canada’s Top 40 Under 40 list.
$40 Million Debt Financing
When asked what drove the decision to raise $40 million in debt financing from RBCx so soon after Spellbook’s $50 million Series B, Stevenson explained:
Growth has accelerated faster than what we expected.
We’re on track to hit $100 million ARR this year after tripling revenue in 2025, and we started seeing a real opportunity to acquire smaller competitors.
The market matured very quickly, leaving competitors with good products unable to get a real foothold in the market.
Debt was the right instrument for that since it lets us move on M&A without diluting our shareholders.
RBCx got it and moved quickly.
Deploying The New Capital
When asked how Spellbook plans to deploy the new capital, particularly around pursuing up to five acquihires over the next two years, Stevenson said:
Acquisitions are the primary focus.
The legal AI market matured really quickly, and a lot of smaller companies spun up.
We expect to do roughly five deals over two years, around $60 million in total spend, though that could shift.
We’re already looking closely at two targets right now, and once every two weeks or so we hear from a company that wants to be acquired.
We’re also hiring aggressively with plans to expand our team to 250 people by year-end, which doubles our team.
Acquisition Targets
When asked what types of companies or capabilities Spellbook is targeting through these acquihires, Stevenson explained:
Contract-focused legal AI companies, primarily.
Teams that have built something meaningful in adjacent parts of the contract lifecycle.
We want talent and technology that help us expand beyond review into the full scope of transactional work.
The key filter is teams that share our philosophy: build AI that fits inside existing workflows rather than asking lawyers to change how they operate.
Early-Mover Advantage
When asked how launching a generative AI tool for lawyers before ChatGPT shaped Spellbook’s growth and product development, Stevenson said:
The biggest thing it gave us is data.
We’ve analyzed over 10 million contracts now, and our suggestion acceptance rate has gone from 5% to 55%.
That feedback loop compounds: every time a lawyer, HR, procurement, or sales professional accepts or rejects a suggestion, the system gets smarter and more calibrated to how they actually work.
That’s very hard to replicate if you’re starting from scratch today.
It also gave us conviction early about what works.
We knew lawyers and in-house weren’t going to adopt some new platform. They needed AI that lives in Microsoft Word and Google Docs, where they already spend their day.
Same philosophy as Cursor for developers. That’s been core to our product from the start.
Path To $100 Million ARR
When asked about the key drivers behind Spellbook’s rapid growth and path toward $100 million ARR, Stevenson explained:
A few things working together.
Product-led growth is a big one: time to value is about two minutes.
Lawyers try it and immediately start catching things they would have missed.
The expansion into in-house legal has been huge too.
In-house teams now represent more than 50% of revenue since we launched Playbooks in 2024.
That opened us up beyond law firms to HR, procurement and sales teams — anyone involved in getting a contract to signing.
And the market has shifted.
Clients now ask their lawyers what AI tools they’re using. It’s table stakes.
That demand pull has been a meaningful tailwind.
Looking ahead, 2027 is about continuing to prove our thesis as a proactive agent since we just launched Autonomous Contract Management (ACM), the first AI-native CLM alternative that supports the entire contract lifecycle, from intake to negotiation to analysis, all while remaining proactive with reminders and risk monitoring to alleviate the cognitive load for teams. ACM works on day one and runs autonomously in the background, intaking and reviewing contracts so deals keep moving forward.
To get there we’re doubling headcount this year to build a world-class team that can meet the demand we’re seeing, including appointing the former S

candidates.text:
Fortitude Announces Up To $100 Million BITMAIN Zcash Miner Commitment And Expands DCG Credit Facility To $70 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Fortitude Announces Up To $100 Million BITMAIN Zcash Miner Commitment And Expands DCG Credit Facility To $70 Million
Fortitude Mining has entered into a letter of intent with BITMAIN providing priority allocation for next-generation Zcash mining equipment through a potential purchase commitment of up to $100 million.
The commitment is indicative and non-binding and remains subject to execution of a definitive purchase agreement once BITMAIN releases final equipment specifications and pricing.
The arrangement allows Fortitude to increase the size of the contemplated purchase, subject to BITMAIN’s approval and equipment availability, or reduce it following the official launch of the new hardware.
Fortitude expects BITMAIN’s next-generation Zcash mining equipment to begin shipping during the second quarter of 2027.
The company currently operates approximately 4.7 GSol/s of Equihash hashrate and has more than 60 MW of contracted power capacity across seven locations in South Dakota, Nebraska, Texas and New York.
Fortitude has also previously ordered 9,000 BITMAIN ANTMINER Z15 Pro miners.
The latest agreement is designed to give the company early access to another generation of equipment as it seeks to increase its Zcash mining capacity.
To support the potential purchase, Fortitude also expanded its credit facility with parent company Digital Currency Group from $50 million to $70 million.
The facility now provides approximately $42.7 million of remaining borrowing capacity before a planned new draw.
The BITMAIN letter of intent requires Fortitude to make a refundable deposit equal to 20% of the contemplated commitment, or $20 million.
Fortitude plans to draw that amount under the DCG credit facility, with the funding expected to be provided in ZEC and subsequently liquidated to fund the deposit.
After the planned $20 million borrowing, Fortitude expects to have borrowed approximately $47.3 million under the facility and have approximately $22.7 million of remaining capacity.
DCG may also provide additional ZEC financing outside the upsized facility to support Fortitude’s capital requirements and growth initiatives through fiscal 2027.
Fortitude is separately progressing with its previously announced proposed business combination with HeartSciences.
If completed, that transaction is expected to make Fortitude a publicly traded company and provide additional access to the capital markets as it expands its Zcash mining and energy infrastructure platform.
KEY QUOTES:
“Fortitude’s vision is to be the largest vertically-integrated Zcash mining platform. Securing a priority supply allocation for BITMAIN’s next-generation equipment, alongside our existing operating base and previously announced Z15 Pro order, positions Fortitude to expand its fleet with industry-leading hardware as it becomes available. We believe there is a significant opportunity to invest in Zcash mining infrastructure today, and Fortitude is well positioned to lead that buildout.”
Jaime Leverton, CEO of Fortitude
“Fortitude is one of the first Zcash mining companies to publicly announce an LOI for our next-generation Zcash mining equipment at this scale, making this an important milestone for both companies and for the Zcash mining ecosystem. This relationship brings together BITMAIN’s leadership in mining technology and engineering with Fortitude’s vertically integrated power, infrastructure and operating capabilities. We see a strong opportunity to build a long-term relationship with Fortitude as the Zcash mining ecosystem continues to scale.”
BITMAIN Executive

Lattis Management Secures More Than $100 Million In Second Close
Lattis Management has completed a second capital close for its flagship Lattis LP vehicle and launched infrastructure-focused Lattis Infrastructure LP, securing more than $100 million in investor commitments during the early part of the third quarter.

candidates.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification
candidates.snippet:
Rainmaker Technology has raised $100 million in Series B funding to expand its atmospheric research organization and reduce the cost of producing freshwater through cloud seeding.
The post Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification
Rainmaker Technology has raised $100 million in Series B funding to expand its atmospheric research organization and reduce the cost of producing freshwater through cloud seeding.
The round included investments from NOA VC, Upfront Ventures, DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital, and Dream Ventures.
El Segundo, California-based Rainmaker develops weather modification technology designed to increase precipitation by flying weather-resistant drones into winter storm clouds and releasing small amounts of silver iodide.
The particles provide surfaces around which ice crystals can form and grow before falling as rain or snow.
Rainmaker has also developed radar and validation systems intended to measure how much additional precipitation is attributable to individual seeding operations.
The company said it became the first private company to physically validate the results of cloud seeding operations earlier in 2026.
Over four months, Rainmaker recorded 82 seeding signatures that it said directly linked precipitation to individual flights.
Those events accounted for more than 145 million verified gallons of freshwater, equivalent to nearly the annual water consumption of 1,800 U.S. households, according to the company.
In August, Rainmaker said it produced 19 million gallons of water in approximately three hours near Homer, Alaska.
The Series B proceeds will support a significant expansion of Rainmaker’s research organization, which includes atmospheric scientists, radar and satellite specialists and materials scientists.
Research will focus on improving decisions around which clouds should be seeded, when operations should occur, how much seeding material should be deployed and where resulting precipitation would provide the greatest benefits for watersheds, agriculture, ecosystems and industry.
Rainmaker also plans to support research at national laboratories and fund weather modification research at U.S. universities.
The company expects its production economics to improve as deployments scale and additional drone teams operate simultaneously.
Rainmaker expects its water production costs during the November 2026 through April 2027 season to fall below many alternative sources of incremental supply, including desalination and programs that pay farmers to leave fields unplanted.
Beyond water production, Rainmaker ultimately plans to apply similar weather modification and atmospheric technologies to other agricultural challenges, including hail damage and poor soil conditions.
KEY QUOTES:
“The future of water is the future of everything. With this historic investment in weather modification technology, Rainmaker will continue to conduct frontier atmospheric research, cloud seed to end drought in the American west, and develop the tech stack that will make the earth more habitable for generations to come.”
Augustus Doricko, Founder and CEO of Rainmaker Technology

candidates.text:
Huntington Ingalls Receives $99.1 Million Navy Contract Modification For DDG 1002 Sea Trials
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Huntington Ingalls Receives $99.1 Million Navy Contract Modification For DDG 1002 Sea Trials
Huntington Ingalls has received a $99.1 million modification to a previously awarded U.S. Navy contract to support sea trials associated with DDG 1002.
The $99,089,863 modification applies to contract N00024-22-C-2300 and increases the contract ceiling to incorporate the DDG 1002 Sea Trials scope. The additional work represents another phase of activity tied to the vessel as the Navy advances testing and evaluation efforts.
Approximately 95% of the work will be performed in Pascagoula, Mississippi, where Huntington Ingalls maintains major shipbuilding operations. The remaining 5% will be distributed across other locations, with each individual location accounting for less than 1% of the total work.
The Navy expects work covered by the modification to be completed by October 2028.
At the time of the award, approximately $59.3 million in shipbuilding and conversion funding will be obligated. The funding includes $28,355,651 in fiscal 2025 Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy funds, representing approximately 48% of the amount being obligated, and $30,959,605 in fiscal 2026 Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy funds, representing the remaining 52%.
The obligated funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year, allowing the Navy to apply the funding across the planned execution period for the contract work.
The modification specifically adds the DDG 1002 Sea Trials scope to the existing contract ceiling. Sea trials are a critical part of the shipbuilding and testing process, providing an opportunity to evaluate vessel performance and associated systems under operational conditions before later program milestones.
The award continues Huntington Ingalls’ work supporting U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs from its Pascagoula operations, which will account for the overwhelming majority of activity under the modification.
The Program Acquisition Executive Maritime in Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity for the award.

ADC Therapeutics Raises $86.6 Million And Restructures Debt To Extend Cash Runway Into 2029
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
ADC Therapeutics Raises $86.6 Million And Restructures Debt To Extend Cash Runway Into 2029
ADC Therapeutics announced a comprehensive financial restructuring that includes an $86.6 million private placement, amendments to its HealthCare Royalty agreement, and a refinancing of its senior secured loan. The company said the combined transactions are designed to strengthen its balance sheet, reduce leverage, increase strategic flexibility, and extend its expected cash runway into 2029.
ADC Therapeutics entered into securities purchase agreements with institutional investors including new investor Bain Capital Life Sciences and existing investors Redmile, TCGX, and Nantahala Capital.
The $86.6 million private investment in public equity financing includes 12.9 million common shares priced at $1.42 per share.
ADC Therapeutics is also selling pre-funded warrants to purchase 48.1 million common shares at $1.32 per warrant, reflecting the common share price less the CHF 0.08 exercise price.
Gross proceeds are expected to total approximately $86.6 million, assuming cash exercise of the pre-funded warrants.
The PIPE is expected to close on October 22, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
ADC Therapeutics plans to use the proceeds to support continued development of ZYNLONTA, including Phase 3 trials in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and marginal zone lymphoma.
The funds will also support working capital, general corporate purposes, and balance sheet strengthening.
Separately, ADC Therapeutics amended its royalty agreement with entities managed by HealthCare Royalty Management.
HealthCare Royalty has provided $300 million of funding to ADC Therapeutics to date.
The amendment eliminates a $150 million payment that otherwise would have been triggered solely by a change of control.
The amended agreement also reduces the amount of third-party indebtedness ADC Therapeutics and its subsidiaries are permitted to incur to $50 million.
The amendment modifies approximately 9.8 million warrants previously issued to HealthCare Royalty, reducing their exercise price from $3.813 per share to $0.10 per share.
The changes also introduce beneficial ownership limitations and remove certain transfer restrictions that had applied through January 1, 2028.
The HealthCare Royalty amendment is conditioned on completion of the PIPE by October 31, 2026, along with effectiveness of the amended loan agreement.
ADC Therapeutics also amended its senior secured loan agreement with Blue Owl Opportunistic Master Fund I and participating lenders.
The company plans to prepay $70 million of term loan principal, along with related accrued interest, fees, and premiums.
Following the prepayment, the outstanding principal balance will be reduced to $50 million.
The remaining $50 million will be payable at maturity in August 2029 unless accelerated earlier.
The revised loan eliminates subsequent scheduled principal amortization and removes the minimum liquidity covenant.
It also establishes a minimum trailing four-quarter U.S. ZYNLONTA sales covenant of $65 million beginning with the quarter ending December 31, 2026.
Warrants covering 527,295 shares that were issued to lenders in 2022 will also be amended.
Their exercise price will decline from $8.30 per share to $1 per share, subject to effectiveness of the loan amendment.
ADC Therapeutics expects ZYNLONTA net product revenue of approximately $21 million for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.
The company reported approximately $189.2 million of cash and cash equivalents as of September 30.
On a pro forma basis, after estimated net PIPE proceeds of approximately $76.3 million and the approximately $69.6 million loan prepayment including fees, ADC Therapeutics would have held approximately $196 million of cash and cash equivalents as of that date.
Jefferies, Guggenheim Securities, and Cantor are serving as placement agents for the PIPE.
Davis Polk & Wardwell and Homburger are serving as legal advisors to ADC Therapeutics.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased to announce this robust set of improvements to our capital structure which reflect confidence in ZYNLONTA’s growth potential from both long-standing and new investors as well as from HCR and our lenders.”
“These efforts extend our expected cash runway and increase strategic optionality, as we approach much anticipated LOTIS-7 and MZL data abstracts in early November with presentations in December at the 68th American Society of Hematology Annual Meeting.”
Ameet Mallik, CEO of ADC Therapeutics

Walker & Dunlop Arranges $86.5 Million Refinancing For Chasen In Richmond
Walker & Dunlop arranged $86.5 million in bridge financing for Chasen, a newly completed 352-unit multifamily community in Richmond, Virginia.
Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Real Estate Finance arranged the financing on behalf of Capital Square.

Amenities include a resort-style pool, fitness center, rooftop terrace, club room with a golf simulator, whiskey lounge, coworking center, dog wash station, and landscaped courtyards.

During the first half of 2026, Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets team sourced more than $13.9 billion from non-agency capital providers, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties.

“Chasen is a newly completed asset in one of Richmond’s most active neighborhoods, and this financing gives Capital Square flexibility as the property continues to build its operating history.”

candidates.text:
Sofinnova Partners Closes €82 Million MD Start IV Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Sofinnova Partners Closes €82 Million MD Start IV Fund
Sofinnova Partners closed its oversubscribed Sofinnova MD Start IV fund at €82 million to create and develop new medtech companies across Europe and the U.S. The fund extends Sofinnova’s medtech company-creation strategy and is expected to launch six to eight new ventures over the next five years.
MD Start IV will support companies from formation through key clinical and operational milestones.
The strategy combines capital with hands-on company building, clinical expertise, entrepreneurial support, and operational resources.
Sofinnova said the fund will focus on addressing significant unmet medical needs through new medical technologies.
The firm’s previous MD Start III fund raised €63 million.
That fund invested in six companies that have collectively secured more than €140 million in follow-on financing.
Portfolio companies created through the MD Start strategy include LimFlow, which was acquired by Inari Medical for up to $415 million.
CorWave has raised more than €100 million.
BrightHeart has obtained FDA and CE Mark clearance and recently raised €11 million in Series A financing.
Moon Surgical has received FDA and CE Mark clearance for its Maestro system, which has been used to treat more than 3,700 patients.
The MD Start IV strategy is led by Sofinnova Partners Anne Osdoit, Cecile Dupont, and Mano Iyer, along with other members of the investment team.
Sofinnova Partners manages more than €4 billion in assets across life sciences and sustainability strategies.
KEY QUOTES:
“Sofinnova MD Start is one of the few strategies in Europe focused on creating medtech companies from the ground up. What makes the model distinctive is the active role our team plays in building and supporting every company from day one. This latest fund will allow us to scale that approach and remain a key part of Sofinnova’s platform across the life sciences value chain.”
Antoine Papiernik, Chairman and Managing Partner of Sofinnova Partners
“We are grateful for the continued support of our existing and new limited partners. Their commitment reflects confidence in our active, hands-on approach to company building. With Sofinnova MD Start IV, we look forward to continuing to work closely with engineers, clinicians, and scientists to advance their transformative medical technologies from the lab to the clinic.”
Anne Osdoit, Partner at Sofinnova Partners

Oro Mobility Raises $80 Million To Scale Driver-Led And Autonomous Fleets
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Oro Mobility Raises $80 Million To Scale Driver-Led And Autonomous Fleets
Oro Mobility has secured an $80 million strategic equity investment from a consortium that includes Cohen Private Ventures and funds or accounts affiliated with Certares Opportunities and Knighthead Capital Management. The investment establishes the Hertz-backed business as a standalone growth platform.
Hertz created Oro as part of its broader transformation strategy and will retain majority economic ownership. Hertz will also continue supporting Oro as its fleet and corporate services partner.
Oro operates approximately 45,000 vehicles across major U.S. mobility markets and is designed to provide an ownership, orchestration, and operations layer connecting vehicles, mobility technology providers, and consumer demand.
The company operates across three primary areas: rideshare rentals, driver-led fleet management, and autonomous vehicle fleet management. The new financing will support expansion of its fleet, operational infrastructure, technology capabilities, workforce, and strategic partnerships across those businesses.
Oro is built on Hertz’s experience in fleet operations, vehicle maintenance, logistics, and asset management. Management sees a growing opportunity to provide professionally managed fleet infrastructure as rideshare demand expands and autonomous vehicle deployments increase.
The structure gives Hertz continued economic exposure to Oro’s growth while allowing the business to operate with dedicated capital and strategic focus as mobility models extend beyond traditional rental cars.
KEY QUOTES:
“At Hertz, our strategy is anchored in the belief that our century of expertise can lead a new era of mobility, and Oro is a powerful example of that in action. As ride-hail demand expands, autonomous vehicle deployments accelerate and consumers increasingly choose mobility services over personal car ownership, demand is growing for purpose-built operators like Oro. This investment underscores the strong foundation we’ve built at Oro and the immense opportunity ahead, validating both Oro’s trajectory and Hertz’s transformation strategy.”
Gil West, CEO Of Hertz And Executive Chairman Of Oro Mobility
“The future of mobility will be powered by professionally managed fleets. As new mobility models emerge, there will be growing demand for companies that can own, finance, operate and maintain vehicles at scale while delivering safe, reliable service. Oro was built to fill that role. This investment gives us the capital, focus and strategic partners to accelerate our growth and support the evolving mobility ecosystem.”
Doria Holbrook, CEO Of Oro Mobility
“We believe Oro has established a differentiated position in a growing and dynamic mobility market. We look forward to supporting the team as they continue to scale Oro, strengthen its capabilities and deliver long-term value.”
Andrew B. Cohen, Chief Investment Officer And Co-Founder Of Cohen Private Ventures

Kampala Capital Secures $80 Million Warehouse Facility From O’Connor Capital Solutions
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Kampala Capital Secures $80 Million Warehouse Facility From O’Connor Capital Solutions
Kampala Capital announced the extension and upsize of a warehouse facility with private funds managed by O’Connor Capital Solutions, providing up to $80 million of financing to support loans originated by Kampala.
The expanded facility is intended to give Kampala additional institutional capital as the Monterrey, Mexico-based non-bank lender continues growing its portfolio.
Kampala provides short-term cross-currency financing to small and medium-sized businesses in Mexico, with a focus on importer and exporter clients.
The company said the new commitment follows significant portfolio growth and strong performance during 2026.
Kampala expects the expanded facility to support growth of its loan portfolio to more than $100 million over the next few years.
The transaction also extends a relationship between Kampala and O’Connor Capital Solutions that has lasted more than five years.
O’Connor said Kampala has expanded its portfolio while maintaining strong credit standards and operating processes.
The facility is part of O’Connor Capital Solutions’ broader specialty finance and lender finance strategy.
O’Connor Capital Solutions operates as the private credit strategy within O’Connor Alternative Investments, which is part of Cantor Fitzgerald Asset Management.
The platform invests across asset-based finance, including real estate, as well as corporate capital solutions.
O’Connor Capital Solutions has invested more than $6 billion since inception.
Kampala began operations in 2017 and focuses on financing foreign exchange loans for importer and exporter SMBs in Mexico.
The company said the larger facility will allow it to accelerate portfolio growth while maintaining its approach to credit selection, risk management, and operational execution.
KEY QUOTES:
“This expanded commitment from O’Connor Capital Solutions is a strong validation of our business model, the quality of our portfolio, and the dedication of our team. We are pleased to further strengthen our partnership with OCS, whose ongoing support has been instrumental in Kampala’s growth. This increased facility enhances our access to institutional capital and positions us to accelerate portfolio expansion while preserving our disciplined approach to credit selection, risk management, and operational execution. We believe this partnership creates a strong foundation for Kampala’s continued growth in the years ahead.”
Adalberto Espinosa, CEO and Co-Founder of Kampala Capital
“We have experienced a successful 5+ year relationship with Adalberto, Armando, and the rest of the Kampala team and are excited to continue the partnership. The team at Kampala has grown the portfolio significantly while maintaining high credit standards and processes, and we’re excited to be a part of the continued growth of the business. Specialty finance and lender finance remains one of our core strategies, and we look forward to continuing to partner with Kampala and our other portfolio companies, executing on our flexible and global mandate.”
Joshua Mercado, Managing Director and Head of Asset-Based Finance at O’Connor Capital Solutions

candidates.text:
IFS Capital Signs S$79 Million MSME Loan Securitization With CapitaLand Investment
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
IFS Capital Signs S$79 Million MSME Loan Securitization With CapitaLand Investment
IFS Capital has signed its inaugural S$79 million loan securitization program backed by a portfolio of micro, small and midsize enterprise loans secured by Singapore real estate. DBS Bank is serving as sole arranger for the transaction.
IFS Capital will sell a defined pool of loans from its existing MSME portfolio to a special purpose vehicle, which will finance the purchase by issuing senior, mezzanine and subordinated notes.
CapitaLand Investment will subscribe for the full aggregate principal amount of the senior notes issued on the first issue date.
IFS Capital will retain the mezzanine and subordinated notes, aligning its interests with the senior note investor over the life of the pool.
The notes will have a four-year tenor, and IFS Capital will continue servicing the underlying loans. Existing borrower relationships will not change.
The securitization will allow IFS Capital to recycle capital currently committed to loans through maturity and redeploy those funds into additional MSME lending.
The company plans to develop securitization into a recurring funding and capital management channel across multiple product portfolios.
IFS Capital’s private credit business provides working capital, asset-based and property-secured financing to MSMEs across Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Hong Kong.
Group lending assets totaled S$475 million as of June 30, 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“A transaction like this rests on an investor’s confidence in how we underwrite and how our loans perform over time. We are pleased to have CapitaLand Investment as an investor in our first securitisation. We have structured the transaction in a way that aligns our interests with those of our investor for the life of the pool. Our intention is to make this a repeatable channel, with capital continuously being put back to work for MSMEs in the region.”
Randy Sim, Group Chief Executive Officer of IFS Capital
“This investment expands CapitaLand Investment’s exposure to Singapore’s real estate private credit market and advances our fund management growth strategy in the credit sector. We are pleased to partner with IFS, whose capabilities and market expertise complement CapitaLand Investment’s regional credit investment platform. The senior secured notes provide stable, risk-adjusted returns backed by a diversified portfolio of real estate assets. We continue to see compelling opportunities in real estate private credit across developed Asia Pacific markets.”
Arjun Pandit, Managing Director and Head of Credit, Private Funds at CapitaLand Investment
“This transaction demonstrates how securitisation can unlock institutional capital, enhance funding diversity and support the flow of capital to the real economy. DBS is pleased to have brought together IFS Capital and CapitaLand Investment in this inaugural transaction. Beyond its significance for the parties involved, it marks an important step forward in the continued development of Singapore’s securitisation market.”
Clifford Lee, Managing Director and Global Head of Investment Banking at DBS Bank

candidates.text:
Tiger Finance Deploys $78 Million In Q3 Asset-Based Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Tiger Finance Deploys $78 Million In Q3 Asset-Based Financing
Tiger Finance committed $78 million in new asset-based financing to retail and consumer products companies during the third quarter of 2026, deploying capital across refinancing transactions, growth initiatives, dividend recapitalizations, and supplemental liquidity facilities.
The lending platform, which operates as a division of Tiger Capital Group, structured the quarterly commitments through revolving credit facilities, term loans, and first-in, last-out debt. The financings supported both private equity-backed and non-sponsored borrowers.
The largest transaction during the quarter was a $33 million FILO term loan for women’s fashion retailer Maurices. Tiger Finance acted as agent on the facility and participated alongside Wingspire Capital as part of a broader refinancing of Maurices’ balance sheet.
The refinancing extended debt maturities and reduced borrowing costs for Maurices, which operates more than 800 stores. The transaction also expanded an existing lending relationship between Tiger and Maurices that began in 2023.
Tiger Finance also provided a $20 million revolving line of credit to Garage Beer, a premium light beer brand backed by Jason and Travis Kelce and Durational Capital Management. The facility is intended to support new product development and expansion into additional markets.
The Garage Beer transaction represents Tiger Finance’s second financing for a portfolio company backed by Durational Capital Management.
The third major commitment was a $25 million term loan to a large U.S. department store chain. The borrower used part of the proceeds to repay maturing higher-cost debt and increase liquidity, including liquidity used to support dividend payments to equity holders.
Tiger Finance focuses on secured lending structures that use assets including working capital, machinery and equipment, fixtures, real estate, and intellectual property as collateral. Its financing solutions for middle-market businesses include first-lien, second-lien, and split-lien facilities, frequently structured as term debt.
The platform draws on Tiger Capital Group’s broader asset valuation capabilities. Tiger said the organization appraises and sells more than $30 billion of inventory, brands, and other consumer assets annually, providing data that informs its underwriting and financing structures.
KEY QUOTE:
“Borrowers across the retail and consumer sectors are seeking flexible financing that both reflects the value of their assets and provides them the capital to execute on their business plans. Tiger appraises and sells in excess of $30 billion annually of inventory, brands, and other consumer assets every day. That lets us lend against them with confidence and structure facilities that go beyond a conventional borrowing base.”
Bob DeAngelis, Executive Managing Director And Group Head Of Tiger Finance

candidates.text:
Endeavor Catalyst Expands Middle East Portfolio To 64 Companies With $76.6 Million Invested
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Endeavor Catalyst Expands Middle East Portfolio To 64 Companies With $76.6 Million Invested
Endeavor Catalyst has expanded its Middle East portfolio to 64 companies across six markets, with $76.6 million invested in the region, up 22 times from $3.5 million a decade ago. The regional growth follows the final close of Endeavor Catalyst Fund V, an oversubscribed $320 million fund that increased the firm’s total assets under management to more than $850 million.
The investment platform now backs companies across Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. Regional portfolio companies include Tabby, MNT-Halan, Tamara, Kitopi, and Moove. Endeavor Catalyst said the Middle East has also become an increasingly important source of realizations within its global portfolio.
Three of the 15 liquidity events across Endeavor Catalyst’s portfolio since the start of 2025 have come from the Middle East, making the region second only to Latin America for recent realizations. The Middle East portfolio has produced five exits in total.
Endeavor Catalyst operates as a co-investment fund, investing alongside venture capital and growth equity firms in companies led by founders who have been selected into the Endeavor network. Fund V will continue backing founders in markets where the firm sees ambition and company creation growing faster than access to capital.
The firm’s Dubai Global Hub is part of that strategy, connecting founders in the region with investors, mentors, and operators across markets. More than 90 Endeavor Entrepreneurs from 20 countries are based in the Dubai hub. Globally, Endeavor’s network includes more than 3,100 entrepreneurs across more than 50 countries, while Endeavor Catalyst has backed 437 companies across 44 Catalyst markets. Its portfolio includes 83 companies valued at $1 billion or more and 39 exits.
KEY QUOTES:
“The past few years have been tumultuous in the Middle East. Some outside the region might think that’s a reason not to invest, but at Endeavor Catalyst we know the opposite is true. The response to the disruption has shown just how ambitious and determined Middle Eastern founders are. With Fund V, we’re continuing our bet that big challenges lead to big impact.”
Yana El Dirani, Regional Lead For Endeavor Catalyst And Managing Director For Endeavor’s Dubai Global Hub

candidates.text:
Tishman Speyer Secures $75 Million Second Close For Korea Living Venture, Bringing Commitments To $395 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Tishman Speyer Secures $75 Million Second Close For Korea Living Venture, Bringing Commitments To $395 Million
Tishman Speyer has secured a $75 million commitment from a German pension fund in the second closing of its Korea Living Venture, bringing total equity commitments to the residential investment vehicle to $395 million.
The new investment builds on KLV’s first closing, which secured $300 million in commitments from APG Asset Management and Bouwinvest.
Combined with Tishman Speyer’s $20 million of sponsor equity, the capital effectively achieves the firm’s initial $400 million fundraising target.
Tishman Speyer expects the equity commitments to support more than $800 million of total investment capacity when anticipated financing is included.
The Korea Living Venture is focused on building a diversified portfolio of residential properties across the Seoul Metropolitan Area, where Tishman Speyer sees increasing demand for rental housing.
The fund primarily targets existing residential properties offering opportunities for value enhancement while maintaining selective exposure to development projects.
Its investment strategy focuses on properties near major transportation hubs with convenient access to business districts and university campuses in Seoul, Icheon, Gyeonggi-do and other high-growth neighborhoods throughout the capital region.
Tishman Speyer said Seoul’s rental market is benefiting from structural demographic and economic changes, including rising housing costs, an increasing number of single-person households and growing populations of foreign residents and international students.
KLV completed its first acquisition in August 2026 with the purchase of Songdo CoStay, a stabilized 411-unit residential property in Songdo, Incheon, South Korea.
The nine-story property is located in the Songdo International Business District, an area that includes multiple universities and approximately 70 biotechnology and life sciences companies.
Songdo CoStay consists of furnished residential units supported by a range of shared amenities.
The acquisition gives KLV an initial operating asset while the venture continues seeking additional investments throughout the Seoul metropolitan region.
KLV also expands Tishman Speyer’s broader global diversification strategy as the real estate investment firm increases its exposure to residential properties and other asset classes across additional markets.
Since 2023, Tishman Speyer has acquired approximately 3,800 residential units across 13 communities in three countries and 10 U.S. states.
Over the same period, the firm has commenced or completed construction of approximately 4,100 rental apartments.
Tishman Speyer currently has approximately 7,400 residential units in its development pipeline.
Across its broader global real estate platform, Tishman Speyer has acquired, developed and operated 600 properties totaling approximately 242 million square feet since its founding in 1978, representing a combined value of approximately $138 billion.
KEY QUOTE:
“This second closing of our KLV fund reflects continued investor conviction in Korea’s living sector. These partnerships position us well as we continue to scale a high-quality, diversified residential portfolio across the Seoul Metropolitan Area.”
Graham Mackie, Head of Pan-Asia at Tishman Speyer

candidates.title: Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology
candidates.snippet:
Vertical Semiconductor, a Boston-based power semiconductor company spun out of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $73 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act.
The post Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology
Vertical Semiconductor, a Boston-based power semiconductor company spun out of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $73 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act.
The funding would support research, development, and commercialization of next-generation vertical gallium nitride power transistors intended to improve electricity delivery for artificial intelligence data centers and other high-performance computing infrastructure.
The proposed financial assistance would be provided through the Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Research and Development Office and is designed to accelerate domestic development and production of advanced power semiconductor technologies.
Vertical Semiconductor is developing a vertical gallium nitride FinFET platform intended to deliver greater power efficiency and higher power density than conventional semiconductor power conversion approaches.
Gallium nitride is a semiconductor material used in high-performance power electronics because of its ability to support efficient electrical switching and operation under demanding conditions.
The company’s vertical transistor architecture is designed to reduce energy losses during power conversion while limiting heat generation and the physical space required for electrical infrastructure.
These capabilities are becoming increasingly important as AI data centers require substantially more electricity to power advanced processors and other computing systems.
Vertical Semiconductor believes that improvements in power conversion efficiency could allow data center operators to deploy additional computing capacity without requiring proportional increases in available grid power.
The company’s technology originated from research supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy.
The proposed CHIPS funding would support further development of the technology and help establish domestic production capabilities for vertical gallium nitride devices.
As part of the initiative, Vertical Semiconductor plans to collaborate with commercial partners on a demonstration involving a 2.5-megawatt AI computing rack.
The proposed system is designed to demonstrate how vertical gallium nitride technology can improve power delivery throughout the data center infrastructure.
According to the company, the demonstration aims to reduce energy losses by approximately 30% while decreasing the physical footprint of power conversion equipment by 50%.
These improvements could allow a greater portion of available electricity to reach computing equipment rather than being lost during conversion and distribution.
The project also intends to demonstrate the benefits of deploying advanced semiconductor devices throughout the AI data center power chain, from grid connections to computing hardware.
Vertical Semiconductor sees the technology as an opportunity to help address one of the primary infrastructure constraints affecting the expansion of AI computing capacity.
The company also expects the technology to have applications in critical energy infrastructure where power conversion efficiency, reliability, and equipment density are important considerations.
The proposed federal funding reflects efforts to advance domestic semiconductor technologies that support both AI infrastructure and broader energy systems.
The letter of intent represents a preliminary funding milestone rather than a final award. The contemplated financial assistance will depend on completion of the applicable federal approval process and definitive agreements.
If finalized, the investment would support Vertical Semiconductor’s commercialization plans while contributing to the development of domestic power semiconductor manufacturing capabilities.
KEY QUOTES:
“Power is the most significant bottleneck in the build-out of AI infrastructure. The CHIPS R&D award will accelerate Vertical Semiconductor’s R&D and commercialization initiatives for vertical GaN, which will expand American compute capacity within existing power constraints.”
Cynthia Liao, CEO And Co-Founder Of Vertical Semiconductor
“The Trump Administration is accelerating American semiconductor innovation to enhance our domestic energy and power resources. This investment expands domestic research, secures critical supply chains, and creates high-paying American jobs.”
Howard Lutnick, U.S. Secretary Of Commerce
“This CHIPS R&D award will secure domestic production of next-generation vertical GaN technology and bolster U.S. leadership in advanced power semiconductor devices. Accelerating domestic R&D for this technology will strengthen America’s ability to convert and deliver power for the grid and super intelligence data centers.”
Bill Frauenhofer, Executive Director Of Semiconductor Investment And Innovation At The U.S. Department Of Commerce

candidates.title: AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure
candidates.snippet:
AMP secured $70 million in project debt financing led by Galvanize to develop AI-powered waste infrastructure in Portsmouth, Virginia. The financing will support construction of a new sortation facility and an organics processing system.
The post AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure
AMP secured $70 million in project debt financing led by Galvanize to develop AI-powered waste infrastructure in Portsmouth, Virginia. The financing will support construction of a new sortation facility and an organics processing system.
The projects are part of AMP’s 20-year partnership with the Southeastern Public Service Authority.
At full scale, the regional system is designed to process more than 500,000 tons of municipal solid waste annually, equivalent to more than 1,400 tons per day.
The system is expected to divert at least half of the processed material from landfills.
AMP’s technology uses AI-powered cameras, robotics, and pneumatic jets to identify and recover plastics, metals, fiber, organic material, and other recyclable materials from municipal waste.
Unlike traditional recycling systems, AMP’s system can process raw municipal solid waste, including sealed trash bags, without requiring consumers to separate recyclable material before collection.
The latest financing builds on more than two years of operating experience at AMP’s existing Portsmouth facility.
AMP is now equipping a second sortation facility in Portsmouth that is expected to become operational in early 2028.
An adjacent facility will process recovered organic material into biochar using indirect heating.
AMP initially plans to use the biochar as daily landfill cover, with potential future applications in construction and cement.
Biochar production will also generate carbon removal credits supporting AMP’s agreement with Google to remove 200,000 metric tonnes of CO2e by 2030.
AMP and SPSA expect the broader system to guarantee that 20% of SPSA’s waste is recycled while diverting at least half of material delivered to AMP’s facilities.
SPSA serves approximately 1.2 million residents across eight member communities.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’ve shown that this model works at commercial scale, and this financing demonstrates that we can pair our technology with long-term project capital to accelerate deployment.”
“Galvanize’s investment is an important validation that AI-powered waste sorting has moved from novel technology to financeable infrastructure, creating a repeatable path for deploying AMP’s systems with communities and waste operators across the country.”
Mary Macpherson, SVP of Finance at AMP
“Waste is a massive, under-modernized infrastructure market, and AMP is changing its economics.”
Suresh Vasan, Partner, Credit & Capital Solutions at Galvanize

candidates.title: Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2
candidates.snippet:
Breye Therapeutics has raised an oversubscribed €67.5 million Series A financing to advance its lead retinal disease candidate danegaptide into a randomized Phase 2 clinical trial. The round was co-led by new investor Mission BioCapital and existing investor Novo Holdings.
The post Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2 appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2
Breye Therapeutics has raised an oversubscribed €67.5 million Series A financing to advance its lead retinal disease candidate danegaptide into a randomized Phase 2 clinical trial. The round was co-led by new investor Mission BioCapital and existing investor Novo Holdings.
Existing investor Sound Bioventures also participated, along with new investors the Ljungström family office, Innovestor Life Science, EIFO, Catalyze Capital, Modi Ventures and Pappas Capital.
Breye plans to use the financing primarily to advance danegaptide in patients with non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or NPDR.
The Phase 2 study is expected to begin in 2027 and is intended to demonstrate clinical proof of concept.
Danegaptide is a first-in-class oral small molecule designed to stabilize retinal vasculature and protect against capillary breakdown and vascular leakage associated with chronically high glucose levels.
A Phase 1b study in NPDR patients showed the drug was well tolerated across all dose levels and produced early signs of clinical activity, including retinal imaging data consistent with reduced vascular leakage.
Breye estimates that diabetic retinopathy affects approximately 130 million people globally and noted that treatment options remain limited for patients with early or moderate-stage NPDR.
The company is developing an oral approach that could complement existing intravitreal therapies, which require injections directly into the eye.
Part of the Series A proceeds will also support Breye’s broader pipeline, including a P2X7 receptor antagonist for intermediate age-related macular degeneration and neuroprotective candidates for glaucoma.
Robert Blazej of Mission BioCapital and Lukas Ljungström of the Ljungström family office will join Breye’s board as part of the financing.
KEY QUOTES:
“This €67.5m Series A financing, which includes significant support from both new and existing investors, reflects the strong confidence in Breye’s vision, strategy, and pipeline. It marks a major milestone for the Company and validates the enormous progress we have made to date. Importantly, it enables us to advance danegaptide, our pioneering, first-in-class oral treatment for diabetic retinopathy, to the next stage of clinical development – bringing a much-needed patient-friendly treatment option closer to those living with this debilitating eye disease.”
Ulrik Mouritzen, Chief Executive Officer of Breye Therapeutics
“Breye is emerging as a leader in the development of innovative retinal disease therapies, as demonstrated by the promising results from its recent Phase Ib study of danegaptide, and we are excited to support the Company at this pivotal stage of growth. With its highly differentiated approach, clear development strategy and experienced team, we believe Breye is uniquely positioned to address a significant unmet need in diabetic retinopathy.”
Robert Blazej, Partner at Mission BioCapital
“Danegaptide has the potential to address a major unmet need in diabetic retinopathy, by offering what we believe will be a highly effective, non-invasive treatment solution. Our continued investment in Breye Therapeutics reflects the strong progress the Company has made and our confidence in the team. Breye is purposefully advancing its mission of delivering innovative therapies for patients with retinal eye diseases, who have very limited treatment options, and we are very proud to continue to support the team.”
Jørgen Søberg Petersen, Senior Partner at Novo Holdings

candidates.title: EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing
candidates.snippet:
EVelution Energy has received U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services approval for an EB-5 investment offering expected to support up to approximately $64.8 million of subordinated financing for its planned solar-powered cobalt processing facility in Yuma County, Arizona.
The post EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing
EVelution Energy has received U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services approval for an EB-5 investment offering expected to support up to approximately $64.8 million of subordinated financing for its planned solar-powered cobalt processing facility in Yuma County, Arizona.
The company is developing what it says will be the first commercial-scale solar-powered cobalt sulfate and cobalt metal processing facility in the U.S.
EVelution plans to combine EB-5 subordinated debt with equity raised through a dedicated Qualified Opportunity Zone fund to finance engineering, permitting, site development and technical validation before arranging conventional construction financing.
The project’s census tract has also been nominated by Arizona for successor designation as a Rural Opportunity Zone under Opportunity Zone 2.0.
With USCIS approval received, EVelution expects the two financing sources to provide the remaining development-stage capital needed to complete engineering, technical and site work.
A bankable feasibility study is targeted for the first quarter of 2027.
Once development work advances toward a final investment decision, EVelution expects to finance construction through a separate capital structure.
The Export-Import Bank of the United States has re-issued a non-binding Letter of Interest indicating potential financing of up to $275 million under its Make More in America initiative, subject to due diligence, underwriting and authorization.
The approximately $450 million project is expected to produce about 7,000 metric tons of contained cobalt annually at full operation.
That would include approximately 4,000 metric tons in battery-grade cobalt sulfate and 3,000 metric tons of alloy-grade cobalt metal.
EVelution estimates that output could satisfy up to approximately 40% of projected U.S. cobalt demand.
Solar facility construction began in June 2026, while cobalt processing facility construction is expected to begin in 2027 following the feasibility study, final investment decision and project financing.
Commercial operations are targeted for 2029.
KEY QUOTES:
“The financing challenge for critical minerals projects is not limited to raising the capital required for construction. Projects must first finance the engineering, technical and development work required to become bankable. Our EB-5 and Opportunity Zone financing strategy is designed to bridge that gap and advance the project toward the institutional capital required for construction.”
Navaid Alam, President and CEO of EVelution Energy

The post Gogoro Secures $61.8 Million In New Equity Investments appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Gogoro Secures $61.8 Million In New Equity Investments
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Gogoro Secures $61.8 Million In New Equity Investments
Gogoro announced approximately $61.8 million in new equity investments from entities controlled by director Chung-Yao Yin and additional strategic investors, providing the electric mobility company with additional capital to support its balance sheet and long-term growth plans.
The company plans to issue approximately 24.94 million ordinary shares at a purchase price of $2.48 per share.
Participants in the financing include Gold Sino Asset Limited and Peng-Lin Investment Limited, both controlled by Yin, as well as Ruen Hua Dyeing & Weaving and Yi Tai Investment.
Following completion of the transaction, Gold Sino is expected to beneficially own approximately 45% of Gogoro’s outstanding ordinary shares.
Peng-Lin is expected to hold approximately 8.8%, while Ruen Hua and its affiliates are expected to beneficially own approximately 21.9% of the company.
The financing represents a second round of new equity investments involving entities controlled by Yin and other strategic investors, further increasing their financial commitment to Gogoro.
Gogoro said the new capital will strengthen its balance sheet and provide additional resources to support continued business development and the execution of its long-term growth strategy.
The transaction has been reviewed and approved by Gogoro’s Audit Committee and Board of Directors.
Closing remains subject to customary conditions, including required Nasdaq clearance.
Gogoro expects the investment to be funded on or before October 13, 2026.
The additional equity comes as Gogoro continues operating and developing its battery-swapping ecosystem for electric two-wheel transportation.
The company’s network supports nearly 700,000 riders and includes more than 2,700 GoStation battery-swapping locations.
Gogoro’s platform is designed to provide riders with rapid access to charged batteries while supporting a broader electric mobility ecosystem spanning vehicles, battery technology, software, and energy infrastructure.
The $61.8 million financing gives the company additional financial flexibility as it continues investing in its network, technology, and broader business strategy.

candidates.snippet:
Braavo Capital has committed more than $60 million to user acquisition cohort financing facilities in 2026, expanding its non-dilutive funding platform for mobile app and game companies.
The post Braavo Capital Commits Over $60 Million To Expand UA Cohort Financing For Mobile Apps appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Braavo Capital Commits Over $60 Million To Expand UA Cohort Financing For Mobile Apps
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Braavo Capital Commits Over $60 Million To Expand UA Cohort Financing For Mobile Apps
Braavo Capital has committed more than $60 million to user acquisition cohort financing facilities in 2026, expanding its non-dilutive funding platform for mobile app and game companies.
The New York-based company provides committed capital that customers can draw as they spend on user acquisition. Rather than structuring advances against an entire company’s revenue or balance sheet, Braavo scopes each advance to a specific user acquisition cohort and is repaid from the revenue generated by that cohort.
Braavo said the model allows mobile companies to fund advertising and customer acquisition without using equity capital for those expenses. The financing is designed around the economics of individual cohorts, including expected return on advertising spend, revenue generation, and the way customer acquisition performance develops over time.
Recent commitments include $15 million for children’s tutoring app Buddy.ai and $15 million for AI-powered skincare app Lovi.
Buddy.ai has worked with Braavo since 2019 and previously completed six user acquisition financing transactions with the company. The latest facility provides the business with committed capacity that can be used to plan a longer period of customer acquisition spending while preserving equity for product development and hiring.
Lovi closed its facility in June and has since tripled its advertising spend. Braavo said its underwriting process combines data integrations with analysis of subscription economics to develop financing structures tailored to individual customers.
The company positions its experience underwriting mobile app businesses as a key part of its ability to assess how user acquisition can scale and how return-on-ad-spend curves may change as spending increases.
Founded in New York City in 2015, Braavo Capital focuses on non-dilutive financing for mobile application companies. The company said it has tracked more than $5 billion in app earnings across 10,000 applications and more than $1.5 billion in user acquisition spending.
The more than $60 million committed this year adds to Braavo’s broader effort to give app developers and publishers an alternative source of growth capital specifically tied to customer acquisition performance.
KEY QUOTES:
“The mechanics of cohort financing aren’t complicated. The harder part is understanding how a company can scale user acquisition, how its ROAS curves will evolve over time, and how much flexibility you can responsibly build into a facility. Our experience lets us structure around a customer’s actual economics rather than starting with a predetermined template.”
Mark Loranger, CEO Of Braavo Capital
“Even when we considered alternatives for a larger cohort financing facility, Braavo still came out on top. Seven years in, I know how they work and even what to expect if something doesn’t go to plan.”
“A committed facility means we can scale user acquisition without tying up equity to do it. We know the terms, we know how the cohorts have to perform, and we can plan a year of user acquisition instead of a quarter. Equity goes into the product and the team.”
Ivan Crewkov, CEO Of Buddy.ai
“I was really impressed with Braavo’s analytical capabilities, the depth of their understanding of the subscription business, and how quickly they developed financing terms tailored to our specific needs. Their integration layer and experience meant they could move quickly as soon as they received our data. It was smooth sailing, and that gave me confidence that we were working with a partner who really understood our business.”
Alexey Shagraev, CEO Of Lovi

candidates.snippet:
Sibelco, a global materials solutions company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $56 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. The funding would support research, development, and commercialization activities involving next-generation high-purity quartz processing technologies for semiconductor manufacturing in the United States.
The post Sibelco Signs Deal For Up To $56 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance High-Purity Quartz Processing In North Carolina appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Sibelco Signs Deal For Up To $56 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance High-Purity Quartz Processing In North Carolina
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Sibelco Signs Deal For Up To $56 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance High-Purity Quartz Processing In North Carolina
Sibelco, a global materials solutions company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $56 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. The funding would support research, development, and commercialization activities involving next-generation high-purity quartz processing technologies for semiconductor manufacturing in the United States.
The agreement, announced October 22, 2026, through Sibelco North America, could strengthen domestic capabilities to produce semiconductor-grade, high-purity quartz, a material used in critical components throughout the chip manufacturing process.
The proposed funding would support Sibelco’s U.S. research and development operations, building on the company’s longstanding presence and technical expertise in Spruce Pine, North Carolina.
High-purity quartz is an important raw material used to manufacture specialized quartz components for semiconductor fabrication. These components must meet demanding purity and performance requirements because contamination during manufacturing can affect semiconductor production quality and efficiency.
As semiconductor manufacturers expand domestic production capacity, access to reliable supplies of high-purity materials has become increasingly important for supply chain resilience and advanced technology development.
Sibelco’s proposed research program would focus on four areas intended to advance processing efficiency, material quality, and the scalability of semiconductor-grade quartz production.
The first involves next-generation leaching technologies, which are used to remove impurities from quartz materials. Improvements in these processes could support the production of higher-purity materials suitable for increasingly sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing applications.
The second area involves advanced hot chlorination technologies, which provide additional processing capabilities for reducing impurities and improving material purity.
A third component focuses on high-purity quartz product engineering, with research intended to enhance material properties and develop products that meet evolving requirements across semiconductor manufacturing processes.
The fourth area involves establishing a technology piloting and demonstration facility to test, validate, and scale new quartz processing methods and products.
This facility would provide infrastructure for evaluating emerging technologies before broader industrial deployment, helping bridge the gap between laboratory research and commercial-scale production.
Together, these activities are intended to support the domestic development of advanced processing technologies and strengthen the availability of critical materials within the U.S. semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.
The proposed award aligns with broader federal efforts under the CHIPS and Science Act to expand semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, strengthen supply chains, and support research and technological innovation in the United States.
The initiative also highlights the importance of North Carolina’s established high-purity quartz industry to advanced manufacturing and national technology infrastructure.
Sibelco expects the proposed funding to accelerate its research and development activities while supporting the continued advancement of specialized materials processing capabilities in the United States.
The agreement remains at the letter-of-intent stage and does not represent a finalized funding award. The proposed financial assistance remains subject to confirmatory due diligence, additional negotiations, and internal U.S. government approvals.
If finalized, the funding would support the development of technologies intended to strengthen the reliability and long-term competitiveness of domestic semiconductor materials production.
KEY QUOTES:
“The Trump Administration is accelerating American semiconductor innovation to enhance our domestic energy and power resources. This investment expands domestic research, secures critical supply chains, and creates high-paying American jobs.”
Howard Lutnick, U.S. Secretary Of Commerce
“This incentive strengthens America’s semiconductor supply chain and creates significant new opportunities for American workers. Bringing Sibelco’s extraordinary technology to the United States puts American workers at the centre of that critically important industry, one that has vital national security interests at its core. It’s a clear example of how a great Belgian company can help build America’s industrial future. We are so proud of everyone who worked so hard to put this amazing deal together.”
Bill White, U.S. Ambassador To Belgium
“This Letter of Intent represents a significant step for Sibelco and reflects the importance of high-purity quartz within the semiconductor manufacturing supply chain. This proposed award would enable us to accelerate our research and development activities in the United States and build on Sibelco’s long-standing presence and expertise in North Carolina. We look forward to working with the U.S. Department of Commerce to advance technologies that support a secure and resilient semiconductor supply chain.”
Hilmar Rode, CEO Of Sibelco

Gaius Capital Closes Debut Private Equity Funds At €56 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Gaius Capital Closes Debut Private Equity Funds At €56 Million
Gaius Capital reached the final close of its debut private equity funds with €56 million in total capital raised.
The total includes €50 million for Gaius Nachfolgekapital I, which closed oversubscribed at its hard cap, along with an additional €6 million raised through a co-investment vehicle.
The final close came approximately four months after Gaius Capital completed a €40 million first close in June 2026.
More than 90% of commitments came from institutional investors across Germany, France, the Benelux region, the United States, and the United Kingdom.
Gaius Capital is an independent private equity firm focused on succession solutions in the DACH Mittelstand.
The firm targets scalable buy-and-build strategies across the micro- and small-cap segments and partners with business owners on succession transitions.
Gaius Capital said its approach is designed to preserve and extend the value created by entrepreneurs while providing a platform for continued growth.
Since its first close, the firm has continued deploying capital and building new succession platforms.
In September 2026, Gaius Capital launched Alpiora Group in Switzerland as its second succession platform.
That followed the firm’s first platform, which is focused on insurance brokers in Germany.
With the fundraising process completed, Gaius Capital plans to build additional succession platforms across resilient-growth service industries in the DACH region.
The firm is also continuing to expand its investment team as it develops additional private equity platforms.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are very grateful to our investors for their trust and support throughout this journey. Reaching the final close at our hard cap, with significant demand from an experienced institutional investor base, is a strong endorsement of our strategy and the opportunity we see in Mittelstand succession. With the fundraise successfully completed, our focus is now on deploying capital thoughtfully and building lasting partnerships with entrepreneurs across the DACH region.”
Jan Mickel, Founding Partner of Gaius Capital

By Amit Chowdhry

IPA Capital Markets Arranges $50 Million Financing For 18-Property Industrial Portfolio
IPA Capital Markets arranged $50 million in financing for an 18-property industrial portfolio located across Texas, Oklahoma, and Georgia.
Frank Montalto, Managing Director, and Ethan Splan, Director, arranged the financing on behalf of the borrower.
The non-recourse loan carries a five-year term and was structured at a 70% loan-to-value ratio.
The financing carries a 6.75% interest rate, with interest-only payments for the full five-year term.
The structure provides the sponsor with long-term financing while preserving cash flow through the interest-only payment schedule.
The transaction also reflects continued lender interest in diversified industrial portfolios across growth-oriented markets in the Southern U.S.
IPA Capital Markets is a division of Marcus & Millichap that provides financing solutions for major private and institutional commercial real estate investors.
The platform works across a wide range of capital structures, including senior debt, mezzanine financing, preferred equity, joint venture equity, and sponsor equity.
Its team supports clients across acquisitions, refinancing transactions, recapitalizations, and broader portfolio financing needs.
The $50 million industrial portfolio financing adds to IPA Capital Markets’ activity across institutional and private commercial real estate transactions.
Parent company Marcus & Millichap maintains a large national commercial real estate transaction platform.
During 2025, Marcus & Millichap closed 8,818 transactions representing approximately $50.8 billion in total sales volume.
The firm’s scale, lender relationships, and capital markets capabilities provide IPA Capital Markets with access to a broad range of financing sources across different property types and transaction structures.
KEY QUOTES:
“This financing reflects the continued strength of well-located industrial assets and the durability of lender demand for stabilized portfolios with strong fundamentals. We were pleased to secure non-recourse financing with competitive leverage and pricing that supports the sponsor’s long-term business plan across these markets.”
Frank Montalto, Managing Director at IPA Capital Markets

Atrium Therapeutics Raises $50 Million Private Placement To Advance Precision Cardiology Pipeline
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
Atrium Therapeutics Raises $50 Million Private Placement To Advance Precision Cardiology Pipeline
Atrium Therapeutics entered into a securities purchase agreement with institutional investors for a $50 million private placement to support development of its precision cardiology pipeline.
Investors participating in the financing include Sirenia Capital Management, Aberdeen Investments, Montanova, Sessa Capital, Casdin Capital, a life sciences-focused institutional investor, and others.
Atrium agreed to sell approximately 5.17 million common shares at $7.93 per share.
The company will also issue pre-funded warrants to purchase approximately 1.13 million common shares at $7.929 per warrant, reflecting the $7.93 common share price less the $0.001 exercise price.
The financing was priced at the market under Nasdaq rules.
Atrium expects the private placement to close on or about October 9, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
The company plans to use the proceeds, together with existing cash, cash equivalents, and investments, to fund development of its two lead product candidates, additional research programs, working capital, and general corporate purposes.
Atrium estimates that the financing and its existing capital will fund operations through 2028.
The company’s lead program, ATR 1072, is being developed for PRKAG2 syndrome.
The FDA has cleared Atrium’s IND for ATR 1072, allowing the company to advance the program into the Corventis Phase 1/2 clinical trial.
Atrium is also developing ATR 1086 for PLN cardiomyopathy.
Its pipeline includes two additional undisclosed research programs targeting rare cardiomyopathies.
Atrium’s technology uses targeted delivery approaches designed to transport RNA therapeutics directly to the heart.
The platform combines the tissue selectivity of monoclonal antibodies and other targeting ligands with oligonucleotide therapeutics, including small interfering RNA.
The technology was originally developed at Avidity Biosciences.
Support: Leerink Partners served as lead placement agent. Cantor, Barclays, and Wells Fargo Securities also served as placement agents.
