candidates.text:
FIRY To Redeem Remaining $49.7 Million Of Notes And Complete $300 Million Debt Repayment
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
FIRY To Redeem Remaining $49.7 Million Of Notes And Complete $300 Million Debt Repayment
FIRY has issued notice to redeem the remaining approximately $49.7 million principal amount of its 10.25% secured notes due 2026, completing repayment of a $300 million debt issuance ahead of maturity.
The redemption is scheduled for October 15, 2026.
FIRY will redeem the remaining notes at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest through, but excluding, the redemption date.
Following the redemption and satisfaction and discharge of the related indenture, FIRY expects to have no remaining notes outstanding and no outstanding indebtedness for borrowed money.
Liens securing the debt will also be released, and FIRY will no longer be subject to the covenants contained in the note indenture.
The company plans to fund the redemption with proceeds from the previously announced sale of its equity stake in Exit Games.
FIRY expects the October redemption alone to save approximately $800,000 in cash interest.
Combined with a separate August 2026 redemption, the debt repayment actions are expected to save approximately $3.6 million in interest that otherwise would have accrued through the notes’ December 15, 2026 maturity date.
FIRY expects to enter 2027 without outstanding borrowed debt.
The company plans to direct the resulting financial flexibility toward its businesses while considering future debt financing when management believes leverage could improve equity returns.
KEY QUOTES:
“The December 15 debt wall is coming down. This redemption completes the retirement of our $300 million Notes ahead of their maturity, with no new capital raised and no shareholder dilution. We believe we have the capital to run and grow our businesses and fund our litigation if necessary. Going forward, we expect to use debt when we believe it can enhance equity returns. The next chapter is about what we build from here.”
Andrew Paradise, CEO and Founder of FIRY
“Retiring the Notes is another step in our 100-year journey. We expect to enter 2027 without outstanding borrowed debt and with greater flexibility. Without debt service, more cash will be available to invest in the businesses as we focus on growing revenue and AEBITDA, supporting our guidance of modest positive operating cash flow in 2027 and revenue more than doubling from 2025 to 2028. We will consider debt in the future when we believe it enhances equity returns.”
Alex Walsh, CFO of FIRY

By Amit Chowdhry

Sensible Biotechnologies Raises $47 Million To Advance Naturally Modified mRNA Platform
Sensible Biotechnologies has secured $47 million in financing to advance and scale its platform for naturally modified mRNA medicines. The financing includes a Series A led by Oxford Science Enterprises and up to $20 million of non-dilutive funding from the Government of Slovakia and the European Union.
New investors OTB Ventures and In-Q-Tel participated in the Series A alongside existing investors Recode Ventures, Isomer Capital, Y Combinator, Backed VC, Kaya VC, Civilization Ventures and BlueYard Capital.
Individual investors included the family office of BioNTech co-founder Christoph Huber and former Eli Lilly Chief Medical Officer Tim Garnett.
Sensible plans to use the capital to expand its VECTOR platform, AI-enabled mRNA design and automated high-throughput screening capabilities and establish clinical-grade manufacturing.
The company’s approach differs from conventional synthetic mRNA manufacturing by using engineered living cells to manufacture naturally modified mRNA.
VECTOR combines computational and AI-enabled sequence optimization, high-throughput screening and proprietary engineered eukaryotic cells.
Sensible’s PromPT technology captures and protects mRNA inside cells before purification.
The company said the approach is designed to reduce immunogenicity and provide high protein expression while avoiding double-stranded RNA contamination that can cause unwanted immune activation.
External evaluations showed no detectable double-stranded RNA contamination, reduced cytokine activation and higher protein expression compared with synthetic mRNA in human immune-cell assays, according to Sensible.
Dr. Vishal Gulati of Recode Ventures and Joel Schoppig of Oxford Science Enterprises will join Sensible’s Board as part of the financing.
KEY QUOTES:
“mRNA transformed vaccines, but we believe its greatest potential lies in therapeutics. The field still relies largely on synthetic manufacturing technology developed more than 40 years ago. We are taking a fundamentally different approach, using living cells to produce naturally modified mRNA while reducing the cost and supply-chain constraints of conventional production. With this financing, we can scale our platform and expand mRNA into therapeutic applications requiring high or repeated dosing that have historically been limited by cost.”
Miroslav Gasparek, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Sensible Biotechnologies
“The promise of computational drug design depends on connecting it to biology and the practical work of making a medicine. How mRNA is made can shape how it behaves, so manufacturing matters from the very start of developing a treatment. Sensible brings design and cell-based production together, giving the team an opportunity to improve both the performance of mRNA and the economics of making it. We led this round because we believe in the team’s ability to build a company that helps pharmaceutical partners develop a broader range of mRNA medicines. With this investment, Sensible can advance toward clinical-grade production and expand the pharmaceutical partnerships that will drive its commercial growth.”
Joel Schoppig, Partner at Oxford Science Enterprises and Board Member at Sensible
“The next wave of mRNA medicines reaches far beyond vaccines: in vivo CAR-T, gene editing, and cancer immunotherapy. Yet much of that promise is capped by the limits of today’s mRNA design and manufacturing. Sensible has rebuilt the process from first principles. Its cell-based platform brings design, optimisation and manufacturing into a single loop, producing purer, low-immunogenicity mRNA at industrial scale. That is why we backed Sensible from its earliest round.”
Dr. Vishal Gulati, FMedSci, Managing Partner at Recode Ventures and Board Member at Sensible
“Sensible represents exactly that kind of scientific innovation that can help shape the future of medicine. Its work to develop a new generation of mRNA technologies reflects the strength of biotechnology innovation emerging from Slovakia and Europe. We are proud to support Sensible as it advances pioneering science with the potential to enable better medicines, expand the possibilities of mRNA therapeutics, and ultimately improve the lives of patients around the world. Such support is an investment Europe truly needs not only in scientific progress, but in our ability to lead the next generation of biotechnology and healthcare innovation.”
Kamil Šaško, Minister of Health of the Slovak Republic

WILDE Raises $40 Million From S2G Investments To Expand Protein Snack Production And Product Innovation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
WILDE Raises $40 Million From S2G Investments To Expand Protein Snack Production And Product Innovation
WILDE, a Lexington, Kentucky-based snack company specializing in protein-rich chips and crackers, has secured a $40 million investment from S2G Investments. The financing will support manufacturing expansion, new product development, and marketing initiatives as the company builds on more than $100 million in sales and distribution across over 35,000 retail locations nationwide.
Founded in 2015 by Jason Wright, WILDE has developed a portfolio of salty snacks made primarily from natural chicken breast, egg whites, and bone broth. Its products are designed to provide the taste and texture associated with traditional snack foods while delivering higher protein content.
The company’s Protein Chips and Protein Crackers offer more than 10 grams of protein per serving, positioning the brand within the growing market for snacks that combine convenience, flavor, and nutritional benefits.
WILDE recently opened a 130,000-square-foot manufacturing facility designed to substantially expand its production capabilities. According to the company, the facility is the only USDA-regulated salty snack manufacturing plant in the world.
The new operation increases WILDE’s production capacity sixfold, providing additional infrastructure to serve its expanding retail distribution network and introduce new products.
The $40 million investment will help the company scale manufacturing operations while broadening its product portfolio beyond its original Protein Chips.
Following the recent introduction of Protein Crackers, WILDE is developing additional snack formats intended to reach new consumers and address a wider variety of eating occasions.
The financing will also support improvements to the company’s visual identity, product packaging, and marketing capabilities as it seeks to establish greater recognition in the broader packaged food industry.
S2G Investments sees an opportunity to expand WILDE’s position as consumers increasingly seek convenient foods that deliver additional nutritional value, particularly protein.
The investment firm focuses on businesses operating across food and agriculture, energy, and oceans. Its investment capabilities include growth equity, structured finance, and other forms of capital designed to help companies expand their operations.
For WILDE, the investment provides resources to support the next phase of growth following the development of a national retail footprint and substantial investments in manufacturing infrastructure.
The company plans to use its expanded production capacity and new product development initiatives to reach additional consumers while maintaining its focus on protein-forward snacks.
KEY QUOTES:
“Building WILDE has never been easy. We started this company to prove that protein snacks don’t have to taste like punishment, and we’ve spent years betting on an idea that didn’t fit neatly into the snack aisle. We stuck with it, built something people crave, and this investment proves that hard work and conviction pay off. Now we have the firepower to go bigger, move faster, and shake up a whole lot more of the snack aisle.”
Jason Wright, Founder And CEO Of WILDE
“WILDE has shown you can have better products with high quality ingredients without sacrificing the taste experience that makes people love salty snacks. Jason created a standout product with Protein Chips, but what excites us most is the opportunity ahead as a snacking platform. Protein Crackers is among my favorite CPG innovations ever. We’re excited to partner with Jason and the team as WILDE scales into a household brand.”
Arthur Chow, Principal, Food & Agriculture At S2G Investments

Healthleap raises $38M for AI that finds undiagnosed conditions in hospital patients
Nickie Louise
Posted On October 7, 2026
0
4.4K Views
0
Shares
Share On Facebook
Tweet It
Malnutrition is one of the most common conditions hiding in plain sight inside U.S. hospitals. Up to half of hospitalized patients may be at risk, according to Healthleap, but fewer than 9% receive a diagnosis. That gap can mean longer hospital stays, worse patient outcomes, and millions of dollars in added costs.
Healthleap thinks software can catch what busy clinical teams miss.
The healthcare AI startup has raised $38 million in combined seed and Series A funding to expand a platform that reads patient records daily and flags people who may be at risk for undetected conditions. The financing includes an $8 million seed round co-led by Sequoia Capital and First Round Capital and a $30 million Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures.
Healthleap’s story started with malnutrition. Co-founder Jemima Meyer was working as a clinical dietitian when she built an early tool to help dietitians find patients who needed attention sooner. She later teamed up with her brother, Josiah Meyer, and the pair founded Healthleap in South Africa in 2022.
What began as a nutrition tool has since become a broader clinical AI platform. Healthleap now sits on top of hospital electronic health record systems, analyzing notes, lab results, vital signs, medications, diagnoses and other patient data for signs that someone may need a closer look.
The software does not diagnose patients. It assigns risk scores and routes them into existing hospital workflows so clinicians can decide what happens next.
From malnutrition screening to a broader hospital AI layer
Healthleap’s pitch is gaining attention partly because the company can point to measurable results.
At the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, Healthleap says its malnutrition program generated $23.8 million in annualized financial impact. That figure included $6.3 million in additional reimbursement and an estimated $17.5 million tied to shorter hospital stays, representing 8,632 annualized bed-days saved. Penn Medicine’s Strategic Decision Support team reviewed the analysis, Healthleap said.
At Cedars-Sinai, the company reports a 39% increase in malnutrition diagnoses with the same staffing levels and $11 million in annual financial impact.
Announcing the funding in a LinkedIn post, Josiah said :
“Somewhere right now, a patient is getting sicker from something that was treatable all along. HealthLeap AI finds these patients. We use existing signals in the patient record to screen every inpatient every day and flag those at high risk, so care teams can act and care for those patients. We started with malnutrition. My sister and co-founder, Jemima, worked as a clinical dietitian and watched patients get found too late.”
Healthleap also has clinical research behind its core malnutrition model. A peer-reviewed study published in *Applied Clinical Informatics* evaluated more than 166,000 hospital admissions over 3.75 years. The company says the system showed 88% higher sensitivity than a modified Malnutrition Screening Tool and identified patients an average of four days before the first dietitian documentation.
The startup has grown from three hospital partners to more than 50 over the past year, with customers including Penn Medicine, Cedars-Sinai, Houston Methodist, Emory Healthcare and Intermountain. CEO Josiah Meyer told TechCrunch that revenue increased more than tenfold during the same period.
“Every week, millions of patients leave hospitals with unresolved health conditions that will erode their health and cost up to 10x more to treat later,” Meyer said. “Finding them now is prevention, and it’s a win for everyone. Patients get treated before they get sicker. Hospitals shorten stays and are paid for the care they deliver. Payers avoid the much higher cost of complications down the road. Our goal is to improve care and save lives by catching these conditions early.”
Malnutrition is becoming the starting point, not the entire product. Healthleap is developing screening programs for delirium, aspiration pneumonia, pressure injuries, and congestive heart failure readmission risk. Meyer says the longer-term goal is to cover more than 40 major conditions and eventually extend the system beyond hospitals into outpatient and home care.
The new funding will go into engineering, product development, sales, and customer success.
Healthleap bets that one of AI ’s most valuable roles in hospitals may be surprisingly straightforward: continuously reading records humans rarely have time to reread, then pointing clinicians to the patients most likely to have been overlooked.
Healthleap Team (Image credit: Healthleap)

candidates.text:
ZAP Surgical Raises $36 Million Led By Catalio Capital To Scale Non-Invasive Brain Surgery
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
ZAP Surgical Raises $36 Million Led By Catalio Capital To Scale Non-Invasive Brain Surgery
ZAP Surgical Systems has secured $36 million in financing led by Catalio Capital Management, with continued support from Baheal, the company’s strategic partner in China. The funding will support the global expansion of ZAP’s non-invasive robotic brain surgery platform and continued development of its technology across neuroscience applications.
ZAP develops the ZAP-X Gyroscopic Radiosurgery platform, a vault-free radiosurgery system designed for non-invasive treatment of brain tumors and other neurological conditions. The company recently shipped its 50th ZAP-X system and is increasing production capacity to support growing demand from academic medical centers, community hospitals, and physician-led practices.
Nearly 10,000 patients have been treated worldwide using ZAP-X, according to the company. The new financing will help ZAP broaden commercial adoption in the United States and other international markets while expanding manufacturing and deployment capacity.
Catalio Capital Management led the round as part of its healthcare and AI investment strategy. Nicholas von Guionneau, M.D., Ph.D., of Catalio is also joining ZAP’s board as an observer.
Beyond its established work in neuro-oncology, ZAP is studying an emerging approach it calls radiomodulation, which uses precisely targeted low-dose ionizing radiation with the goal of influencing neurological activity. The company and its collaborators have evaluated the concept in multiple mammalian brain models over the past decade.
ZAP recently reported preliminary findings from a first-in-human pilot study evaluating radiomodulation delivered with the ZAP-X platform in patients with severe treatment-resistant depression. The company characterized the early results as encouraging and said broader multicenter studies are being planned, beginning with treatment-resistant depression and addiction. These neuropsychiatric applications remain investigational, and additional clinical research will be required to establish safety and efficacy.
Founded in 2014 by neurosurgeon John R. Adler, M.D., ZAP is focused on expanding access to non-invasive robotic therapeutics in neuroscience. Adler is Emeritus Dorothy & TK Chan Professor of Neurosurgery and Radiation Oncology at Stanford University.
Baheal has supported ZAP’s expansion in China, while Catalio’s investment is expected to help accelerate U.S. adoption and broader international growth.
KEY QUOTES:
“This financing reflects our conviction that ZAP Surgical is uniquely positioned to usher in a new wave of non-invasive radiosurgery globally. With rising healthcare costs in developed nations and underserved populations in emerging markets, intelligent robotics will play an indispensable role in reducing cost structures while elevating the standard of care. ZAP’s mission to make non-invasive brain therapy broadly accessible aligns perfectly with our strategy of backing disruptive healthcare technologies.”
Nicholas von Guionneau, M.D., Ph.D., Catalio Capital Management
“We are delighted to welcome Catalio as a new capital partner. As our understanding of the brain deepens, neuroscience will see unprecedented therapeutic breakthroughs over the coming decade. Scaling non-invasive, cost-effective therapy to tens of millions of patients worldwide will require strong, mission-aligned partners. Baheal has already been instrumental in advancing our presence in China and Catalio’s strategic support will be invaluable as we accelerate adoption throughout the U.S. and expand our commercial footprint.”
John R. Adler, M.D., Founder And CEO Of ZAP Surgical Systems

candidates.text:
D2 Capital Advisors Arranges $35.83 Million Construction Financing For Somerset Phase II In Philadelphia
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
D2 Capital Advisors Arranges $35.83 Million Construction Financing For Somerset Phase II In Philadelphia
D2 Capital Advisors arranged and closed a $35.83 million construction financing package for Somerset Phase II, a 170-unit multifamily development at 2202 E. Somerset Street in Philadelphia’s Port Richmond neighborhood.
The project is the next phase of Riverwards Group’s Somerset Station master plan.
The financing package includes a $19.87 million senior construction loan from Silver Heights Capital and $15.96 million in Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy financing from Nuveen Green Capital.
D2 Capital Advisors arranged both tranches on behalf of Riverwards Group, which is led by principals Mo Rushdy and Larry McKnight, P.E., LEED-GA.
The two financing components will fund construction of the 146,158-square-foot project.
Somerset Phase II will include 76 studio apartments, 38 one-bedroom units, and 56 two-bedroom units, along with on-site garage parking.
The development also benefits from a grandfathered 10-year, 100% real estate tax abatement.
Urban Renewal Builders, Riverwards Group’s affiliated general contractor, is constructing the project.
Both the senior loan and the C-PACE financing were structured on a non-recourse basis.
Combined with more than $10 million in sponsor equity, the financing supports a total project cost of approximately $46 million.
The transaction was led by Jack Cortese and David Frankel of D2 Capital Advisors.
The team structured the layered senior debt and C-PACE financing with the goal of maximizing proceeds while reducing Riverwards Group’s overall cost of capital.
Somerset Phase II is located next to the 220-unit first phase of Somerset Station.
Phase I is complete and fully occupied and was sold to the Philadelphia Housing Authority in May 2025 for $58.1 million.
The new financing fully funds another 170 units, which are expected to be delivered in early 2028.
The project is also expected to position the broader Somerset Station master plan for a future third phase.
Riverwards Group has operated across Philadelphia’s Riverwards neighborhoods since 2009 and has delivered more than 1,500 homes and multifamily units.
Its portfolio includes Somerset Station, Kensington Courts, Avenue V, N5 Square, and The Lenora.
D2 Capital Advisors has arranged more than $1.25 billion in financings nationwide across commercial real estate asset classes.
KEY QUOTES:
“Somerset Phase II shows what a proven sponsor and a proven site can do for a financing. Riverwards built Phase I on this same site, delivered it, and sold it to the Philadelphia Housing Authority, so Silver Heights and Nuveen were underwriting a team and a product that had already delivered here. Layer in a thinning supply pipeline ahead of an early 2028 delivery, and we were able to put together a $35.8 million capital stack that fits the business plan and sets Riverwards up well for what comes next at Somerset Station.”
Jack Cortese, D2 Capital Advisors
“We completed significant site work at the property during Phase I, so Phase II was positioned for vertical construction to begin quickly. It was critical for us to get credit for the value we created through that site work and the Phase II entitlements. Jack and the D2CA team made sure we captured that value and delivered proceeds that align with our business plan. Our Riverwards projects have been a reliable source of naturally occurring affordable housing in Philadelphia’s neighborhoods, and Phase II will continue that.”
Mo Rushdy, Principal of Riverwards Group
“This financing demonstrates the benefits of combining senior debt with C-PACE financing. Our longstanding relationship with Nuveen Green Capital and experience executing multiple transactions together helped deliver a streamlined capital stack, lower overall cost of capital, and greater certainty of execution for the Sponsor. We are pleased to partner with Nuveen, D2 Capital Advisors, and Riverwards Group on this transaction.”
Seth Greenwald, Managing Partner of Silver Heights Capital
“We were proud to partner with D2 Capital Advisors to provide C-PACE financing, administered through the Philadelphia Energy Authority, for this exciting new multifamily property in Philadelphia. Through C-PACE, Riverwards Group was able to access a significant non-recourse capital layer at a competitive fixed rate, reducing its overall cost of capital and helping make the project financially viable while delivering much-needed housing to this growing area of the city. This transaction underscores how C-PACE, as a flexible and cost-effective financing platform, can be a crucial part of a capital stack and can positively impact construction financing by bridging the gap between senior debt and equity.”
Mike Doty, Senior Director of Originations at Nuveen Green Capital

L3Harris Technologies has received a $33.1 million contract modification from the U.S. Space Force for the Unified Messaging System effort, increasing the cumulative value of the contract to approximately $1.527 billion.
The post L3Harris Receives $33.1 Million Space Force Contract Modification, Raising Total Value To $1.53 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
L3Harris Receives $33.1 Million Space Force Contract Modification, Raising Total Value To $1.53 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
L3Harris Receives $33.1 Million Space Force Contract Modification, Raising Total Value To $1.53 Billion
L3Harris Technologies has received a $33.1 million contract modification from the U.S. Space Force for the Unified Messaging System effort, increasing the cumulative value of the contract to approximately $1.527 billion.
The $33,141,075 modification raises the contract’s total face value from approximately $1.494 billion. Work will be performed in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, with completion expected by October 2028.
The Space Force is obligating approximately $2.4 million in fiscal 2026 research, development, test, and evaluation funding at the time of the award. Space Systems Command at Peterson Space Force Base in Colorado is the contracting activity under contract FA8823-20-C-0004.
The Unified Messaging System work fits within L3Harris’s broader position as a major defense technology contractor supporting military operations across the space, air, land, sea, and cyber domains. The company develops technologies spanning secure communications, command and control, intelligence and surveillance, missile warning and tracking, electronic warfare, satellite systems, and advanced missile technologies.
L3Harris reorganized its operations in 2026 around three mission-focused business segments: Space & Mission Systems, Communications & Spectrum Dominance, and Missile Solutions. Space & Mission Systems incorporates satellite and payload technologies, missile warning and defense capabilities, mission networks, and other defense and civil government programs, while Communications & Spectrum Dominance includes resilient communications and electronic warfare technologies.
The company also has extensive experience developing secure command-and-control and communications infrastructure for U.S. military customers. Its technologies include satellite command and control, secure satellite communications, tactical communications networks, real-time information distribution, and ground infrastructure used to connect sensors, operators, and other military assets.
In the space domain, L3Harris provides end-to-end technologies that include satellites, payloads, ground systems, mission planning, integration, data processing, and missile warning and tracking. Its portfolio includes work for the U.S. Space Force, Space Development Agency, and Missile Defense Agency, including systems intended to detect and track ballistic and hypersonic threats.
L3Harris generated $21.9 billion in revenue in 2025 and ended that year with $38.7 billion in backlog, reflecting the scale of its defense and government technology portfolio. Space & Mission Systems was its largest business based on 2025 revenue.

Oshkosh Defense Receives $32 Million Army Contract Modification For Heavy Tactical Vehicle Support
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Oshkosh Defense Receives $32 Million Army Contract Modification For Heavy Tactical Vehicle Support
Oshkosh Defense LLC has received a $31,972,227 U.S. Army contract modification for systems technical support services covering the Family of Heavy Tactical Vehicles, associated trailers, and related kits.
The modification, identified as P00018, was issued under previously awarded contract W56HZV-22-D-0004. The additional award expands Oshkosh Defense’s work supporting the Army’s heavy tactical vehicle fleet and the equipment used alongside those platforms.
Under the contract, Oshkosh Defense will provide systems technical support for the Family of Heavy Tactical Vehicles. The scope also covers trailers and associated kits, giving the Army a contracting mechanism to obtain technical assistance across multiple elements of the heavy tactical vehicle ecosystem rather than focusing on an individual vehicle configuration.
The Family of Heavy Tactical Vehicles supports military logistics missions that require moving personnel, equipment, supplies, and other loads in demanding operating environments. Continued technical support is important as the Army operates and sustains these vehicles across their service lives, including configurations that may require maintenance, engineering assistance, updates, or other technical services.
Specific work locations and funding amounts have not yet been established. Instead, the Army will determine both as individual orders are issued under the broader contract.
The Army expects the modification-related work to be completed by October 14, 2027.
The Army solicited the procurement online and received one bid. Army Contracting Command at Detroit Arsenal, Michigan, is the contracting activity.
Oshkosh Defense, based in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, develops and supports tactical wheeled vehicles and related systems for U.S. and international military customers. The latest modification extends its support role for the Army’s heavy tactical vehicle fleet while allowing specific technical requirements, funding, and performance locations to be established through subsequent orders.
The award is modification P00018 to contract W56HZV-22-D-0004.

candidates.title: Xcimer Energy Secures Additional $30.5 Million DOE Award
candidates.snippet:
Xcimer Energy has finalized an agreement for up to $30.5 million in additional funding through the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program, advancing the company's effort to commercialize laser fusion energy.
The post Xcimer Energy Secures Additional $30.5 Million DOE Award appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Xcimer Energy Secures Additional $30.5 Million DOE Award
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Xcimer Energy Secures Additional $30.5 Million DOE Award
Xcimer Energy has finalized an agreement for up to $30.5 million in additional funding through the U.S. Department of Energy’s Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program, advancing the company’s effort to commercialize laser fusion energy.
The additional award brings potential DOE Milestone Program funding available to Xcimer to $39.5 million.
Combined with a separate $4 million ARPA-E award received in 2024, Xcimer has secured up to $43.5 million in non-dilutive federal funding.
The latest funding corresponds to the second budget period of the DOE Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program and will be distributed as Xcimer achieves agreed technical and development milestones.
Xcimer is developing an excimer laser architecture specifically designed for use in a commercial fusion power plant.
The company’s approach uses gas lasers, gas optics and a two-beamline architecture designed to repeatedly deliver megajoule-scale laser energy while reducing the cost and complexity associated with other high-energy laser systems.
Xcimer is targeting electricity generation from commercial fusion during the mid-2030s.
Earlier in 2026, the Department of Energy approved the preconceptual design and technology roadmap for Athena, Xcimer’s planned commercial fusion power-plant architecture.
The company expects its first commercial fusion plant to begin operating around 2035.
Xcimer also launched operations in June at Phoenix, which it describes as the world’s largest privately owned laser system.
Phoenix is being used to demonstrate important elements of Xcimer’s excimer-laser and gas-optics architecture.
The company is simultaneously exploring defense applications for portions of its laser technology.
In September, Xcimer and RTX announced a partnership to develop directed-energy air defense systems based on Xcimer’s pulsed lasers.
The companies intend to demonstrate the integration and containerization of Xcimer laser technology with RTX air defense systems.
RTX also invested in Xcimer as part of the relationship.
KEY QUOTES:
“America invented laser fusion, and America should lead its commercialization. The Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program is built to turn American scientific leadership into commercial capability by putting private capital and private-sector execution behind ambitious, measurable goals. Xcimer is making real progress toward a new generation of laser fusion technology, and this award will help accelerate that work.”
Darío Gil, Under Secretary for Science at the U.S. Department of Energy
“We have moved from proving that the physics works to building the industrial technology that can turn fusion into a commercial energy source. This additional milestone funding gives us another powerful mechanism to accelerate that work while keeping the majority of the investment and risk in the private sector. We are building the laser, manufacturing systems and supply chain required to make commercial laser fusion possible.”
Conner Galloway, Co-Founder and CEO of Xcimer Energy

candidates.snippet:
High Lander has reached $30 million in total funding as the autonomous aviation software company expands in the United States and increases its focus on defense, homeland security, and other dual-use applications.
The post High Lander Reaches $30 Million In Funding To Accelerate U.S. Defense And Homeland Security Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
High Lander Reaches $30 Million In Funding To Accelerate U.S. Defense And Homeland Security Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
High Lander Reaches $30 Million In Funding To Accelerate U.S. Defense And Homeland Security Expansion
High Lander has reached $30 million in total funding as the autonomous aviation software company expands in the United States and increases its focus on defense, homeland security, and other dual-use applications.
The latest financing includes an additional strategic investment from EDGE Group along with participation from STEP, Protego, and Kinetica. High Lander plans to use the capital to expand its international operations, continue developing its autonomous aviation platforms, and strengthen its presence across national security markets.
Founded in 2018, High Lander develops software infrastructure for autonomous aviation, drone fleet operations, and low-altitude airspace management. Its technology portfolio includes Vega UTM, Orion DFM, and the newer Andromeda platform.
Vega is an Unmanned Traffic Management platform designed to coordinate uncrewed aircraft operating across complex airspace environments. Orion provides Drone Fleet Management capabilities that enable organizations to remotely manage fleets, missions, and autonomous operations.
High Lander is now extending that infrastructure into defense and homeland security through Andromeda, an AI-powered operational intelligence platform designed to create a unified view of low-altitude airspace.
Andromeda uses an open, hardware-agnostic architecture that can integrate sensors and effectors from multiple vendors under a single intelligent control layer. High Lander said the approach enables organizations to combine detection, classification, tracking, and operational response technologies while maintaining a common operational picture.
The platform is intended to help governments and other organizations distinguish authorized activity from unidentified or unauthorized aircraft as the number of drones and autonomous systems operating at low altitude increases.
The new funding will support further development of Andromeda as well as High Lander’s Vega and Orion products. The company also plans to accelerate expansion in the United States and additional international markets while pursuing strategic partnerships across autonomous systems, aerospace, defense technology, and homeland security.
EDGE Group’s latest investment builds on an existing strategic relationship with High Lander. The company said participation from STEP, Protego, and Kinetica also expands its network within the U.S. autonomous systems market and the broader global defense technology ecosystem.
High Lander is positioning its software as an infrastructure layer connecting autonomous aircraft, aviation management, and security systems. As drone adoption expands across commercial and government markets, the company sees increasing demand for software capable of coordinating both routine autonomous operations and security responses within increasingly crowded low-altitude airspace.
KEY QUOTES:
“High Lander is entering a new phase. Over the past several years, we have built the technological infrastructure that enables countries and organizations to manage a world in which autonomous systems are becoming an integral part of the airspace. We are now taking that same infrastructure to a new scale, expanding into new markets, the security sector, and strategic collaborations with leading technology players worldwide. The completion of this funding round allows us to accelerate key strategic initiatives and significantly expand our international operations. Our vision is to become the software layer that connects autonomy, aviation, and security, giving countries the ability to understand and control what is happening in low-altitude airspace.”
Alon Abelson, Founder And CEO Of High Lander
“As drone adoption continues to expand, the need for a unified aerial picture, threat detection, and coordinated real-time response is becoming increasingly critical. High Lander is developing technology that addresses these challenges, and its ability to integrate diverse systems and technologies under a single command-and-control layer is particularly significant. We believe the combination of the company’s technology, team, and strategic partnerships provides a strong foundation for expansion into international markets.”
Lital Leshem, Co-Founder And Managing Partner At Protego

National Math Stars Receives $30 Million NSF Grant
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
National Math Stars Receives $30 Million NSF Grant
National Math Stars received a $30 million grant from the National Science Foundation to expand its programs identifying and supporting mathematically exceptional young students.
The funding comes from the NSF Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships and will be deployed over four years.
National Math Stars plans to expand its programs from 10 states to areas representing approximately 75% of the U.S. population.
Founded in 2023, the nonprofit identifies young students with advanced mathematical ability and provides resources designed to support their development over multiple years.
In 2026, National Math Stars worked with three state education agencies and nearly 1,000 school districts to screen second- and third-grade students.
More than 20,000 children scoring in the top 2% on existing standardized mathematics assessments received recognition through the Math Awards Program.
Students can subsequently apply to the organization’s Stars Program.
The long-term program provides advanced coursework, enrichment opportunities, advising, community, and financial assistance based on need.
More than 900 students are currently participating as National Math Stars.
With the new NSF funding, the organization plans to screen more than 1.8 million second-, third-, and fourth-grade students annually.
By 2030, NMS expects to support more than 4,100 students through its 10-year programs and aims to reach 12,000 students annually by 2035.
The grant will also fund development and testing of an AI-assisted digital platform designed to provide personalized academic guidance at a lower cost per student.
KEY QUOTES:
“We aim to find extraordinary young mathematicians in every part of the country and foster their talents. These children are a future generation of researchers, inventors, and founders, but early support is essential to make those futures possible.”
Ilana Walder-Biesanz, Founder and CEO of National Math Stars
“This will ensure that talented children can develop their abilities regardless of where they live or their family’s income.”
Erwin Gianchandani, NSF Assistant Director for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships

Vates has raised €30 million, approximately $33.6 million, in funding led by IRIS's Growth fund and Bpifrance through its Large Venture fund, giving the open-source virtualization company new capital to accelerate technology development, expand its enterprise go-to-market organization and scale internationally.

candidates.text:
Vates Raises €30 Million To Accelerate North American Growth And Open-Source Virtualization Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Vates Raises €30 Million To Accelerate North American Growth And Open-Source Virtualization Platform
Vates has raised €30 million, approximately $33.6 million, in funding led by IRIS’s Growth fund and Bpifrance through its Large Venture fund, giving the open-source virtualization company new capital to accelerate technology development, expand its enterprise go-to-market organization and scale internationally.
The financing marks Vates’ first major outside funding after nearly a decade of self-funded growth.
Vates develops XCP-ng, an open-source virtualization platform, and the Vates Virtualization Management Stack, or Vates VMS. The company now serves more than 1,000 customers across approximately 100 countries.
North America already accounts for close to 50% of Vates’ business, with customers including Harman, AMD and North Carolina State University.
About 90% of the company’s revenue is generated outside France.
Vates grew more than 65% in 2025 and was recently included for the first time in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Server Virtualization Platforms.
The company said the new financing is therefore intended to accelerate an established North American business rather than fund an initial entry into the market.
Vates plans to invest significantly in the next generation of its virtualization platform, particularly across performance, storage, security, automation and management of large-scale virtualization environments.
Those investments will also address changing infrastructure requirements associated with artificial intelligence and other emerging workloads.
The company will also expand its enterprise sales, marketing and customer-facing resources, with North America representing a major focus.
Vates intends to increase its presence among large enterprises, public-sector organizations and service providers while investing further in channel partnerships and technology alliances.
Another portion of the funding will be directed toward expanding Vates’ global partner ecosystem, including distributors, systems integrators, service providers and technology partners.
The company sees those relationships as increasingly important as customers undertake larger infrastructure transformation and migration programs.
The investment comes during a period of significant change in the virtualization market.
Broadcom’s acquisition of VMware has prompted many organizations to reconsider their virtualization strategies as they evaluate licensing structures, vendor concentration, infrastructure complexity and long-term platform flexibility.
Vates is positioning its open-source architecture as an alternative for enterprises seeking greater control over their virtualization environments.
Its platform combines open-source technology with enterprise support, professional services and operational capabilities intended for business-critical workloads.
The company emphasizes interoperability, portability and transparency as ways for customers to reduce dependence on a single infrastructure vendor while retaining flexibility as their technology strategies change.
Vates said open source will remain central to its operating model following the new investment.
The company’s co-founders will remain majority shareholders after the transaction, preserving their control of the business.
IRIS and Bpifrance are joining as investors to provide additional capital and experience as Vates expands its organization and international operations.
The company plans to continue scaling globally while increasing its investment in North America, where it already generates a substantial portion of its business.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are not raising funds to change our strategy, but to accelerate the one we have pursued from the beginning. Today, we have the technology, the teams, an international presence and recognition. North America is already our largest market, and this funding gives us the resources to build on that traction and operate at an entirely different scale”
Olivier Lambert, CEO and Co-Founder of Vates
“Vates demonstrates that open source can meet the highest requirements of the market. Its virtualization platform is now adopted by organizations of all sizes around the world, including large enterprises operating critical environments where security requirements are particularly demanding. We are proud to support Olivier and his team in this new stage of their development and to actively contribute to making Vates a global reference in virtualization,”
Nicolas Herschtel, Partner at IRIS
“The virtualization market is undergoing a profound transformation, and organizations are looking for trusted alternatives that offer greater flexibility, transparency and control. Vates has built a compelling enterprise-grade open-source platform that responds directly to these evolving customer needs. Its strong technology, premium level of support to customers and growing international footprint, particularly in North America, position the company to capture a significant opportunity in the global infrastructure software market. We are proud to support Vates in its ambition to become a world-class technology leader.”
Cindy Ung, Investment Director, Large Venture at Bpifrance

candidates.snippet:
Arboretum LifeSciences has launched with $30 million in Series A funding to expand access to genetic testing for common diseases and build a molecular information platform supporting precision medicine and genomically stratified clinical trials. The financing was led by F-Prime, GV, .406 Ventures, Hims & Hers, Amgen and other healthcare investors.
The post Arboretum Raises $30 Million Series A And Launches Precision Medicine Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Arboretum Raises $30 Million Series A And Launches Precision Medicine Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Arboretum Raises $30 Million Series A And Launches Precision Medicine Platform
Arboretum LifeSciences has launched with $30 million in Series A funding to expand access to genetic testing for common diseases and build a molecular information platform supporting precision medicine and genomically stratified clinical trials. The financing was led by F-Prime, GV, .406 Ventures, Hims & Hers, Amgen and other healthcare investors.
Arboretum was founded by leaders from the Broad Institute’s Data Sciences Platform and combines artificial intelligence, genomic testing and clinical data.
The company is initially focused on common conditions such as cardiovascular, metabolic and autoimmune diseases, areas where precision medicine has advanced more slowly than in oncology and rare disease.
For healthcare systems, Arboretum provides clinical genetic testing and access to a collaborative research network.
The model is intended to identify patients who may be at risk for preventable diseases, return actionable genomic findings and build molecular datasets capable of supporting research and precision clinical trials.
For biopharmaceutical companies, Arboretum plans to provide genomically stratified clinical development capabilities, patient matching and datasets that can support target discovery, trial design and commercialization.
The company has established healthcare partnerships with Advocate Health, Geisinger, Providence Healthcare and Cardiovascular Associates of America.
At Advocate Health, its testing will support the organization’s cardiogenetics service line and Advocate CV Genetics Registry.
At Geisinger, Arboretum will provide clinical genetic testing supporting MyCode-Connect, while its work with Providence will integrate testing and research infrastructure with existing registries.
Cardiovascular Associates of America will use point-of-care genetic testing across its specialty practice network.
KEY QUOTES:
“We started Arboretum to solve one of the biggest problems in therapeutics development: identifying genetically-defined populations that will have outsized benefit from common disease therapies. Twenty years ago, the field of oncology opted to leverage molecular information to find therapies that would treat smaller populations but have more transformative outcomes than general chemotoxic agents. This is a moment in time to make a similar bet on diseases like coronary artery disease, diabetes, and neurodegeneration. The goal of Arboretum is to build the scientific and operational infrastructure that turns that thesis into better therapies.”
Anthony Philippakis, M.D., Ph.D., Co-Founder and CEO of Arboretum and General Partner at GV
“Our focus is on building a durable and actionable research network that places patients at the center. Improving patient care is our utmost goal. By engaging patients in research, and designing clinical trials around the biological signal of each patient rather than population averages, we give patients better therapeutic options and create the clinical evidence needed for tomorrow’s diagnostics and therapeutics.”
Clare Bernard, Ph.D., President of Arboretum
“Drug developers in common diseases have historically had limited access to the large-scale genomic and clinical datasets critical to helping understand differences in disease biology and translate genetic insights into potential new treatment options. Arboretum is building a bridge from molecular information to real therapeutic impact, helping deepen our understanding of disease biology and supporting development of the next generation of precision medicines.”
Michael Montalto, Ph.D., Vice President of Precision Medicine at Amgen
“Precision medicine has enormous potential for patients with common diseases, but healthcare systems need scalable ways to integrate genetic testing into routine care. Our partnership with Arboretum allows us to expand access to clinically indicated genetic testing while contributing to high-quality molecular and clinical data that can improve patient care today and accelerate research and clinical trials for the future.”
Terry Gilliland, President and CEO of Geisinger

Trustar Bankshares Raises $28.1 Million To Support Growth And Forbright Branch Acquisition
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Trustar Bankshares Raises $28.1 Million To Support Growth And Forbright Branch Acquisition
Trustar Bankshares has entered into an agreement for a $28.1 million private placement led by JCSD Mclean Investors and certain Trustar directors. The financing is intended to provide additional capital as Trustar Bank prepares to complete its previously announced acquisition of certain branches and related assets from Forbright Bank.
Trustar will sell $28.1 million of common stock and, to the extent JCSD’s investment would exceed 9.9% voting ownership, newly created non-voting convertible preferred stock.
The company expects to issue 1,372,700 common shares and 877,300 shares of Convertible, Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A.
Both securities are priced at $12.50 per share.
The private placement is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to close concurrently with Trustar Bank’s Forbright branch acquisition.
That transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and was expected to close as early as the fourth quarter of 2026.
Trustar plans to use proceeds for general corporate purposes, including supporting the capital of Trustar Bank after completion of the branch acquisition.

Together with our previously announced branch acquisition, this additional capital positions us well to continue expanding our franchise, serving our clients and communities, and building long-term value for our shareholders.”
Shaza Andersen, Chief Executive Officer of Trustar Bankshares and Trustar Bank

candidates.text:
XIVER Secures €28 Million Senior Debt Financing From ABN AMRO For €55 Million Investment Program
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
XIVER Secures €28 Million Senior Debt Financing From ABN AMRO For €55 Million Investment Program
ABN AMRO is providing €28 million in senior debt financing to Dutch semiconductor company XIVER as part of a €55 million investment program designed to expand manufacturing capacity and technological capabilities.
Eindhoven-based XIVER develops and manufactures integrated photonic chips, infrared sensor technologies, medical imaging technologies and advanced thin-film products.
The investment program will support upgrades to XIVER’s manufacturing facilities and equipment base.
One of the largest investments is the acquisition of an ASML deep ultraviolet lithography system, which the company expects to strengthen its production capacity and technical capabilities.
XIVER was carved out of Philips at the High Tech Campus Eindhoven and acquired by Dutch investors in early 2025.
Since the transaction, the company has expanded its operations and built relationships with a growing group of international customers.
The new production capacity is intended to meet increasing demand for semiconductor and photonics technologies driven by markets including artificial intelligence, defense and other strategic technology applications.
ABN AMRO said the financing aligns with its strategy of supporting European companies operating in strategically important sectors including technology, energy, defense and mobility.
KEY QUOTES:
“As global competition for critical technologies intensifies, Europe must continue to invest in innovative semiconductor and photonics companies that strengthen its technological capabilities and economic resilience. At ABN AMRO, supporting these strategic sectors is a key part of our ambition to contribute to Europe’s technological resilience and long-term economic strength. We are proud to support XIVER’s growth journey and contribute to the scaling of a Dutch technology company that is becoming an increasingly important player in the global semiconductor ecosystem.”
Hans Jansen, Senior Corporate Banker at ABN AMRO
“I am extremely proud of what our team has achieved in such a short period of time. With the support of our investors and ABN AMRO, we can now substantially scale our production capacity to meet the rapidly growing production requirements of our global customer base. At the same time, these investments further strengthen our technological and industrial position and represent an important next step towards establishing XIVER in a strategically controlling position within the global semiconductor value chain.”
Wil van de Wiel, CEO of XIVER
“We can now accelerate the further expansion of our position within the European semiconductor and photonics ecosystem. Demand for our products and services is being driven by major global developments in AI, defence and the semiconductor industry as a whole. XIVER has the technology, infrastructure and industrialisation expertise required to play an increasingly important role in these rapidly growing markets.”
Cees Meeuwis, Founder and Lead Investor of XIVER

candidates.snippet:
6K Additive has executed a final $27.4 million secured loan agreement with the Export-Import Bank of the United States to expand domestic manufacturing capacity for critical materials used in aerospace, defense, space, energy and advanced industrial applications.
The post 6K Additive Secures $27.4 Million EXIM Loan For U.S. Manufacturing Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
6K Additive Secures $27.4 Million EXIM Loan For U.S. Manufacturing Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
6K Additive Secures $27.4 Million EXIM Loan For U.S. Manufacturing Expansion
6K Additive has executed a final $27.4 million secured loan agreement with the Export-Import Bank of the United States to expand domestic manufacturing capacity for critical materials used in aerospace, defense, space, energy and advanced industrial applications.
The six-year facility is available for drawdown through June 30, 2028.
The financing includes an initial 12-month interest-only period followed by amortizing principal payments during the remaining five years.
The loan will carry a fixed Commercial Interest Reference Rate determined five business days before the first disbursement. The published rate cited in the announcement was 5.38%.
Up to $25.2 million of the facility will finance eligible project costs, while up to $2.2 million will finance an 8.9% EXIM exposure fee on disbursements.
6K estimated an all-in annual borrowing cost of approximately 6.86% based on then-current published rates. The facility also includes a 0.5% annual commitment fee on undrawn and uncanceled commitments during the drawdown period.
Proceeds are immediately available to reimburse 6K for equipment and infrastructure purchases related to expansion of its Burgettstown, Pennsylvania, manufacturing facility.
The expansion includes four new buildings and additional manufacturing equipment intended to increase production of nickel, titanium, tungsten, C-103 and other advanced metal powders.
The loan was approved through EXIM’s Make More in America Initiative in coordination with the U.S. Department of War’s Defense Production Act Title III initiative.
6K said the financing was initially approved by EXIM’s board in December 2025, subject to completion of final loan documentation.
KEY QUOTES:
“Finalizing this agreement with EXIM marks an important milestone for 6K Additive and reinforces the strategic importance of expanding domestic production of the critical materials essential to America’s defense and advanced manufacturing industries. This investment directly supports the Make More in America Initiative and provides 6K Additive with the funding required to execute our planned capacity expansion while preserving our existing capital to support continued growth. We greatly appreciate EXIM Chairman John Jovanovic’s leadership and support in bringing this agreement to completion.”
Frank Roberts, CEO of 6K Additive

candidates.title: Mistlabs Launches Ambi Following $26 Million Funding Round To Advance Real-Time Ambient AI And AI-to-AI Communication
candidates.snippet:
Mistlabs launched Ambi, an ambient intelligence platform designed to reason in real time, anticipate user needs, and eventually enable communication between independent AI agents.
The post Mistlabs Launches Ambi Following $26 Million Funding Round To Advance Real-Time Ambient AI And AI-to-AI Communication appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Mistlabs Launches Ambi Following $26 Million Funding Round To Advance Real-Time Ambient AI And AI-to-AI Communication
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Mistlabs Launches Ambi Following $26 Million Funding Round To Advance Real-Time Ambient AI And AI-to-AI Communication
Mistlabs launched Ambi, an ambient intelligence platform designed to reason in real time, anticipate user needs, and eventually enable communication between independent AI agents.
The launch follows $26 million in Pre-A funding led by Luminous Ventures and Huaqin Technology.
Mistlabs said the financing will support development of its standalone AI wearable in addition to continued expansion of the Ambi platform.
Ambi is launching out of beta on Apple devices and is currently designed to work across the iPhone, Apple Watch, Mac, and MacBook.
Mistlabs describes Ambi as a system that goes beyond traditional AI summarization and task completion by continuously building contextual understanding of a user throughout the day.
The platform is designed to identify opportunities to act proactively rather than waiting for a direct prompt.
Ambi retains information about users’ preferences, priorities, communication style, and work patterns in memory, allowing its understanding to carry across supported devices.
The company said this persistent context allows Ambi to provide recommendations, identify missing information, flag irregularities, and continue working on projects even when the user is no longer actively focused on them.
One of Ambi’s features, called Routine, allows multiple agents to perform recurring tasks.
For example, during a meeting discussing competitors, Ambi can analyze and fact-check the conversation in real time while simultaneously researching competing products and preparing information for a follow-up proposal.
Mistlabs said Ambi can also continue evaluating a project after a meeting has ended and proactively flag new developments or issues that may require attention.
The company plans to expand the system further through agent-to-agent communication.
Under that model, individual Ambi agents would be able to communicate with one another on behalf of their respective users, subject to permissions granted by those users.
During meetings, the agents could identify overlapping priorities, surface areas of disagreement, and potentially suggest mutually acceptable outcomes as discussions take place.
Mistlabs said this capability is intended to allow AI systems to act not only as assistants but also as collaborators or mediators.
The company plans to introduce agent-to-agent communication in the coming months.
Mistlabs is also developing its own wearable AI hardware designed specifically around Ambi.
The company said the wearable is intended to give Ambi a richer understanding of the user and surrounding context beyond what is available through existing devices.
Ambi is currently designed with privacy considerations that include not storing audio by default.
Mistlabs said its broader strategy is to move beyond AI systems focused primarily on one-off prompts, task management, and summarization toward continuously available contextual intelligence.
The company is headquartered in San Francisco and is led by CEO Peter Mo.
KEY QUOTES:
“Most AI platforms today are built around completing tasks, but Ambi is our first step toward answering a different question: what happens when AI can understand, reason and act in real time? What entirely new use cases have become possible? We’re moving beyond AI that simply waits for a prompt. Ambi introduces real-time reasoning and actions that can happen sometimes before the user even thinks to ask; and in the coming months it will extend to mediating between users and maintaining intelligence across platforms.”
Peter Mo, CEO of Mistlabs
“While we’re starting with the iPhone, Apple Watch, MacBook and Mac, our move into standalone hardware sets the stage for Ambi’s intelligence to extend across entirely new device types in the future.”
Peter Mo, CEO of Mistlabs

candidates.snippet:
Dan-O's Seasoning has secured a $25 million strategic investment from The Newcastle Network, marking the consumer-focused private equity firm's first investment in the food category.
The post Dan-O’s Seasoning Secures $25 Million Strategic Investment From The Newcastle Network appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Dan-O’s Seasoning Secures $25 Million Strategic Investment From The Newcastle Network
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Dan-O’s Seasoning Secures $25 Million Strategic Investment From The Newcastle Network
Dan-O’s Seasoning has secured a $25 million strategic investment from The Newcastle Network, marking the consumer-focused private equity firm’s first investment in the food category.
The Louisville, Kentucky-based seasoning company plans to use the capital to expand retail and online distribution, introduce additional product formats, and bring more of its products to consumers as it continues scaling nationally.
Dan-O’s was founded in 2015 by Dan Oliver, who initially sold an early version of the company’s Original seasoning blend at a local farmers market. The business has since expanded into a national brand sold through more than 22,000 retailers and online.
The company has also built a community of more than 15 million home cooks across its audience and social channels. Dan-O’s attributes a significant part of its growth to customers experimenting with its blends, sharing recipes, combining flavors, and using the products across a broad range of meals.
Founder Dan Oliver and CEO Phillip Crosby will continue leading the company following the investment.
For The Newcastle Network, the transaction represents the firm’s first move into food and supports a broader strategy of backing founder-led consumer brands that have developed strong communities before expanding distribution.
The firm sees an opportunity for emerging brands to take share from established food companies by combining product differentiation with direct relationships with consumers. Newcastle plans to support Dan-O’s with capital and operational expertise spanning data science, technology, and go-to-market execution.
Dan-O’s has grown from a farmers market business into one of the faster-growing seasoning brands in the U.S. Its products are positioned as flavor-focused alternatives to traditional herbs and spices, and the company plans to continue expanding into new formats while maintaining its focus on its existing consumer community.
The Newcastle Network’s broader portfolio includes footwear company Kizik, collectibles business Super7, pet brand Pet Life Unlimited, and now Dan-O’s Seasoning.
The investment gives Dan-O’s additional resources to expand its retail footprint, increase online availability, and develop new ways for consumers to use its seasoning products.
KEY QUOTES:
“The brands we’re most excited about don’t just sell products, they change behavior. Dan has built far more than a seasoning company. He’s created a platform that inspires millions of home cooks to experiment, create, and enjoy cooking more. That’s rare, it’s incredibly difficult to replicate, and it’s exactly the kind of business we’re looking to back as we build our food portfolio. The Dan-O’s investment is just the beginning.”
Chris Casgar, Managing Partner At The Newcastle Network
“I started out at a farmers market with one goal: get people to put some Dan-O’s on it, have fun in the kitchen, and make food they were excited to share. Our Fan-O’s took it from there. They started shakin’ it on everything, mixing flavors, creating their own recipes, and making Dan-O’s part of their own cooking stories. They’ve built this into something way bigger than me. With Newcastle’s support, we’ll keep bringing more Dan-Good flavor, helping more people cook with confidence, and making time in the kitchen even more fun.”
Dan Oliver, Founder Of Dan-O’s Seasoning

candidates.text:
Melius Raises $25 Million To Expand AI Agents Lab For Creative Work
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
Melius Raises $25 Million To Expand AI Agents Lab For Creative Work
Melius has raised $25 million to expand its AI-powered creative operating system, including a $5 million seed round led by General Catalyst and a $20 million Series A led by CRV. Genius Ventures, Vine Ventures, and Anti Fund also participated.
The New York-based company plans to use the funding to grow its team, expand its go-to-market and sales organization, and continue building out its agents lab for creative work.
Melius provides creative teams with a shared operating system where teams of AI agents can handle much of the production work involved in developing creative assets. The company is designed to reduce the need for users to work across multiple disconnected generative AI tools or rely heavily on prompt engineering.
Melius was co-founded by CEO Joowon Kim, CTO Young Kim, and COO Arnav Ramu. Joowon Kim and Young Kim previously worked together at Ramp, while Ramu has experience as an entrepreneur as well as in software investing at Hg and investment banking at Guggenheim.
The company emerged from stealth in July 2026 and reached a seven-figure run rate less than three months later. Thousands of teams are now using Melius to build creative assets.
Melius is focused on automating work across images, video, and audio so creative professionals can spend more time developing ideas while AI agents handle more of the production process.
KEY QUOTES:
“Creative teams don’t have an idea-quantity problem; they have a resource problem. Generative AI made content cheap to produce, but using it still means prompt-engineering your way through a dozen different tools. We built Melius so teams of AI agents handle everything between an idea and the finished asset, so people can spend their time being creative instead of operating tools.”
Joowon Kim, Co-Founder And CEO Of Melius
“Watching Joowon, Young, and Arnav pivot and execute at speed showed exactly the kind of conviction and execution we look for in founders. While most generative AI tools for creative teams are single-purpose, a prompt box here, an editor there, Melius has now built a true operating system where agents can take a workflow from first draft to finished asset. As AI agents get more capable, that full-workflow is where the advantage will compound.”
Yuri Sagalov, Managing Director At General Catalyst
“From our very first meeting, Joowon, Young and Arnav have been obsessed with one thing: helping people create exactly what they imagine with AI. That kind of clarity attracts great people, and we’ve been super impressed by how quickly they’ve brought A+ talent onto the team. With years of trust from building together at Ramp and a bias toward shipping fast, they’re exactly the team to win this market.”
Veronica Orellana And Reid Christian, General Partners At CRV

candidates.text:
Furientis Raises $25 Million Seed Funding And Secures First Department Of War Contract For 100-Mile Interceptor
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Furientis Raises $25 Million Seed Funding And Secures First Department Of War Contract For 100-Mile Interceptor
Furientis has raised $25 million in seed funding led by Benchmark and secured its first funded government contract, supporting development of a 100-mile-range interceptor vehicle intended for homeland defense.
Benchmark General Partner Chetan Puttagunta is joining the company’s Board in connection with the financing.
The government contract is structured as a prototyping Other Transaction Agreement with the Department of War.
The financial value of the government award was not disclosed.
Under the agreement, Furientis will continue developing its interceptor and demonstrate the flight vehicle’s performance against Department requirements.
The Los Angeles-based defense technology company is focused on producing lower-cost defensive interceptors at significantly greater volumes than traditional missile production programs.
Furientis is designing its system around manufacturability from the beginning rather than optimizing only for maximum technical performance and then addressing production requirements later.
The company evaluates components based in part on whether they can be manufactured at a rate supporting 1,000 interceptor vehicles annually per factory.
Furientis is also targeting a final assembly process requiring less than one hour per interceptor.
Where appropriate, the company uses commercial off-the-shelf components rather than automatically specifying aerospace or military-grade parts.
It also manufactures important components internally, including solid rocket motors and seekers.
Furientis tests prototypes in the field on a roughly biweekly cadence, allowing the company to modify designs based on flight data rather than waiting through long conceptual development cycles.
The seed financing and government contract will support additional investment in vertically integrated manufacturing, expanded flight-test operations and hiring across engineering and manufacturing at the company’s Los Angeles operation.
Furientis was founded by Brody Franzen and Aris Simsarian.
KEY QUOTES:
“Furientis exists to resupply our critical deficiency in defensive munitions. Recent events have shown these threats are not theoretical, and the U.S. is genuinely running low on the systems that protect the American people. That is fundamentally a production and manufacturing problem, and it’s the one we built this company to solve.”
Brody Franzen, Co-Founder and CEO of Furientis
“Furientis is building truly remarkable technology with the aim of creating a platform that can scale rapidly with the lowest cost in the world. The team is comprised of some of the most talented propulsion, hardware, and software engineers in the world.”
Chetan Puttagunta, General Partner at Benchmark

candidates.text:
Mojo Vision Secures $24.4 Million Government Award To Advance Micro-LED Displays And Domestic Manufacturing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Mojo Vision Secures $24.4 Million Government Award To Advance Micro-LED Displays And Domestic Manufacturing
Mojo Vision has received $24.4 million in additional U.S. government funding to advance its micro-LED platform, expand domestic manufacturing capabilities, and develop monolithic full-color microdisplays for near-eye augmented reality applications. The funding was awarded under an Other Transaction Authority agreement through the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Policy. The package includes $20 million from the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program and $4.4 million from U.S. Army Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance.
Mojo said the award is the largest government funding package it has received to date.
The program will focus on developing ultra-bright monolithic microdisplays using Mojo’s proprietary quantum dot color conversion technology. The displays are intended to improve brightness and reliability while reducing size, weight, and power requirements for near-eye augmented reality systems used in defense applications.
Mojo expects the work to support equipment that gives warfighters improved situational awareness while reducing display system size and weight.
The program is also expected to advance the underlying technologies shared across Mojo’s broader product platform, including micro-LED technology, CMOS integration, and wafer-scale manufacturing.
Those technologies support both the company’s display products and its optical interconnect business. Mojo is developing its micro-LED platform for applications that include next-generation AI glasses and optical interconnects designed for AI computing infrastructure.
The company’s technology stack includes 300mm silicon architecture, GaN-on-silicon micro-LED emitters, photodetectors, proprietary quantum dots, custom micro-lens arrays, multicore fiber bundles, and proprietary software.
Mojo positions its platform as a scalable, manufacturing-ready architecture that can be configured for multiple applications while addressing conventional trade-offs involving brightness, size, bandwidth density, and power consumption.
The government program also supports a broader objective of strengthening domestic production of advanced microdisplays for defense applications. Microdisplays are used across systems including pilot heads-up displays, advanced night vision equipment, weapon optics, and unmanned platforms.
Mojo said the latest award will strengthen the manufacturing foundation underlying both its defense-oriented display products and commercial micro-LED technologies.
KEY QUOTES:
“This award accelerates our work to put ultra-bright, full-color displays into the hands of the warfighter and strengthen America’s ability to manufacture them. We built Mojo around a simple idea: the same micro-LED technology that changes how people see information can change how computing systems move data. This program strengthens the technology and manufacturing foundation behind both.”
Nikhil Balram, CEO Of Mojo Vision
“Microdisplays are crucial components in delivering information to the joint warfighter and are integrated into solutions across all domains including heads-up-displays for pilots, advanced night vision goggles, weapon optics, and unmanned systems. Securing a domestic supply of advanced MicroLED displays is vital for the Department’s next-generation defense applications, ensuring both performance and security.”
Michael Cadenazzi, Assistant Secretary Of War For Industrial Base Policy
