Sunbound Acquires Richter Healthcare Consultants And Raises $24 Million Series A
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Sunbound Acquires Richter Healthcare Consultants And Raises $24 Million Series A
Sunbound has acquired Richter Healthcare Consultants, combining its AI-powered revenue operating system for senior living with Richter’s more than 25 years of experience in revenue cycle management, accounting, Medicaid eligibility, reimbursement, and consulting for post-acute and senior care providers.
The acquisition follows Sunbound’s $24 million Series A funding round led by TTV Capital, with participation from Bling Capital, Fika Ventures, Live Oak Bank, and Ziegler Linkage Fund. The financing brings Sunbound’s total funding to $36 million and will support business expansion and continued product development.
Richter serves skilled nursing, senior living, home health, and hospice operators nationwide. Its services span outsourced revenue cycle management, accounting and controller services, Medicaid eligibility, reimbursement and clinical consulting, audit and compliance support, and EHR implementation and optimization.
Jennifer Richter, CPA, Founder and CEO of Richter, will remain with the combined company in a new role focused on industry partnerships and product strategy. Sunbound said customers of both companies will continue receiving uninterrupted service while gaining access to the combined platform’s broader capabilities over time.
The transaction also expands Sunbound further into skilled nursing, where billing and reimbursement workflows can be particularly complex. Together, Sunbound and Richter are on track to process approximately $3 billion in annualized payment volume.
Sunbound’s platform is designed to manage the revenue cycle from admission through payment. Its technology covers admissions, private payments, end-to-end revenue cycle management, and working capital, while combining automation with human revenue specialists who manage exceptions and more complex financial workflows.
The company said operators using its claims platform achieve a 99% claims collection rate and 96% first-pass acceptance rate. Sunbound also claims its private payments tools can save more than 40 hours per community each month by moving families toward digital payments and automating collections-related workflows.
Its admissions product is designed to verify payer coverage and a prospective resident’s ability to pay in approximately 30 seconds before a bed is committed. By combining those capabilities with Richter’s clinical, financial, and operational expertise, Sunbound plans to offer senior care providers a more comprehensive alternative to using multiple vendors for revenue and financial operations.
TTV Capital said the investment reflects growing demand for modern financial technology across senior living and skilled nursing. Sunbound is also backed by industry investors including Omega Healthcare Investors and Live Oak Ventures.
KEY QUOTES:
“Senior living operators spend significant time and effort dealing with manual and inefficient financial workflows. The industry deserves a modern solution that simplifies payments for both senior living operators and their families. Our platform directly addresses the operational inefficiencies, financial underperformance, and cash flow issues that have plagued operators for years. By joining forces with Richter, a company with deep expertise in skilled nursing and post-acute care, we can transform revenue operations for even more care providers.”
Manny Cominsky, Co-Founder And CEO Of Sunbound
“Our clients trust us with their most critical work, and that trust has always come from our team’s deep expertise in this industry. Partnering with Sunbound puts modern technology behind everything that our team already does well. Sunbound’s software handles the high-volume, repetitive tasks that have traditionally slowed things down, so our clients see faster results, and our team can focus on the work where their expertise makes the biggest difference.”
Jennifer Richter, CPA, Founder And CEO Of Richter Healthcare Consultants
“Healthcare finance is incredibly complex, and most senior living and skilled nursing operators lack modern financial technology. Sunbound’s AI-powered revenue operating system brings structure and predictability to an industry that has long needed it, and the company’s rapid growth signals strong product-market fit. We’re proud to invest in Sunbound as the company embarks on a clear expansion path to bring intelligent payment operations to the broader senior living and skilled nursing market.”
Neil Kapur, Partner At TTV Capital

candidates.text:
Acta Pharmaceuticals Raises $24 Million Seed To Advance Alzheimer’s Disease Early Intervention Pipeline
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 15, 2026
Acta Pharmaceuticals Raises $24 Million Seed To Advance Alzheimer’s Disease Early Intervention Pipeline
Acta Pharmaceuticals has raised $24 million in total seed financing to advance a pipeline of therapies designed for earlier intervention in Alzheimer’s disease, including its lead gamma-secretase modulator, GSM-779690T.
The Boston-based company was created to translate more than four decades of Alzheimer’s research from scientific founder Dr. Rudolph E. Tanzi into potential new therapies. Its lead program is the result of approximately 25 years of gamma-secretase modulator research conducted by Tanzi and the late Dr. Steven L. Wagner at Massachusetts General Hospital and the University of California, San Diego.
GSM-779690T is being developed as a once-daily oral small-molecule treatment intended for early-stage, long-duration disease modification and potentially prevention. The drug is designed to lower levels of Aβ42, an amyloid-beta protein associated with plaque formation, while increasing Aβ37 and Aβ38, which can interfere with aggregation. Unlike earlier gamma-secretase inhibitors, the approach selectively modulates the enzyme while seeking to preserve its normal biological functions.
Acta is evaluating GSM-779690T in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study in healthy adult volunteers. The trial is designed to assess safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics across single and multiple ascending doses. Preclinical studies cited by the company showed single-digit nanomolar potency against Aβ42, a near 1:1 brain-to-plasma ratio in mice, and oral bioavailability across multiple species.
Beyond its lead program, Acta is developing combination therapies based on research using Alzheimer’s-in-a-Dish, a laboratory platform developed by Tanzi and Massachusetts General Hospital colleagues. The models recreate important features of Alzheimer’s pathology and the aging brain and allow researchers to screen large numbers of approved drugs and natural compounds. The research has identified more than 30 validated combinations that the company said can curb Alzheimer’s pathology, with Acta licensing related intellectual property from MGH and advancing selected candidates toward clinical evaluation.
Tanzi’s research has played a significant role in the scientific understanding of Alzheimer’s disease. He co-discovered the familial Alzheimer’s genes APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 and has authored more than 800 scientific papers and holds approximately 50 patents. He is Director of the Genetics and Aging Research Unit and the McCance Center for Brain Health at Massachusetts General Hospital and serves as Joseph P. and Rose F. Kennedy Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School.
Acta said approximately $70 million in preclinical development funding supported the research that ultimately led to GSM-779690T. The company’s shareholders include Alzheimer’s Disease Research Foundation, Dolby Family Ventures, Gamma Bio Investors, family offices, and other mission-driven investors.
The new financing will support Acta as it moves its lead program through clinical development while expanding a broader pipeline aimed at intervening earlier in the Alzheimer’s disease process. GSM-779690T remains investigational and has not been approved by any regulatory authority.
KEY QUOTES:
“We founded Acta Pharmaceuticals to translate more than four decades of Dr. Rudolph Tanzi’s discoveries into new Alzheimer’s disease treatments to enable early intervention and prevention. GSM-779690T is the culmination of 25 years of research at Massachusetts General Hospital and the University of California, San Diego and approximately $70 million in preclinical development funding. We’re privileged to build on Drs. Tanzi and Wagner’s pioneering GSM research and decades of discoveries to give the broadest group of people the opportunity for early prevention and treatment of one of the world’s most devastating and costly diseases.”
George Alex, Co-Founder And CEO Of Acta Pharmaceuticals
“We’re entering a golden age in Alzheimer’s research. Our understanding of genetic risk, new diagnostic tools and growing evidence showing that lifestyle habits can delay and even prevent disease give us an unprecedented opportunity to proactively protect brain health, just as we protect heart health today—before symptoms start. Our vision is that GSM-779690T could someday serve as the equivalent of a ‘statin for the brain’: a once-daily oral therapy designed to restore a healthier balance of amyloid-beta protein generation in the brain before irreversible damage occurs, giving people an opportunity to intervene with the AD pathological process as early as possible. All the Alzheimer’s research undertaken during the past four decades is coming to fruition at this moment, and I’ve never been more optimistic that Alzheimer’s prevention is within reach.”
Dr. Rudolph E. Tanzi, Scientific Founder Of Acta Pharmaceuticals
“As the culmination of more than 25 years of structural innovation, we believe GSM-779690T is a potential best-in-class gamma-secretase modulator for the treatment and potential prevention of Alzheimer’s disease. Acta evaluated hundreds of analogues to optimize potency, brain penetration and drug-like properties, ultimately identifying a single structurally distinct development candidate. Published preclinical studies demonstrated single-digit nanomolar potency against amyloid-beta 42 together with exceptional brain penetration, supporting efficacy at lower dose levels.”
Kevin Rynearson, Ph.D., Chief Scientific Officer Of Acta Pharmaceuticals

candidates.text:
University of Pennsylvania Receives $22.5 Million Gift From Gabriel And Stephanie Gilinski
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
University of Pennsylvania Receives $22.5 Million Gift From Gabriel And Stephanie Gilinski
The University of Pennsylvania has received a $22.5 million gift from Gabriel Gilinski and Stephanie Gilinski to expand financial aid and establish endowed faculty positions within Penn Arts & Sciences.
The gift will establish the Gabriel Gilinski and Stephanie Gilinski Endowed Scholarship for undergraduate students in the College of Arts & Sciences, including students coming to Penn from Latin America.
It will also establish two endowed professorships spanning Penn’s history, political science and economics departments.
A visiting professorship will also be created to bring distinguished scholars to Penn for teaching, research and academic collaboration.
The scholarship expands Penn’s broader affordability initiatives, including its Quaker Commitment to meet demonstrated undergraduate financial need with grant-based, no-loan financial aid.
Gabriel Gilinski graduated from Penn in 2008 with a political science degree and a minor in economics.
He currently chairs Grupo Nutresa, a Latin American food company with more than 50,000 employees, 45 factories and operations spanning 17 countries.
The company’s philanthropic arm, Fundación Nutresa, supports educational scholarships as well as healthcare and nutrition programs.
KEY QUOTES:
“Penn is at its best when we bring talented students together with outstanding faculty and give them the opportunity to learn from one another. Gabriel and Stephanie’s generous commitment expands access to a Penn education while investing in the scholars whose outstanding teaching and research enrich our academic community. We are deeply grateful for their partnership.”
J. Larry Jameson, President of the University of Pennsylvania
“On behalf of the School of Arts & Sciences, I am delighted to express our profound gratitude to Gabriel and Stephanie Gilinski. Arts & Sciences is built upon the eminence of our faculty, who pursue the highest standards in their fields while unlocking the brilliance and potential of future generations. It is also shaped by international students and scholars, who bring their unique approaches to bear on some of the most pressing issues of our time. The Gilinskis’ generosity will have a profound impact, not just for individual students and scholars, but for the entire Penn community.”
Mark Trodden, Dean of the School of Arts & Sciences and Thomas S. Gates, Jr. Professor of Physics & Astronomy
“I’m a firm believer in the importance of the liberal arts and in the value of the critical thinking skills I developed through my studies in the College. Exceptional faculty are at the heart of Penn’s mission, and we are proud to support the recruitment and retention of scholars who bring complex problems to life in the classroom, make groundbreaking discoveries in their research, and provide students with unique opportunities to discover and learn.”
“Across Latin America, access to education creates lasting change for families, and I’ve seen the ripple effect it can have, shaping not just one life but an entire community. Penn gives international scholars a place to bring their own perspectives and experiences, and they leave shaped by everything they’ve learned from the classmates around them. That’s part of what makes a Penn education so special to me. I’m proud that this scholarship will make attending Penn possible for students for generations to come.”
Gabriel Gilinski

OuterSignal Raises $22M Series A to Bring Agentic Personalization to Every Consumer Brand
News provided by
OuterSignal
Sep 30, 2026, 06:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Co-led by Long Journey Ventures and Abstract Ventures, the round follows a January launch and rapid growth that now has OuterSignal powering thousands of consumer businesses and hundreds of millions of orders.
NEW YORK , Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OuterSignal , the agentic customer intelligence platform that tells brands who their customers actually are and activates them 1:1, today announced a $22M Series A co-led by Long Journey Ventures and Abstract Ventures, with participation from BAM Ventures, Top Shelf Ventures, SuperAngel.Fund , and Jerry Yang's AME Cloud Ventures. As angels, participation included Dave Heath , Rohan Shah, Alex Haro , Emery Wells, Kim Perell , Michael Preysman , Michael Perry, Ken Nguyen , Raad Mobrem , Zach Sims , Sahil Bloom, Steve Carroll, Michael Loeb , Rich Vogel, Troy Ossinoff , Sahil Bhaiwala , James Beshara and Nik Sharma, along with dozens of executives from OuterSignal's customer base.
Every day, hundreds of millions of consumers are treated like strangers. The gym buff, the new mom and the retiree get the same email, see the same products and load the same homepage because brands know almost nothing about who they are. OuterSignal transforms that, using public context to build a full picture of the person behind the purchase. From there, OuterSignal's agents put that to work.
That changes the work of nearly every team:
Influencer and partnerships teams learn when a notable customer buys and can reach out while it matters.
Lifecycle marketers build audiences around real personas, so college students and busy executives each get bespoke flows and campaigns written for them.
Acquisition teams send precise segments to media platforms and run ads that speak to the people who actually buy.
Product and merchandising teams see who is behind every SKU and category they manage.
OuterSignal customers report measurable lift across retention, acquisition, conversion and influencer marketing. Brands on the platform include AG1, HexClad, Jones Road Beauty, True Classic, Jomashop, Lucy, Gratsi, Magic Mind, and thousands more.
"We built OuterSignal to solve the very problem I had running consumer businesses over the last 15 years," said Zach Zelner, co-founder and CEO of OuterSignal. "Generative AI finally makes truly 1:1 experiences possible, but only if you understand each person on the other end. This round allows us to continue building best-in-class intelligence that drives person-level personalization across billions of touchpoints."
"OuterSignal's platform unlocks a new paradigm for agentic personalization. Their growth has been remarkable and we're proud to back them as they power delightful marketing and experiences for all consumer businesses," said Ramtin Naimi, Founder & General Partner, Abstract Ventures.
"OuterSignal is building something no consumer brand will want to run without. Technology like this is rare, and so is a company that moves this fast. We're thrilled to partner with them," said Lee Jacobs, Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Long Journey Ventures.
"As a retention team, everything starts with really knowing our customers, and OuterSignal has given us a clearer picture of who they are than we've ever had. It's also uncovered something we didn't expect: a huge number of creators and influencers who already cook with HexClad and love it. OuterSignal has become integral to how we build influencer partnerships, because the best voices for our brand are the ones already in our kitchens," said Noah Pine, Director of Retention at HexClad.
"We launch innovation designed to reach new customer targets, and OuterSignal shows us just how distinct those audiences are — data we use to sharpen our messaging and targeting. It's also uncovered creators already engaged with our community, from micro-influencers to major names, that we'd never have found otherwise. We're now building partnerships with people who already know and use the product. That's the difference," said Leala Francis, SVP of Customer Strategy, Product, and Member Experience Innovation at AG1.
"We thought we knew who our customer was, but OuterSignal showed us a much fuller picture of the real people buying from us. That changes how we think about everything, from the creators we partner with to how we talk to our community," said Cody Plofker, CEO of Jones Road Beauty.
OuterSignal will use the funding to deepen its research engine, build personalization that generates a version of every message for every customer, and grow the team across engineering, go-to-market, operations and customer experience. Brands can try OuterSignal free at outersignal.com .
About OuterSignal
OuterSignal is the agentic customer intelligence platform that tells brands who their customers actually are and activates them 1:1. It connects to a brand's commerce platform or CRM, builds a full picture of every customer, and powers the segments, VIP alerts, personalized campaigns and ad audiences that follow. OuterSignal launched in January 2026, works with thousands of consumer businesses, and is headquartered in New York. Learn more at outersignal.com .
Media contact: Donna Felix, [email protected]

candidates.snippet:

candidates.text:
University Of Washington-Led Optoelectronics Center Receives $22 Million NSF Award
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
University Of Washington-Led Optoelectronics Center Receives $22 Million NSF Award
The University of Washington-led Center for Integration of Modern Optoelectronic Materials on Demand is expected to receive $22 million from the U.S. National Science Foundation over the next five years to continue research involving advanced optoelectronics and semiconductor materials.
Known as NSF IMOD, the center brings together researchers from 14 universities across the U.S.
It was originally established in 2021 as an NSF Science and Technology Center.
The new funding represents a second five-year period of support for the center.
NSF IMOD combines research across chemistry, physics, engineering, and materials science to develop materials capable of integrating light and electronics.
Potential applications include photorealistic virtual reality displays, quantum communications, semiconductor technology, and future photonic computing systems.
One major research focus involves quantum dots.
The center’s researchers have developed techniques for printing quantum dots and positioning them within specific cavities that could eventually be used in quantum communications and quantum computing systems.
The team intends to further develop the quantum dots and supporting structures during the next five years.
NSF IMOD also runs extensive education and workforce development programs.
Graduate students participate in interdisciplinary training spanning chemical synthesis, quantum mechanics, materials science, and advanced semiconductor technologies.
Students also gain industry experience through internships with companies and national laboratories.
Partners include UbiQD, Nanopattern Technologies, FOM Technologies, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Tandem PV, and Nanosys-Shoei Chemical.
During its first five years, NSF IMOD researchers published 140 papers, hosted 36 undergraduate students through its Research Experience for Undergraduates program, and conducted more than 85 outreach events.
The 14 participating institutions include the University of Washington, UC Berkeley, Columbia University, University of Chicago, Northwestern University, University of Pennsylvania, University of Maryland, Georgia Tech, University of Colorado Boulder, Arizona State University, Rice University, Lehigh University, City College of New York, and University of Maryland, Baltimore County.
KEY QUOTES:
“The point of this center is to tackle problems that are too big for one scientist or even two or three to tackle by themselves.”
David Ginger, Director of NSF IMOD and Professor of Chemistry at the University of Washington
“We’re really excited to see our students start taking important roles, and then eventually we hope they move into leadership roles in this space of commercializing new semiconductor materials.”
David Ginger, Director of NSF IMOD and Professor of Chemistry at the University of Washington
“Just as the atomic structure of a quantum dot produces unique and exciting properties, the exceptionally interdisciplinary structure of NSF IMOD is enabling foundational science and technological innovations that would not otherwise be possible.”
Birgit Schwenzer, Program Director in the NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences

candidates.text:
Helical Fusion Raises $20.6 Million In Series B Second Close With Fuji Electric And Other Investors
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Helical Fusion Raises $20.6 Million In Series B Second Close With Fuji Electric And Other Investors
Helical Fusion raised JPY 3.23 billion, or approximately $20.6 million, in the second close of its Series B financing as it advances development of its commercial fusion program. Fuji Electric joined the round as both a strategic investor and an Official Partner of Helical Fusion’s Helix Program.
Additional investors included Hazama Ando, Fujikura, Tokyo Gas, KKT, Urata, Kepple Group, and Ecrowd NEXT, along with other corporate and individual investors.
Including grants, loans, and other financing, Helical Fusion’s cumulative funding has reached approximately JPY 13.15 billion, or $83.8 million.
The company plans to use the new capital to accelerate the Helix Program, its roadmap toward commercially viable fusion power.
Helical Fusion is developing Helix HARUKA, an integrated demonstration device, and Helix KANATA, which is intended to become its first fusion power plant capable of net-electricity generation in the 2030s.
Construction of Helix HARUKA is underway at the National Institute for Fusion Science campus in Toki City, Japan.
More than 30 Japanese companies are participating in development and manufacturing for the project.
Fuji Electric and Helical Fusion began working together in 2025 when Fuji Electric agreed to supply power equipment for Helical Fusion’s high-temperature superconducting magnet development.
The expanded relationship will include collaboration on products, services, and technologies required for future fusion power systems.
KEY QUOTES:
“The Helix Program is steadily moving forward. At the Helix HARUKA construction site, our team and industrial partners are working together every day to turn fusion technology into real hardware.”
“Japan has accumulated nearly 70 years of knowledge in Helical Stellarator research and has one of the world’s strongest manufacturing and engineering ecosystems. We intend to bring these strengths together to realize commercial fusion power and create a new global energy industry.”
Takaya Taguchi, Co-Founder and CEO of Helical Fusion

candidates.title: Polyphron Raises $20M to Predict Drug Toxicity in Human Tissue Before Clinical Trials
candidates.snippet: An MRI in late 2023 found a mass on Matthew Osman's pancreas. It turned out to be benign, but the months of not knowing made him ask why medicine still cannot predict what happens inside the human body. Today, his company Polyphron grows living human heart tissue in an automated foundry and uses it to teach AI what a drug will do next, backed by a fresh $20M. Find out why Osman believes the real bottleneck in AI-driven biology has nothing to do with generating ideas.

The investment consists of approximately $10 million in financing led by Tiger Global, with participation from Mark Cuban Companies, expected to close during the week of the announcement, and an additional $10 million commitment from Tiger Global to a previously announced private investment in public equity (PIPE) financing.

candidates.text:
FORT Robotics Secures About $20 Million In New Funding Commitments Led By Tiger Global And Mark Cuban Companies
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
FORT Robotics Secures About $20 Million In New Funding Commitments Led By Tiger Global And Mark Cuban Companies
FORT Robotics, a Philadelphia-based provider of safety technology for autonomous machines and robotics systems, has secured approximately $20 million in additional financing commitments from existing investors, including Tiger Global and Mark Cuban Companies. The investment consists of approximately $10 million in financing led by Tiger Global, with participation from Mark Cuban Companies, expected to close during the week of the announcement, and an additional $10 million commitment from Tiger Global to a previously announced private investment in public equity (PIPE) financing.
The PIPE investment is expected to close in connection with FORT’s proposed business combination with Newbury Street II Acquisition Corp. (NASDAQ: NTWO), a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company.
Including previously announced PIPE investments, the latest commitments bring total committed PIPE capital associated with the proposed transaction to more than $50 million.
FORT plans to use the additional financing to expand its workforce, strengthen operating capacity, and support growing customer demand across industries adopting robotics and physical artificial intelligence.
The company develops safety and security infrastructure intended to help autonomous machines operate reliably in environments where they interact with people and other equipment.
Its technology is marketed as a Trust Layer for Physical AI, providing capabilities designed to improve machine safety, secure communications, and operational control.
FORT’s products are used across warehousing, manufacturing, construction, transportation, agriculture, mining, energy, defense, and other industrial applications.
The company reports that its technology has been deployed across more than 19,500 units serving over 600 customers worldwide.
Its customer base includes Agility Robotics, DoorDash, Cobot, Zoox, Textron, and Google DeepMind.
As businesses introduce more advanced autonomous machines into workplaces and other operating environments, FORT sees increasing demand for safety infrastructure that can be integrated across different robotics platforms.
The company focuses on helping manufacturers and end users improve safety, support certification requirements, and accelerate deployment of autonomous systems.
The new financing will support FORT’s efforts to serve expanding customer opportunities, particularly in warehousing, construction, defense, and other markets where robotic systems are being introduced at greater scale.
Tiger Global has invested in FORT since 2022, when it led the company’s Series B financing.
The latest commitment follows several business developments, including an expanded partnership with Agility Robotics and the introduction of FORT’s Connectivity Aggregation software product.
FORT was founded in 2018 and has secured 25 patents covering technologies associated with robotics safety and autonomous operations.
The company is pursuing a public listing through its proposed merger with Newbury Street II Acquisition Corp.
Upon completion, the combined business is expected to operate as FORT Robotics Holdings and trade on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol FROB, subject to applicable approvals.
FORT is positioning the proposed listing as an opportunity to become a publicly traded company principally dedicated to safety infrastructure for physical AI.
The business combination remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, along with other closing conditions.
The additional funding commitments are intended to support FORT’s growth plans as it prepares for the proposed transaction and expands its technology across the robotics industry.
KEY QUOTES:
“As the opportunity for physical AI continues to expand, we believe FORT plays a critical role in building an independent safety layer that is foundational to its adoption. Our continued investment reflects our conviction in FORT’s progress and promise.”
Griffin Schroeder, Partner At Tiger Global
“Automation and autonomy are expanding across nearly every major industry, creating a significant need for solutions that make intelligent machines safe, secure, and reliable. Tiger Global’s increased commitment gives us additional resources to scale our team and operating capacity as we respond to growing customer demand. We believe the opportunity for FORT has never been greater, and this investment positions us to move faster as physical AI adoption accelerates.”
Samuel Reeves, Founder And CEO Of FORT Robotics

candidates.title: Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility
candidates.snippet:
Michigan State University received a $20 million grant from the U.S. National Science Foundation to establish the Integrated Diamond and Carbon Research in Space Applications facility, or IDiCaRS, a shared-use research center focused on semiconductor technologies designed for extreme environments.
The post Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility
Michigan State University received a $20 million grant from the U.S. National Science Foundation to establish the Integrated Diamond and Carbon Research in Space Applications facility, or IDiCaRS, a shared-use research center focused on semiconductor technologies designed for extreme environments.
The facility will bring together advanced diamond and carbon materials research, electronic device fabrication, and high-energy radiation testing to accelerate the development of electronics capable of operating in space and other harsh environments.
Space radiation can damage conventional semiconductor devices, presenting challenges for spacecraft operating beyond low Earth orbit and for future missions traveling farther into space.
IDiCaRS will create an end-to-end research infrastructure to develop diamond and related carbon materials, fabricate electronic devices, and test how those devices respond to radiation.
The facility will be led by Wen Li, MSU Research Foundation Distinguished Professor in the College of Engineering and executive director of Fraunhofer USA Center Midwest.
High-energy radiation testing will use heavy-ion beams at Michigan State University’s Facility for Rare Isotope Beams.
MSU described the project as a first-of-its-kind niche facility, including a diamond foundry intended to allow researchers to move more quickly from materials development through device fabrication and harsh-environment testing.
Diamond is considered promising for space electronics because of properties including high thermal conductivity and resistance to high temperatures, radiation, and electrical stress.
By combining capabilities that are currently distributed across different facilities and locations, IDiCaRS is intended to shorten development cycles and help establish shared testing and qualification approaches for electronics used in extreme environments.
The facility will leverage existing capabilities and partnerships involving the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams, the MSU Space Electronics Initiative, and Fraunhofer USA Center Midwest.
Research conducted through IDiCaRS could support development of more radiation-resistant and thermally capable semiconductors, potentially reducing spacecraft reliance on heavy shielding and redundant systems.
The technologies could enable smaller, lighter, and more efficient spacecraft systems while also contributing to high-power electronics and next-generation communications technologies on Earth.
IDiCaRS will operate as a shared-use resource for academic, industry, and government researchers.
Aerospace, defense, and satellite companies will be able to collaborate on radiation-hardened electronics for missions beyond low Earth orbit, while semiconductor and materials companies can access diamond growth, device fabrication, and radiation-testing capabilities.
Potential applications beyond space include power systems, electric vehicles, telecommunications, and other advanced electronics.
The project will also expand workforce development opportunities in Michigan.
Students will gain access to advanced semiconductor materials, manufacturing processes, research facilities, and specialized equipment.
Plans include updated undergraduate and graduate coursework, a graduate certificate, and an undergraduate minor connected with the facility’s research areas.
Education and outreach efforts will also include space electronics programs for middle and high school students and opportunities for community college students.
MSU said the facility is intended to strengthen Michigan’s position in semiconductors and advanced manufacturing while accelerating development of technologies needed for future space exploration.
KEY QUOTES:
“IDiCaRS will strengthen MSU’s ability to bring together researchers, industry partners and advanced research capabilities to tackle some of the most important challenges facing space electronics and semiconductors. Just as importantly, it will give our students hands-on experience with cutting-edge technologies and help prepare the highly skilled workforce needed to keep Michigan competitive in semiconductors and advanced manufacturing.”
John Papapolymerou, Dean of the College of Engineering and Director of the MSU Space Electronics Initiative
“We are building a first-of-its-kind niche facility — a diamond foundry — here at MSU. The goal is to give researchers in space and automotive electronics a place to move more quickly from developing a material or device to testing how it performs under harsh environmental conditions that can damage electronics in space.”
Wen Li, MSU Research Foundation Distinguished Professor in the College of Engineering and Executive Director of Fraunhofer USA Center Midwest
“We are excited to bring the FRIB Laboratory’s heavy-ion beam infrastructure to the IDiCaRS initiative to help expand MSU’s reach of cutting-edge research for extreme environments. Joining forces in advanced material science positions us to make a lasting impact on space exploration and semiconductor innovation while preparing the next generation of STEM leaders.”
Thomas Glasmacher, Director of the FRIB Laboratory
“This grant represents the culmination of decades of collaborative research between Michigan State University and Fraunhofer USA in advanced diamond and carbon materials science. What began as fundamental research partnerships has evolved into a shared-use facility that will accelerate the translation of next-generation semiconductor materials from the laboratory to the marketplace, strengthening America’s position in critical materials innovation for years to come.”
Thomas Schuelke, President of Fraunhofer USA and Professor in the College of Engineering

candidates.title: Restate Raises $20 Million Series A Led By Singular
candidates.snippet:
Restate raised $20 million in Series A funding led by Singular, bringing the durable execution infrastructure company's total funding to $27 million. Redpoint Ventures and Capital One Ventures also participated in the round.
The post Restate Raises $20 Million Series A Led By Singular appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Restate Raises $20 Million Series A Led By Singular
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Restate Raises $20 Million Series A Led By Singular
Restate raised $20 million in Series A funding led by Singular, bringing the durable execution infrastructure company’s total funding to $27 million. Redpoint Ventures and Capital One Ventures also participated in the round.
Restate plans to use the financing for continued product development and expansion in the U.S., including the opening of a commercial hub in San Francisco.
The company was founded by members of the team behind Apache Flink.
Restate develops durable execution infrastructure designed to help distributed applications and AI agents recover from interruptions while preserving state and workflow progress.
The technology is already used by hundreds of companies.
Restate supports durable execution for Replit Agent and enterprise workflows at companies including DOSS and BILT Rewards.
The company’s architecture is based on a purpose-built distributed log and event-driven orchestrator that combines execution, state, and communication.
Restate does not require an external database or search system.
The company also recently introduced Bring Your Own Cloud, which allows customers to run managed Restate deployments within their own cloud accounts and virtual private clouds.
Restate said the approach is becoming increasingly important as AI agents run longer processes, call external tools, interact with other agents, and need to recover reliably from system failures.
KEY QUOTES:
“Durable execution solved an important problem: it made individual processes reliable. But software is increasingly made up of services, agents, workflows and state that all need to stay reliable as they interact.”
“We believe durability has to become a property of the infrastructure itself.”
Stephan Ewen, CEO and Co-Founder of Restate
“What excites us about Restate is that they are redefining where durable execution can be applied.”
Henri Tilloy, Partner at Singular

AblePay Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By F-Prime
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
AblePay Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By F-Prime
AblePay Health raised $20 million in Series A funding to expand its healthcare affordability and patient payment platform. F-Prime led the round, with participation from A1 Health Ventures and .406 Ventures.
AblePay plans to use the funding to accelerate growth, expand its technology platform, and reach additional healthcare systems and patients.
The company focuses on helping patients manage out-of-pocket medical expenses while improving payment performance for healthcare providers.
AblePay said Americans paid approximately $591 billion out of pocket for healthcare in 2025, representing a 6% increase from the prior year.
The company’s technology integrates with healthcare providers and provides guaranteed non-recourse payment on an accelerated and predictable timeline.
Patients receive flexible payment options and can potentially save on their out-of-pocket balances.
Members also receive access to an advocacy team that assists with billing questions and issues.
AblePay was founded in 2016 and is now entering its second decade of operations.
The new capital will support additional product development and expansion as the company seeks to address affordability challenges for both patients and healthcare organizations.
KEY QUOTES:
“Healthcare affordability affects both sides of the bill. Patients need a better way to manage the cost of care, and providers need a better way to collect the revenue they have already earned.”
John Fistner, Founder and CEO of AblePay Health
“AblePay has built a differentiated model that addresses a significant market pain point for both healthcare providers and patients. The company combines a compelling patient value proposition with meaningful financial and operational benefits for healthcare organizations.”
Nikhil Marathe, Principal at F-Prime

candidates.snippet:
Basalt Health has raised $20 million in Series A funding led by returning investor NEA to expand its AI platform for post-acute care admissions. Existing investors Frist Cressey Ventures and 25m Health also participated. The round brings Basalt's total funding to approximately $24.5 million.
The post Basalt Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By NEA appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Basalt Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By NEA
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Basalt Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By NEA
Basalt Health has raised $20 million in Series A funding led by returning investor NEA to expand its AI platform for post-acute care admissions. Existing investors Frist Cressey Ventures and 25m Health also participated. The round brings Basalt’s total funding to approximately $24.5 million.
Basalt uses AI to process post-acute care referrals arriving through fax, portals or electronic medical record integrations and evaluate patients against a facility’s clinical criteria.
The platform also supports admissions, benefit verification and prior authorization workflows.
At Lifepoint Health, Basalt reduced median chart processing time by 86%, from 8.5 minutes to 1.2 minutes.
Basalt has worked with Lifepoint since its 2025 seed round and expects to expand to 49 additional Lifepoint markets by the end of 2026.
The company is also deploying across 62 ScionHealth hospitals by year-end, where the platform is expected to manage incoming referrals across a network of more than 6,000 practitioners.
Basalt plans to use the Series A proceeds to extend its platform from admissions into discharge and payer workflows.
The company will also expand its sales, marketing, implementation and engineering teams.
KEY QUOTES:
“Case managers are still sending 70-page packets and waiting for responses, while patients remain stranded in hospital beds. Basalt turns that uncertainty into fast, defensible decisions. This funding gives us the power to transform one of healthcare’s most stubbornly inefficient systems.”
Ben Hackett, Founder and CEO of Basalt Health
“Basalt is tackling a massive healthcare challenge with a rare combination of clinical impact, operational value, and rapid adoption. The company’s AI-powered platform is becoming essential infrastructure for care teams, and we’re thrilled to continue our partnership with Ben and the Basalt team to transform how patients move into post-acute care.”
Blake Wu, Partner at NEA and Basalt Health Board Member
“Basalt is what we mean when we say AI should disappear into the workflow. Case managers don’t see a chatbot. They see the right bed, faster, with a clear reason behind the decision. Ben and the team have done the hard work of making AI reliable on the documents healthcare actually runs on, and that’s why two major health systems are scaling it network-wide. We’re proud to have been part of the journey from the start.”
Merrill Anovick, General Partner at 25madison and Basalt Health Board Member
“Basalt represents the kind of innovation healthcare needs right now: technology that creates measurable value while fitting naturally into existing clinical and operational workflows. Their platform helps organizations identify opportunities sooner, streamline operations and patient access, and support better outcomes without increasing burden on frontline teams. We’re excited to see the company continue to scale its impact through this next phase of growth.”
Al Smith, Senior Vice President and Chief Information Officer of Lifepoint Health
“What started as a new technology platform with an innovation partner, has quickly transformed how our team members’ work every day. Basalt helps our teams work faster, make more informed decisions, and deliver a better experience for our patients and our partners.”
Sarah Stuart, SVP Growth and Transformation at ScionHealth

candidates.text:
Kopin Secures Additional $18.6 Million U.S. Army Award For Color MicroLED Technology
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Kopin Secures Additional $18.6 Million U.S. Army Award For Color MicroLED Technology
Kopin Corporation secured an additional $18.6 million sole-source award from the Office of the Secretary of War through U.S. Army Contracting Command under the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program.
The new award brings Kopin’s cumulative IBAS funding to $34 million.
The funding represents the second major U.S. government investment supporting Kopin’s color MicroLED microdisplay technology.
Kopin plans to use the latest award to develop two additional MicroLED display configurations for ground-soldier and pilot applications.
The funding will also support expanding U.S.-based MicroLED manufacturing capabilities.
Kopin said the investment is intended to accelerate the onshoring of MicroLED manufacturing processes for advanced defense and commercial applications.
The company is developing the additional displays for next-generation soldier visual systems and pilot heads-up displays.
These applications require high brightness, rugged durability, power efficiency, and reliable performance across demanding operating environments.
Kopin said the technology could also support future weapon sights, helmet-mounted systems, and augmented reality platforms.
The award also advances Kopin’s broader strategy of supplying display and optical technologies across defense, medical, enterprise, and AI infrastructure markets.
KEY QUOTES:
“Securing additional IBAS funding represents significant continued validation of Kopin’s MicroLED technology and its importance to next-generation U.S. defense systems.”
Michael Murray, CEO of Kopin
“Combined with our previous IBAS investment, the U.S. government has now committed $34 million through IBAS to advance MicroLED technology.”
Michael Murray, CEO of Kopin
“This enables Kopin to accelerate the development and U.S.-based manufacturing of additional high-performance MicroLED displays designed for next-generation soldier and pilot systems while separately enabling the foundational MicroLED platform technology for our AI Interconnect products.”
Michael Murray, CEO of Kopin

candidates.title: Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million
candidates.snippet:
Atombeam has raised $18.3 million through a Regulation A+ offering hosted on StartEngine, bringing the AI infrastructure company's total funding to more than $55 million.
The post Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million
Atombeam has raised $18.3 million through a Regulation A+ offering hosted on StartEngine, bringing the AI infrastructure company’s total funding to more than $55 million.
The company plans to use the capital to accelerate commercialization of Neurpac, its data compaction and encryption software, while advancing its Persistent Cognitive Machine, or PCM, through independent benchmarking and customer pilots. Atombeam said PCM completed its first full build in September.
Atombeam said its intellectual property portfolio includes 678 patent filings, with 308 issued or allowed and 370 pending. Neurpac is designed to reduce the volume of machine-generated data that must move across networks while allowing the original data to be restored at the receiving end.
According to the company, Neurpac can typically remove 50% to 90% of the data that needs to move in the use cases described in its announcement. Atombeam said the software can compact small packets that are difficult for conventional compression systems and increase effective bandwidth on infrastructure customers already own. The company cited deployments and validation across satellite, defense, and commercial communications.
Atombeam is separately developing PCM as an AI architecture with persistent memory and continuous learning capabilities. The company is targeting resource-constrained environments in which conventional large language models can be limited by computing, memory, power, or connectivity requirements.
Atombeam’s broader strategy combines AI-powered data infrastructure with a new model architecture designed for continuous learning. The company sees both technologies as responses to the growing network, data-center, and computing demands generated by connected devices and AI workloads.
KEY QUOTES:
“Closing this round marks an inflection point for Atombeam. We now have the capital, the team, and the technology to accelerate Neurpac adoption while bringing PCM through independent benchmarking and into customer pilots. Neurpac is in production with customers today, measured on their own traffic. PCM is something genuinely new: an AI that keeps learning after it ships and becomes an expert in the organization it serves with no data center behind it. In November we will put it beside conventional language models in independent benchmarks.”
“With Neurpac we are solving the challenges Large Language models exacerbate – wired, cellular and satellite networks and data centers pushed to the brink by heavy AI workloads and the barrage of data from connected machines. Simultaneously, with PCM we are creating a form of AI that addresses the very weaknesses of LLMs that lead to unprecedented network congestion and data centers that use as much power as small cities. In these ways we are using AI to address both the challenges of AI adoption today while creating the innovations required to realize AI’s full potential in the future.”
Charles Yeomans, Co-Founder, Chairman And CEO Of Atombeam

candidates.snippet:
Trebellar has raised $18 million in Series A funding to expand its AI-native platform for corporate real estate management. Blossom Capital led the round, with participation from Haystack, Alt Capital, 1Flourish and Bynd.
The post Trebellar Raises $18 Million Series A To Bring AI To Corporate Real Estate Management appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Trebellar Raises $18 Million Series A To Bring AI To Corporate Real Estate Management
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Trebellar Raises $18 Million Series A To Bring AI To Corporate Real Estate Management
Trebellar has raised $18 million in Series A funding to expand its AI-native platform for corporate real estate management. Blossom Capital led the round, with participation from Haystack, Alt Capital, 1Flourish and Bynd.
Trebellar is developing an AI-driven system of record intended to help enterprise real estate teams manage information that has traditionally been spread across spreadsheets, PDFs and separate software systems.
The platform combines information involving leases, space, employee headcount and utilization into a unified view.
Trebellar also incorporates commute times, transit access and employee sentiment to help corporate real estate teams evaluate whether properties are meeting organizational needs.
Rather than providing only a static analysis, the platform tracks the reasoning behind real estate decisions, their subsequent results and potential next actions.
Current customers include Meta, Uber, Merck and Cohesity.
The company was founded by engineers and operators with experience at Salesforce, Google, Waymo and Verkada alongside professionals with corporate real estate expertise.
Trebellar recently added Dave Radcliffe as an adviser. Radcliffe oversaw substantial growth of Google’s real estate portfolio during the tenures of Eric Schmidt, Larry Page and Sundar Pichai.
The company plans to use the Series A to expand its engineering and go-to-market teams, strengthen its AI capabilities and add enterprise customers.
KEY QUOTES:
“Real estate has been the one back-office function still running on spreadsheets and outside consultants. We built Trebellar to give leaders the independence to make these decisions themselves, with the same speed and confidence every other part of the business already has.”
Diego Ferreiro Val, Co-Founder and CEO of Trebellar
“What Trebellar has built is exactly what corporate real estate has been missing: Purpose-built AI that actually thinks about the problem the way we do, not just another dashboard. It’s quickly becoming a key part of how our team thinks about real estate decisions.”
Dave Gunter, VP of Global Workplace Services at Meta
“Corporate real estate is one of the last major categories AI hasn’t reached yet, not because the opportunity isn’t there, but because the problem needed technology built specifically for it, not a repurposed dashboard or another services relationship. Diego, David, and Adam are the right team to build that.”
Ophelia Brown, Blossom Capital

W4 Games Raises $18 Million Series B To Expand Godot Enterprise Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
W4 Games Raises $18 Million Series B To Expand Godot Enterprise Platform
W4 Games has raised $18 million in Series B funding to expand its international team, accelerate development of its enterprise technology and support growing commercial adoption of the open-source Godot Engine. The round was led by Tencent, with participation from OSS Capital, Lux Capital, Naval Ravikant and Tobias Lütke’s family office.
The financing brings W4 Games’ total funding to $33 million.
W4 Games also signed a multi-year strategic partnership with Tencent focused on expanding the company’s business and the broader Godot ecosystem in Asia.
Under the partnership, W4 Games and Tencent will work together on go-to-market initiatives, localization, ecosystem development, advocacy and market development aimed at increasing Godot adoption among enterprises, game studios and developers throughout the region.
W4 Games was founded by core Godot developers and contributors to provide commercial technology, cloud services, professional support and other tools for studios building games with the open-source engine.
The company plans to use the Series B financing to increase its international workforce by approximately 50% and continue expanding its enterprise products.
Godot is an MIT-licensed open-source game engine stewarded by the independent nonprofit Godot Foundation.
W4 Games said Godot adoption has increased substantially over the past several years. According to SteamDB data cited by the company, the number of games built with Godot and published on Steam grew more than 50% year-over-year in both 2024 and 2025.
W4 Games’ analysis of Gamalytic data also found that the number of Godot-built games generating more than $1 million in annual sales increased from two to more than 50 during the past three years.
The company also pointed to growing adoption among younger developers. Godot’s share of submissions to events including Global Game Jam and GMTK Game Jam increased from approximately 10% in 2022 to 50%.
W4 Games plans to continue contributing technology created through its enterprise work back to the Godot project when possible, allowing improvements developed for commercial customers to benefit the broader open-source community.
KEY QUOTES:
“This collaboration with Tencent marks an important next step for W4 Games as we expand globally and bring Godot to more studios and developers. With Tencent as both a strategic partner and an investor, we have an opportunity to accelerate the adoption of enterprise-ready Godot technologies, particularly in Asia, while continuing to strengthen the open-source ecosystem that sits at the heart of everything we do.”
Nicola Farronato, Co-CEO of W4 Games
“Over the past few years, Godot has emerged as one of the world’s fastest-growing game engine technologies, with W4 Games at the forefront of its adoption by major studios and enterprises. We’re excited to work with Tencent to build on the momentum and further establish Godot Engine as a leading platform for companies creating the next generation of video games.”
Juan Linietsky, Godot Engine Creator and Founder of W4 Games

Aventra Raises $17.5 Million To Scale Piranha Autonomous Precision Payload System
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Aventra Raises $17.5 Million To Scale Piranha Autonomous Precision Payload System
Aventra Defense Systems has raised $17.5 million in strategic financing led by Konvoy to scale production of its Piranha autonomous precision payload platform and develop additional long-range strike, one-way attack and intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance systems. Existing investor Lavrock Ventures participated alongside Booz Allen Ventures, Sands Capital and Langford Industries.
The financing also includes a funding facility from Western Alliance Bank.
Aventra plans to move Piranha from field-evaluation quantities into low-rate initial production while expanding manufacturing capacity at its facility in Herndon, Virginia.
The company will also increase flight testing and demonstrations with additional military services, combatant commands and allied partners.
Aventra intends to qualify additional payload and communications configurations spanning ISR, electronic warfare and kinetic missions.
The funding will also support hiring across engineering and manufacturing and the development of an additional platform that has not yet been announced.
Piranha uses high-altitude balloons and stratospheric air currents to carry autonomous payload systems over long distances.
The company is positioning the system as a lower-cost alternative for delivering ISR and precision effects compared with conventional long-range platforms.
Founded in 2025, Aventra has already deployed Piranha in U.S. Army exercises, including Arcane Thunder 26, along with additional evaluations and testing involving U.S., allied and partner forces.
The company said Piranha has completed approximately 400 flights demonstrating autonomous stratospheric reentry, long-range glide and delivery of kinetic and ISR effects.
Aventra said it has also secured its first series of delivery contracts as the system moves toward production.
KEY QUOTES:
“In under a year and with a lean capital investment, we took Piranha from concept to field deployment overseas, secured our first series of delivery contracts, and matured the system into a fully integrated platform. Today’s conflicts and the wars of the future will be won with volume, persistence, and affordability, which is why we’re working so hard to deliver more range and more kinetic effect. By using high-altitude balloons and stratospheric air currents to carry mass downrange without burning fuel, our approach delivers effects at greater distances, from higher altitudes, and at a fraction of the cost of conventional standoff munitions. We are leveraging physics to reshape economics and put cost-effective tools in the hands of the warfighter.”
Michael Weigand, Co-Founder and CEO of Aventra Defense Systems
“Affordable mass is ultimately a manufacturing problem. The Pentagon needs low-cost autonomous systems in volumes the traditional industrial base was never built to deliver. Aventra pairs a design that is inherently inexpensive to produce with a team that has already put hardware in operators’ hands at breakneck speed. That combination of resilient supply, scalable production, and proven field performance is exactly what our critical industries thesis is built around.”
Jason Chapman, General Partner at Konvoy
“When we first backed Aventra, Piranha was a concept and a team with a sharp view of the problem. A year later, it has flown in several major Army exercises and is under multiple contracts. We’ve seen what happens when a team brings commercial speed and manufacturing discipline to a munitions category the Pentagon has long overpaid for, and Aventra is on that path. We’re proud to keep backing a team that treats affordability and producibility as design requirements from day one.”
Alex Poulin, Partner at Lavrock Ventures
“Aventra is demonstrating how innovative, cost-effective systems can deliver meaningful results at the speed and scale of today’s missions. The company’s rapid progress in bringing its technology from concept into the hands of warfighters reflects a team with the vision and urgency to turn information into action. We’re proud to support Aventra, whose progress reflects Booz Allen Ventures’ commitment to helping companies turn innovative technologies into real-world capabilities for our nation’s most critical missions.”
Travis Bales, Managing Director of Booz Allen Ventures

candidates.text:
University Of Maryland-Led Biomanufacturing Lab Receives $17.3 Million NSF Award
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
University Of Maryland-Led Biomanufacturing Lab Receives $17.3 Million NSF Award
A University of Maryland-led project received a $17.3 million National Science Foundation award to create an AI-powered and remotely accessible laboratory for biomanufacturing research. The four-year initiative, called the Collaborative for the Realization of Autonomous Biomanufacturing Lab, or CRAB Lab, will combine artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and real-time biological measurements.
The laboratory will be housed at the Institute for Bioscience and Biotechnology Research in Rockville, Maryland, while allowing researchers elsewhere in the U.S. to remotely access its capabilities.
The project is led by William Bentley, Robert E. Fischell Distinguished Professor and Director of the Robert E. Fischell Institute for Biomedical Devices.
University of Maryland Department of Computer Science Assistant Professor Alan Zaoxing Liu is a co-principal investigator alongside Gregory Payne, Martha Wang, and Hussain Dahodwala.
Ang Li of UMD’s Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering is co-leading the project’s AI efforts.
The CRAB Lab is one of 20 Programmable Cloud Laboratory Node sites supported by an NSF initiative focused on developing AI-enabled infrastructure for automated science and engineering.
Researchers will be able to program workflows that design, conduct, and analyze biomanufacturing experiments remotely.
Automated laboratory instruments and AI systems will collect information during experiments and help determine what actions should be taken next.
Liu’s research group is responsible for developing the data and AI infrastructure supporting the laboratory.
This work includes managing large volumes of measurement data, coordinating experiments from beginning to end, and developing models capable of identifying what Liu describes as biological vital signs.
Those signals could help determine whether a biomanufacturing process is operating as intended or beginning to deviate from expected conditions.
The project will also use bioelectronic measurement technologies developed through University of Maryland partnerships with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
The technologies are designed to generate high-volume and high-speed biological measurements that can be used to train AI models.
Those models could identify combinations of measurements linked to product quality and other characteristics while experiments are still underway.
The CRAB Lab is expected to initially serve 30 biopharmaceutical companies through the Advanced Mammalian Biomanufacturing Innovation Center.
Remote access is also intended to make sophisticated automated laboratory infrastructure available to researchers at institutions that may not have comparable equipment of their own.
The initiative could ultimately help researchers accelerate experimentation related to medicines including vaccines and cancer therapies while improving reproducibility and reducing the time required to move from an idea to experimental results.
KEY QUOTES:
“This is a tremendously exciting moment. I’ve been building the systems that make AI fast and reliable, and this award is a chance to apply that work to something as tangible as making medicines.”
Alan Zaoxing Liu, Assistant Professor in the University of Maryland Department of Computer Science
“Almost everything in modern medicine, from vaccines to cancer therapies, depends on biomanufacturing, but the experiments behind it are slow, expensive and often hard to reproduce. We’re building AI agents that can design an experiment, hand it to the robots, monitor the data in real time and decide what to try next, so a scientist can log in from anywhere and have results the next morning.”
Alan Zaoxing Liu, Assistant Professor in the University of Maryland Department of Computer Science
“That shortens the path from idea to result by months. Just as important, a graduate student at a small school will have the same AI-driven lab at their fingertips as a large company, and that kind of access changes who gets to do the science.”
Alan Zaoxing Liu, Assistant Professor in the University of Maryland Department of Computer Science

candidates.title: Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power
candidates.snippet:
Hephaestus has emerged from stealth after raising $17.2 million to advance rare-earth-free high-temperature superconducting materials and develop a fusion reactor based on negative triangularity plasma geometry. The latest funding round was led by CiRi Ventures, with existing investors including Prescience Ventures, Teampact Ventures, Climate Capital, Unruly Capital, and CiRi Ventures.
The post Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power
Hephaestus has emerged from stealth after raising $17.2 million to advance rare-earth-free high-temperature superconducting materials and develop a fusion reactor based on negative triangularity plasma geometry. The latest funding round was led by CiRi Ventures, with existing investors including Prescience Ventures, Teampact Ventures, Climate Capital, Unruly Capital, and CiRi Ventures.
Founded in London in 2019, Hephaestus is focused on reducing two significant cost and scalability challenges associated with fusion power: the high-temperature superconducting magnets used to confine plasma and edge-localized modes, or ELMs, that can increase the complexity and cost of conventional tokamak designs.
The company used an AI-based plasma solver to evaluate a broad range of tokamak design parameters and identified negative triangularity as a potentially lower-cost configuration. Negative triangularity reverses the conventional D-shaped plasma geometry used in many tokamaks.
Hephaestus said subsequent results from research facilities including DIII-D, JET, and SMART have demonstrated that negative triangularity can provide strong plasma performance without ELM instabilities.
The company moved into hardware development with Anvil 0, which it completed in 2024. Hephaestus describes the device as the world’s first tokamak designed specifically for negative triangularity from its inception.
Hephaestus is also developing high-temperature superconducting materials using its proprietary MaDi-AI materials discovery platform. The company said it has identified, manufactured, and characterized multiple novel HTS materials at laboratory scale, with validation from the U.K.’s National Physical Laboratory.
Most HTS magnets currently used in fusion rely on REBCO, or rare-earth barium copper oxide. Hephaestus is developing alternatives that do not use rare-earth materials, with the goal of making superconductors less expensive to manufacture, easier to scale, and less dependent on geographically concentrated supply chains.
The new funding will support the company’s next major milestones. Hephaestus plans to begin HTS manufacturing at a new 70,000-square-foot facility in New Jersey in 2027.
By 2030, the company is targeting a demonstration of the commercial potential of negative triangularity through a net-energy-gain reactor designed to achieve Q greater than 1.
Hephaestus has also begun early-access discussions with other fusion developers interested in sourcing its HTS technology. The company is expanding hiring across its New Jersey, London, and Rome locations as it builds both its materials manufacturing capabilities and fusion development program.
KEY QUOTES:
“Fusion has the potential of adding tens of GW’s per year of clean stable power to the grid, but that only happens if it becomes affordable and scalable. That’s why we chose negative triangularity, and why we’re manufacturing our own novel HTS magnets, to realise fusion’s full industrial potential.”
Jack Zamattio, CEO And Founder Of Hephaestus

candidates.text:
Hunt Capital Partners Closes Financing For $17.1 Million Kansas City Affordable Housing Rehabilitation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Hunt Capital Partners Closes Financing For $17.1 Million Kansas City Affordable Housing Rehabilitation
Hunt Capital Partners, Riverstone Platform Partners and Kansas City Metropolitan Lutheran Ministry have closed financing for a $17.1 million rehabilitation of The Alexandria, a 55-unit affordable housing community in Kansas City, Missouri.
The property is located at 1328 E. Armour Boulevard and consists of two four-story buildings originally constructed separately in 1923.
The buildings were later connected through a shared elevator and lobby system and were most recently renovated using Low-Income Housing Tax Credit equity in 2006.
The Alexandria was 94% occupied at the time of the financing and had a waiting list of six qualified households.
The project will preserve 55 studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom homes serving households earning up to 30% and 60% of area median income.
All 55 homes will be covered by a 20-year Project-Based Section 8 Housing Assistance Payment contract.
The property has historically operated under a Section 8 HAP agreement that expires in 2029 and is expected to be renewed for another 20 years.
Planned improvements include upgrades to security, a secured and gated parking lot, building access and video surveillance.
Residents will also have access to voluntary supportive services including budget counseling, employment coaching, housing stabilization assistance and health and wellness programs.
The capital stack includes $9.1 million of federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits syndicated by Hunt Capital Partners and $6.4 million of state Low-Income Housing Tax Credits syndicated by Monarch Private Capital.
UMB Bank provided a $13 million construction loan, while Cedar Rapids Bank & Trust provided a $4.5 million permanent loan.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are honored to once again work alongside Riverstone Platform Partners, Metropolitan Lutheran Ministry, and UMB Bank to provide affordable housing in the Kansas City metro area. The rehabilitation of The Alexandria will preserve homes for families who need them the most.”
Jeff Weiss, President of Hunt Capital Partners
“Every week we see another affordable property somewhere in this country convert to market rate, drop out of its HAP contract or get run into the ground by an owner who has stopped reinvesting. The Alexandria is proof that there’s another way. The team stepped in, rebuilt the capital stack, and recommitted this property to affordability for decades. Fifty-five families get to stay in their homes, in their neighborhood, without the fear of displacement, and that’s the whole point of this work.”
Kelley Hrabe, Founder and Managing Partner of Riverstone Platform Partners
“We are proud to be the nonprofit partner of The Alexandria development that is not only preserving 55 homes of affordable housing but transforming them into beautiful places to live. We are excited to add this to our ever-growing portfolio of affordable housing.”
Scott Cooper, Executive Director of Kansas City Metropolitan Lutheran Ministry
“UMB is excited to play a role in the redevelopment of The Alexandria. Preserving buildings like The Alexandria is a great way to provide affordable housing to areas that are in need as housing costs continue to rise. We are proud to support the redevelopment of The Alexandria and to monitor construction progress in the coming months!”
Brady Ridnour, Vice President at UMB Bank

candidates.text:
Switched Source Raises More Than $17 Million To Expand Grid Capacity Technology
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
Switched Source Raises More Than $17 Million To Expand Grid Capacity Technology
Switched Source secured more than $17 million in funding to scale deployment of its Phase-EQ grid technology and expand manufacturing and production capacity. Cubit Capital led the round, with participation from ABB, Emerald Technology Ventures, Red Cedar Ventures, Southern States, Southwire Company, and additional strategic investors.
The financing will support a broader pipeline of Phase-EQ deployments across North America, while also funding manufacturing, testing, quality, and supply chain expansion.
Switched Source is adding manufacturing, quality, and supply chain roles at its Chicago headquarters.
The company also plans to continue developing additional solutions for utility distribution systems.
Switched Source’s flagship Phase-EQ product is an automated power-flow control device designed for distribution grids.
The system dynamically balances power across the three phases on distribution circuits, helping utilities improve reliability, power quality, and available load-serving capacity.
The technology is designed to address uneven and volatile electricity demand created by trends such as electric vehicle charging and heat pump adoption.
Switched Source said each Phase-EQ deployment can enable service for approximately 100 to 200 additional homes without requiring construction of new infrastructure.
The company’s technology has surpassed 150,000 operating hours across 12 utility service areas.
Field data from active deployments has shown increases of 10% to 25% in load-serving capacity.
Switched Source said Phase-EQ deployments typically require 14 to 20 weeks from purchase order to site activation, compared with one to three years for many conventional distribution infrastructure upgrades.
The funding follows the launch of a five-year, $99 million project under the U.S. Department of Energy’s Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships Program.
That project will deploy Phase-EQ units in the Southeast to support storm restoration and help utilities rebalance power when distribution feeders are reconfigured.
The system is also intended to help utilities restore service faster and reduce the risk of overloading constrained power lines.
Switched Source has been developing grid-enhancing power-flow control technologies since 2016, with a focus on helping utilities unlock existing infrastructure capacity and improve grid flexibility.
KEY QUOTES:
“Utilities are planning for a grid that is changing faster than it ever has before, but many of the tools they have at their disposal take years to implement and are 40+ year commitments. We need to give utilities more options: tools that can be deployed quickly, improve the performance of the grid they already have, and preserve flexibility as demand evolves. This investment allows us to put more of those tools in utilities’ hands at a time when speed to power, affordability, and reliability all matter.”
Charles Murray, Co-Founder and CEO of Switched Source
“At Cubit Capital, we partner with courageous leaders confronting foundational problems. Grid capacity is one of these growing challenges, with consequences for utilities, businesses, and the communities they serve. Switched Source combines leadership that understands the utility market with technology that has demonstrated its value in operating environments. With major utility rollouts already underway, they have built a strong foundation for continued growth and a pragmatic pathway for modernizing our electric infrastructure at scale.”
Philip Carson, Partner at Cubit Capital
“Utilities need technologies that integrate with existing electrical systems while improving the flexibility and performance of the distribution grid. Switched Source has developed a field-tested approach to a real operational challenge. We see an opportunity for its technology to support utilities as they add capacity, improve efficiency, and prepare their networks for continued load growth.”
Deni Miller, U.S. Electrification Business Lead at ABB
“As utilities face mounting pressure to improve reliability while keeping customer costs affordable, interest in non-wires solutions has never been greater. Switched Source stands out because the team understands how utilities make decisions. They have translated that insight into a practical technology that unlocks existing grid capacity today, helping utilities meet growing demand faster and more cost-effectively.”
Frank Balas, Senior Investment Director at Emerald Technology Ventures
“The distribution grid will require solid-state solutions to support rising electricity demand and increasing grid complexity. We see Switched Source as a proven leader with deployed equipment that provides tangible benefits to utilities and their customers.”
John Paserba, President and CEO of Southern States
