The post Ditto Wins $17 Million USSOCOM Contract For Enterprise-Wide Edge Data Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Ditto Wins $17 Million USSOCOM Contract For Enterprise-Wide Edge Data Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Ditto Wins $17 Million USSOCOM Contract For Enterprise-Wide Edge Data Platform
U.S. Special Operations Command awarded Ditto a $17 million contract to deploy its resilient edge data platform across USSOCOM. The Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies program awarded the contract.
The contract moves Ditto from pilot deployments into enterprise-wide fielding and is intended to enable real-time information sharing between personnel and autonomous systems operating at the tactical edge.
Ditto’s platform is designed for denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited connectivity environments where conventional cloud- or server-dependent systems can become unavailable.
The APFIT program was established through the fiscal 2022 National Defense Authorization Act to accelerate mature technologies developed by small businesses and non-traditional defense contractors into operational deployment.
Ditto said the award follows approximately three years of collaboration with Special Operations Forces users across multiple USSOCOM components.
The platform uses a peer-to-peer, server-optional architecture that allows devices to communicate directly and synchronize information even when traditional network connectivity is unavailable.
When connections are disrupted and later restored, Ditto said data automatically converges without data loss.
The system is also transport agnostic, allowing it to operate across different communications infrastructure and network conditions.
The contract was awarded through the U.S. Air Force’s Business and Enterprise Systems Product Innovation office and builds on Ditto’s work supporting Air Force Special Operations Command.
KEY QUOTES:
“Special operations don’t pause when the network drops, and neither can the data. That’s the entire reason Ditto exists. Crossing into enterprise fielding with the most demanding operators in the world is the clearest proof I can point to that it works where it matters most.”
Adam Fish, CEO and Co-Founder of Ditto
“What drew me to serve on Ditto’s Government Advisory Board was the platform’s operational relevance to the challenges SOF faces every day. In special operations, the difference between a successful mission and a failed one often comes down to who has the picture and who doesn’t. The Ditto platform is purpose-built for exactly the kind of contested environments SOF operates in.”
Rear Adm. Matthew Burns, U.S. Navy (Ret.)
“Years of end-user collaboration got us here. USSOCOM has operated alongside the Ditto platform in demanding environments, and this award reflects their confidence that it’s ready for the enterprise. The work ahead is about getting proven capability into the hands of more operators, faster. That’s what APFIT was designed to do, and that’s exactly what Ditto will deliver.”
Eric Hanft, SVP of Public Sector at Ditto

Flare Capital Partners Leads the Round, Bringing Total Funding to $30 Million; GenHealth’s AI Agents Complete Intake, Eligibility, Prior Authorization, Billing, and Denials Inside the Systems Providers Already Use, with Customers Getting Paid 30%+ More
GenHealth.ai , the healthcare AI company building AI agents that run the medical back office, today announced a $16.5 million Series A led by Flare Capital Partners . Existing investors Craft Ventures and Obvious Ventures participated, along with new investors Eniac Ventures, InHealth Ventures, Epsilon Health Investors, and ARTIS. The round brings GenHealth’s total funding to $30 million.
The United States spends about $1 trillion a year on healthcare administration, and most of that work is still done by people clicking through systems that do not talk to each other. Getting care approved and paid for means hundreds of actions across EHRs, payer portals, fax lines, and phone calls. Those bottlenecks delay treatment for patients and leave providers and suppliers chasing revenue they have already earned.
GenHealth’s AI agents connect those systems and carry the work through to completion. The agents run intake, eligibility verification, prior authorization, billing, denials, and custom workflows end to end, inside the EHR, payer portals, fax, and phone systems a practice already uses. A practice brings GenHealth on the way it would hire a person: staff shows the agents how they work, the practice creates user accounts for the AI, and the agents learn those exact workflows before going live. GenHealth’s US-based billing team handles exceptions, and staff stays in the loop for decisions that need judgment.
“The problem with automating healthcare administration was never just the AI. It’s that the AI is not connected to the systems providers already use, like the EHRs, plan portals, fax, and bank accounts,” said Ricky Sahu, Co-Founder and CEO at GenHealth.ai. “At GenHealth we built those connections ourselves and created rails for workflows to run on, with context from our own model trained on 140 million patients. The result is patients getting care faster and providers getting paid over 30% more, which is unheard of in RCM.”
GenHealth was founded in 2023 by Sahu and Ethan Siegel after Sahu’s decade building interoperability APIs for the largest US health plans at 1upHealth and CareJourney. The company’s agents are built on its Large Medical Model, a foundation model trained on the coded claims and clinical histories of more than 140 million patients.
“Provider organizations do not need another system of record. They need the work done,” said Vic Lanio, Partner at Flare Capital Partners. “GenHealth is not just agentified SaaS. They have agents working alongside humans, in the providers’ current systems, completing the work. That’s why we led this round.”
Customers include medical groups, durable medical equipment suppliers, and health plans. “We transitioned to GenHealth for full-service intake and billing and couldn’t be happier,” said Jack Bachman, Owner and CEO at Piedmont Medical Solutions. “By leveraging AI to make the process faster and easier, they’ve automated more work with better results than our previous outsourced team, which was five times their size. As a true partner that does not use offshore billing workers, they catch problems sooner and offer a level of transparency we never had before.”
GenHealth will use the funding to grow its engineering and go-to-market teams, extend its agents into additional workflows for provider groups and health plans, and continue improving the model underneath them. The company has grown to more than 20 employees since its seed round and is hiring across engineering, operations, and go-to-market. Open roles are listed at genhealth.ai/jobs .
About GenHealth.ai
GenHealth.ai builds AI agents that run the medical back office. Its agents complete intake, eligibility, prior authorization, billing, and denials end to end inside the EHRs, payer portals, fax lines, and phone systems that providers already use, with US-based billers and customer staff in the loop for exceptions. GenHealth’s agents are built on its Large Medical Model, trained on the coded claims and clinical histories of more than 140 million patients. The company is headquartered in Boston and works with medical groups, DME suppliers, and health plans. Learn more at genhealth.ai .
About Flare Capital Partners
Flare Capital Partners is a Boston-based venture capital firm focused on healthcare technology. The firm invests in early-stage companies transforming the business of healthcare and partners with leading health systems, health plans, and industry executives. Learn more at flarecapital.com .

candidates.text:
Rhino USA Secures $15 Million Asset-Backed Facility From Texas Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Rhino USA Secures $15 Million Asset-Backed Facility From Texas Capital
Rhino USA has closed a $15 million asset-backed loan facility with Texas Capital to support inventory investment, working capital optimization, and continued expansion across national retail, e-commerce, and international markets.
The Austin, Texas-based company designs truck, towing, and off-road adventure gear and has been expanding across multiple distribution channels, including its own website, Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart.com, and retail locations in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and Europe.
Rhino USA said revenue has doubled over the past two years and quadrupled over the past three years as the company has expanded its product line and customer base. The business now serves millions of customers and employs more than 90 people.
The company was co-founded by brothers Cameron and Dylan Repic, with their father Ted Repic later joining as CEO. Rhino USA began in Murrieta, California, before relocating its headquarters to Austin. Its products are positioned around truck, towing, recovery, and off-road use and are backed by a lifetime guarantee.
The new financing was arranged through Texas Capital’s Asset Based Lending team. Rhino USA plans to use the facility to invest ahead of anticipated demand by increasing inventory levels, strengthening its U.S. distribution network, and supporting hiring in Central Texas and Georgia.
The financing also supports Rhino USA’s broader retail expansion strategy as the company seeks to increase its presence with major national retailers. Management sees inventory availability and supply chain flexibility as important components of maintaining growth as distribution expands across physical retail and digital channels.
Rhino USA is also developing RhinoWorld, a 182-acre brand campus and product proving ground located outside Austin. Plans for the property include an innovation laboratory, content studio, more than eight miles of obstacle terrain, and potential future access for first responder training and community programs. The site is located in a federally designated Opportunity Zone, and Rhino USA said it has already added three full-time positions there in 2026.
The company intends to use RhinoWorld as a location for developing, testing, and demonstrating products under real-world conditions while further expanding its operations in Texas.
KEY QUOTES:
“This financing is a vote of confidence in what we’ve built and where we’re headed. We’ve been on a winning trajectory, and this capital gives us the fuel to sustain that momentum and push even harder. Texas Capital understood our business, our vision and what it takes to win at this level. This collaboration reflects the strength of the platform we’ve spent ten years building, and we’re just getting started.”
Ted Repic, CEO Of Rhino USA
“Inventory depth and supply chain agility are how an American brand competes at national scale. This facility lets us invest ahead of demand in inventory, in our U.S. distribution network, and in the people we’re hiring in Central Texas and Georgia. The Texas Capital team understood that from day one, and having a Texas-based financial services firm with national reach matters as we keep building here.”
Jeremy Bell, COO Of Rhino USA
“We are proud to support Rhino USA’s continued expansion with a financing solution tailored to its needs. As the company continues to scale its operations and broaden its market reach, we look forward to serving as a trusted financial partner in the next phase of its growth.”
Grant Weiss, Managing Director In Asset Based Lending At Texas Capital

candidates.text:
Everphone Secures €15 Million Corporate Loan From Commerzbank And KfW
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Everphone Secures €15 Million Corporate Loan From Commerzbank And KfW
Everphone secured a €15 million corporate loan from Commerzbank and KfW to finance additional workplace devices for its Device-as-a-Service business.
The company plans to use the proceeds to purchase new laptops, smartphones, tablets, and other workplace devices that are provided to corporate customers’ employees under long-term rental arrangements.
The financing represents an important shift in Everphone’s capital structure.
For the first time, the company is using a corporate loan based on its overall creditworthiness rather than financing secured against individual pools of devices.
The transaction builds on Everphone’s roughly 10-year relationship with Commerzbank, which serves as its primary bank.
KfW is participating through its Venture Tech Growth Financing program.
The participation marks KfW’s second financing involving Everphone following an earlier transaction in 2023 and 2024.
Everphone said the new financing structure significantly reduces its refinancing costs.
The interest margin is approximately 20 basis points lower than under its previous financing.
Because financing costs represent a major component of unit economics in Device-as-a-Service, the company said the reduced margin directly improves profitability.
Longer financing terms are also expected to allow Everphone to purchase larger device volumes at lower unit costs.
This is particularly important for replacement devices, which Everphone provides to customers at no additional charge when hardware fails.
The lower financing costs contributed to Everphone reporting positive earnings before taxes for the first time in August 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“Everphone demonstrates how technology, the circular economy, and a scalable business model can be combined. We are delighted to contribute with our purchasing financing to enabling Everphone to capitalize on its growth opportunities and expand its market position further.”
Mirjam Kuppe-Klötzer, Senior Specialist Corporate Lending at Commerzbank Corporate Clients
“Especially during the growth phase, scale-ups need financing solutions that combine speed and predictability. This is precisely where we come in with KfW’s Venture Tech Growth Financing together with Commerzbank, supporting Everphone in positioning itself as an integral tech and sustainability partner for its customers.”
Jochen Eichmann, Head of Venture Tech Growth Financing at KfW
“Profitability in Device-as-a-Service is achieved at the unit economics level, and financing costs are one of the biggest items there. Our corporate finance team has set up several facilities in recent years, reducing the interest margin with every round. The structure with Commerzbank and KfW represents the biggest step yet for inventory.”
Veronika von Heise-Rotenburg, CFO of Everphone

candidates.text:
Meticulous Raises $15 Million Series A Led By Chemistry To Expand Software Testing Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Meticulous Raises $15 Million Series A Led By Chemistry To Expand Software Testing Platform
Meticulous raised $15 million in Series A funding to expand its software testing platform as AI coding tools accelerate the pace at which developers generate code. The round was led by Chemistry, with additional participation from Menlo Ventures.
Angel investors included former Stripe executive Lachy Groom; Poolside co-founder and co-CEO Jason Warner; Dropbox co-founder Arash Ferdowsi; former Adobe Chief Product Officer Scott Belsky; Vercel founder Guillermo Rauch; Segment founder and former OpenAI engineering lead Calvin French-Owen; Hex CTO Caitlin Colgrove; and former Cursor Head of Engineering Jason Ginsberg, who is now a Member of Technical Staff at xAI.
Meticulous is developing technology intended to address a growing bottleneck in AI-assisted software development: while AI agents can generate code increasingly quickly, testing and reviewing those changes can slow deployment.
The company provides an autonomous testing system that automatically creates and maintains thousands of user flows designed to cover edge cases across large software codebases.
Meticulous uses deterministic browsers and automated test generation, execution, and maintenance to reduce noise while identifying how software changes affect applications.
The platform can detect changes as small as a single-pixel difference across recorded user flows before code is shipped to production.
Its technology also gives engineers, product managers, and designers visibility into how proposed changes affect software before those changes are merged.
AI coding agents can use the same information to iterate on their own work before submitting it for human review.
Customers include Notion, ElevenLabs, Dropbox, Wiz, and LaunchDarkly.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’re moving into an era where code generation is relatively inexpensive, but that means code review and the feedback loop become the bottleneck. Meticulous helps us simultaneously move fast and raise the quality bar.”
Zach Davis, Director of Engineering at LaunchDarkly
“We piloted the tool, were immediately impressed and rolled it out across the entire engineering organization. Meticulous is unlike anything else, developers love it and it is now an essential guardrail of our software development process.”
Erdem Alparslan, Head of Developer Experience at Notion
“As we move closer and closer to truly exhaustive testing we’ve observed that this allows our customers to move at unprecedented speed. We’re excited to take the platform to the next level to allow another step change in velocity for our customers.”
Quentin Spencer-Harper, CTO of Meticulous
“Meticulous has built one of the most deeply loved products that I have come across in my eighteen years of investing.”
Ethan Kurzweil, Managing Partner at Chemistry

candidates.snippet:
Consano Bio has raised more than $15 million in an oversubscribed financing to advance C-1101, its investigational multi-protein biologic therapy for chronic painful lumbosacral radiculopathy, also known as chronic sciatica.
The post Consano Bio Raises More Than $15 Million To Advance C-1101 For Chronic Sciatica appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Consano Bio Raises More Than $15 Million To Advance C-1101 For Chronic Sciatica
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Consano Bio Raises More Than $15 Million To Advance C-1101 For Chronic Sciatica
Consano Bio has raised more than $15 million in an oversubscribed financing to advance C-1101, its investigational multi-protein biologic therapy for chronic painful lumbosacral radiculopathy, also known as chronic sciatica.
The financing exceeded the company’s $15 million target and was backed by a syndicate of accredited private investors.
Including the latest transaction, Consano Bio has raised more than $45 million since its founding three years ago.
The company plans to use the proceeds to complete its ongoing randomized, double-blind Phase 1 clinical trial of C-1101 and advance additional scientific and intellectual property work around C-1101 and other assets.
The C-1101-101 study is enrolling patients with chronic painful lumbosacral radiculopathy in Australia and the U.S.
Consano expects enrollment to be completed in early 2027, with clinical data anticipated during the first half of 2027.
Those results are intended to inform the next stages of clinical development.
The FDA granted C-1101 Fast Track designation for treatment of lumbosacral radiculopathy in August 2026.
Consano said there are currently no FDA-approved pharmaceutical treatments specifically for chronic sciatica.
C-1101 is a platelet-derived multi-protein biologic designed to modulate inflammation while stimulating and enhancing cellular repair at the site of injury.
The therapy contains consistent concentrations of cytokines, growth factors and matrix proteins and is delivered through an epidural injection directly to the site of nerve injury.
Consano is positioning C-1101 as a potential disease-modifying approach rather than a treatment focused solely on temporary symptom relief.
KEY QUOTE:
“C-1101 represents a new category of disease-modifying biologics, designed to activate cellular repair and alleviate the pain and dysfunction that results from orthopedic conditions. LSR is where we begin, and we believe the potential of this approach extends well beyond a single condition. The recently closed financing allows us to complete our first clinical study and to assess how C-1101 affects patients with chronic LSR versus an epidural saline injection. This is an exciting time for Consano Bio, and we are building toward what could transform how these conditions are treated.”
Andrew Hall, Chief Executive Officer of Consano Bio

Medincell has secured an additional €13.8 million in non-dilutive financing from European commercial banks and Bpifrance, bringing the biopharmaceutical company’s total non-dilutive financing secured since July 2026 to €41.8 million.

candidates.text:
Medincell Secures €13.8 Million In Non-Dilutive Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Medincell Secures €13.8 Million In Non-Dilutive Financing
Medincell has secured an additional €13.8 million in non-dilutive financing from European commercial banks and Bpifrance, bringing the biopharmaceutical company’s total non-dilutive financing secured since July 2026 to €41.8 million.
The latest financing follows €28 million in non-dilutive bank financing announced in July. Medincell said the new capital was secured on market terms and does not include equity-linked instruments, meaning the financing will not dilute existing shareholders.
The company has also taken steps to reduce and extend its outstanding debt. In July 2026, Medincell repaid €23.2 million to the European Investment Bank, including €20 million of principal and related capitalized interest. The principal repayment represented 50% of its existing EIB financing facility.
Combined with the new financing, those actions have extended Medincell’s debt maturity profile through September 2031. The company reported €84.8 million in cash and cash equivalents as of March 31, 2026.
Medincell is a clinical- and commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing long-acting injectable medicines using its proprietary BEPO and BEPO Star drug-delivery technologies. The technologies are designed to enable controlled delivery of therapeutic drugs for periods ranging from several days to several months following a subcutaneous or local injection.
Risperidone LAI became the first treatment based on BEPO technology to receive FDA approval, initially for schizophrenia in April 2023 and subsequently for Bipolar I Disorder in October 2025. Teva markets the treatment in the U.S. under the UZEDY brand.
Medincell reached another commercial milestone in October 2026 when a once-monthly olanzapine long-acting injectable treatment for adults with schizophrenia received FDA approval. Teva plans to launch the product in the U.S. under the WELTRUZA brand during the fourth quarter of 2026. A European Marketing Authorization Application for the treatment was accepted by the European Medicines Agency in May 2026.
Beyond its commercial products, Medincell maintains a pipeline of therapeutic candidates ranging from formulation-stage programs through Phase 3 clinical trials. The Montpellier, France-based company employs more than 150 people representing over 27 nationalities and works with pharmaceutical companies and foundations to develop long-acting treatment options across multiple therapeutic areas.

candidates.snippet:
DashFuel, a cloud-native software platform serving petroleum wholesalers, carriers, and retailers, has received a growth investment from Five Elms Capital. The funding will support the company's product development, artificial intelligence capabilities, go-to-market expansion, and customer success initiatives as it scales its operations across the petroleum distribution industry.
The post DashFuel Receives Growth Investment From Five Elms Capital To Expand Petroleum Distribution Software Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
DashFuel Receives Growth Investment From Five Elms Capital To Expand Petroleum Distribution Software Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
DashFuel Receives Growth Investment From Five Elms Capital To Expand Petroleum Distribution Software Platform
DashFuel, a cloud-native software platform serving petroleum wholesalers, carriers, and retailers, has received a growth investment from Five Elms Capital. The funding will support the company’s product development, artificial intelligence capabilities, go-to-market expansion, and customer success initiatives as it scales its operations across the petroleum distribution industry.
Founded in 2022, DashFuel provides an integrated operating platform designed to address the complex operational requirements of petroleum distribution. The industry faces challenges involving fluctuating fuel prices, logistics coordination, regulatory compliance, and fragmented technology systems that often require extensive manual processes.
DashFuel addresses these challenges by consolidating quoting, tank monitoring, dispatch, delivery, billing, reconciliation, and back-office integration into a single platform. Its technology enables petroleum operators to improve operational visibility, automate workflows, reduce administrative burdens, and protect margins while supporting business growth.
The company has established a growing customer base across the United States and reports strong gross and net revenue retention. Its platform is designed to help wholesalers and carriers expand operations without proportionally increasing headcount, while maintaining control over critical business processes.
The investment from Five Elms Capital will enable DashFuel to accelerate development of its core platform, particularly through additional AI-powered automation and workflow intelligence capabilities. These investments are intended to help customers make faster operational decisions, reduce manual intervention, and improve efficiency across petroleum distribution activities.
DashFuel also plans to expand its sales and go-to-market organization to reach additional petroleum distributors and transportation operators. Alongside these efforts, the company will continue investing in customer success and support infrastructure to maintain service quality as its customer base grows.
Five Elms Capital specializes in growth investments in business-to-business software companies, particularly those delivering AI-powered solutions for specialized industries. The firm manages more than $3 billion in assets, employs over 80 professionals, and has invested in more than 70 software platforms worldwide.
Through the partnership, Five Elms will provide capital and operational expertise to support DashFuel’s growth strategy, product innovation, customer retention, and market expansion.
KEY QUOTES:
“Petroleum distribution runs on thin margins and moves fast, prices shift multiple times a day, and a single operational miss can cost thousands of dollars and a customer relationship. We built DashFuel to give operators the infrastructure to compete: real-time visibility, intelligent automation, and end-to-end workflow control that the industry has long needed. This investment lets us build faster and reach more of the market that needs it.”
Miles Moen, Founder And CEO Of DashFuel
“DashFuel has built something genuinely rare: a modern, end-to-end platform with a team that has earned deep customer trust by delivering real, measurable results. The petroleum distribution market is large, underserved by legacy technology, and ready for a purpose-built solution like DashFuel. We’re excited to partner with Miles and the team as they scale.”
Thomas Kershisnik, Partner At Five Elms Capital

candidates.title: October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services
candidates.snippet:
Siris Capital has announced the formation of October Capital, a new private equity firm focused on investing in services businesses that help enterprises adopt, integrate, and scale transformative technologies.
The post October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services
Siris Capital has announced the formation of October Capital, a new private equity firm focused on investing in services businesses that help enterprises adopt, integrate, and scale transformative technologies.
October Capital is led by Frank Baker, who co-founded Siris in 2011 and will serve as CEO and Managing Partner. The firm launches with three investments already in place, including the completed acquisition of Takkion and signed acquisitions of EQ Retirement Solutions and Lenvi.
October Capital builds on a 15-year technology investment track record established at Siris. Over that period, Siris deployed more than $9.5 billion of equity capital, including more than $3 billion in services businesses. The firm said its services investments generated its strongest outcomes for investors.
October Capital will initially concentrate on three areas where its investment team has existing expertise: infrastructure supporting the AI economy, physical security technology, and financial infrastructure.
Within AI infrastructure, the firm plans to target services businesses that support the growing buildout of computing and power infrastructure required to deploy artificial intelligence at scale. In physical security, October Capital will focus on companies helping enterprises modernize systems used to address evolving threats.
The firm’s financial infrastructure strategy will target services supporting the modernization of financial markets, including businesses enabling automation, digital payments, and adoption of digital assets.
Baker leads a team of 16 investment professionals, including Managing Directors Dave Calamai and Seth Harward and Principals Kevin O’Brien and Grant Weisberg.
October Capital’s first completed platform investment is Takkion, a services provider to the energy industry that the firm believes is positioned to benefit from growing electricity demand associated with AI data center development.
The firm has also signed an agreement to acquire EQ Retirement Solutions, which provides pension programs with automation tools and digital payments infrastructure supporting more than 10 million members and approximately £10 billion in annual payments.
Its signed acquisition of Lenvi adds a provider of loan servicing platforms and AI-powered analytics used for areas including fraud detection and provisioning. Lenvi serves more than 150 lenders and supports over £100 billion of credit assets under management.
The formation of October Capital also follows the announced $4.2 billion sale of Equiniti to Bullish, a transaction intended to create a global transfer agent serving tokenized securities and digital assets.
October Capital is headquartered in West Palm Beach, Florida.
KEY QUOTES:
“Technologies such as AI and blockchain are going to reshape the global economy, but none of that promise matters until it works in the field. Services businesses bridge that gap, helping enterprises adopt and deploy these technologies at scale. It’s an enormous opportunity, and one we are well positioned to capture.”
Frank Baker, CEO And Managing Partner Of October Capital

Lippincott To Acquire Athletics To Expand Digital And AI Brand Capabilities
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Lippincott To Acquire Athletics To Expand Digital And AI Brand Capabilities
Lippincott has entered into an agreement to acquire Athletics, a New York-based brand and innovation studio, expanding its capabilities across digital experiences, creative technology and AI-powered brand activation. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close on November 2, 2026.
At closing, Athletics’ approximately 25 employees will join Lippincott while continuing to operate from the studio’s existing Brooklyn office.
Athletics combines branding and design with digital experiences, prototyping and creative technology.
The company has also developed Sesame, proprietary AI software used to create customized brand activation tools.
Lippincott plans to combine those capabilities with its existing strategy, design and engineering practices.
Management sees an opportunity to help clients move more quickly from defining a brand strategy to applying it across digital and physical customer experiences.
Athletics’ approach emphasizes prototyping and iterative development as part of the creative process, allowing teams to make brand concepts tangible earlier and refine them through testing.
The acquisition is intended to further integrate those capabilities with Lippincott’s global scale and strategic consulting work.
Lippincott has operated for more than 80 years and advises organizations on brand, experience and marketing strategy.
The firm sees AI and increasingly fragmented customer touchpoints as creating greater demand for brand systems that can be consistently applied across technology and experiences.
KEY QUOTES:
“Brands today must do much more than stand for something. They have to show up coherently across an increasingly complex set of experiences and technologies, while leaders simultaneously navigate the opportunities created by AI. Athletics’ focus on practicality strengthens our ability to translate ambitious ideas into tangible applications. Together, we can help our clients not only define what’s next for their brands, but build, activate and scale it.”
Michael D’Esopo, CEO of Lippincott
“Lippincott is a natural home for the next chapter of Athletics. We share a belief that the strongest creative work happens when strategy, design and technology come together from the beginning, with clients as part of the team and making as part of the thinking. Lippincott brings extraordinary depth in brand and business strategy and global scale. Combined with our studio approach, experimentation capabilities and proprietary technology, our entire leadership team believes we have an opportunity to take on bigger challenges and create greater impact for our clients.”
Jameson Proctor, CEO of Athletics

candidates.snippet:
ITpipes has received a strategic growth investment from Luminate Capital Partners to accelerate product development and expand its use of artificial intelligence across sewer and stormwater pipe inspection. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
The post ITpipes Secures Strategic Growth Investment From Luminate Capital Partners appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
ITpipes Secures Strategic Growth Investment From Luminate Capital Partners
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
ITpipes Secures Strategic Growth Investment From Luminate Capital Partners
ITpipes has received a strategic growth investment from Luminate Capital Partners to accelerate product development and expand its use of artificial intelligence across sewer and stormwater pipe inspection. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
ITpipes provides pipe inspection software used by more than 300 utilities, municipalities and CCTV contractors across the U.S. and Canada.
The platform is built on Esri ArcGIS and aligned with NASSCO PACP, MACP and LACP standards.
ITpipes plans to use Luminate’s investment to further develop AiDetect and broader capabilities for collecting, managing and analyzing underground infrastructure condition data.
AiDetect uses artificial intelligence to help identify defects found during pipe inspections.
ITpipes said the system achieves 97% defect-detection accuracy and reduces coding and quality assurance time by at least 50%.
Results are reviewed by NASSCO-certified experts.
The company plans to expand beyond AI-assisted defect coding toward a broader system of record that combines inspections, defect information and asset history to support maintenance planning, prioritization and capital allocation.
The investment comes as utilities face aging infrastructure and significant capital requirements.
ITpipes cited the American Society of Civil Engineers’ 2025 Report Card, which assigned U.S. wastewater infrastructure a D+ and estimated an annual capital investment gap of approximately $69 billion.
Lincoln International provided M&A advisory services to ITpipes shareholders, while Holland & Knight provided legal advice.
Kirkland & Ellis advised Luminate.
KEY QUOTES:
“For fifteen years, utilities and contractors have trusted ITpipes with the condition data behind their rehabilitation and capital decisions, and that trust is the foundation our AI is built on. AiDetect works because it’s trained on real inspection data and checked by NASSCO-certified experts, not because it’s the newest thing on the market. Partnering with Luminate lets us build faster for the cities, counties, and contractors who count on us, with the same reliability that earned their trust.”
Ned Bebawy, CEO of ITpipes
“ITpipes has earned something rare in this market: the trust of the utilities, municipalities, and contractors who depend on accurate inspection data every day. Ned and the team have paired that reputation with real product innovation, including AiDetect, and we’re excited to partner with them to build the tools their customers need, reliable, easy to use, and grounded in how the work actually gets done.”
Andrew Baldwin, Partner at Luminate Capital

MOYOM Biotech has completed a new financing round from the Cathay Consumer Co-Creation Fund to accelerate international growth of its regenerative aesthetics business. Financial terms of the financing were not disclosed.

Its flagship brand is Aphranel, a CaHA-based regenerative aesthetics product designed to provide immediate structural support, regenerative stimulation and complete biodegradation.
MOYOM’s underlying platform includes its proprietary ACD-MT raspberry-shaped through-hole CaHA microspheres and PCD-ETT physically cross-linked CMC gel technology.

Aphranel received Class III medical device registration from China’s National Medical Products Administration in February 2025.
The product subsequently received certification under the European Union Medical Device Regulation in May 2026.
Since its commercial launch in May 2025, Aphranel has been introduced at more than 700 medical aesthetics clinics across China.
MOYOM plans to use Cathay Capital’s investment and global network to accelerate clinical translation, pursue additional regulatory approvals and expand into overseas markets.
The company also plans to continue investing in next-generation regenerative biomaterials.

candidates.snippet:
Locus Lock has raised a strategic funding round led by Range Ventures to accelerate deployment of its software-defined GNSS technology across aerospace, defense, and autonomous systems. In-Q-Tel participated alongside Backswing Ventures, Aurelia Foundry, Techstars, Golden Seeds, Creations VC, POV Ventures and other investors.
The post Locus Lock Raises Strategic Funding Led By Range Ventures For Software-Defined GNSS appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Locus Lock Raises Strategic Funding Led By Range Ventures For Software-Defined GNSS
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Locus Lock Raises Strategic Funding Led By Range Ventures For Software-Defined GNSS
Locus Lock has raised a strategic funding round led by Range Ventures to accelerate deployment of its software-defined GNSS technology across aerospace, defense, and autonomous systems. In-Q-Tel participated alongside Backswing Ventures, Aurelia Foundry, Techstars, Golden Seeds, Creations VC, POV Ventures and other investors.
Locus Lock is developing positioning, navigation, and timing technology for environments where satellite navigation may be degraded, jammed, spoofed, or denied.
Rather than tying advanced GNSS capabilities to specialized hardware, Locus Lock runs signal processing in software on general-purpose computing infrastructure.
The architecture is designed to allow positioning capabilities to be updated as threats, missions and supported platforms change.
Locus Lock said it is already integrating its technology into platforms spanning air, ground, maritime, and space applications after years of development and field testing with aerospace and defense customers.
The new capital will support customer deployments, continued development of software-defined PNT technology, expansion of the engineering team and the launch of Leo200.
Leo200 is scheduled to launch in October 2026 as a software-defined GNSS receiver platform intended to provide a path from engineering evaluation through integration and deployment.
An Evaluation Kit will initially allow engineering teams to test the technology within their own systems.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’ve spent the past several years demonstrating Locus Lock in real-world RF environments with some of the top defense primes, putting the technology through the kinds of conditions our customers and partners face in the field. The threat is advancing at software speed, but the rest of the industry is still trying to counter it at hardware speed. Locus Lock closes that gap by bringing the adaptability of software to resilient positioning, allowing capabilities to evolve as quickly as the threats do.”
Hailey Nichols, Founder and CEO of Locus Lock
“Positioning and navigation underpin nearly every modern defense system and the threats to GPS are evolving faster than traditional receiver development cycles. A software-defined approach creates the ability to adapt positioning capabilities much more rapidly as threats, missions, and platforms change. Locus Lock is building an architecture for PNT that reflects where both the technology and the operating environment are going and aligns to the demand signal we’ve seen from the U.S. and allied nations.”
Nat Puffer, Partner at In-Q-Tel
“When networking, radio and automotive moved from purpose-built hardware to software on general-purpose compute, multi-year design cycles became release cycles measured in weeks, and entire industries were reshaped as a result. GNSS is one of the last critical technologies still tied to hardware, and it’s the one where adaptability matters most. Jamming and spoofing evolve at software speed, and new constellations and signals are coming online faster than any hardware roadmap can absorb. A receiver that has to be redesigned to keep up will always be behind. Hailey and the team have proven a software-defined architecture works in real contested environments, and we think it becomes the foundation for how every autonomous platform navigates.”
Chris Erickson, Partner at Range Ventures

HappyCo has received a significant investment from Lone View Capital to accelerate development and adoption of its property operations platform for multifamily housing. The financial terms were not disclosed.
The post HappyCo Secures Investment From Lone View Capital To Expand AI-Powered Property Operations Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
HappyCo Secures Investment From Lone View Capital To Expand AI-Powered Property Operations Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
HappyCo Secures Investment From Lone View Capital To Expand AI-Powered Property Operations Platform
HappyCo has received a significant investment from Lone View Capital to accelerate development and adoption of its property operations platform for multifamily housing. The financial terms were not disclosed.
HappyCo’s existing management team, led by founder and CEO Jindou Lee, will continue leading the company following the transaction.
Founded in 2011, HappyCo began as a property inspection solution and has expanded into a broader platform spanning maintenance, asset management, and sourcing workflows.
A major part of the company’s recent development has been JoyAI, an artificial intelligence orchestration layer designed to automate and optimize operational tasks for on-site property teams.
HappyCo serves many of the largest multifamily owners and operators, including the majority of the National Multifamily Housing Council’s top 50 managers. Its products have been deployed across more than five million apartment homes.
The company has built its platform using more than a decade of maintenance interactions and data from approximately one billion inspected items.
HappyCo plans to use Lone View’s backing to continue investing in product development, AI capabilities and customer success while expanding the reach of its platform.
Houlihan Lokey served as financial adviser to HappyCo and DLA Piper served as its legal counsel. Ropes & Gray served as legal counsel to Lone View.
KEY QUOTES:
“For more than a decade, we’ve been focused on solving real operational problems for our customers. Today marks the beginning of the next chapter in that journey. Our customers consistently tell us two things: they want best-in-class software and they want products to work together seamlessly. Our partnership with Lone View will enable us to continue building exceptional products and collaborating with other great companies to deliver even more value for our customers.”
Jindou Lee, Founder and CEO of HappyCo
“We’re excited to partner with Jindou and the entire HappyCo team as they execute on the next phase of their vision. HappyCo has built a market-leading platform, earned the trust of the industry’s largest owners and operators, and established a strong foundation for future growth. We look forward to bringing our experience scaling technology businesses to help HappyCo build on their strong momentum and support their long-term growth.”
Doug Ceto, Partner at Lone View Capital

The post Rising Tide Raises Seed Round Led By Left Lane Capital For AI-Powered Property Management Network appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Rising Tide Raises Seed Round Led By Left Lane Capital For AI-Powered Property Management Network
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Rising Tide Raises Seed Round Led By Left Lane Capital For AI-Powered Property Management Network
Rising Tide has closed an undisclosed seed financing led by Left Lane Capital to expand its network of independently owned residential property management companies.
Left Lane incubated Rising Tide alongside founder and CEO Blake Mohseni based on the firms’ view that property management represents a large, fragmented market where artificial intelligence can automate administrative work without eliminating local operating relationships.
Rising Tide is building what it describes as a federation of independent property management businesses.
Rather than consolidating acquired companies under one national brand, Rising Tide provides capital and shared technology while allowing participating operators to retain their local names, teams and customer relationships.
The company is targeting a property management market it estimates exceeds $100 billion and includes more than 240,000 firms.
Rising Tide believes many smaller operators lack the technology, systems and back-office infrastructure available to larger institutional platforms.
Its strategy centers on using AI to reduce administrative workloads so local operators can spend more time working directly with property owners and tenants.
The company is developing those tools through The Lab, where Rising Tide builds and tests AI applications inside operating property management companies.
The Lab is currently working with three property management firms. Rising Tide retains ownership of the technology it develops, while participating operators receive access at no cost and retain control of their business data.
Left Lane Capital was founded in 2019 and invests in high-growth internet and consumer technology companies from offices in New York and London.
KEY QUOTES:
“AI is changing the definition of what premier service looks like in property management. It gives our operators more room for the relationships with owners and tenants that actually built their business. This funding brings that same approach to more independent property management firms: real technology, real capital, and partnership instead of a takeover.”
Blake Mohseni, Founder and CEO of Rising Tide
“We have invested over $100 million into AI companies transforming traditional services industries, from accounting to dental. Property management is universal, mission-critical, and not for the faint of heart. Blake and his team have the thoughtful approach needed to bring AI to the industry and drive modernization alongside tenured operators.”
Vinny Pujji, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Left Lane Capital
